meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

examples.text: Aakif Ndel.
examples.trans: Aakif Ndel.

examples.text: Yo Aakif
examples.trans: I Aakif

meanings.note: Indicates position or movement downward.

examples.text: La cocina está abajo.
examples.trans: The kitchen is downstairs.

examples.text: Te espero abajo en el patio.
examples.trans: I will wait for you downstairs in the courtyard.

examples.text: Claro que vamos a abandonar la sala, pero no porque lo digas tú.
examples.trans: Of course we're going to leave the hall, just not because you say so.

examples.text: Yo abandonar
examples.trans: I abandonar

meanings.note: Often seen in plural compounds such as cera de abejas ('beeswax') and miel de abejas ('bee honey').

examples.text: Una abeja se posó en la flor del limonero.
examples.trans: A bee landed on the lemon tree blossom.

examples.text: La tela está cubierta con cera pura de abejas.
examples.trans: The cloth is coated with pure beeswax.

meanings.note: Used literally or figuratively (ablandarse, to soften up).

examples.text: El vapor ablanda la madera.
examples.trans: Steam softens the wood.

examples.text: Con una sonrisa siempre se ablanda.
examples.trans: With a smile he always softens up.

meanings.note: A legal professional (feminine: la abogada).

examples.text: El abogado está aquí.
examples.trans: The lawyer is here.

examples.text: Vemos los abogados desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lawyers from the door.

examples.text: Hola, ¿Hiba Abouk?
examples.trans: Hello, Hiba Abouk?

examples.text: Yo Abouk
examples.trans: I Abouk

meanings.note: Describes clothing, blankets, or rooms that keep out the cold.

examples.text: Es una pieza abrigada.
examples.trans: It is a warm piece.

examples.text: Tengo una manta abrigada, así que esta noche estoy muy cómodo.
examples.trans: I have a warm blanket, so tonight I am very comfortable.

meanings.note: Warm outer coat worn in cold or rainy weather.

examples.text: El abrigo está aquí.
examples.trans: The coat is here.

examples.text: Vemos los abrigos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coats from the door.

meanings.note: Months of the year are lowercase and masculine in Spanish.

examples.text: En abril llueve a menudo.
examples.trans: In April it often rains.

examples.text: Llegaron a la ciudad en abril.
examples.trans: They arrived in the city in April.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle abierto.

examples.text: Abro la ventana por la mañana.
examples.trans: I open the window in the morning.

examples.text: Ayer abrimos la tienda temprano.
examples.trans: Yesterday we opened the shop early.

meanings.note: In en absoluto, means 'not at all'.

examples.text: Hay un silencio absoluto aquí.
examples.trans: There is complete silence here.

examples.text: No me molesta en absoluto.
examples.trans: It does not bother me at all.

meanings.note: Feminine counterpart of abuelo.

examples.text: Mi abuela amasaba pan casero todos los domingos.
examples.trans: My grandmother kneaded homemade bread every Sunday.

examples.text: Guardamos la receta de limón de nuestra abuela.
examples.trans: We keep our grandmother's lemon recipe.

meanings.note: Plural los abuelos also means 'grandparents'.

examples.text: El abuelo está aquí.
examples.trans: The grandfather is here.

examples.text: Vemos los abuelos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the grandfathers from the door.

meanings.note: Meaning shifts between ser (boring) and estar (bored).

examples.text: Este documento es muy aburrido.
examples.trans: This document is very boring.

examples.text: Hoy no estoy nada aburrido.
examples.trans: Today I am not bored at all.

examples.text: Aburrirme hasta morir.
examples.trans: Boring myself to death.

examples.text: Yo aburrir
examples.trans: I aburrir

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from acabar.

examples.text: Es una pieza acabada.
examples.trans: It is a finished piece.

examples.text: Estamos acabados
examples.trans: We are finished

acabar.gloss: to finish; to have just (acabar de)

meanings.en: to finish; to have just (acabar de)
meanings.note: Acabar de + infinitive means 'to have just done something'.

examples.text: Acabo de llegar del mercado.
examples.trans: I have just arrived from the market.

examples.text: Ya acabamos el trabajo de hoy.
examples.trans: We already finished today's work.

meanings.note: 1st-person singular present indicative of base lemma acabar; used in the periphrasis acabar de + infinitive to express an action that just happened.
Used standalone for completing a task or with gerund/preposition (acabar haciendo algo) for ending up doing something.

examples.text: Pues, mira, acabo de llegar de Los Ángeles y vengo agotada.
examples.trans: Well, look, I just got back from Los Angeles and I'm exhausted.

examples.text: Muy fuerte lo que acabo de hacer, muy fuerte.
examples.trans: What I've just done is really wild, really wild.

examples.text: En cuanto acabo las reuniones en la oficina, me bajo al bar a por un pincho.
examples.trans: As soon as I finish my meetings at the office, I head down to the bar for a bite.

related.gloss: to finish; to have just (with de)

acaso.gloss: perhaps; by chance (por si acaso = just in case)

meanings.en: perhaps; by chance (por si acaso = just in case)
meanings.note: Most common in everyday speech inside the fixed phrase por si acaso ('just in case').

examples.text: Llevo un paraguas pequeño por si acaso llueve.
examples.trans: I carry a small umbrella just in case it rains.

examples.text: Horneamos otra bandeja de pan por si acaso vienen más vecinos.
examples.trans: We baked another tray of bread just in case more neighbours come.

meanings.note: Por accidente means 'by accident'.

examples.text: El accidente está aquí.
examples.trans: The accident is here.

examples.text: Vemos los accidentes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the accidents from the door.

examples.text: Qué bien. Será de acción.
examples.trans: How great. It must be an action play.

examples.text: Yo acción
examples.trans: I acción

meanings.note: Used both for cooking oil (aceite de oliva) and lubricating oil on hinges.

examples.text: Pon dos gotas de aceite en la bisagra seca.
examples.trans: Put two drops of oil on the dry hinge.

examples.text: Aliñamos la sopa caliente con aceite de oliva.
examples.trans: We dress the hot soup with olive oil.

examples.text: Tiene acento argentino.
examples.trans: She has an Argentine accent.

examples.text: Me gusta mucho tu acento.
examples.trans: I really like your accent.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Aceptamos el presupuesto para arreglar la sala.
examples.trans: We accept the budget to fix the room.

examples.text: ¿Aceptan pago en efectivo en este puesto?
examples.trans: Do they accept cash payment at this stall?

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for the pedestrian walkway beside a street.

examples.text: La acera está aquí.
examples.trans: The pavement is here.

examples.text: Vemos las aceras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pavements from the door.

acercar.gloss: to bring closer; to move closer

meanings.en: to bring closer; to move closer
meanings.note: Spelling changes c -> qu before -e (acerqué, acerque).

examples.text: Acerca la lámpara a la mesa de trabajo, por favor.
examples.trans: Bring the lamp closer to the workbench, please.

examples.text: Acercamos dos sillas de madera junto al piano.
examples.trans: We move two wooden chairs closer to the piano.

meanings.en: to bring her closer; to move it closer
meanings.note: Compound infinitive of base lemma acercar plus the feminine singular direct object enclitic pronoun la (referring to a female person or a feminine noun such as la cámara or la silla).

meanings.en: to introduce her to; to draw her nearer (figurative)
meanings.note: Used figuratively for helping someone connect with another person, audience, or profession.

examples.text: Lo que hay que hacer es acercarla un poco más a la cámara.
examples.trans: What you have to do is bring it a little closer to the camera.

examples.text: Intenté acercarla al mundo del teatro, pero ella prefería hacer series.
examples.trans: I tried to bring her closer to the theater world, but she preferred doing TV series.

meanings.note: Strong metal alloy used in piano strings, tools, and kitchenware.

examples.text: Las cuerdas agudas del piano son de acero fino.
examples.trans: The high piano strings are made of thin steel.

examples.text: Guarda los tornillos de acero en esta caja pequeña.
examples.trans: Keep the steel screws in this small box.

meanings.note: Spelling changes g -> j before o (acojo).

examples.text: El patio acoge a muchos vecinos.
examples.trans: The courtyard welcomes many neighbours.

examples.text: La casa nos acogió con cariño.
examples.trans: The house hosted us warmly.

meanings.note: Takes personal a before a person (acompañar a Carmen); also used for musical accompaniment (con el violín).

examples.text: Te acompaño hasta la parada del autobús.
examples.trans: I will walk with you to the bus stop.

examples.text: El vecino acompaña a la pianista con su violín.
examples.trans: The neighbour accompanies the pianist on his violin.

examples.text: ¿Te acuerdas de mi prima?
examples.trans: Do you remember my cousin?

examples.text: Me acuerdo perfectamente.
examples.trans: I remember perfectly.

meanings.note: Used with de for what you remember: me acuerdo de esta lámpara. Stem o changes to ue.

examples.text: ¿Te acuerdas de mi nombre?
examples.trans: Do you remember my name?

examples.text: No me acuerdo de dónde está la llave.
examples.trans: I don't remember where the key is.

meanings.note: Several musical notes played together.

examples.text: Toca un acorde muy suave.
examples.trans: She plays a very soft chord.

examples.text: Este acorde suena triste.
examples.trans: This chord sounds sad.

meanings.en: action! (cue to begin acting or rolling)
meanings.note: Quoted English filmmaking cue used in Paquita Salas during international or English-language auditions in place of Spanish ¡acción!.

examples.text: El director de casting levantó la mano y gritó: «¡"Action"!».
examples.trans: The casting director raised his hand and shouted: "'Action'!"

examples.text: En cuanto oigas «action», miras a cámara y sueltas el texto sin dudar.
examples.trans: As soon as you hear "action," look at the camera and deliver your lines without hesitating.

examples.text: Uno sale al escenario y ve lo difícil que es ser actor.
examples.trans: You step out onto the stage and see how hard it is to be an actor.

examples.text: Yo actor
examples.trans: I actor

meanings.note: Feminine plural of base lemma actriz; following Spanish orthography, final -z changes to -c- before -es.

examples.text: Como todas las actrices, está un poco loca.
examples.trans: Like all actresses, she's a little crazy.

examples.text: Pero tengo mucho lío con lo de los actores, las actrices, la tele...
examples.trans: But I have a huge mess on my hands with the actors, the actresses, TV...

examples.text: Paquita descubrió a varias de las mejores actrices de su generación.
examples.trans: Paquita discovered several of the best actresses of her generation.

examples.text: Mi prima es actriz.
examples.trans: My cousin is an actress.

examples.text: Las actrices esperan fuera.
examples.trans: The actresses are waiting outside.

examples.text: Eso es muy actual. Eso está en las noticias todo el día.
examples.trans: That's very topical. That's on the news all day long.

examples.text: Hablamos de actual en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about current, topical at the office.

meanings.note: Takes a written accent on ú in singular and 3rd plural present (actúo, actúa).

examples.text: Siempre actúa con mucha calma.
examples.trans: She always acts very calmly.

examples.text: Los músicos actúan el sábado en la plaza.
examples.trans: The musicians perform in the square on Saturday.

meanings.note: Refers both to the water-soluble paint medium (pintar a la acuarela) and to a finished watercolour painting.

examples.text: Javier pintó el patio con tinta y acuarela.
examples.trans: Javier painted the courtyard in ink and watercolour.

examples.text: Colgamos dos acuarelas pequeñas junto a la ventana.
examples.trans: We hung two small watercolours beside the window.

meanings.note: Relating to sound and room acoustics.

examples.text: Es una pieza acústica.
examples.trans: It is an acoustic piece.

examples.text: ¡Arquitecto acústico! ¿Diseña usted salas de conciertos?
examples.trans: An acoustic architect! Do you design concert halls?

examples.text: ¿La habrá adaptado una chiquita que se llama Hedda Gabler?
examples.trans: Could a young girl called Hedda Gabler have adapted it?

examples.text: Yo adaptar
examples.trans: I adaptar

meanings.note: Warm invitation to enter a room or proceed.

examples.text: ¡Adelante, la puerta está abierta!
examples.trans: Come in, the door is open!

examples.text: Adelante, puede sentarse aquí.
examples.trans: Go right ahead, you may sit here.

examples.text: Sí, he adelgazado tres kilos porque para la película tuve que engordar diez.
examples.trans: Yes, I've lost three kilos because for the movie I had to put on ten.

examples.text: Hablamos de adelgazar en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about lost weight at the office.

meanings.note: Además de + noun means 'in addition to / besides'.

examples.text: Compramos limones y, además, dos tarros de miel.
examples.trans: We bought lemons and, in addition, two jars of honey.

examples.text: La sala es luminosa y además muy silenciosa.
examples.trans: The room is bright and also very quiet.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: ¿Puedes adivinar quién llamó hoy?
examples.trans: Can you guess who called today?

examples.text: Adivinó la respuesta enseguida.
examples.trans: She guessed the answer right away.

meanings.note: Standard farewell across the Spanish-speaking world.

examples.text: ¡Adiós y buen viaje!
examples.trans: Goodbye and have a good trip!

examples.text: Dijo adiós desde la puerta.
examples.trans: She said goodbye from the doorway.

meanings.note: Plural adoquines: traditional paving stones in historic streets.

examples.text: El adoquín está aquí.
examples.trans: The cobblestone is here.

examples.text: Vemos los adoquines desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cobblestones from the door.

meanings.note: Expresses strong fondness in everyday speech.

examples.text: Adoro el olor a café recién hecho.
examples.trans: I adore the smell of freshly brewed coffee.

examples.text: Mis abuelos adoran este jardín.
examples.trans: My grandparents adore this garden.

examples.text: Pero ¿adónde vas, Lidia? ¿Qué haces así vestida?
examples.trans: Where are you going, Lidia? What are you doing dressed like that?

examples.text: Hablamos de adónde en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about where to at the office.

examples.text: Vamos al aeropuerto.
examples.trans: We're going to the airport.

examples.text: No hay aeropuerto aquí.
examples.trans: There's no airport here.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; llave de afinar is a piano tuning wrench.

examples.text: Carmen afina el piano de madera antes del viernes.
examples.trans: Carmen tunes the wooden piano before Friday.

examples.text: Afinamos cada cuerda con mucha paciencia y silencio.
examples.trans: We tune every string with great patience and quiet.

meanings.note: Opposite of apretar (to tighten).

examples.text: Aflojo el tornillo con cuidado.
examples.trans: I loosen the screw carefully.

examples.text: El mecánico aflojó la tuerca vieja.
examples.trans: The mechanic loosened the old nut.

agarrar.gloss: to grip; to stick; to take hold

meanings.en: to grip; to stick; to take hold
meanings.note: Said of paint or glue adhering to dry wood, as well as gripping with the hand.

examples.text: La pintura nueva agarra muy bien sobre madera seca.
examples.trans: Fresh paint sticks very well on dry wood.

examples.text: Agarra fuerte el otro extremo de la mesa.
examples.trans: Grip the other end of the table firmly.

agarro.gloss: I grab / I hold on to

meanings.en: I grab; I catch; I hold tightly
meanings.note: 1st-person singular present indicative of base lemma agarrar; in Peninsular Spanish it implies gripping firmly or securing a talent/opportunity before it slips away (unlike Latin America, it has no vulgar taboo sense in Spain).

examples.text: Si no la agarro a tiempo, se nos escapa a otra agencia.
examples.trans: If I don't grab hold of her in time, she'll slip away from us to another agency.

examples.text: Agarro el bolso, llamo un taxi y me planto en el rodaje en diez minutos.
examples.trans: I grab my bag, call a taxi, and show up on set in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Agencia de viajes = travel agency.

examples.text: Reservamos el billete en una agencia de viajes.
examples.trans: We booked the ticket at a travel agency.

examples.text: Hay varias agencias abiertas en esta avenida.
examples.trans: There are several branch offices open on this avenue.

meanings.note: In everyday Spanish, una agenda primarily refers to a physical or digital organizer/calendar where appointments and contacts are kept (a false friend when English 'agenda' means hidden ulterior motive, which is intenciones ocultas).
Refers to a busy professional's calendar of meetings and appearances (tener la agenda apretada).

examples.text: Sí, míralo en la agenda, Paquita, que sí lo apunté.
examples.trans: Yes, look it up in the planner, Paquita, I really did write it down.

examples.text: Esta semana tiene la agenda llena de entrevistas y pruebas de vestuario.
examples.trans: This week her schedule is packed with interviews and wardrobe fittings.

examples.text: Que no lloro, es que estoy un poco agobiada.
examples.trans: I'm not crying, I'm just a bit overwhelmed.

examples.text: Hablamos de agobiado en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about overwhelmed, stressed at the office.

meanings.en: got overwhelmed; panicked; felt suffocated with stress
meanings.note: 3rd-person singular preterite indicative of base lemma agobiar (typically pronominal agobiarse in Peninsular Spanish, a quintessential everyday verb for feeling stressed out or claustrophobic under pressure).
Transitive sense when an external situation or person pressures someone excessively.

examples.text: La chica se agobió un poquillo y yo me la traje aquí de fugitiva.
examples.trans: The girl got a little overwhelmed and I brought her out here like a runaway.

examples.text: El director la agobió con tantas notas antes de la primera toma.
examples.trans: The director overwhelmed her with so many notes before the first take.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza agradable.
examples.trans: It is a pleasant piece.

examples.text: Tranquilo y agradable, gracias, aunque esta maleta pesa mucho hoy.
examples.trans: Quiet and pleasant, thank you, though this suitcase weighs a lot today.

meanings.note: Feminine noun that takes el in the singular before stressed initial /a/ (el agua fría).

examples.text: Quiero un vaso de agua fría.
examples.trans: I want a glass of cold water.

examples.text: El agua de la ducha sale caliente.
examples.trans: The shower water comes out hot.

examples.text: Quería esperar después de los Goya para decírtelo, pero no lo puedo aguantar.
examples.trans: I wanted to wait until after the Goyas to tell you, but I can't hold it in.

examples.text: Hablamos de aguantar en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about hold in at the office.

meanings.note: Covers a sewing needle (aguja de coser), the hands of a clock (las agujas del reloj), and a magnetic compass needle.

examples.text: La aguja de acero azul apunta siempre hacia el norte.
examples.trans: The blued steel needle always points north.

examples.text: Busqué hilo y una aguja fina para coser el botón.
examples.trans: I looked for thread and a fine needle to sew the button.

meanings.note: Covers everything from tiny screw holes in wood to holes in clothing or walls.

examples.text: Hay dos agujeros pequeños para los tornillos en la madera.
examples.trans: There are two small screw holes in the wood.

examples.text: El perro cavó un agujero junto al árbol del jardín.
examples.trans: The dog dug a hole beside the garden tree.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization or understanding.

examples.text: ¡Ah, ya entiendo el mapa!
examples.trans: Ah, now I understand the map!

examples.text: ¿Ah, sí? Qué buena noticia.
examples.trans: Oh really? What good news.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.text: Voy para allá ahora mismo.
examples.trans: I am heading there right now.

examples.text: Ahora tenemos cuatro mesas libres.
examples.trans: Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Points to something at medium distance or near the listener.

examples.text: Deja las llaves ahí en la mesa.
examples.trans: Leave the keys there on the table.

examples.text: Ahí viene el autobús.
examples.trans: There comes the bus.

meanings.note: Al aire libre means 'outdoors'.

examples.text: El aire es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The air is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el aire.
examples.trans: We talk about the air.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine singular; cinta aislante is 'electrical tape'.

examples.text: Necesito un rollo de cinta aislante negra.
examples.trans: I need a roll of black electrical tape.

examples.text: El cristal grueso es un buen material aislante.
examples.trans: Thick glass is a good insulating material.

examples.text: Aquí tiene su pizza dos mitades, alitas y panes de ajo con queso.
examples.trans: Here is your half-and-half pizza, wings, and cheesy garlic bread.

examples.text: Hablamos de ajo en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about garlic at the office.

meanings.note: Exclamation of discovery or agreement.

examples.text: ¡Ajá, aquí estaban mis gafas!
examples.trans: Aha, here were my glasses!

examples.text: Ajá, eso explica el ruido.
examples.trans: Aha, that explains the noise.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

ala.gloss: wow! / come on! (variant of ¡hala!; title word in ¡Ala... Dina!)

meanings.note: Used in the title of the hit early-2000s Spanish TVE sitcom ¡Ala... Dina! (starring Lidia San José and Paz Padilla), which puns on the exclamation ¡hala! and the genie name Aladina.

meanings.en: wing (of a bird, plane, or building)
meanings.note: As a feminine noun (el ala, plural las alas; takes el in the singular due to stressed initial /ˈa/), it means 'wing'.

examples.text: Niña, el pico. Es Lidia San José, la niña de «¡Ala... Dina!».
examples.trans: Girl, watch your mouth. That's Lidia San José, the kid from "¡Ala... Dina!"

examples.text: ¡Ala, qué exagerada eres cuando te pones dramática!
examples.trans: Come on, how dramatic you get when you're putting on a scene!

meanings.note: Metal wire used for hanging lanterns or repairs.

examples.text: El alambre está aquí.
examples.trans: The wire is here.

examples.text: Vemos los alambres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the wires from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine noun taking el in the singular before stressed a- (el alba, al alba).

examples.text: Rocío enciende el horno de la cocina al alba.
examples.trans: Rocio lights the kitchen oven at dawn.

examples.text: El patio huele a azahar fresco desde el alba.
examples.trans: The courtyard smells of fresh orange blossom from daybreak.

meanings.note: Edible thistle bud prized in La Rioja and Navarre cuisine (frequently mentioned in Paquita Salas in connection with her hometown Navarrete); collective singular mucha alcachofa is idiomatic in Spanish for abundant local produce.

meanings.en: handheld reporter's microphone; showerhead (colloquial Peninsular Spanish)
meanings.note: In Spanish entertainment and press slang, la alcachofa refers to a reporter's foam-covered handheld mic thrust at celebrities on red carpets.

examples.text: En Navarrete hay mucha alcachofa, mucho pimiento, hay melocotón...
examples.trans: In Navarrete there are lots of artichokes, lots of peppers, peaches...

examples.text: Pero, bueno, así sale la alcachofa de tierna en esta tierra.
examples.trans: Well anyway, that's how tender the artichokes turn out in this region.

examples.text: En cuanto salió del estreno, le pusieron tres alcachofas delante para sacarle titulares.
examples.trans: As soon as she walked out of the premiere, reporters shoved three microphones in her face to get headlines out of her.

alegrar.gloss: to make glad; to cheer up

meanings.en: to make glad; to cheer up
meanings.note: Me alegra / nos alegra means 'it makes me/us glad'.

examples.text: Esa noticia nos alegra mucho.
examples.trans: That news makes us very glad.

examples.text: Las flores alegran toda la mesa.
examples.trans: The flowers brighten up the whole table.

meanings.note: Same singular form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: El vals empieza con un ritmo ligero y alegre.
examples.trans: The waltz begins with a light, cheerful rhythm.

examples.text: Los colores alegres dan mucha vida al patio.
examples.trans: Cheerful colours bring lots of life to the courtyard.

alegro.gloss: I'm glad (with me) / I brighten up

meanings.en: I am glad; I am happy (as me alegro)
meanings.note: 1st-person singular present indicative of base lemma alegrar, overwhelmingly used pronominally as me alegro (de algo / de que + subjunctive) to express warmth or congratulations.

meanings.en: I cheer up; I brighten (something) up
meanings.note: Transitive non-reflexive use: alegrar el día a alguien ('to make someone's day').

examples.text: Venga, vale. Me alegro de verte.
examples.trans: Alright, okay. I'm glad to see you.

examples.text: Me alegro muchísimo de que te hayan cogido para la serie.
examples.trans: I'm so glad they cast you in the series.

meanings.note: Common in warm Peninsular greetings like ¡Qué alegría verte! ('How lovely to see you!') and dar una alegría a alguien ('to bring someone great news/joy').

examples.text: Oye, a ver si ves a mi Pepe, que le vas a dar mucha alegría.
examples.trans: Hey, see if you drop in on my Pepe—you're going to make him so happy.

examples.text: ¡Qué alegría! Ven, dame un beso. ¿Qué tal?
examples.trans: What a joy to see you! Come here, give me a kiss. How are things?

related.gloss: to cheer up; to make happy

alejar.gloss: to move away; to step back (alejarse)

meanings.en: to move away; to step back (alejarse)
meanings.note: From lejos ('far'); reflexive alejarse means 'to step back / move further away'.

examples.text: Aléjate dos pasos para ver el cartel entero.
examples.trans: Step back two paces to see the whole sign.

examples.text: Alejamos las tazas limpias del borde de la mesa.
examples.trans: We move the clean cups away from the edge of the table.

examples.text: A ver, para que nos organicemos bien y no haya líos, lo haremos por orden alfabético.
examples.trans: Alright, so we stay organised and avoid arguments, we'll go in alphabetical order.

examples.text: Hablamos de alfabético en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about alphabetical at the office.

meanings.note: From Hispanic Arabic al-ḥánbal.

examples.text: La alfombra está aquí.
examples.trans: The rug is here.

examples.text: Vemos las alfombras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rugs from the door.

meanings.note: Indefinite pronoun used in statements and questions.

examples.text: ¿Necesita algo más de la cocina?
examples.trans: Do you need anything else from the kitchen?

examples.text: Hay algo dentro de la caja.
examples.trans: There is something inside the box.

meanings.note: Used with de to describe fabric or heavy art paper: una camisa de algodón, papel de algodón.

examples.text: Las sábanas blancas son de algodón fresco.
examples.trans: The white sheets are made of cool cotton.

examples.text: Dibujó el mapa sobre papel grueso de algodón.
examples.trans: He drew the map on heavy cotton paper.

meanings.note: Refers exclusively to people.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de llamar a la puerta.
examples.trans: Someone just knocked at the door.

examples.text: ¿Hay alguien en recepción?
examples.trans: Is anyone at the front desk?

meanings.note: Shortens to algún before masculine singular nouns (algún problema).

examples.text: ¿Tiene algún cartel en la puerta?
examples.trans: Does it have any sign on the door?

examples.text: Compré algunas manzanas rojas.
examples.trans: I bought some red apples.

meanings.note: Air drawn into and expelled from the lungs, or the ability to breathe easily.

examples.text: Recuperó el aliento rápidamente.
examples.trans: He caught his breath quickly.

examples.text: Se quedó sin aliento.
examples.trans: He ran out of breath.

examples.text: Aquí tiene su pizza dos mitades, alitas y panes de ajo con queso.
examples.trans: Here is your half-and-half pizza, wings, and cheesy garlic bread.

examples.text: Hablamos de alita en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about chicken wings at the office.

examples.text: (SUSPIRA ALIVIADA)
examples.trans: (SIGHS RELIEVED)

examples.text: Yo ALIVIADA
examples.trans: I ALIVIADA

meanings.note: ¡Qué alivio! means 'What a relief!'.

examples.text: El alivio es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The relief is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el alivio.
examples.trans: We talk about the relief.

meanings.note: Allá va is a natural everyday phrase before flipping a switch or starting something.

examples.text: Allá va la primera prueba de la lámpara.
examples.trans: Here goes the first test of the lamp.

examples.text: Pon las sillas plegadas más allá del arco.
examples.trans: Put the folded chairs further past the arch.

meanings.note: Points to a place farther away from both speakers.

examples.text: La farmacia está allí en la esquina.
examples.trans: The pharmacy is over there on the corner.

examples.text: Vivimos allí durante seis años.
examples.trans: We lived there for six years.

meanings.note: Feminine noun taking el in the singular before stressed /a/ (el alma, las almas).

examples.text: El alma está aquí.
examples.trans: The soul is here.

examples.text: Vemos las almas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the souls from the door.

meanings.note: Plural almacenes.

examples.text: El almacén está aquí.
examples.trans: The storeroom is here.

examples.text: Vemos los almacenes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the storerooms from the door.

meanings.note: Classic Mediterranean baking ingredient in tarts and biscuits.

examples.text: Rocío hornea galletas crujientes de almendra y limón.
examples.trans: Rocio bakes crunchy almond and lemon biscuits.

examples.text: Tostamos las almendras cinco minutos en el horno.
examples.trans: We toast the almonds for five minutes in the oven.

meanings.note: Soft bed pillow.

examples.text: La almohada está aquí.
examples.trans: The pillow is here.

examples.text: Vemos las almohadas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pillows from the door.

meanings.note: Related to the verb almorzar ('to have lunch'); in parts of Spain (including Valencia) el almuerzo can also refer to a hearty mid-morning snack.

examples.text: Servimos el almuerzo en el patio a las dos.
examples.trans: We serve lunch in the courtyard at two o'clock.

examples.text: No me muevo de la recepción hasta la hora del almuerzo.
examples.trans: I am not moving from the front desk until lunchtime.

meanings.note: Used reflexively (alojarse) for staying at a hotel or inn.

examples.text: Muchos viajeros se alojan aquí.
examples.trans: Many travellers stay here.

examples.text: Nos alojamos en una casa tranquila.
examples.trans: We stayed at a quiet inn.

meanings.note: Covers both renting from a landlord and renting out to a guest.

examples.text: Alquilamos una habitación con balcón.
examples.trans: We rent a room with a balcony.

examples.text: Ellos alquilaron un piso cerca del río.
examples.trans: They rented a flat near the river.

meanings.note: Monthly rent paid for a flat or building.

examples.text: El alquiler está aquí.
examples.trans: The rent is here.

examples.text: Vemos los alquileres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rents from the door.

meanings.note: Followed by de before a noun: alrededor de la mesa ('around the table').

examples.text: Pusimos seis sillas alrededor de la mesa grande.
examples.trans: We placed six chairs around the big table.

examples.text: Miró alrededor para saludar a todos los amigos.
examples.trans: She looked around to greet all the friends.

meanings.note: Alto y claro means 'loud and clear'.

examples.text: Es una pieza alta.
examples.trans: It is a tall piece.

examples.text: Alto y claro. ¿Estás junto a la fuentecita de piedra?
examples.trans: Loud and clear. Are you beside the little stone fountain?

examples.text: ¿Cuál es tu altura?
examples.trans: What is your height?

examples.text: Tiene una buena altura.
examples.trans: She is a good height.

am.gloss: am (quoted English verb in self-tape audition)

meanings.note: Quoted English audition word in Paquita Salas, spoken phonetically by Spanish actresses recording rudimentary English self-tapes (notice how English uses 'I am 25 years old' whereas Spanish uses tener: tengo 25 años).

examples.text: En su vídeo de presentación en inglés, ella repite despacio: «Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old».
examples.trans: In her English self-tape introduction, she repeats slowly: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old."

examples.text: Siempre se traba al decir «I am» cuando se pone nerviosa delante de la cámara.
examples.trans: She always stumbles when saying "I am" whenever she gets nervous in front of the camera.

related.gloss: I have (used for age in Spanish: tengo ... años)

meanings.note: Muy amable is a warm thank-you ('very kind of you').

examples.text: Es una pieza amable.
examples.trans: It is a kind piece.

examples.text: Oh, qué amable es usted, señor. Solo medio vaso.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

examples.text: Lleva hasta a Amaia Salamanca.
examples.trans: He even represents Amaia Salamanca.

examples.text: Yo Amaia
examples.trans: I Amaia

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with its noun.

examples.text: Es una pieza amarilla.
examples.trans: It is a yellow piece.

examples.text: ¡Acaba de parar un taxi amarillo frente a la verja de hierro!
examples.trans: A yellow taxi just pulled up outside the iron gate!

meanings.note: Derived from masa ('dough'); regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Tomás amasa la harina con agua templada y sal.
examples.trans: Tomas kneads the flour with warm water and salt.

examples.text: Amasamos diez minutos hasta que la masa queda elástica.
examples.trans: We knead for ten minutes until the dough turns elastic.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender with the two items it refers to: ambos (masculine/mixed) and ambas (feminine).

examples.text: Pegamos etiquetas rojas en ambos tarros de cristal.
examples.trans: We stuck red labels on both glass jars.

examples.text: Conozco a los dos hermanos y ambos cocinan muy bien.
examples.trans: I know both brothers and both of them cook very well.

meanings.note: In colloquial Peninsular Spanish, americano commonly refers to the United States (e.g., inglés americano vs. colloquial inglés inglés for British English), though estadounidense is preferred in formal journalism. Also refers broadly to the Americas.

meanings.en: suit jacket; blazer (in feminine: la americana)
meanings.note: Note that the feminine noun una americana specifically means a tailored blazer or suit jacket in Spain.

examples.text: Magüi, ¿esto es inglés inglés o inglés americano?
examples.trans: Magüi, is this British English or American English?

examples.text: Nos han pedido que prepare el casting con acento americano.
examples.trans: They asked us to have her prepare the audition with an American accent.

meanings.note: Feminine form of amigo. Note that Spanish allows adverbial gradation like ser muy amiga suya ('to be a very close friend of hers/his'), treating amiga almost adjectivally.

examples.text: Pues Paca es muy amiga suya. Sí, somos muy amigas.
examples.trans: Well, Paca is a very close friend of hers. Yes, we're very good friends.

examples.text: Te presento a una amiga mía que trabaja en producción.
examples.trans: Let me introduce you to a friend of mine who works in production.

meanings.note: Feminine plural of base lemma amiga; expressions like íntimas amigas ('close/bosom friends') are frequently used by Paquita in showbiz networking—often exaggerating how well she knows a celebrity.

examples.text: Pues Paca es muy amiga suya. Sí, somos muy amigas.
examples.trans: Well, Paca is a very close friend of hers. Yes, we're very good friends.

examples.text: Íntimas amigas. Pónmela al teléfono.
examples.trans: Bosom friends. Put her on the phone for me.

meanings.note: Feminine: la amiga.

examples.text: El amigo está aquí.
examples.trans: The friend is here.

examples.text: Vemos los amigos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the friends from the door.

meanings.en: friendly; exhibition (sports match, often playful metaphor for casual romance)
meanings.note: In Spanish sports—and humorously in Paquita Salas dating banter—un partido amistoso ('a friendly/exhibition match') means a no-strings-attached encounter outside official competition.
Used for warm relations, tone, or legal settlements (acuerdo amistoso). For a 'friendly person' (warm/sociable), Spanish more commonly uses simpático or amable.

examples.text: Yo estoy dispuesto a jugar un partido amistoso.
examples.trans: I am willing to play a friendly match.

examples.text: Llegaron a un acuerdo amistoso para rescindir el contrato sin ir a juicio.
examples.trans: They reached an amicable agreement to terminate the contract without going to court.

meanings.en: friendly; exhibition (plural adjective or noun for friendly matches)
meanings.note: Masculine plural of base lemma amistoso; can function as an adjective (partidos amistosos) or substantivized masculine plural noun (jugar unos amistosos).

examples.text: Aunque uno se retire de la liga, todavía hay partidos amistosos.
examples.trans: Even if someone retires from the league, there are still friendly matches.

examples.text: Después de la ruptura mantuvieron tratos muy amistosos en los rodajes.
examples.trans: After the breakup they kept things on very friendly terms on set.

examples.text: ¿Por qué no lo dejas ya, mi amor? No te cogen.
examples.trans: Why don't you give it up already, my love? They never pick you.

examples.text: Mi amor, no pasa nada, tienes aquí un futuro muy bonito. Te lo prometo.
examples.trans: My love, it's alright, you have a lovely future right here. I promise you.

examples.text: Paquita, amor, hola. Voy como las locas en medio de las fotos.
examples.trans: Paquita, honey, hi. I'm rushing like crazy in the middle of the photo shoot.

ampliar.gloss: to extend; to expand; to enlarge

meanings.en: to extend; to expand; to enlarge
meanings.note: Stress falls on the -í- with an accent mark in singular and 3rd plural present forms (amplío, amplía); ampliar la estancia = extend one's stay.

examples.text: Queremos ampliar nuestra estancia en la posada dos días más.
examples.trans: We want to extend our stay at the inn by two more days.

examples.text: Van a ampliar la terraza del café este verano.
examples.trans: They are going to expand the café terrace this summer.

meanings.note: Describes roomy bedrooms or courtyards.

examples.text: Es una pieza amplia.
examples.trans: It is a spacious piece.

examples.text: ¡En absoluto! Y este escritorio amplio bajo la ventana es ideal para mi trabajo.
examples.trans: Not at all! And this wide desk under the window is ideal for my work.

ana.gloss: Ana (Spanish female given name; Ana y los siete)

meanings.note: In Paquita Salas, «Ana y los siete» refers to the iconic 2002–2005 TVE family dramedy created by and starring Ana Obregón, a nostalgic touchstone of Spanish television pop culture.

examples.text: Y luego triunfó muchísimo con «Ana y los siete» en televisión.
examples.trans: And then it was a huge hit on television with "Ana and the Seven."

examples.text: Ana siempre soñó con protagonizar una comedia familiar en horario estelar.
examples.trans: Ana always dreamed of starring in a prime-time family comedy.

meanings.note: Opposite of estrecho (narrow).

examples.text: Es una pieza ancha.
examples.trans: It is a wide piece.

examples.text: ¡Cuidado, Ernesto, la jarra tiene la boca muy ancha!
examples.trans: Careful, Ernesto, the pitcher has a very wide spout!

meanings.note: Measurement from side to side.

examples.text: La anchura es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The width is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la anchura.
examples.trans: We talk about the width.

and.gloss: and (quoted English conjunction in audition line)

meanings.note: Quoted English word in Paquita Salas from Mariona Terés's self-tape audition line, illustrating the comedic struggle of Spanish actors faking fluency in English-language castings. Spanish equivalent: y (or e before i-/hi-).

examples.text: Leyó el papelito a cámara diciendo: «Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old».
examples.trans: She read the little slip of paper to the camera, saying: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old."

examples.text: Magüi le apuntó la pronunciación de «and» en una libreta para el casting internacional.
examples.trans: Magüi wrote down the pronunciation of "and" for her in a notebook for the international audition.

anda.gloss: come on! / oh please! / no way!

meanings.en: come on!; get out of here!; oh please!
meanings.note: Quintessential Peninsular Spanish conversational interjection (grammaticalized from the imperative of andar, 'to walk') expressing affectionate dismissal, disbelief, surprise (¡Anda, mira quién está aquí!), or gentle encouragement.

meanings.en: walks; goes around (3rd-person singular present) / walk! (imperative)
meanings.note: Literal inflected form of base verb andar (él/ella anda, tú anda).

examples.text: —Anda, qué tonterías dices. —Que sí, que yo soy gay.
examples.trans: "Oh come on, what nonsense you're talking." "Seriously, I'm gay."

examples.text: —¿Pero qué vas a ser tú la Sirenita? Anda...
examples.trans: "How on earth are you going to be the Little Mermaid? Come off it..."

andando.gloss: walking / on foot / let's get moving!

meanings.note: Gerund of base lemma andar (featured in the Paquita Salas theme song lyrics). Ir andando is the most idiomatic Peninsular Spanish expression for 'to go on foot / walk somewhere' (more common in Spain than ir caminando).
Used standalone as an energetic prompt to get going or start working right away.

examples.text: Pasión, tesón, que andando se hace el camino en esta profesión.
examples.trans: Passion, tenacity—because it's by walking forward that you forge your path in this profession.

examples.text: Como hacía buen día en Madrid, fuimos andando desde la oficina hasta el teatro.
examples.trans: Since it was a nice day in Madrid, we walked from the office to the theater.

related.gloss: path; road (echoing Machado's se hace camino al andar)

meanings.note: Core Peninsular Spanish verb for walking; note its irregular preterite stem anduv- (anduve, anduvo). Also used as a masculine noun or in la forma de andar ('one's gait / way of walking').
Used with adjectives or gerunds for ongoing states: ¿Cómo andas? ('How are you doing?'), andar liado ('to be swamped/busy').

examples.text: La reconocí enseguida por su voz y su forma de andar.
examples.trans: I recognized her right away by her voice and her way of walking.

examples.text: Vamos a andar un rato por el Retiro para despejarnos la cabeza.
examples.trans: Let's walk around Retiro Park for a bit to clear our heads.

meanings.note: Plural andenes.

examples.text: El andén está aquí.
examples.trans: The platform is here.

examples.text: Vemos los andenes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the platforms from the door.

meanings.note: A finger ring or a circular metal fitting.

examples.text: El anillo está aquí.
examples.trans: The ring is here.

examples.text: Vemos los anillos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rings from the door.

meanings.note: Describes a cheerful, active place or person.

examples.text: Es una pieza animada.
examples.trans: It is a lively piece.

examples.text: ¡Brindo por la Posada del Limonero: el lugar tranquilo más animado de Valencia!
examples.trans: Here is to the Lemon Tree Inn—the loudest quiet place in Valencia!

meanings.note: Masculine plural of base lemma animal (nouns ending in a consonant form their plural by adding -es).

examples.text: Porque, bueno, es un campo, es pueblo, animales... otra vida más tranquila.
examples.trans: Because, well, it's the countryside, it's a village, animals... a quieter kind of life.

examples.text: En el rodaje había niños y animales, que es lo más complicado en el cine.
examples.trans: On the shoot there were children and animals, which is the trickiest thing in filmmaking.

meanings.note: Single word meaning 'last night' (never la última noche).

examples.text: Anoche llovió mucho en la ciudad.
examples.trans: Last night it rained heavily in the city.

examples.text: ¿Dormiste bien anoche?
examples.trans: Did you sleep well last night?

meanings.note: Infinitive used as a masculine noun; al anochecer means 'at dusk / at nightfall'.

examples.text: Encendemos los farolillos del patio al anochecer.
examples.trans: We light the courtyard lanterns at dusk.

examples.text: En verano el aire refresca mucho al anochecer.
examples.trans: In summer the air cools down a lot at nightfall.

anotar.gloss: to note down; to write down

meanings.en: to note down; to write down
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Anoto el teléfono en mi cuaderno.
examples.trans: I write the phone number in my notebook.

examples.text: La recepcionista anotó la hora.
examples.trans: The receptionist noted down the time.

meanings.note: Slightly formal/concise preposition meaning 'in front of' or 'faced with'.

examples.text: Nos detuvimos ante el portón verde de madera.
examples.trans: We stopped in front of the green wooden gate.

examples.text: Rocío pasa la mañana de pie ante el horno.
examples.trans: Rocio spends the morning standing in front of the oven.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.text: Llegué diez minutos antes.
examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Placed after a noun, means 'historic' or 'old-fashioned'.

examples.text: Es una pieza antigua.
examples.trans: It is an old piece.

examples.text: Encantada, Tomás, ¡siempre que nadie hable de vender pianos antiguos!
examples.trans: Gladly, Tomas, as long as nobody talks about selling old pianos!

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza anual.
examples.trans: It is an annual piece.

examples.text: ¡A menos que escriba para la guía anual de viajes de Valencia!
examples.trans: Unless he writes for the annual Valencia travel guide!

examples.text: Hice un anuncio en televisión.
examples.trans: I did a commercial on television.

examples.text: Veo muchos anuncios.
examples.trans: I see many commercials.

examples.text: Cuenta una anécdota divertida.
examples.trans: She tells a funny story.

examples.text: Tengo muchas anécdotas.
examples.trans: I have lots of stories.

meanings.note: Describes lights, devices and fires that are not on; from apagar, to switch off.

examples.text: El móvil está apagado.
examples.trans: The phone is switched off.

examples.text: Todas las luces del pasillo están apagadas.
examples.trans: All the hallway lights are off.

examples.text: Este aparato funciona muy bien.
examples.trans: This device works very well.

examples.text: Es un aparato moderno.
examples.trans: It is a modern gadget.

meanings.note: Spelling changes c -> qu before -e (aparqué).

examples.text: El repartidor aparca la furgoneta junto a la entrada.
examples.trans: The delivery driver parks the van beside the entrance.

examples.text: No se puede aparcar delante del portón del patio.
examples.trans: You cannot park in front of the courtyard gate.

meanings.en: to appear; to show up; to pop up (on screen or in person)
meanings.note: Inchoative -ecer verb with irregular 1st-person singular present aparezco (/apaˈɾeθko/). Note the dative of experience in te tiene que aparecer ('it should pop up on your screen').

examples.text: Te tiene que aparecer en la esquina el botón de grabar.
examples.trans: The record button should show up for you in the corner.

examples.text: Porque si no se termina una relación, no va a aparecer otra relación.
examples.trans: Because unless one relationship ends, another relationship won't come along.

examples.text: Pues este apártalo.
examples.trans: Well, set this one aside.

examples.text: Yo apartar
examples.trans: I apartar

meanings.note: Used for the formal opening of a shop, café, or exhibition, as well as opening hours (horario de apertura).

examples.text: Este viernes celebramos la gran apertura del café del patio.
examples.trans: This Friday we celebrate the grand opening of the courtyard café.

examples.text: El horario de apertura de la librería está en la puerta.
examples.trans: The bookshop's opening hours are on the door.

examples.text: Me apetece desayunar.
examples.trans: I feel like having breakfast.

examples.text: Yo apetecer
examples.trans: I apetecer

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb.

examples.text: Todo el público aplaudió al terminar la canción.
examples.trans: The whole audience clapped when the song ended.

examples.text: Los vecinos aplauden desde las mesas del patio.
examples.trans: The neighbours applaud from the courtyard tables.

examples.text: Pido un aplauso para ellos otra vez, por favor.
examples.trans: I ask for another round of applause for them, please.

examples.text: Yo aplauso
examples.trans: I aplauso

examples.text: Esta aplicación tiene un máximo de palabras.
examples.trans: This app has a word limit.

examples.text: Yo aplicación
examples.trans: I aplicación

meanings.en: backed; believed in; took a chance on (with por)
meanings.note: 1st- or 3rd-person singular imperfect indicative of base lemma apostar. The construction apostar por alguien ('to bet on / champion someone') is ubiquitous in Spanish talent management and media.
Literal wagering sense; note the traditional Peninsular idiom no apostar un duro por algo ('to give something zero chance of succeeding').

examples.text: Y ha apostado por mí, que por mí no apostaba mucha gente, la verdad.
examples.trans: And she backed me when not many people believed in me, honestly.

examples.text: Nadie apostaba un duro por aquella obra, y acabó llenando el teatro todo el año.
examples.trans: Nobody would bet a cent on that play, and it ended up selling out the theater all year.

meanings.en: bet, gambled; backed, believed in (with por)
meanings.note: Past participle of 'apostar'. In Peninsular Spanish, 'apostar por alguien' is a common idiom meaning to back someone, take a chance on them, or believe in their talent.

examples.text: Y ha apostado por mí, que por mí no apostaba mucha gente, la verdad.
examples.trans: And she took a chance on me, when honestly not many people were betting on me.

examples.text: Siempre hemos apostado por el talento joven en nuestra agencia.
examples.trans: We have always backed young talent at our agency.

apoyar.gloss: to lean; to rest; to support

meanings.en: to lean; to rest; to support
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; apoyar algo contra la pared means 'to lean something against the wall'.

examples.text: Apoya la escalera con cuidado contra el ladrillo.
examples.trans: Lean the ladder carefully against the brick.

examples.text: Apoyamos las sillas dobladas debajo del arco.
examples.trans: We lean the folded chairs under the arch.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb; aprender a + infinitive means 'to learn how to'.

examples.text: Aprendo rápido todos los nombres de los huéspedes.
examples.trans: I quickly learn all the guests' names.

examples.text: Mi tía aprendió a tocar el piano de niña.
examples.trans: My aunt learned to play the piano as a girl.

meanings.note: Final -z changes to -c- before -es in the plural (aprendices); feminine singular can be la aprendiz or la aprendiza.

examples.text: El joven aprendiz prepara la masa del pan cada mañana.
examples.trans: The young apprentice prepares the bread dough every morning.

examples.text: Mis dos aprendices de cocina trabajaron de maravilla el miércoles.
examples.trans: My two kitchen apprentices worked wonderfully on Wednesday.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: aprieto).

examples.text: Aprieto bien el tapón del termo.
examples.trans: I tighten the thermos cap firmly.

examples.text: Apretó el botón del timbre dos veces.
examples.trans: He pressed the doorbell button twice.

aprobar.gloss: to approve; to pass (an inspection or exam)

meanings.en: to approve; to pass (an inspection or exam)
meanings.note: Stem-changing o -> ue in stressed present forms (apruebo, aprueba); participle aprobado means 'approved / passed'.

examples.text: El ayuntamiento aprobó la licencia del café histórico.
examples.trans: The city council approved the licence for the historic café.

examples.text: Mi hermana aprobó el examen de música con muy buena nota.
examples.trans: My sister passed the music exam with a very high mark.

examples.text: Aprovecha esa oportunidad.
examples.trans: Take that opportunity.

examples.text: Aprovecho el viaje para leer.
examples.trans: I use the journey to read.

meanings.note: Past participle of 'apuntar' (often used with 'tener' as an adjectival participle). 'Tener algo apuntado' means to have something written down in a notebook or planner.
From the reflexive 'apuntarse a algo' (to sign up for a class, audition, or list).

examples.text: Lo miro, pero que no tengo apuntado
examples.trans: I'll check, though I don't have it written down.

examples.text: Tenía tu teléfono apuntado en la agenda, pero no la encuentro.
examples.trans: I had your phone number written down in my planner, but I can't find it.

related.gloss: to write down, to point, to sign up

meanings.note: Everyday word in Spain for writing down a note or phone number.

examples.text: Apunto la dirección en un papel.
examples.trans: I jot down the address on a piece of paper.

examples.text: ¿Apuntaste el nombre del cliente?
examples.trans: Did you write down the guest's name?

meanings.note: Usually plural (los apuntes) for written notes.

examples.text: El apunte está aquí.
examples.trans: The note is here.

examples.text: Vemos los apuntes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notes from the door.

meanings.note: Demonstrative determiner for distant space or past time (aquella, aquellos, aquellas).

examples.text: Recuerdo muy bien aquel domingo.
examples.trans: I remember that Sunday very well.

examples.text: Aquella casa tiene cien años.
examples.trans: That house over there is a hundred years old.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave.
examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Architectural stone archway or violin bow.

examples.text: El arco está aquí.
examples.trans: The arch is here.

examples.text: Vemos los arcos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the archs from the door.

meanings.note: False friend reminder: la arena means 'sand' (as on a beach or riverbed), though it also gave English 'arena' via the sand-strewn floor of Roman amphitheatres.

examples.text: El hueco bajo la piedra estaba lleno de arena seca.
examples.trans: The cavity under the stone was full of dry sand.

examples.text: Caminamos descalzos por la arena tibia de la playa.
examples.trans: We walked barefoot along the warm sand of the beach.

examples.text: Pone muy buen acento argentino.
examples.trans: She puts on a great Argentine accent.

examples.text: Es una película argentina.
examples.trans: It is an Argentine film.

meanings.note: Tall storage closet or bedroom wardrobe.

examples.text: El armario está aquí.
examples.trans: The wardrobe is here.

examples.text: Vemos los armarios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the wardrobes from the door.

meanings.note: Plantas aromáticas means culinary garden herbs.

examples.text: Es una pieza aromática.
examples.trans: It is an aromatic piece.

examples.text: Buen sitio. Dos sillas firmes, mirando a las plantas aromáticas en vez de a la ventana.
examples.trans: Good spot. Two solid chairs, facing the garden herbs instead of the lobby window.

meanings.note: Feminine: la arquitecta.

examples.text: El arquitecto está aquí.
examples.trans: The architect is here.

examples.text: Vemos los arquitectos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the architects from the door.

arreglar.gloss: to fix; to repair; to tidy

meanings.en: to fix; to repair; to tidy
meanings.note: Everyday verb for repairing things or sorting out problems.

examples.text: El vecino arregla la lámpara del salón.
examples.trans: El vecino fixes the lounge lamp.

examples.text: Ayer arreglamos la puerta del jardín.
examples.trans: Yesterday we repaired the garden gate.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.text: Las habitaciones están arriba.
examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.

examples.text: Mira arriba hacia el balcón.
examples.trans: Look up toward the balcony.

meanings.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective 'arriesgado' (from the verb 'arriesgar', to risk). Used to describe high-stakes strategies, creative choices, or bold people.

examples.text: Con Clara... Con Clara seguimos una estrategia un poquito arriesgada.
examples.trans: With Clara... With Clara we are following a slightly risky strategy.

examples.text: Es una decisión muy arriesgada para su primer papel protagonista.
examples.trans: It is a very risky decision for her first leading role.

related.gloss: to risk, to take a chance

examples.text: No tiene ni una arruga.
examples.trans: She doesn't have a single wrinkle.

examples.text: Esta crema quita las arrugas.
examples.trans: This cream removes wrinkles.

examples.text: No quiero arruinar la sorpresa.
examples.trans: I don't want to ruin the surprise.

examples.text: La lluvia arruina el peinado.
examples.trans: The rain ruins the hairstyle.

examples.text: Fernando Canelón es representante de los artistas más importantes de este país.
examples.trans: Fernando Canelón is the agent for the most important artists in this country.

examples.text: Yo artista
examples.trans: I artista

examples.text: Hombre, Arturo.
examples.trans: Well, Arturo.

examples.text: Yo Arturo
examples.trans: I Arturo

meanings.note: Feminine noun taking el in the singular (el asa de la maleta / la taza).

examples.text: El asa de la maleta es de cuero.
examples.trans: The suitcase handle is made of leather.

examples.text: Sujeta la cesta por las dos asas.
examples.trans: Hold the basket by both handles.

meanings.note: Participle of asar used as an adjective (tomate asado, pimientos asados).

examples.text: La sopa de tomate asado huele de maravilla.
examples.trans: The roasted tomato soup smells wonderful.

examples.text: Servimos verduras asadas con pan recién hecho.
examples.trans: We serve roasted vegetables with freshly baked bread.

asegurar.gloss: to make sure (asegurarse de); to secure

meanings.en: to make sure (asegurarse de); to secure
meanings.note: Asegúrate de que... means 'make sure that...'.

examples.text: Asegúrate de cerrar bien la verja.
examples.trans: Make sure you close the gate properly.

examples.text: El técnico aseguró que todo funciona.
examples.trans: The technician assured us everything works.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: asiento, asintió).

examples.text: Mi hermano asintió en silencio.
examples.trans: My brother nodded quietly.

examples.text: Ella asiente con una sonrisa amable.
examples.trans: She nods with a kind smile.

meanings.note: Past participle of 'asesinar'. Used with 'haber' to form compound tenses ('ha asesinado') or adjectivally ('el hombre asesinado').

examples.text: que ha asesinado a una pareja de enamorados?".
examples.trans: that he murdered a couple of lovers?".

examples.text: En el thriller interpreta al inspector que investiga quién ha asesinado al juez.
examples.trans: In the thriller, he plays the inspector investigating who murdered the judge.

meanings.note: Seat of a chair, bench, or train.

examples.text: El asiento de madera se dobla hacia arriba.
examples.trans: The wooden seat folds upward.

examples.text: Guardamos dos asientos junto a la ventana.
examples.trans: We saved two seats beside the window.

asomar.gloss: to peek out; to stick out

meanings.en: to peek out; to stick out
meanings.note: Describes something peeking from a window, pocket, or hinge.

examples.text: Un papel blanco asoma del sobre.
examples.trans: A white sheet peeks out of the envelope.

examples.text: El sol ya asoma por los tejados.
examples.trans: The sun is already peeking over the roofs.

meanings.note: Describes surprised wonder.

examples.text: Es una pieza asombrada.
examples.trans: It is an amazed piece.

examples.text: ¡Señora Carmen, parece asombrada! ¿Conoce usted Calle del Limonero número doce?
examples.trans: Madam Carmen, you look amazed! Do you know Number twelve Calle del Limonero?

meanings.note: Third-person singular present indicative of 'aspirar'. Frequently used in script stage directions '(ASPIRA)' to indicate a character taking a deep breath of air.
Followed by the preposition 'a' ('aspirar a'), it means to aspire to or aim for an ambition or role.

examples.text: Este aire... (ASPIRA) Este aire vale oro.
examples.trans: This air... (INHALES) This air is worth its weight in gold.

examples.text: Ella aspira a conseguir el papel principal en la nueva serie.
examples.trans: She aspires to land the lead role in the new series.

related.gloss: to inhale; to aspire; to vacuum

meanings.note: Masculine plural of 'asunto'. Refers to professional dealings, projects, personal affairs, or subject lines in emails.

examples.text: "cosas y la llamaban para muchos asuntos,
examples.trans: "things, and they used to call her for many different matters,

examples.text: Tengo que resolver varios asuntos urgentes en la oficina antes del rodaje.
examples.trans: I have to settle several urgent matters at the office before the shoot.

meanings.en: (that you) scare, frighten; (with no) don't scare
meanings.note: Second-person singular (tú) present subjunctive of 'asustar' (or 'asustarse'). Used in negative commands such as 'no me asustes' (don't scare me) and 'no te asustes' (don't be scared / don't freak out).

examples.text: Oye, no me asustes, Paquita. No, no, no te preocupes.
examples.trans: Hey, don't scare me, Paquita. No, no, don't worry.

examples.text: No te asustes si ves a mucha gente esperando en la sala del casting.
examples.trans: Don't be scared if you see a lot of people waiting in the audition room.

meanings.en: I scared, I frightened; (with me) I got scared
meanings.note: First-person singular (yo) preterite indicative of 'asustar'. Used transitively ('te asusté', I scared you) or pronominally ('me asusté', I got scared).

examples.text: Oye, Paquita, que yo lo siento si te asusté ayer,
examples.trans: Hey, Paquita, I am sorry if I scared you yesterday,

examples.text: Me asusté muchísimo cuando vi tantas llamadas perdidas tuyas.
examples.trans: I got really scared when I saw so many missed calls from you.

meanings.note: Así que means 'so / therefore'.

examples.text: Hazlo así, despacio.
examples.trans: Do it like this, slowly.

examples.text: Llueve mucho, así que entramos.
examples.trans: It is raining hard, so let us go inside.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from atar (to tie).

examples.text: Es una pieza atada.
examples.trans: It is a tied piece.

examples.text: Hay una pequeña tarjeta de cartón atada al asa.
examples.trans: There is a small cardboard card tied to the handle.

meanings.note: Describes a jammed door, zip, or pipe.

examples.text: Es una pieza atascada.
examples.trans: It is a stuck piece.

examples.text: atascada
examples.trans: stuck

atascar.gloss: to jam; to get stuck; to clog

meanings.en: to jam; to get stuck; to clog
meanings.note: Spelling changes c -> qu before -e (atasqué).

examples.text: La humedad del invierno atascó el cajón de abajo.
examples.trans: The winter damp jammed the bottom drawer.

examples.text: No fuerces la llave si se atasca la cerradura.
examples.trans: Do not force the key if the lock jams.

meanings.note: Le atiende... is standard polite phone/desk phrasing in Spain.

examples.text: La encargada atiende el mostrador hoy.
examples.trans: La encargada is tending the front desk today.

examples.text: Nos atendieron con mucha amabilidad.
examples.trans: They assisted us very kindly.

atornillar.gloss: to screw on; to fasten with screws

meanings.en: to screw on; to fasten with screws
meanings.note: From tornillo ('screw'); opposite desatornillar.

examples.text: Mateo atornilla las bisagras de latón en el marco.
examples.trans: Mateo screws the brass hinges into the frame.

examples.text: Atornillamos la placa nueva junto al timbre de entrada.
examples.trans: We screwed the new plaque next to the front bell.

examples.text: Es guapo y es atractivo. Ay, Belinda, es gay. Estoy segurísima.
examples.trans: He's handsome and attractive. Oh, Belinda, he's gay. I'm completely sure.

examples.text: Hablamos de atractivo en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about attractive at the office.

meanings.note: Wooden or metal rest that holds sheet music open.

examples.text: Pon la hoja de música sobre el atril del piano.
examples.trans: Put the sheet of music on the piano's music stand.

examples.text: El atril de nogal se pliega hacia dentro.
examples.trans: The walnut music stand folds inward.

meanings.note: Indicates position or movement toward the rear.

examples.text: Da un paso atrás, por favor.
examples.trans: Take one step back, please.

examples.text: Hombros atrás y respira hondo.
examples.trans: Shoulders back and breathe deeply.

meanings.note: Unaccented aun means 'even' (aun así = even so), distinct from aún (still/yet).

examples.text: Aun con lluvia, el patio es bonito.
examples.trans: Even in the rain, the courtyard is pretty.

examples.text: Aun así, llegamos a tiempo.
examples.trans: Even so, we arrived on time.

meanings.note: Takes indicative for known facts and subjunctive for hypotheticals.

examples.text: Salimos aunque llueve un poco.
examples.trans: We are going out even though it is raining a bit.

examples.text: Esperaré aquí aunque tarde diez minutos.
examples.trans: I will wait here even if he takes ten minutes.

meanings.note: Adjective (invariable for gender; plural 'autorales') derived from 'autor'. Frequently used in Spanish film and theater circles ('cine autoral', 'proyecto autoral') to describe indie or director-driven artistic work as opposed to mainstream commercial fare.

examples.text: Tendría que ser una cosa... muy concreta, muy autoral.
examples.trans: It would have to be something... very specific, very auteur.

examples.text: El director busca un sello más autoral e íntimo para su próxima película.
examples.trans: The director is looking for a more auteur and intimate style for his next film.

meanings.note: Wide main street in a city.

examples.text: La avenida está aquí.
examples.trans: The avenue is here.

examples.text: Vemos las avenidas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the avenues from the door.

meanings.en: notified, let know, warned, given a heads-up
meanings.note: Past participle of 'avisar'. In everyday Spanish, 'avisar' is the standard verb for letting someone know or giving them a heads-up ('no me has avisado', you didn't let me know).

examples.text: ¿Qué haces aquí? Que no me has avisado ni me has escrito.
examples.trans: What are you doing here? You didn't let me know or even text me.

examples.text: Si me hubieras avisado antes, habría cambiado la reunión de hora.
examples.trans: If you had let me know earlier, I would have rescheduled the meeting.

related.gloss: to let know, to notify, to warn

examples.text: Te aviso cuando llegue.
examples.trans: I'll let you know when I arrive.

examples.text: El correo avisaba del cambio.
examples.trans: The email warned about the change.

meanings.note: Written notice or spoken heads-up.

examples.text: El aviso está aquí.
examples.trans: The notice is here.

examples.text: Vemos los avisos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notices from the door.

examples.text: Voy en avión.
examples.trans: I'm going by plane.

examples.text: No hay aviones hoy.
examples.trans: There are no flights today.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise, sympathy, or mild dismay.

examples.text: ¡Ay, casi olvido el paraguas!
examples.trans: Oh, I nearly forgot my umbrella!

examples.text: ¡Ay, qué susto me has dado!
examples.trans: Goodness, what a fright you gave me!

meanings.note: Pairs naturally with preterite tense.

examples.text: Ayer arreglamos la caldera.
examples.trans: Yesterday we fixed the boiler.

examples.text: Llegué a Valencia ayer por la tarde.
examples.trans: I arrived in Valencia yesterday afternoon.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; ayudar a + infinitive.

examples.text: ¿Te ayudo con esas dos cajas?
examples.trans: Shall I help you with those two boxes?

examples.text: Siempre ayudamos a los nuevos vecinos.
examples.trans: We always help the new neighbours.

meanings.note: Municipal government building and town council in Spain.

examples.text: El ayuntamiento está aquí.
examples.trans: The City Hall is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ayuntamientos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the City Halls from the door.

meanings.note: Affirmative 'tú' imperative of 'ayudar' ('ayuda') with the enclitic feminine singular direct object pronoun 'la' attached. The written accent on the 'ú' preserves the stress on the verb stem.

forms.title: Imperative Forms of ayudar with Pronouns

examples.text: Por favor, ayúdala, no da pie con bola.
examples.trans: Please help her, she can't get anything right.

examples.text: Pues, por favor, ayúdala, de verdad. Vale.
examples.trans: Well, please help her, really. Okay.

meanings.note: Plural azules; azul marino means 'navy blue'.

examples.text: Es una pieza azul.
examples.trans: It is a blue piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Commonly masculine (sin azúcar = without sugar).

examples.text: El azúcar es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The sugar is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el azúcar.
examples.trans: We talk about the sugar.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb; everyday cooking word for adding ingredients to a pot or bowl (añade el caldo).

examples.text: Añade una pizca de sal y dos hojas de laurel a la sopa.
examples.trans: Add a pinch of salt and two bay leaves to the soup.

examples.text: Añadimos zumo de limón fresco a la crema templada.
examples.trans: We added fresh lemon juice to the warm cream.

meanings.note: Tener ... años expresses age; hace ... años means '... years ago'.

examples.text: El año está aquí.
examples.trans: The year is here.

examples.text: Vemos los años desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the years from the door.

meanings.note: Accented aún is interchangeable with todavía.

examples.text: El café aún está caliente.
examples.trans: The coffee is still hot.

examples.text: Aún no han abierto la puerta.
examples.trans: They have not opened the door yet.

b&b.gloss: B&B, De boca en boca (Spanish TV series)

meanings.en: B&B, De boca en boca (Spanish television series)
meanings.note: Title of the Spanish comedy-drama television series 'B&B, de boca en boca' (2014–2015, Telecinco), set at a fashion and lifestyle magazine and starring Belén Rueda, Gonzalo de Castro, and Macarena García. Referenced in Paquita Salas as a recognizable Spanish TV credit.

examples.text: Sí. ¿Te acuerdas de la de "B&B",
examples.trans: Yes. Do you remember the girl from "B&B",

examples.text: Muchos actores jóvenes se dieron a conocer en series españolas como "B&B".
examples.trans: Many young actors made a name for themselves in Spanish series like "B&B".

examples.text: Quizás sabe cantar y bailar.
examples.trans: Maybe she can sing and dance.

examples.text: Yo bailar
examples.trans: I bailar

meanings.note: Second-person singular (tú) present indicative of 'bailar'. Common in auditions and casting interviews when asking actors about their special skills alongside acting and singing.

examples.text: A ver, ¿cómo bailas?
examples.trans: Let's see, how do you dance?

examples.text: Si cantas, bailas, un caballo, una esgrima...
examples.trans: Whether you sing, dance, ride a horse, do fencing...

examples.text: Llevas la cremallera bajada.
examples.trans: Your zip is down.

examples.text: Las persianas están bajadas.
examples.trans: The blinds are down.

bajar.gloss: to go down; to bring down; to lower

meanings.en: to go down; to bring down; to lower
meanings.note: Works both intransitively (go downstairs) and transitively (bring down).

examples.text: Bajo a la cocina a preparar té.
examples.trans: I go down to the kitchen to make tea.

examples.text: Bajamos las maletas por la escalera.
examples.trans: We bring the suitcases down the stairs.

meanings.note: Bajo llave means 'under lock and key'; as an adjective (bajo/baja), means 'low' or 'ground' (planta baja).

examples.text: Nos sentamos bajo el limonero.
examples.trans: We sit under the lemon tree.

examples.text: Guarda la caja bajo llave.
examples.trans: Keep the box under lock and key.

meanings.note: Everyday word in Spain for one shelf of a bookcase or cupboard; estante is the general word.

examples.text: Los vasos están en la balda de arriba.
examples.trans: The glasses are on the top shelf.

examples.text: Pon el pan en la segunda balda.
examples.trans: Put the bread on the second shelf.

examples.text: Pues he montado una banda. ¡Estoy supercontenta!
examples.trans: Well, I've put together a band. I'm super happy!

examples.text: Hablamos de banda en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about band at the office.

meanings.note: Used both for a serving tray and an oven baking tray (bandeja de horno).

examples.text: Saca la bandeja dorada del horno con cuidado.
examples.trans: Take the golden tray out of the oven carefully.

examples.text: Clara lleva cuatro tazas de té en la bandeja.
examples.trans: Clara carries four cups of tea on the tray.

meanings.note: Diminutive of banco (with c -> qu spelling change).

examples.text: Sujeta firme el banquito antes de subir al estante.
examples.trans: Hold the step stool steady before climbing to the shelf.

examples.text: Pusimos un banquito bajo de madera junto al limonero.
examples.trans: We put a low wooden bench beside the lemon tree.

examples.text: ¡Qué barbaridad!
examples.trans: How outrageous!

examples.text: Cuesta una barbaridad.
examples.trans: It costs a fortune.

meanings.note: Formed as an affectionate diminutive of la barba ('beard'); standard everyday Spanish for the chin.

examples.text: El músico apoyó el violín bajo la barbilla.
examples.trans: The musician rested the violin under his chin.

examples.text: Se tocó la barbilla mientras pensaba la respuesta.
examples.trans: He touched his chin while thinking over the answer.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural changes final -z to -c- (los barnices).

examples.text: Una capa fina de barniz protege la madera de la lluvia.
examples.trans: A thin coat of varnish protects the wood from the rain.

examples.text: Debajo del barniz viejo se veían las marcas originales.
examples.trans: Underneath the old varnish the original marks were visible.

barra.gloss: bar; pry bar; loaf (of bread); counter

meanings.en: bar; pry bar; loaf (of bread); counter
meanings.note: Versatile feminine noun: una barra de hierro ('an iron bar'), una barra de pan ('a baguette/loaf'), or la barra del café ('the café counter').

examples.text: Mateo metió la barra plana de hierro bajo la piedra.
examples.trans: Mateo slid the flat iron bar under the stone.

examples.text: Compramos dos barras de pan recién horneado.
examples.trans: We bought two loaves of freshly baked bread.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb (barro = I sweep).

examples.text: Barro las hojas secas del patio.
examples.trans: I sweep the dry leaves from the courtyard.

examples.text: Esta mañana barrimos la entrada.
examples.trans: This morning we swept the entrance.

meanings.note: Local city district with its own shops and squares.

examples.text: El barrio está aquí.
examples.trans: The neighbourhood is here.

examples.text: Vemos los barrios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the neighbourhoods from the door.

meanings.note: In baking, la base de la tarta means 'the pastry crust / base'.

examples.text: La base de almendra queda dorada y muy crujiente.
examples.trans: The almond crust turns out golden and very crisp.

examples.text: Ponemos una base de fieltro bajo las patas.
examples.trans: We put a felt base under the legs.

meanings.note: Usually used in 3rd person: basta con... means 'it is enough to have...' and ¡basta! means 'enough!'.

examples.text: Con media cucharada de miel basta para endulzar el té.
examples.trans: Half a spoonful of honey is enough to sweeten the tea.

examples.text: Bastan diez minutos de horno para dorar los bollos.
examples.trans: Ten minutes in the oven are enough to brown the rolls.

meanings.note: Tirar a la basura means 'to throw in the bin'.

examples.text: La basura es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The rubbish is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la basura.
examples.trans: We talk about the rubbish.

meanings.note: Feminine noun. 'No tener batería' or 'quedarse sin batería' is the standard way to say one's phone battery is dead. (Small disposable AA/AAA batteries are called 'pilas'.)
In music, 'la batería' is the drum set, while 'el/la batería' refers to the drummer.

examples.text: ¿Qué hora es? No tengo batería.
examples.trans: What time is it? I have no battery.

examples.text: Déjame el cargador un momento, que me estoy quedando sin batería en el móvil.
examples.trans: Lend me your charger for a second, my phone is running out of battery.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb used in cooking for eggs, cream, and lemon curd.

examples.text: Bate los huevos despacio hasta que espumen bien.
examples.trans: Whisk the eggs slowly until they foam up well.

examples.text: Batimos el zumo de limón con azúcar blanco fino.
examples.trans: We beat the lemon juice with fine white sugar.
