examples.text: Hoy conduzco yo.
examples.trans: Today I'm driving.

examples.text: Iba a conducir Magüi.
examples.trans: Magüi was going to drive.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Mateo conecta el cable nuevo a la lámpara del techo.
examples.trans: Mateo connects the new wire to the ceiling lamp.

examples.text: Primero desconecta la corriente y luego conecta el enchufe.
examples.trans: First turn off the power and then wire the socket.

meanings.en: to trust, rely on, have faith in
meanings.note: Intransitive with the preposition 'en' ('confiar en alguien'). Takes a written accent in boot-verb forms ('confío', 'confías', 'confía', 'confían').

meanings.en: to entrust or confide (something to someone)
meanings.note: Used transitively when sharing a secret or responsibility ('confiar un secreto').

examples.text: Es que, Magüi... ¿Puedes confiar en mí un momento?
examples.trans: Look, Magüi... Can you trust me for one second?

examples.text: Estamos contentos, la gente confía mucho en nosotros.
examples.trans: We're happy; people put a lot of trust in us.

examples.text: Esperamos tu confirmación.
examples.trans: We're waiting for your confirmation.

examples.text: No tengo confirmación todavía.
examples.trans: I don't have confirmation yet.

meanings.note: 2nd-person singular ('tú') present indicative of 'confiar'. Note the hiatus accent on the 'í' breaking the diphthong.

examples.text: Te lo van a dar, ¿confías? Relaja.
examples.trans: They're going to give you the part—do you trust me? Relax.

examples.text: Si no confías en tu representante, esto no va a funcionar.
examples.trans: If you don't trust your agent, this isn't going to work.

meanings.note: Special fused form of con + mí.

examples.text: Ven conmigo al patio un minuto.
examples.trans: Come out to the courtyard with me for a minute.

examples.text: ¿Quieres desayunar conmigo?
examples.trans: Do you want to have breakfast with me?

conocer.gloss: to know (a person or place); to meet

meanings.en: to know (a person or place); to meet
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg conozco; preterite conocí often means 'met for the first time'.

examples.text: Conozco muy bien este barrio.
examples.trans: I know this neighbourhood very well.

examples.text: Ayer conocimos al nuevo vecino.
examples.trans: Yesterday we met the new neighbour.

meanings.note: Feminine singular participle/adjective of 'conocer'. Often followed by 'por' ('conocida por...' = 'known for...').
Used as a feminine noun ('una conocida') to distinguish an acquaintance from a close friend ('una amiga').

forms.title: Adjective and noun forms of conocido

examples.text: Navarrete... Navarrete para mí lo es todo. Es conocida por su gran carácter.
examples.trans: Navarrete... Navarrete is everything to me. She's known for her strong personality.

examples.text: Es una actriz muy conocida en el mundo del teatro musical.
examples.trans: She is a very well-known actress in the musical theater world.

meanings.note: In colloquial Peninsular Spanish, 'tener conocimiento' means having good judgment, reason, or human-like awareness (often said humorously of babies or pets, or in 'perder el conocimiento' = 'to faint').
Used in the plural for practical skills ('conocimientos de inglés').

examples.text: Si parece que tiene conocimiento. Qué curioso.
examples.trans: Why, it almost looks like it has human sense! How funny.

examples.text: No tenía ningún conocimiento previo del guion antes de la prueba.
examples.trans: She had no prior knowledge of the script before the screen test.

conocéis.gloss: you all know / are familiar with (conocer)

meanings.en: you (all) know, are familiar with, or have met
meanings.note: 2nd-person plural informal ('vosotros/as') present indicative of 'conocer', standard throughout Peninsular Spanish when addressing two or more people informally.

examples.text: Es una serie que se llama "House of Cards", no sé si la conocéis.
examples.trans: It's a series called "House of Cards"—I don't know if you guys have heard of it.

examples.text: ¿Ya conocéis a la nueva directora de casting de la cadena?
examples.trans: Have you all met the network's new casting director yet?

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: consigo, consiguió).

examples.text: Siempre consigue mesa junto a la ventana.
examples.trans: She always gets a table by the window.

examples.text: Por fin conseguimos abrir el cofre.
examples.trans: We finally managed to open the chest.

examples.text: Mi consejo es que cuando una relación termina, hay que dejar que se vaya.
examples.trans: My advice is that when a relationship ends, you have to let it go.

examples.text: Te voy a dar un consejo. Nunca te fíes de nadie.
examples.trans: I'm going to give you a piece of advice. Never trust anyone.

meanings.note: Verbs ending in -uir insert -y- before a/e/o (construyo, construye, construyó).

examples.text: Construimos dos mesas largas de madera en el taller.
examples.trans: We built two long wooden tables in the workshop.

examples.text: Construyeron esta posada de piedra hace más de ochenta años.
examples.trans: They built this stone guesthouse over eighty years ago.

consígame.gloss: get me (formal imperative of conseguir + me)

meanings.en: get me, obtain for me, arrange for me
meanings.note: Formal singular ('usted') affirmative imperative of stem-changing 'conseguir' (e -> i) with enclitic pronoun 'me'. Written with an accent mark to preserve stress on the antepenultimate syllable.

examples.text: Y dicen: "Ay, Paquita, consígame usted una visita".
examples.trans: And they say: "Oh, Paquita, get me an appointment."

examples.text: Por favor, consígame dos entradas para el estreno de esta noche.
examples.trans: Please get me two tickets for tonight's premiere.

examples.text: Tengo muchos contactos aquí.
examples.trans: I have many contacts here.

examples.text: Es un contacto del cine.
examples.trans: He's a film contact.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: cuento).

examples.text: Mi abuela cuenta historias preciosas.
examples.trans: My grandmother tells lovely stories.

examples.text: Conté doce tazas en el armario.
examples.trans: I counted twelve cups in the cupboard.

meanings.en: to tell you, recount to you
meanings.note: Infinitive of 'contar' ('to tell a story/news' or 'to count') fused with the informal singular indirect object pronoun 'te'.

forms.title: Infinitive contar with indirect object clitics

examples.text: Lo que pasa es que una persona que yo me pare aquí a contarte, no hay.
examples.trans: The thing is, there isn't anyone special worth stopping here to tell you about.

examples.text: Llámame luego, que tengo un cotilleo buenísimo que contarte.
examples.trans: Call me later—I have some amazing gossip to tell you.

meanings.note: Feminine singular of 'contento'. Typically takes 'estar' ('estoy muy contenta') or change-of-state 'ponerse' ('ponerse contenta' = 'to become happy'); with 'ser', it describes disposition rather than mood.

examples.text: Nada, muy contenta porque estoy grabando una serie nueva.
examples.trans: Nothing much, just really happy because I'm shooting a new series.

examples.text: ¿En serio le han dado el papel? Se va a poner muy contenta.
examples.trans: Did they really give her the role? She's going to be thrilled.

meanings.note: Mandatory fusion of preposition 'con' + 'ti' (from Latin 'cum tecum'; never *'con ti'). Also appears in the colloquial Spanish idiom 'quedarse contigo' ('to pull your leg / mess with you').

examples.text: Mira, ¿ves? Aquí no hay nada contigo.
examples.trans: Look, see? There's no issue with you here.

examples.text: Te lo digo en serio, que no me quedo contigo.
examples.trans: I'm telling you seriously, I'm not pulling your leg.

meanings.note: Indicates physical contact or contrast.

examples.text: Apoya la escalera contra la pared.
examples.trans: Lean the ladder against the wall.

examples.text: Los farolillos brillan contra el cielo.
examples.trans: The lanterns glow against the sky.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: El hotel contrata personal en verano.
examples.trans: The hotel hires staff in summer.

examples.text: Contrataron a una nueva encargada.
examples.trans: They hired a new manager.

meanings.note: Rental lease or employment agreement.

examples.text: El contrato está aquí.
examples.trans: The contract is here.

examples.text: Vemos los contratos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the contracts from the door.

meanings.note: Wooden outer or inner shutter hinged beside a window.

examples.text: La contraventana está aquí.
examples.trans: The window shutter is here.

examples.text: Vemos las contraventanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the window shutters from the door.

meanings.note: Plural conversiones.

examples.text: La conversión está aquí.
examples.trans: The conversion is here.

examples.text: Vemos las conversiones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the conversions from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie in present, e -> i in preterite 3rd: convirtió); pairs with en.

examples.text: Quieren convertir el local en cafetería.
examples.trans: They want to turn the premises into a cafe.

examples.text: La lluvia convirtió el paseo en aventura.
examples.trans: The rain turned the walk into an adventure.

meanings.en: I will turn (into), I will transform (into)
meanings.note: 1st-person singular future indicative of 'convertir'. Always takes the preposition 'en' to introduce the resulting state ('convertir a alguien en una estrella').

examples.text: Te convertiré en una estrella.
examples.trans: I will turn you into a star.

examples.text: Convertiré esta pequeña agencia en la más importante del país.
examples.trans: I will turn this little agency into the most important one in the country.

meanings.en: I treat, I'm buying, it's on me
meanings.note: 1st-person singular present indicative of 'convidar'. Has a warm, slightly traditional/castizo Peninsular flavor compared to the everyday 'invito yo' ('convidar a alguien a una copa').

examples.text: A la copa... convido yo.
examples.trans: The drink... is on me.

examples.text: Hoy os convido a unos torreznos para celebrar el contrato.
examples.trans: Today I'm treating you all to some torreznos to celebrate the contract.

examples.text: Llegamos a las copas.
examples.trans: We'll make it for the drinks.

examples.text: Tomamos una copa después.
examples.trans: We'll have a drink afterwards.

meanings.note: Feminine noun used for paper copies, spare keys (copia de la llave), and backups.

examples.text: Guardé una copia de la receta en el cajón de la cocina.
examples.trans: I kept a copy of the recipe in the kitchen drawer.

examples.text: ¿Me haces una copia de la llave del portón, por favor?
examples.trans: Will you make me a copy of the gate key, please?

meanings.note: Plural corazones.

examples.text: El corazón está aquí.
examples.trans: The heart is here.

examples.text: Vemos los corazones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hearts from the door.

meanings.note: Worn with a collared shirt.

examples.text: La corbata está aquí.
examples.trans: The necktie is here.

examples.text: Vemos las corbatas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the neckties from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of equivocado (wrong).

examples.text: Es una pieza correcta.
examples.trans: It is a right piece.

examples.text: ¡Si hubiera cogido la maleta correcta, ninguno de nosotros estaría aquí esta noche!
examples.trans: If he had picked up the right bag, none of us would be standing here tonight!

examples.text: El correo es de ayer.
examples.trans: The email is from yesterday.

examples.text: Tengo cien correos nuevos.
examples.trans: I have a hundred new emails.

meanings.note: Entrar/salir corriendo = to run in / run out.

examples.text: Corro para no perder el tren.
examples.trans: I run so I do not miss the train.

examples.text: Los niños corrieron hacia la fuente.
examples.trans: The children ran toward the fountain.

examples.text: Corta. Magüi, que no puedes hacer eso con la luz.
examples.trans: Cut. Magüi, you cannot do that with the light.

examples.text: Yo Corta
examples.trans: I Corta

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Corto el pan en rebanadas finas.
examples.trans: I slice the bread into thin slices.

examples.text: La panadera cortó cuatro trozos de bizcocho.
examples.trans: The baker cut four pieces of sponge cake.

meanings.note: 3rd-person plural ('ustedes') imperative / present subjunctive of 'cortar'. Even in Spain (where 'vosotros' is otherwise used), directors traditionally shout '¡Corten!' (alongside '¡Acción!') to address the crew on set.

examples.text: ¡Hola! ¡Corten!
examples.trans: Hello! Cut!

examples.text: Cuando el director grite "¡corten!", no os mováis de vuestra marca.
examples.trans: When the director yells "cut!", don't move from your mark.

meanings.note: Golden crust of bread or cake, or tree bark.

examples.text: La corteza está aquí.
examples.trans: The crust is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cortezas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the crusts from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of largo (long).

examples.text: Es una pieza corta.
examples.trans: It is a short piece.

examples.text: Dejó una nota corta pidiendo guardarla hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: He left a short note asking us to keep it until Friday.

examples.text: Ser buena persona es una cosa bonita en la vida.
examples.trans: Being a good person is a lovely thing in life.

examples.text: Yo cosa
examples.trans: I cosa

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: ¿Vas a la fiesta de los Cosmo?
examples.trans: Are you going to the Cosmo party?

examples.text: No tengo invitación para los Cosmo.
examples.trans: I don't have an invitation to the Cosmos.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Lidia va a Cosmopolitan esta noche.
examples.trans: Lidia is going to Cosmopolitan tonight.

examples.text: Falta la confirmación para Cosmopolitan.
examples.trans: Confirmation for Cosmopolitan is missing.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: cuesta).

examples.text: El desayuno cuesta seis euros.
examples.trans: Breakfast costs six euros.

examples.text: Todo el pedido costó treinta euros.
examples.trans: The whole order cost thirty euros.

meanings.note: Feminine noun. Common in phrases like 'por costumbre' ('out of habit'), 'como de costumbre' ('as usual'), and 'la costumbre' ('force of habit').
Refers to social or cultural traditions ('las buenas costumbres').

examples.text: Yo qué sé por qué lo hice, la costumbre. De tanto decirlo...
examples.trans: How should I know why I did it—force of habit. From saying it so much...

examples.text: Tiene la costumbre de repasar el texto justo antes de salir al escenario.
examples.trans: She has a habit of reviewing her lines right before walking onstage.

related.gloss: to be in the habit of / to get used to

meanings.en: course (in the quoted English phrase "of course" = por supuesto)
meanings.note: Quoted English word in 'Paquita Salas', where Spanish actors and agents playfully drop basic English stock phrases like 'of course' to bluff fluency on their CVs for international castings.

examples.text: Lidia, ¿sabes inglés? "Of course".
examples.trans: Lidia, do you know English? "Of course."

examples.text: Le preguntaron si hablaba inglés fluido, soltó un "of course" y luego no entendió ni papa.
examples.trans: They asked her if she spoke fluent English; she dropped an "of course" and then didn't understand a single word.

meanings.note: Informal praise. Masculine un crack is used for the female referent in this learner line, matching the corroborated audio. Feminine una crack is also attested; the adapted spelling crac also exists.

examples.text: Ella es una crack.
examples.trans: She is brilliant.

examples.text: Eres un crack con los números.
examples.trans: You're brilliant with numbers.

meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg crezco.

examples.text: El limonero crece fuerte al sol.
examples.trans: The lemon tree grows strong in the sun.

examples.text: Has crecido mucho estos tres años.
examples.trans: You have grown a lot these three years.

meanings.note: Preterite 3rd sg/pl spells y: creyó, creyeron.

examples.text: Creo que el tren llega a tiempo.
examples.trans: I think the train is arriving on time.

examples.text: No podía creer tanta buena suerte.
examples.trans: He could not believe such good luck.

meanings.note: Crema de limón is smooth lemon curd/custard filling for tarts.

examples.text: La crema de limón espesa despacio a fuego suave.
examples.trans: The lemon curd thickens slowly over gentle heat.

examples.text: Deja enfriar la crema antes de rellenar las tartas.
examples.trans: Let the cream cool before filling the tarts.

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for a zip fastener.

examples.text: La cremallera está aquí.
examples.trans: The zip is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cremalleras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the zips from the door.

meanings.en: I think, I suppose, I believe
meanings.note: 1st-person singular present indicative of 'creer'. Extremely frequent discourse hedge ('yo creo que...'); with pronominal 'me lo', '¡No me lo creo!' means 'I can't believe it!'. Also homographic with 'creo' from 'crear' ('I create').

examples.text: Es de una señora mayor que yo creo que se murió.
examples.trans: It belonged to an older lady who I think passed away.

examples.text: Yo llevaba unos días que lo veía venir, ¿sabes? No me lo creo.
examples.trans: For a few days now I could feel it coming, you know? I can't believe it.

examples.text: Solo me pones de criada.
examples.trans: You only ever cast me as a maid.

examples.text: Yo criado
examples.trans: I criado

meanings.en: crisis, slump, rough patch (professional, personal, or economic)
meanings.note: Feminine noun that is invariable in the plural ('una crisis' / 'varias crisis'). Often used without an article after 'en' ('estar en crisis').

examples.text: Porque estamos en crisis y vuelta a empezar todo desde cero.
examples.trans: Because we're in a crisis, and it's back to starting everything from scratch.

examples.text: La agencia superó una grave crisis cuando su actriz estrella se marchó.
examples.trans: The agency overcame a serious crisis when its star actress walked out.

meanings.note: Refers to window glass or crystal.

examples.text: El cristal está aquí.
examples.trans: The windowpane is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cristales desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the windowpanes from the door.

meanings.note: Plural of 'croqueta'; a staple Spanish tapa and comfort food frequently referenced in 'Paquita Salas'.

examples.text: De croquetas, empanadillas...
examples.trans: Of croquettes, turnovers...

examples.text: En la oficina de Paquita nunca faltan unas buenas croquetas de jamón.
examples.trans: At Paquita's office there is never a shortage of good ham croquettes.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza crujiente.
examples.trans: It is a crispy piece.

examples.text: ¡Hornea muchas esquinas crujientes, cariño!
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, my dear!

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells z -> c: crucé.

examples.text: Cruzo el puente de piedra cada día.
examples.trans: I cross the stone bridge every day.

examples.text: Cruzamos la plaza hacia el mercado.
examples.trans: We crossed the square toward the market.

examples.text: Es una crítica para televisión.
examples.trans: It is a critique of television.

examples.text: La película tuvo buenas críticas.
examples.trans: The film got good reviews.

meanings.note: Bound paper notebook.

examples.text: El cuaderno está aquí.
examples.trans: The notebook is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cuadernos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notebooks from the door.

meanings.note: Also used as a masculine noun (el cuadrado, 'the square') and in metros cuadrados ('square metres').

examples.text: Sacaron un paquete cuadrado envuelto en lino.
examples.trans: They lifted out a square bundle wrapped in linen.

examples.text: En la lata había cuatro tarjetas cuadradas de papel.
examples.trans: In the tin there were four square paper cards.

meanings.note: Refers to a framed square pane in a divided window as well as a wall painting.

examples.text: Ya he limpiado los cuatro cuadros superiores del ventanal.
examples.trans: I have already wiped the top four panes of the large window.

examples.text: Colgamos un cuadro antiguo encima de la librería.
examples.trans: We hung an old painting above the bookcase.

meanings.note: Apocopated form of the indefinite determiner 'cualquiera', used before singular masculine or feminine nouns.

examples.text: Una gorda te vale para hacer cualquier época.
examples.trans: A plus-size actress works for playing any period.

examples.text: Una gorda vale para cualquier época si lo hace bien.
examples.trans: A plus-size actress works for any era if she does it well.

meanings.note: Unaccented in statements and time clauses (interrogative: cuándo).

examples.text: Avísame cuando llegue el taxi.
examples.trans: Let me know when the taxi arrives.

examples.text: Cuando llueve, huele a tierra mojada.
examples.trans: When it rains, it smells like wet earth.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Vuelvo dentro de cuarenta minutos.
examples.trans: I will be back in forty minutes.

examples.text: Son las seis y cuarenta y cinco.
examples.trans: It is six forty-five.

meanings.note: Y cuarto = quarter past; menos cuarto = quarter to.

examples.text: El cuarto está aquí.
examples.trans: The quarter is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cuartos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the quarters from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Tenemos cuatro mesas dentro.
examples.trans: We have four tables inside.

examples.text: La habitación cuatro da al patio.
examples.trans: Room four looks out onto the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Peninsular word for a cleaning bucket (un cubo de agua).

examples.text: Llena el cubo hasta la mitad con agua templada.
examples.trans: Fill the bucket halfway with warm water.

examples.text: Baja el cubo y la esponja de la escalera.
examples.trans: Bring the bucket and the sponge down from the ladder.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb in present and preterite, but has the irregular past participle cubierto ('covered').

examples.text: Alguien cubrió los lados del hueco con ladrillos rojos.
examples.trans: Someone lined the sides of the cavity with red bricks.

examples.text: Rocío cubre la masa con un paño limpio.
examples.trans: Rocío covers the dough with a clean cloth.

meanings.note: Table or soup spoon; cucharita is a teaspoon.

examples.text: Pon una cuchara limpia junto a cada cuenco.
examples.trans: Set a clean spoon beside each bowl.

examples.text: Prueba la sopa de lentejas con esta cuchara.
examples.trans: Taste the lentil soup with this spoon.

meanings.note: Built from cuchara ('spoon') + -ada.

examples.text: Pon una cucharada de miel dorada en el té.
examples.trans: Put a spoonful of golden honey in the tea.

examples.text: Añade dos cucharadas de azúcar a la masa.
examples.trans: Add two spoonfuls of sugar to the dough.

meanings.note: Small spoon for coffee, tea, or dessert.

examples.text: La cucharilla está aquí.
examples.trans: The teaspoon is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cucharillas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teaspoons from the door.

meanings.note: Deep rounded bowl without handles, often ceramic or wooden.

examples.text: Sirvo la sopa caliente en cuencos blancos.
examples.trans: I serve the hot soup in white bowls.

examples.text: Hay un cuenco lleno de limones sobre la mesa.
examples.trans: There is a bowl full of lemons on the table.

meanings.en: awareness, realization (in 'darse cuenta de'); account, bill, check
meanings.note: Feminine noun central to idioms like 'darse cuenta (de)' ('to realize/notice') and 'tener en cuenta' ('to keep in mind').
Also third-person singular present indicative (and 'tú' imperative) of 'contar'.

examples.text: Que te das cuenta de que detrás ahí una pared.
examples.trans: That you realize there's a wall right behind there.

examples.text: Pues que te des cuenta de que lo que a ti te guste me da igual.
examples.trans: Well, realize that I couldn't care less what you like.

cuento.gloss: I tell, I recount; story, tale

meanings.en: I tell, I recount; I count
meanings.note: First-person singular present indicative of the stem-changing verb 'contar' (o > ue); used conversationally in '¿Te cuento una cosa?' to introduce gossip or news.
Also a masculine noun ('un cuento'), used both literally and in expressions like 'tener mucho cuento' ('to be overly dramatic').

examples.text: ¿Te cuento una cosa?
examples.trans: Can I tell you something?

examples.text: Os cuento, yo me lo he preparado a mi manera.
examples.trans: Let me tell you all, I've prepared it my own way.

meanings.note: Used for piano or guitar strings as well as rope.

examples.text: El macillo golpea tres cuerdas de acero a la vez.
examples.trans: The hammer strikes three steel strings at once.

examples.text: Esa cuerda central suena clara después de afinarla.
examples.trans: That middle string sounds clear after tuning it.

meanings.note: De cuero = made of leather.

examples.text: El cuero es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The leather is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el cuero.
examples.trans: We talk about the leather.

examples.text: Si no, se queda en el aire esta cuestión y no es así.
examples.trans: Otherwise this matter stays up in the air, and it isn't true.

examples.text: Yo cuestión
examples.trans: I cuestión

meanings.note: Con cuidado = carefully; ¡Cuidado con...! = Mind the...!

examples.text: El cuidado es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The care is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el cuidado.
examples.trans: We talk about the care.

cuidar.gloss: to look after; to take care of

meanings.en: to look after; to take care of
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Cuidamos cada detalle de la casa.
examples.trans: We look after every detail of the house.

examples.text: Ella cuida las plantas del balcón.
examples.trans: She tends the balcony plants.

examples.text: Cuido de tu madre y jugamos a un montón de cosas:
examples.trans: I take care of your mother and we play a lot of things:

examples.text: Yo Cuido
examples.trans: I Cuido

meanings.note: Por nuestra culpa = because of us; no es culpa suya = it is not your fault.

examples.text: La culpa está aquí.
examples.trans: The fault is here.

examples.text: Vemos las culpas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the faults from the door.

meanings.note: Compound masculine noun ('cumple' + 'años') that is invariable in number: 'el cumpleaños' (singular) and 'los cumpleaños' (plural).

examples.text: Por un cumpleaños mío.
examples.trans: For a birthday of mine.

examples.text: Celebramos su cumpleaños con una fiesta sorpresa en el bar.
examples.trans: We celebrated her birthday with a surprise party at the bar.

cumplir.gloss: to fulfil; to keep (a promise); to turn (an age)

meanings.en: to fulfil; to keep (a promise); to turn (an age)
meanings.note: Used both for fulfilling a dream or promise (cumplir un sueño / una promesa) and for birthdays (cumplir treinta años).

examples.text: El pedido de las sillas cumplió un sueño de hace treinta años.
examples.trans: The chair order fulfilled a dream from thirty years ago.

examples.text: Mi hermana cumple veinticinco años este sábado.
examples.trans: My sister turns twenty-five this Saturday.

meanings.note: Built from curioso.

examples.text: Nos gusta curiosear en el mercado viejo.
examples.trans: We like browsing around the old market.

examples.text: Curioseó los libros del estante.
examples.trans: He browsed curiously through the books on the shelf.

meanings.note: Por curiosidad = out of curiosity.

examples.text: La curiosidad es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The curiosity is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la curiosidad.
examples.trans: We talk about the curiosity.

meanings.note: Describes either an inquisitive person or an intriguing detail.

examples.text: Es una pieza curiosa.
examples.trans: It is a curious piece.

examples.text: ¡Qué curioso! La letra de esa etiqueta me resultaba muy familiar.
examples.trans: How curious! The handwriting on that tag felt very familiar to me.

examples.text: Venga, poneos las pilas. Ahora vengo. A currar, ¿eh?
examples.trans: Come on, get moving. I'll be right back. Get to work, okay?

examples.text: Venga, a currar.
examples.trans: Come on, back to work.

examples.text: Chicos, enhorabuena por el curro.
examples.trans: Kids, congratulations on the hard work.

examples.text: Yo curro
examples.trans: I curro

meanings.en: rummy (colloquial rural Spanish name for the game of rummy / Rummikub)
meanings.note: Informal phonetic adaptation of 'rummy' used among older generations in Spain for traditional tabletop card or tile rummy games.

examples.text: al dominó, al "currumi"...
examples.trans: dominoes, "rummy"...

examples.text: Por las tardes las señoras del pueblo jugaban al currumi en la terraza.
examples.trans: In the afternoons the village ladies played rummy on the terrace.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun choosing from options (plural: cuáles).

examples.text: Hay dos calles: ¿cuál cojo?
examples.trans: There are two streets: which one do I take?

examples.text: ¿Cuál es tu taza de té?
examples.trans: Which one is your teacup?

meanings.note: Takes a written accent in direct and indirect questions (dime cuándo).

examples.text: ¿Cuándo llega el inspector municipal a la posada?
examples.trans: When does the city inspector arrive at the inn?

examples.text: Avísame cuándo sale el primer pan del horno.
examples.trans: Let me know when the first bread comes out of the oven.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with its noun.

examples.text: ¿Cuántos bizcochos puedes hornear?
examples.trans: How many sponge cakes can you bake?

examples.text: ¿Cuánto tiempo tenemos antes de las doce?
examples.trans: How much time do we have before twelve?

meanings.note: Second-person singular ('tú') affirmative imperative of 'contar' with enclitic pronoun 'me'; written with an accent mark to preserve stress on the stem diphthong.

examples.text: Aquí, de fiesta, cuéntame.
examples.trans: Here, partying—tell me what's up.

examples.text: Bueno, ven. Ven, siéntate y cuéntame.
examples.trans: Alright, come here. Come, sit down and tell me.

meanings.note: Describes warm sound, light, or hospitality.

examples.text: Es una pieza cálida.
examples.trans: It is a warm piece.

examples.text: Enchufa la lámpara de latón de Mateo... ¡ay, mira qué luz amarilla tan cálida!
examples.trans: Plug in Mateo's brass lamp... oh, look how warm that yellow light is!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la cámara'); in film/TV production, 'el/la cámara' also refers to the camera operator, and 'a cámara' means looking directly into the lens.
Used in formal or technical contexts such as 'cámara frigorífica' (walk-in cooler) or legislative chambers.

examples.text: Esta cámara me la regaló Paco.
examples.trans: Paco gave me this camera as a gift.

examples.text: Mira a cámara y di tu nombre antes de empezar la separata.
examples.trans: Look at the camera and say your name before starting the audition sides.

meanings.note: Antepenultimate stress (esdrújula) always carries a written accent mark; cápsula del tiempo = time capsule.

examples.text: Escondieron una pequeña cápsula del tiempo debajo del árbol.
examples.trans: They hid a small time capsule underneath the tree.

examples.text: Dentro de la cápsula metálica había una carta y dos monedas.
examples.trans: Inside the metal capsule there were a letter and two coins.

examples.text: ¿La fiesta es de cóctel?
examples.trans: Is the party cocktail dress?

examples.text: Llevo un vestido de cóctel.
examples.trans: I'm wearing a cocktail dress.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb with written accent.

examples.text: ¿Cómo se llama usted?
examples.trans: What is your name?

examples.text: ¿Cómo encuentro la ferretería?
examples.trans: How do I find the hardware shop?

meanings.note: Always carries a written accent on the first syllable.

examples.text: Es una pieza cómoda.
examples.trans: It is a comfortable piece.

examples.text: Tengo una manta abrigada, así que esta noche estoy muy cómodo.
examples.trans: I have a warm blanket, so tonight I am very comfortable.

meanings.note: Cortar en dados means 'to dice into neat cubes'.

examples.text: Corta las patatas y las zanahorias en dados pequeños.
examples.trans: Cut the potatoes and carrots into small cubes.

examples.text: Los dados de verdura se cuecen rápido en el caldo.
examples.trans: The diced vegetables cook quickly in the broth.

meanings.note: Second-person singular ('tú') affirmative imperative of 'dar' with enclitic indirect object pronoun 'me'; unaccented because it follows standard paroxytone stress rules.

examples.text: Qué alegría. Ven, dame un beso. ¿Qué tal?
examples.trans: What a joy. Come here, give me a kiss. How's it going?

examples.text: Mamá, dame un besito.
examples.trans: Mom, give me a little kiss.

meanings.en: giving; taking (a walk); teaching/running (a class or workshop)
meanings.note: Gerund (present participle) of 'dar'; used in progressive constructions ('estar dando') and adverbial clauses like 'dando paseos' ('taking walks').

examples.text: Pasábamos las horas en el campo dando paseos con las ovejas.
examples.trans: We used to spend hours in the countryside taking walks with the sheep.

examples.text: Estoy dando un taller-teatro para niños.
examples.trans: I am teaching a theater workshop for children.

dar.gloss: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)

meanings.en: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg doy and preterite di/dio; dar las doce = strike twelve.

examples.text: La ventana da al patio soleado.
examples.trans: The window looks out onto the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: El reloj acaba de dar las doce.
examples.trans: The clock has just struck twelve.

meanings.note: Second-person singular ('tú') present indicative of 'dar'; appears in theatre/acting idioms like 'dar la réplica' ('to feed cue lines / read opposite an actor') and 'darse cuenta' ('to realize').

examples.text: Tú le das la réplica, yo dirijo, venga.
examples.trans: You read the cue lines opposite her, I'll direct—come on.

examples.text: Que te das cuenta de que detrás ahí una pared.
examples.trans: That you realize there's a wall right behind there.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: David llama a la oficina.
examples.trans: David calls the office.

examples.text: David espera noticias.
examples.trans: David is waiting for news.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Debajo de + noun means 'underneath something'.

examples.text: Hay una llave pegada debajo.
examples.trans: There is a key taped underneath.

examples.text: Mira debajo de las ruedas.
examples.trans: Look underneath the wheels.

deben.gloss: they must, they should; they owe

meanings.en: they must, they ought to, they should
meanings.note: Third-person plural present indicative of 'deber' followed by an infinitive to express obligation or strong advisability ('deben de + inf.' expresses probability).
Transitive sense of 'deber' used with money, favors, or gratitude.

examples.text: Eso lo deben hacer los directores de casting.
examples.trans: Casting directors should be the ones doing that.

examples.text: Todavía me deben el pago del último capítulo de la serie.
examples.trans: They still owe me payment for the last episode of the series.

meanings.note: With a noun object (le debo la verdad), means 'to owe'; before an infinitive, means 'should / ought to'.

examples.text: Le debo diez euros de cambio.
examples.trans: I owe you ten euros in change.

examples.text: Todo funciona como debe ser.
examples.trans: Everything works as it should.

debo.gloss: I must, I should; I owe

meanings.en: I must, I should, I ought to
meanings.note: First-person singular present indicative of 'deber', expressing personal obligation or duty when followed directly by an infinitive.
Transitive sense ('te debo dinero / un favor').

examples.text: Uy, Belinda, debo llamarla.
examples.trans: Oh, Belinda—I must call her.

examples.text: Te debo un favor enorme por conseguirme esa prueba.
examples.trans: I owe you a huge favor for getting me that audition.

meanings.note: Unit for measuring sound volume.

examples.text: El decibelio está aquí.
examples.trans: The decibel is here.

examples.text: Vemos los decibelios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the decibels from the door.

meanings.note: Describes someone confident and resolute.

examples.text: Es una pieza decidida.
examples.trans: It is a bold piece.

examples.text: El hermano mayor era decidido y ruidoso, siempre corría en las escalas de música.
examples.trans: The older brother was bold and loud, always rushing through his music scales.

meanings.note: First-person plural present indicative of 'decir'; often used after '¿Y si...?' ('What if we say...?') to propose a plan in colloquial Peninsular Spanish.

examples.text: Y dije: "¿Y si decimos que te han cogido para uno de esos?".
examples.trans: And I said: "What if we say they picked you for one of those?"

examples.text: Siempre decimos la verdad a nuestros representados, aunque duela.
examples.trans: We always tell the truth to our clients, even if it hurts.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.text: ¿Qué dice la carta exactamente?
examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?

examples.text: Dime la verdad sin miedo.
examples.trans: Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Infinitive 'decir' with attached neuter/masculine direct object pronoun 'lo'; common after prepositions like 'de tanto decirlo' ('from saying it so much').

forms.title: Infinitive decir with enclitic direct object pronouns

examples.text: Yo qué sé por qué lo hice, la costumbre. De tanto decirlo...
examples.trans: How should I know why I did it—force of habit. From saying it so much...

examples.text: Es muy fácil pensarlo, pero cuesta mucho decirlo en voz alta.
examples.trans: It's very easy to think it, but it's hard to say it out loud.

examples.text: Luego os comunicamos nuestra decisión.
examples.trans: We'll let you know our decision later.

examples.text: Yo decisión
examples.trans: I decisión

dedicar.gloss: to dedicate; to do for a living (dedicarse a)

meanings.en: to dedicate; to do for a living (dedicarse a)
meanings.note: ¿A qué te dedicas? / ¿A qué se dedica? asks someone's profession.

examples.text: ¿A qué te dedicas actualmente?
examples.trans: What do you do for a living right now?

examples.text: Dedica la tarde a tocar el piano.
examples.trans: She devotes the afternoon to playing the piano.

meanings.note: Covers both fingers (dedos de la mano) and toes (dedos del pie).

examples.text: Sujeta la hoja antigua con dos dedos limpios.
examples.trans: Hold the old sheet with two clean fingers.

examples.text: Los dedos vuelan suaves sobre las teclas blancas.
examples.trans: Her fingers glide gently over the white keys.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.

examples.text: Déjame ayudarte con esa caja.
examples.trans: Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Built from delante ('in front'), because an apron hangs down the front of the body.

examples.text: Rocío se ata el delantal limpio antes de encender el horno.
examples.trans: Rocio ties on her clean apron before turning on the oven.

examples.text: Colgamos los delantales blancos detrás de la puerta de la cocina.
examples.trans: We hung the white aprons behind the kitchen door.

delante.gloss: in front; ahead (delante de = in front of)

meanings.en: in front; ahead (delante de = in front of)
meanings.note: Followed by de before a noun: delante de la puerta.

examples.text: Hay una furgoneta azul aparcada delante de la posada.
examples.trans: There is a blue van parked in front of the inn.

examples.text: Camina tú delante con la linterna encendida.
examples.trans: Walk ahead with the flashlight switched on.

meanings.note: El cierre delantero = the front latch.

examples.text: Es una pieza delantera.
examples.trans: It is a front piece.

examples.text: Hay una cerradura diminuta en el cierre delantero, y miren pegada debajo: ¡una vieja llave de latón!
examples.trans: There is a tiny keyhole on the front latch, and look taped underneath: an old brass key!

examples.text: Estaba muy delgadita.
examples.trans: She was very slim.

examples.text: Yo delgado
examples.trans: I delgado

meanings.note: Stronger praise for food and baking.

examples.text: Es una pieza deliciosa.
examples.trans: It is a delicious piece.

examples.text: están deliciosos
examples.trans: they are delicious

demasiado.gloss: too much; too many; too (as adv)

meanings.en: too much; too many; too (as adv)
meanings.note: Agrees as a determiner before a noun (demasiado tiempo); invariable as an adverb before an adjective.

examples.text: Tres años era demasiado tiempo.
examples.trans: Three years was too much time.

examples.text: No camines demasiado rápido.
examples.trans: Do not walk too fast.

meanings.note: Dentro de + time means 'in (after) a certain amount of time'.

examples.text: Hay cuatro mesas dentro.
examples.trans: There are four tables inside.

examples.text: Vuelvo dentro de diez minutos.
examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes.

depender.gloss: to depend (depender de = to depend / rest on)

meanings.en: to depend (depender de = to depend / rest on)
meanings.note: Regular -er verb; always takes the preposition de before its object.

examples.text: La pintura del lunes depende del tiempo que haga.
examples.trans: Monday's painting depends on the weather.

examples.text: Todo el concierto depende de esa nota central.
examples.trans: The whole concert rests on that middle note.

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for a retail clerk (feminine: la dependienta).

examples.text: El dependiente está aquí.
examples.trans: The shop clerk is here.

examples.text: Vemos los dependientes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shop clerks from the door.

examples.text: Este aparato también depila.
examples.trans: This device also removes hair.

examples.text: Me depilo las piernas en casa.
examples.trans: I remove hair on my legs at home.

meanings.note: A la derecha / a mano derecha = on the right.

examples.text: La derecha está aquí.
examples.trans: The right is here.

examples.text: Vemos las derechas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rights from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of izquierdo; el derecho means 'the right one'.

examples.text: El cajón derecho guarda las cucharas limpias de postre.
examples.trans: The right-hand drawer holds the clean dessert spoons.

examples.text: Mantén el cuadro bien derecho sobre la pared blanca.
examples.trans: Keep the picture nice and straight on the white wall.

meanings.note: Describes feeling discouraged or beaten.

examples.text: Es una pieza derrotada.
examples.trans: It is a defeated piece.

examples.text: ¡No se siente derrotado todavía! Siga mirando hacia la esquina.
examples.trans: Do not sit down defeated yet! Keep looking toward the corner.

examples.text: Después de lo que he hecho por esa desagradecida, ahora se va.
examples.trans: After everything I've done for that ungrateful girl, now she leaves.

examples.text: Hablamos de desagradecido en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about ungrateful person at the office.

meanings.note: ¡Qué desastre! = What a disaster!

examples.text: El desastre está aquí.
examples.trans: The disaster is here.

examples.text: Vemos los desastres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the disasters from the door.

meanings.note: Built from the reversing prefix des- + atar ('to tie').

examples.text: Desate la cuerda despacio para no romper el hilo.
examples.trans: Untie the string slowly so as not to snap the twine.

examples.text: Clara desató el nudo del paquete con cuidado.
examples.trans: Clara untied the knot on the parcel carefully.

examples.text: Me apetece desayunar.
examples.trans: I feel like having breakfast.

examples.text: Yo desayunar
examples.trans: I desayunar

meanings.note: Con desayuno incluido = with breakfast included.

examples.text: El desayuno está aquí.
examples.trans: The breakfast is here.

examples.text: Vemos los desayunos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the breakfasts from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Descanso media hora después de comer.
examples.trans: I rest half an hour after lunch.

examples.text: Los huéspedes descansaron muy bien.
examples.trans: The guests rested very well.

meanings.note: Also used as an adjective meaning 'unknown'.

examples.text: El desconocido está aquí.
examples.trans: The stranger is here.

examples.text: Vemos los desconocidos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the strangers from the door.

examples.text: Igual aquí hay una joya por descubrir.
examples.trans: Maybe there is a gem to discover here.

examples.text: Yo descubrir
examples.trans: I descubrir

meanings.note: Reduction in price.

examples.text: El descuento está aquí.
examples.trans: The discount is here.

examples.text: Vemos los descuentos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the discounts from the door.

meanings.note: Marks a starting point in space or time.

examples.text: No hablamos desde aquel domingo.
examples.trans: We have not spoken since that Sunday.

examples.text: Abrimos al público desde mañana.
examples.trans: We open to the public starting tomorrow.

meanings.en: he/she/it desires, wishes; you (formal) wish or would like
meanings.note: Third-person singular (and 'usted') present indicative of 'desear'.

examples.text: Desear algo que tanta gente desea.
examples.trans: To desire something that so many people desire.

examples.text: ¿Desea usted tomar un cafelito mientras espera a Paquita?
examples.trans: Would you like to have a little coffee while you wait for Paquita?

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; ¡deseadnos suerte! means 'wish us luck!'.

examples.text: Te deseo mucha suerte en tu nuevo trabajo.
examples.trans: I wish you lots of luck in your new job.

examples.text: Les deseamos una estancia tranquila en Valencia.
examples.trans: We wish you a peaceful stay in Valencia.

desenfocar.gloss: to throw out of focus, to blur

meanings.en: to throw out of focus, defocus, blur; to lose focus
meanings.note: Regular '-ar' verb (with 'c > qu' spelling change before 'e', e.g., 'desenfoque'); formed from 'des-' + 'enfocar' and used both in camera work and figuratively.

examples.text: No, ¿ves? Eso es desenfocar.
examples.trans: No, see? That's throwing it out of focus.

examples.text: Ten cuidado al mover el objetivo para no desenfocar el primer plano.
examples.trans: Be careful when moving the lens so you don't blur the close-up.

examples.text: Venga, desfilando.
examples.trans: Come on, marching out.

examples.text: Yo desfilar
examples.trans: I desfilar

desgastar.gloss: to wear out; to wear down

meanings.en: to wear out; to wear down
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: El paso del tiempo desgasta la piedra.
examples.trans: The passage of time wears down the stone.

examples.text: Tanto caminar desgastó las suelas.
examples.trans: Walking so much wore thin the soles.

meanings.note: Por desgracia = unfortunately.

examples.text: La desgracia es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The misfortune is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la desgracia.
examples.trans: We talk about the misfortune.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells z -> c: deslicé.

examples.text: Deslizo la carta bajo la puerta.
examples.trans: I slip the letter under the door.

examples.text: Una moneda se deslizó dentro de la caja.
examples.trans: A coin slid inside the box.

meanings.en: disorients, confuses; (with 'se') gets disoriented or loses one's bearings
meanings.note: Third-person singular present indicative of 'desorientar'; very commonly used pronominally ('desorientarse').

examples.text: Es que a veces se desorienta un poco.
examples.trans: It's just that sometimes she gets a bit disoriented.

examples.text: Con tantos cambios de guion, cualquiera se desorienta en el rodaje.
examples.trans: With so many script changes, anyone gets disoriented on set.

related.gloss: to disorient; to lose one's bearings

meanings.note: Private study or small manager's office.

examples.text: El despacho está aquí.
examples.trans: The office is here.

examples.text: Vemos los despachos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the offices from the door.

meanings.note: Everyday single-word opposite of rápido.

examples.text: Camina despacio por las escaleras.
examples.trans: Walk slowly on the stairs.

examples.text: Gira la rueda muy despacio.
examples.trans: Turn the wheel very slowly.

meanings.note: Built from shaking off pereza (sleepy laziness).

examples.text: Me desperezo al abrir la ventana.
examples.trans: I stretch awake when opening the window.

examples.text: El barrio se despereza poco a poco.
examples.trans: The neighbourhood stretches awake little by little.

meanings.note: Literally 'waker-upper', from despertar.

examples.text: El despertador está aquí.
examples.trans: The alarm clock is here.

examples.text: Vemos los despertadores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the alarm clocks from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: despierta).

examples.text: Me despierto temprano sin reloj.
examples.trans: I wake up early without an alarm.

examples.text: El olor a café despertó a toda la casa.
examples.trans: The smell of coffee woke the whole house.

meanings.note: Stem-changing e -> ie (despliego) like plegar;vosotros imperative is regular desplegad.

examples.text: Desplegamos las sillas de madera en el patio soleado.
examples.trans: We unfolded the wooden chairs in the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: Abrió su maleta y desplegó un gran mapa de la ciudad.
examples.trans: He opened his suitcase and unfolded a large map of the city.

meanings.note: Después de + noun/infinitive means 'after'.

examples.text: Hablamos después del desayuno.
examples.trans: We will talk after breakfast.

examples.text: ¿Qué hacemos después de eso?
examples.trans: What do we do after that?

examples.text: Mi destino está claramente trazado.
examples.trans: My destiny is clearly mapped out.

examples.text: Yo destino
examples.trans: I destino

meanings.note: Built from des- + tornillo (screw).

examples.text: El destornillador está aquí.
examples.trans: The screwdriver is here.

examples.text: Vemos los destornilladores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the screwdrivers from the door.

meanings.note: Storage attic right under the roof (plural: desvanes).

examples.text: El desván está aquí.
examples.trans: The attic is here.

examples.text: Vemos los desvanes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the attics from the door.

meanings.note: Detrás de + noun means 'behind something'.

examples.text: El jardín está detrás de la casa.
examples.trans: The garden is behind the house.

examples.text: Hay otra página detrás del aviso.
examples.trans: There is another page behind the notice.

devolver.gloss: to return (an item); to give back

meanings.en: to return (an item); to give back
meanings.note: Conjugates like volver (o -> ue, past participle devuelto).

examples.text: Hoy devuelvo el libro a la biblioteca.
examples.trans: Today I am returning the book to the library.

examples.text: Devolvimos la llave en recepción.
examples.trans: We returned the key at the front desk.

meanings.en: I gave; (in 'darse un beso / darse cuenta') I had / I realized
meanings.note: First-person singular preterite indicative of 'dar'; written without an accent mark because it is monosyllabic under modern RAE orthography.
Also the irregular second-person singular ('tú') affirmative imperative of 'decir'.

examples.text: Aquí me di mi primer beso.
examples.trans: Right here I had my first kiss.

examples.text: Di lo que piensas sin miedo, que estamos en confianza.
examples.trans: Say what you think without fear—we're among friends.

meanings.note: Plural diablos in ¿dónde/qué diablos? means 'where/what on earth?'.

examples.text: El diablo está aquí.
examples.trans: The devil is here.

examples.text: Vemos los diablos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the devils from the door.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from dibujar.

examples.text: Es una pieza dibujada.
examples.trans: It is a drawn piece.

examples.text: Miren el plano doblado que asoma por la bisagra: ¡hay una puerta secreta dibujada en esta planta!
examples.trans: Look at the folded blueprint sticking out of the hinge—there is a hidden door drawn on this floor!

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; the noun is el dibujo, a drawing.

examples.text: Mi hija dibuja un gato.
examples.trans: My daughter is drawing a cat.

examples.text: ¿Me dibujas el camino al hotel?
examples.trans: Will you sketch me the way to the hotel?

meanings.note: Sketch or decorative pattern.

examples.text: El dibujo está aquí.
examples.trans: The drawing is here.

examples.text: Vemos los dibujos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the drawings from the door.

meanings.en: they say, they tell; people say, rumor has it
meanings.note: Third-person plural present indicative of 'decir'; frequently used impersonally in Spanish ('dicen que...') to report hearsay or industry gossip.

examples.text: Y dicen: "Ay, Paquita, consígame usted una visita".
examples.trans: And they say: "Oh, Paquita, get me an appointment."

examples.text: Que se les sube mucho de pluma, dicen.
examples.trans: They come across way too camp, so they say.

meanings.note: Irregular past participle of 'decir'; heavily used in Peninsular Spanish compound past ('he dicho / ha dicho') for events earlier the same day.
Also used as a masculine noun ('un dicho popular').

examples.text: Ha dicho Camilla que esta tarde.
examples.trans: Camilla said this afternoon.

examples.text: Pero he dicho: mira, me hago el viaje, que la noticia lo merece.
examples.trans: But I said to myself: look, I'll make the trip, because the news is worth it.

meanings.note: Single fused word for diez + y + nueve.

examples.text: Escribió diecinueve razones en un papel.
examples.trans: He wrote nineteen reasons on a sheet of paper.

examples.text: El tren sale a las diecinueve horas.
examples.trans: The train leaves at nineteen hundred hours.

meanings.note: Compound numeral (diez + y + seis); carries an acute accent on -éis.

examples.text: Faltan dieciséis compases para cerrar la segunda parte.
examples.trans: Sixteen bars are missing to close the second part.

examples.text: Hemos preparado dieciséis tazas blancas en la bandeja.
examples.trans: We set out sixteen white cups on the tray.

meanings.note: Diez sobre diez = ten out of ten.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para empezar.
examples.trans: There are ten minutes left before starting.

examples.text: Su recepción merece un diez.
examples.trans: Your front desk deserves a ten.

meanings.note: Feminine noun; common in 'haber diferencia' ('there to be a difference'), 'marcar la diferencia' ('to make a difference'), and 'a diferencia de' ('unlike').

examples.text: Lo primero, hay mucha diferencia entre un casting y otro.
examples.trans: First of all, there is a big difference between one audition and another.

examples.text: La actitud marca la diferencia cuando entras por esa puerta.
examples.trans: Attitude makes all the difference when you walk through that door.

meanings.note: Two-form adjective invariable for gender ('un papel diferente / una actriz diferente'); in the show it appears in the Spanish title of 'Inspector Rex' ('Rex, un policía diferente').

examples.text: De "Rex, un policía diferente", se pone...
examples.trans: From "Inspector Rex" ("Rex, a Different Kind of Cop"), he gets...

examples.text: Los productores buscan un perfil totalmente diferente para la protagonista.
examples.trans: The producers are looking for a totally different profile for the lead actress.

examples.text: Uno sale al escenario y ve lo difícil que es ser actor.
examples.trans: You step out onto the stage and see how hard it is to be an actor.

examples.text: Yo difícil
examples.trans: I difícil

meanings.note: Feminine noun ending in -dad.

examples.text: La dignidad es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The dignity is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la dignidad.
examples.trans: We talk about the dignity.

meanings.note: First-person singular irregular preterite indicative ('j'-stem) of 'decir'.

examples.text: ¿Sabes lo que les dije a los niños el otro día?
examples.trans: Do you know what I told the kids the other day?

examples.text: Y dije: "¿Y si decimos que te han cogido para uno de esos?".
examples.trans: And I said: "What if we say they picked you for one of those?"

meanings.note: Describes something very small, such as a tiny keyhole.

examples.text: Es una pieza diminuta.
examples.trans: It is a tiny piece.

examples.text: diminuta
examples.trans: tiny

dina.gloss: Dina (genie protagonist of the Spanish sitcom '¡Ala... Dina!')

meanings.en: Dina (given name; title character of the TVE sitcom '¡Ala... Dina!')
meanings.note: Proper name from the hit Spanish sitcom '¡Ala... Dina!' (2000–2002, a pun on 'Aladina' and '¡Hala, Dina!'), in which Lidia San José co-starred as Eva alongside Paz Padilla's genie Dina.

examples.text: Niña, el pico. Es Lidia San José, la niña de "¡Ala... Dina!".
examples.trans: Watch your mouth, girl. That's Lidia San José, the girl from "¡Ala... Dina!"

examples.text: Toda una generación recuerda a Dina haciendo magia en televisión.
examples.trans: An entire generation remembers Dina doing magic on television.

meanings.note: From dinero plus the ending -al for a large amount: costar un dineral.

examples.text: Este coche cuesta un dineral.
examples.trans: This car costs a fortune.

examples.text: Gastamos un dineral en el viaje.
examples.trans: We spent a fortune on the trip.

examples.text: Me saco un dinerito extra.
examples.trans: I earn a little extra money.

examples.text: Siempre viene bien un dinerito.
examples.trans: A little extra cash always comes in handy.

meanings.note: Uncountable singular in Spanish.

examples.text: El dinero es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The money is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el dinero.
examples.trans: We talk about the money.

examples.text: ¡Ay, Dios mío!
examples.trans: Oh, my goodness!

examples.text: Menos mal, gracias a Dios.
examples.trans: Thank goodness.

meanings.note: Plural direcciones.

examples.text: La dirección está aquí.
examples.trans: The address is here.

examples.text: Vemos las direcciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the addresss from the door.

meanings.note: Formed from directa + -mente.

examples.text: Sube directamente a la segunda planta.
examples.trans: Go straight up to the second floor.

examples.text: Pregúntale a ella directamente.
examples.trans: Ask her directly.

meanings.note: Also used adverbially (salir directo = walk straight out).

examples.text: Es una pieza directa.
examples.trans: It is a direct piece.

examples.text: Sí, Rocío. Aunque dé media vuelta y salga directo por la puerta.
examples.trans: Yes, Rocio. Even if he turns around and walks straight back out the gate.

examples.text: Esta lo hace muy bien, tía. Hace lo que le pide el director.
examples.trans: She acts really well, girl. She does whatever the director asks of her.

examples.text: Hablamos de director en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about director at the office.

meanings.note: Masculine plural of 'director' (feminine 'directora'). In the entertainment industry, 'directores de casting' (casting directors) are the key figures who audition and select actors for roles.

examples.text: Eso lo deben hacer los directores de casting,
examples.trans: Casting directors should do that,

examples.text: Paquita conoce a todos los directores de cine y televisión de Madrid.
examples.trans: Paquita knows all the film and television directors in Madrid.

dirigir.gloss: to direct; to run; to lead

meanings.en: to direct; to run; to lead
meanings.note: Spelling change g -> j before -o/-a (dirijo, dirija) to keep the /x/ sound.

examples.text: Rocío dirige la cocina del café con mucha alegría.
examples.trans: Rocio runs the café kitchen with great cheer.

examples.text: El director dirigió la pequeña orquesta desde el centro de la sala.
examples.trans: The conductor led the small orchestra from the centre of the room.

meanings.en: I direct (a play, film, rehearsal, or company)
meanings.note: First-person singular present indicative of dirigir. Spelling changes from g to j before -o to preserve the velar fricative /x/ sound.

meanings.en: I address, I steer, I head
meanings.note: Also used transitively or reflexively (dirigirse a) to mean addressing someone or heading toward a place.

examples.text: Tú le das la réplica, yo dirijo, venga.
examples.trans: You feed her the lines, I'll direct, come on.

examples.text: Ahora mismo dirijo un proyecto de teatro independiente en Madrid.
examples.trans: Right now I am directing an independent theater project in Madrid.

meanings.en: I would say, I would tell; he/she/you would say
meanings.note: First- and third-person singular conditional form of the irregular verb decir (stem dir-). Frequently used to soften statements, give polite excuses, or hedge opinions (diría yo).

examples.text: Te diría que te pasases, pero reunión...
examples.trans: I would tell you to drop by, but I have a meeting...

examples.text: Excitante diría yo.
examples.trans: Exciting, I would say.

examples.text: Quiero pedir disculpas.
examples.trans: I want to apologise.

examples.text: Acepto tus disculpas.
examples.trans: I accept your apology.

meanings.note: Disculpe (usted) / Disculpa (tú) is polite 'excuse me'.

examples.text: Disculpe, ¿sabe qué hora es?
examples.trans: Excuse me, do you know what time it is?

examples.text: Nos disculpamos por el pequeño retraso.
examples.trans: We apologized for the brief delay.

meanings.note: Formal talk or prepared speech.

examples.text: El discurso está aquí.
examples.trans: The speech is here.

examples.text: Vemos los discursos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the speechs from the door.

meanings.note: Stronger than English 'discussion'—usually means an argument.

examples.text: La discusión está aquí.
examples.trans: The argument is here.

examples.text: Vemos las discusiones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the arguments from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb.

examples.text: Rara vez discutimos en el trabajo.
examples.trans: We rarely argue at work.

examples.text: Discutieron por una tontería antigua.
examples.trans: They argued over an old trifle.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: El arquitecto diseña bibliotecas tranquilas.
examples.trans: El arquitecto designs quiet libraries.

examples.text: Diseñaron un patio lleno de luz.
examples.trans: They designed a courtyard full of light.

meanings.note: Covers architectural, acoustic, graphic, and furniture design.

examples.text: Javier abre un pequeño estudio de diseño en nuestra calle.
examples.trans: Javier is opening a small design studio on our street.

examples.text: El diseño sencillo del cartel se lee desde la acera.
examples.trans: The simple design of the sign can be read from the pavement.

meanings.note: Often paired with de (disfrutar de su té = enjoy your tea).

examples.text: Disfruto mucho del silencio de la mañana.
examples.trans: I really enjoy the morning quiet.

examples.text: Disfrutaron de una cena tranquila.
examples.trans: They enjoyed a peaceful dinner.

examples.text: A mí disimular se me da muy bien.
examples.trans: Putting on a brave face comes very naturally to me.

examples.text: Yo disimular
examples.trans: I disimular

meanings.note: Irregular past participle of disponer used as an adjective, typically constructed with estar + dispuesto + a + infinitive.
With ser, means resourceful or sharp; as a participle, means arranged or set up.

examples.text: Yo estoy dispuesto a jugar un partido amistoso.
examples.trans: I am willing to play a friendly match.

examples.text: Siempre está dispuesto a ayudar a sus compañeros de reparto.
examples.trans: He is always ready and willing to help his castmates.

related.gloss: to arrange, to dispose, to have available

meanings.note: A dos metros de distancia means 'from two metres away'.

examples.text: Las letras oscuras se leen bien a buena distancia.
examples.trans: The dark letters read clearly from a good distance.

examples.text: Hay poca distancia desde la posada hasta la plaza.
examples.trans: It is a short distance from the inn to the square.

examples.text: Es una chica muy divertida.
examples.trans: She is a very funny girl.

examples.text: Fue una tarde divertida.
examples.trans: It was a fun afternoon.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb; dividir en means 'to divide into'.

examples.text: Dividimos el trabajo grande en tres partes sencillas.
examples.trans: We divide the big job into three simple parts.

examples.text: ¿Cómo dividís las tareas de la mañana aquí?
examples.trans: How do you split the morning tasks here?

meanings.note: Adverb formed from divino ('divine') + -mente. Very common in colloquial Peninsular Spanish as an enthusiastic reply to how one is doing.

examples.text: Yo divinamente, no me puedo quejar.
examples.trans: I'm doing wonderfully, I can't complain.

examples.text: La cena salió divinamente y todos quedaron encantados.
examples.trans: Dinner turned out splendidly and everyone was delighted.

meanings.en: division, league tier (especially in sports or show business)
meanings.note: Feminine noun. In Spanish idiom, jugar en primera división ('to play in the first division / Premier League') means operating at the top tier of one's profession.
General sense of dividing something into parts or an organizational branch.

examples.text: Claro, como ahora juegas en primera división.
examples.trans: Of course, since now you play in the first division.

examples.text: Pues por mucho que juegue en primera división, sigue siendo humilde.
examples.trans: Well, no matter how much she plays in the big leagues, she stays humble.

meanings.note: First note of the solfège scale (do, re, mi, fa, sol, la, si).

examples.text: El do suena limpio y redondo en esta octava.
examples.trans: C sounds clean and round in this octave.

examples.text: Empieza la escala despacio desde el do central.
examples.trans: Start the scale slowly from middle C.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from doblar.

examples.text: Es una pieza doblada.
examples.trans: It is a folded piece.

examples.text: Mira, hay un sobre blanco doblado en el asa.
examples.trans: Look, there is a folded white envelope on the handle.

doblar.gloss: to fold; to double; to turn (a corner)

meanings.en: to fold; to double; to turn (a corner)
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Doblo la servilleta con cuidado.
examples.trans: I fold the napkin neatly.

examples.text: Dobla la esquina junto a la farmacia.
examples.trans: Turn the corner beside the pharmacy.

meanings.note: El doble de... means 'double the amount of...'.

examples.text: El doble está aquí.
examples.trans: The double is here.

examples.text: Vemos los dobles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doubles from the door.

meanings.note: Las doce = twelve o'clock.

examples.text: El reloj da las doce al mediodía.
examples.trans: The clock strikes twelve at noon.

examples.text: Aquí tienes doce euros de cambio.
examples.trans: Here is twelve euros in change.

meanings.note: Media docena means 'half a dozen' (six).

examples.text: Compramos una docena de tazas blancas en el mercado.
examples.trans: We bought a dozen white cups at the market.

examples.text: Rocío usa media docena de huevos para el bizcocho.
examples.trans: Rocio uses half a dozen eggs for the sponge cake.

meanings.note: Official or legal paper.

examples.text: El documento está aquí.
examples.trans: The document is here.

examples.text: Vemos los documentos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the documents from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: duele, duelen).

examples.text: Hoy me duele un poco la cabeza.
examples.trans: My head hurts a little today.

examples.text: Esas palabras duras duelen hondo.
examples.trans: Those harsh words cut deep.

meanings.note: Dolor de cabeza = headache.

examples.text: El dolor está aquí.
examples.trans: The pain is here.

examples.text: Vemos los dolores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pains from the door.

meanings.note: El domingo = on Sunday; los domingos = on Sundays.

examples.text: El domingo está aquí.
examples.trans: The Sunday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los domingos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Sundays from the door.

meanings.note: Masculine singular noun in Spanish (jugar al dominó), borrowed from French domino. Note the final stress mark distinguishing it from domino ('I dominate').
Also the third-person singular preterite indicative of dominar ('to dominate, to master').

examples.text: Por las tardes jugaban al dominó, al "currumi"...
examples.trans: In the afternoons they used to play dominoes, "currumi"...

examples.text: Los abuelos echan la partida de dominó en el bar de la plaza.
examples.trans: The grandfathers play a game of dominoes at the bar in the square.

meanings.note: Respectful Spanish title used directly before a man's given name (don Ernesto).

examples.text: El don está aquí.
examples.trans: The Mr / Sir is here.

examples.text: Vemos los dones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Mr / Sirs from the door.

meanings.note: Unaccented in relative clauses; accented dónde in questions.

examples.text: Esta es la plaza donde compramos flores.
examples.trans: This is the square where we buy flowers.

examples.text: Siéntate donde estés más cómodo.
examples.trans: Sit where you feel most comfortable.

meanings.note: Describes gold colour or golden-brown baked crust.

examples.text: Es una pieza dorada.
examples.trans: It is a golden piece.

examples.text: El del papel dorado del estante de arriba. ¿Por qué?
examples.trans: The one in gold paper from the top shelf. Why?

meanings.note: Derived from oro ('gold'); in cooking, dorar means to sauté or bake until golden brown.

examples.text: Remueve la cebolla tres minutos hasta dorar en aceite de oliva.
examples.trans: Stir the onion for three minutes until golden in olive oil.

examples.text: Los bollos de canela se doraron enseguida en el horno caliente.
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls turned golden brown quickly in the hot oven.

meanings.note: From dormir, to sleep; also used for a numb arm or leg.

examples.text: El bebé ya está dormido.
examples.trans: The baby is already asleep.

examples.text: Los huéspedes siguen dormidos.
examples.trans: The guests are still asleep.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue in present: duermo; o -> u in preterite 3rd: durmió).

examples.text: Duermo ocho horas cada noche.
examples.trans: I sleep eight hours every night.

examples.text: Anoche dormí de maravilla aquí.
examples.trans: Last night I slept wonderfully here.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender with the plural noun that follows: doscientos gramos (masculine) vs. doscientas páginas (feminine).

examples.text: La receta pide doscientos gramos de almendra molida.
examples.trans: The recipe calls for two hundred grams of ground almonds.

examples.text: El edificio antiguo tiene más de doscientos años.
examples.trans: The old building is more than two hundred years old.

examples.text: Es buena en drama y es buena en comedia.
examples.trans: She is good at drama and she is good at comedy.

examples.text: Yo drama
examples.trans: I drama

meanings.note: Darse una ducha = to take a shower.

examples.text: La ducha está aquí.
examples.trans: The shower is here.

examples.text: Vemos las duchas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the showers from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine: la dueña.

examples.text: El dueño está aquí.
examples.trans: The owner is here.

examples.text: Vemos los dueños desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the owners from the door.

meanings.note: Masculine plural of dueño ('owner, proprietor, master'). In plural (los dueños), it refers either to male owners or to a mixed-gender couple/group of owners.

examples.text: Vienen... Vienen los dueños.
examples.trans: They're coming... The owners are coming.

examples.text: Los dueños del local nos pidieron que bajáramos la música.
examples.trans: The owners of the venue asked us to turn the music down.

related.gloss: to take ownership of, to seize

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine; los dulces = sweets/pastries.

examples.text: Es una pieza dulce.
examples.trans: It is a sweet piece.

examples.text: ¿Podemos servir mantequilla salada con mermelada dulce de fresa?
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with sweet strawberry jam?

meanings.note: Marks how long an action lasted (durante seis años).

examples.text: Vivió aquí durante seis años.
examples.trans: She lived here for six years.

examples.text: No sonó el teléfono durante la cena.
examples.trans: The phone did not ring during dinner.

meanings.note: Hacerse el duro = to act tough.

examples.text: Es una pieza dura.
examples.trans: It is a hard piece.

examples.text: se hacía el duro
examples.trans: acted tough

meanings.note: Masculine despite ending in -a: el día, ¡Buenos días!.

examples.text: El día está aquí.
examples.trans: The day is here.

examples.text: Vemos los días desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the days from the door.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb with written accent.

examples.text: Mira dónde señala con el lápiz.
examples.trans: Look where he is pointing with his pencil.

examples.text: ¿Dónde van las cucharillas y las servilletas?
examples.trans: Where do the teaspoons and the napkins go?

meanings.note: Plural los dúos.

examples.text: El dúo está aquí.
examples.trans: The duet is here.

examples.text: Vemos los dúos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the duets from the door.

meanings.note: Unadapted English adjective used in Paquita Salas during the hilarious English-language audition scene ("It's easy, but it's very important"), where Spanish actors struggle with basic English lines on their CV. In Spanish, the equivalent is fácil.

examples.text: "It's easy, but it's very important".
examples.trans: "It's easy, but it's very important." (English audition line in the show)

examples.text: En el casting en inglés tenía que decir "It's easy" con mucha intensidad dramática.
examples.trans: In the English audition she had to say "It's easy" with a lot of dramatic intensity.

echa.gloss: misses (echa de menos); throws, puts, pours

meanings.en: misses (in echar de menos); throws, casts, pours, puts in
meanings.note: Third-person singular present indicative (or second-person singular informal imperative) of echar. In the show's phrase te echa de menos, the idiom echar de menos means 'to miss someone'.

examples.text: -Te echa mucho de menos, Paca.
examples.trans: -She misses you a lot, Paca.

examples.text: Siempre le echa mucha pasión a cada papel que interpreta.
examples.trans: She always puts a lot of passion into every role she plays.

related.gloss: to throw, to pour, to put; to fire
to kick out, to throw out

echar.gloss: to pour; to toss; to miss (echar de menos)

meanings.en: to pour; to toss; to miss (echar de menos)
meanings.note: Echar un vistazo = take a glance; echar de menos = miss someone.

examples.text: Echa un poco más de agua caliente.
examples.trans: Pour a little more hot water.

examples.text: Te he echado mucho de menos.
examples.trans: I have missed you very much.

meanings.note: Reflected sound in a courtyard or hall.

examples.text: El eco está aquí.
examples.trans: The echo is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ecos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the echos from the door.

examples.text: ¿Qué edad tienes?
examples.trans: How old are you?

examples.text: Tenemos la misma edad.
examples.trans: We are the same age.

meanings.note: Multi-storey town building.

examples.text: El edificio está aquí.
examples.trans: The building is here.

examples.text: Vemos los edificios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the buildings from the door.

meanings.note: False friend: means 'polite', whereas 'educated' is culto or formado.

examples.text: Es una pieza educada.
examples.trans: It is a polite piece.

examples.text: ¿Voz educada? ¿Joven o mayor?
examples.trans: Polite voice? Young or older?

meanings.note: Pagar en efectivo means 'to pay in cash'.

examples.text: El efectivo es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The cash is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el efectivo.
examples.trans: We talk about the cash.

meanings.note: Un efecto de la luz means 'a trick of the light'.

examples.text: La luz dorada crea un efecto precioso sobre el cristal.
examples.trans: The golden light creates a lovely effect on the glass.

examples.text: El descanso hizo efecto enseguida en su tobillo.
examples.trans: The rest took effect right away on her ankle.

examples.text: Estás un poco tensa, ¿eh?
examples.trans: You're a bit tense, aren't you?

examples.text: Cuidado con eso, ¿eh?
examples.trans: Careful with that, okay?

examples.text: Natalie Portman es un ejemplo perfecto.
examples.trans: Natalie Portman is a perfect example.

examples.text: Yo ejemplo
examples.trans: I ejemplo

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Plural elecciones.

examples.text: La elección está aquí.
examples.trans: The choice is here.

examples.text: Vemos las elecciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the choices from the door.

examples.text: Qué elegancia. ¡Guapa!
examples.trans: Such elegance. Gorgeous!

examples.text: Yo elegancia
examples.trans: I elegancia

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: elijo, eligió).

examples.text: Elijo una mesa bajo el árbol.
