examples.trans: I choose a table under the tree.

examples.text: Elegimos este barrio por su calma.
examples.trans: We chose this neighbourhood for its calm.

meanings.note: Third-person feminine singular pronoun.

examples.text: Ella conoce muy bien esta calle.
examples.trans: She knows this street very well.

examples.text: Este regalo es para ella.
examples.trans: This gift is for her.

examples.text: Muchos nervios. ¿Y ellos cómo tienen que estar?
examples.trans: Such nerves. And how nervous must they be?

examples.text: Yo ellos
examples.trans: I ellos

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb (unstressed -i- in elogio, elogia).

examples.text: Todos los clientes elogiaron la tarta casera de limón.
examples.trans: All the customers praised the homemade lemon tart.

examples.text: La inspectora elogió el cuidado del patio histórico.
examples.trans: The inspector praised the care given to the historic courtyard.

meanings.note: Used in baking to describe well-kneaded dough (una masa suave y elástica).

examples.text: Sabes que la masa está lista cuando queda suave y elástica.
examples.trans: You know the dough is ready when it turns smooth and springy.

examples.text: Ató la caja de pasteles con una cinta elástica.
examples.trans: She tied the pastry box with an elastic band.

meanings.en: deceitful woman, liar, fibber, trickster; lying, mendacious
meanings.note: Feminine form of embustero (derived from embuste, 'lie, scheme, tall tale'). Used both as an adjective and a noun in expressive Peninsular Spanish, slightly more dramatic or traditional than mentirosa.

examples.text: Que si mentirosa... Que si embustera...
examples.trans: Calling me a liar... Calling me a fibber and a fraud...

examples.text: No le creas ni una palabra a esa embustera.
examples.trans: Don't believe a single word from that deceitful liar.

meanings.note: Third-person singular present indicative of emocionar. In Spanish, emocionar primarily means to touch or move someone to tears/deep feeling, not merely 'to make excited'.

examples.text: Pero le ves la cara, te emociona, te llega.
examples.trans: But you see her face, she moves you, she gets right to you.

examples.text: Me emociona muchísimo ver cómo crecen los actores jóvenes.
examples.trans: It moves me deeply to see how young actors grow.

related.gloss: to move emotionally, to touch, to excite

examples.text: Enhorabuena, estoy emocionadísimo.
examples.trans: Congratulations, I'm deeply moved.

examples.text: Yo emocionado
examples.trans: I emocionado

meanings.en: small savory turnovers or pasties (typically fried or baked with tuna, tomato, and egg)
meanings.note: Feminine plural of empanadilla (diminutive of empanada). In Peninsular Spanish, empanadillas are small half-moon pastries (especially empanadillas de Móstoles, a famous Spanish pop-culture touchstone from Martes y Trece).

examples.text: De croquetas, empanadillas...
examples.trans: Of croquettes, savory turnovers...

examples.text: Paquita preparó una bandeja de empanadillas de bonito para la visita.
examples.trans: Paquita made a tray of tuna turnovers for the guests.

meanings.note: From empapar ('to soak through').

examples.text: Llegamos del patio con los abrigos empapados.
examples.trans: We came in from the courtyard with soaked coats.

examples.text: Cambia ese trapo empapado por uno seco, por favor.
examples.trans: Swap that soaked cloth for a dry one, please.

empañar.gloss: to fog up; to mist over

meanings.en: to fog up; to mist over
meanings.note: Often reflexive (empañarse) for glasses, mirrors, or windows steaming up: se me empañan las gafas.

examples.text: Con el vapor del té caliente se me empañan las gafas.
examples.trans: With the steam from the hot tea my glasses mist up.

examples.text: La lluvia fría empañó los cristales de la ventana.
examples.trans: The cold rain fogged up the windowpanes.

meanings.note: Unadapted English noun featured in the English audition scene in Paquita Salas ("It is very important to give this envelope to the emperor"). The Spanish equivalent is emperador.

examples.text: "It is very important to give this envelope to the emperor".
examples.trans: "It is very important to give this envelope to the emperor." (English audition script line)

examples.text: Se bloqueó al pronunciar la palabra "emperor" delante del director de casting.
examples.trans: She froze up when pronouncing the word "emperor" in front of the casting director.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: empiezo); empezar a + infinitive.

examples.text: Empiezo el turno a las siete.
examples.trans: I start my shift at seven.

examples.text: La película empezó cinco minutos tarde.
examples.trans: The film started five minutes late.

examples.text: Llevo la empresa PS Management y somos expertos en descubrir nuevos talentos.
examples.trans: I run PS Management, and we are experts at discovering new talent.

examples.text: Hablamos de empresa en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about company, agency at the office.

meanings.note: Seen on shop doors opposite tirar (pull).

examples.text: Empuja la puerta de madera suavemente.
examples.trans: Push the wooden door gently.

examples.text: Empujamos la mesa hacia la sombra.
examples.trans: We pushed the table into the shade.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

examples.text: En verdad estoy enamorada de ti. No espero que te enamores de mí por eso, pero piénsatelo.
examples.trans: Truthfully, I'm in love with you. I don't expect you to fall in love with me because of that, just think about it.

examples.text: Hablamos de enamorado en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about in love at the office.

meanings.en: lovers, sweethearts (used as a plural noun: una pareja de enamorados)
meanings.note: Masculine plural of enamorado (past participle of enamorar, 'to cause to fall in love'). Used substantively in plural to mean a couple in love or lovers.
As an adjective with estar (están enamorados), describes people who are in love.

examples.text: "¿Cómo puede ser que un hombre tan bueno sea el mismo que ha asesinado a una pareja de enamorados?".
examples.trans: "How can it be that such a good man is the same one who murdered a pair of lovers?"

examples.text: Paseaban por el parque como dos jóvenes enamorados.
examples.trans: They strolled through the park like two young lovers.

examples.text: Paco está enamoradísimo todavía.
examples.trans: Paco is still head over heels in love.

examples.text: Están enamoradísimos los dos.
examples.trans: The two of them are madly in love.

examples.text: En verdad estoy enamorada de ti. No espero que te enamores de mí por eso, pero piénsatelo.
examples.trans: Truthfully, I'm in love with you. I don't expect you to fall in love with me because of that, just think about it.

examples.text: Hablamos de enamorar en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about fall in love at the office.

encajar.gloss: to fit snugly; to slot into place

meanings.en: to fit snugly; to slot into place
meanings.note: Built from caja (box).

examples.text: La pieza nueva encaja sin esfuerzo.
examples.trans: The new part fits effortlessly.

examples.text: Todas las pistas encajaron al final.
examples.trans: All the clues clicked together at the end.

meanings.note: Visillo de encaje = lace window curtain.

examples.text: El encaje es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The lace is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el encaje.
examples.trans: We talk about the lace.

encantada.gloss: pleased to meet you (f.); delighted, charmed

meanings.en: pleased to meet you, delighted (used by a female speaker upon introduction)
meanings.note: Feminine singular past participle of encantar ('to delight, to charm, to enchant'). Standard polite formula said by women when being introduced (short for encantada de conocerte).
Also means thrilled with something (está encantada con el papel) or, with casa encantada, 'haunted house'.

examples.text: Lidia San José, encantada. Pues me has jodido toda la prueba.
examples.trans: Lidia San José, pleased to meet you. Well, you've ruined my whole audition.

examples.text: Encantada de conocerte por fin en persona, me han hablado mucho de ti.
examples.trans: Delighted to finally meet you in person; I've heard so much about you.

related.gloss: to delight, to love, to enchant

meanings.note: Said on introduction or when gladly accepting an invitation (encantado / encantada).

examples.text: Es una pieza encantada.
examples.trans: It is a delighted piece.

examples.text: ¡Encantada! Con leche y un poco de azúcar, por favor.
examples.trans: Gladly! With milk and a little sugar, please.

meanings.note: Adjective ending in -dor creates its feminine singular by adding -a (encantadora) and plural with -es/-as.

examples.text: ¡Qué retrato tan encantador de los cinco amigos!
examples.trans: What a charming portrait of the five friends!

examples.text: La posada tiene un patio interior encantador.
examples.trans: The inn has a delightful interior courtyard.

meanings.note: Works like gustar: me encanta el té = I love tea (tea delights me).

examples.text: Me encanta el olor a pan caliente.
examples.trans: I love the smell of warm bread.

examples.text: De niño le encantaban los trenes.
examples.trans: As a boy he loved trains.

meanings.note: Feminine of el encargado.

examples.text: La encargada está aquí.
examples.trans: The manager is here.

examples.text: Vemos las encargadas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the managers from the door.

encargar.gloss: to put in charge; to take charge of (encargarse de)

meanings.en: to put in charge; to take charge of (encargarse de)
meanings.note: Spelling changes c/g -> gu before -e (encargué); encargarse de means 'to handle / take care of'.

examples.text: Clara se encarga hoy de los carteles y las mesas.
examples.trans: Clara is taking charge of the signs and tables today.

examples.text: Encargamos veinte kilos de harina fresca al molino.
examples.trans: We ordered twenty kilos of fresh flour from the mill.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: enciendo); opposite of apagar.

examples.text: Enciendo la lámpara al anochecer.
examples.trans: I switch on the lamp at dusk.

examples.text: Encendimos la caldera a las siete.
examples.trans: We lit the boiler at seven.

meanings.note: Built from enchufe (plug/socket).

examples.text: Enchufo la cafetera en la cocina.
examples.trans: I plug in the coffee maker in the kitchen.

examples.text: Enchufó la lámpara junto al sillón.
examples.trans: He plugged in the lamp beside the armchair.

examples.text: ¿Puedes mirar ese enchufe?
examples.trans: Can you check that socket?

examples.text: El enchufe está detrás de la mesa.
examples.trans: The socket is behind the desk.

meanings.note: Por encima = on top / over the surface.

examples.text: Pon azúcar glas por encima.
examples.trans: Put powdered sugar on top.

examples.text: Hay un cartel encima de la puerta.
examples.trans: There is a sign above the door.

meanings.note: Standard Peninsular Spanish word for a kitchen countertop.

examples.text: Pasa un paño húmedo por toda la encimera de piedra.
examples.trans: Wipe a damp cloth across the whole stone worktop.

examples.text: Enharinamos la encimera limpia antes de estirar la masa.
examples.trans: We flour the clean counter before rolling out the pastry.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: encuentro).

examples.text: No encuentro mis gafas de leer.
examples.trans: I cannot find my reading glasses.

examples.text: Encontramos una panadería estupenda.
examples.trans: We found a terrific bakery.

meanings.note: Gathering or encounter.

examples.text: El encuentro está aquí.
examples.trans: The meeting is here.

examples.text: Vemos los encuentros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the meetings from the door.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells z -> c: enderecé.

examples.text: Enderezo el cuadro de la pared.
examples.trans: I straighten the picture on the wall.

examples.text: El dueño se enderezó la corbata azul.
examples.trans: El dueño straightened his blue tie.

examples.text: Este montón. Muy bien, vamos a ver las energías. ¡La carta del sol, Paquita!
examples.trans: This pile. Very good, let's check the energy. The Sun card, Paquita!

examples.text: Hablamos de energía en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about energies, vibes at the office.

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for feeling angry or upset with someone.

examples.text: Es una pieza enfadada.
examples.trans: It is an angry piece.

examples.text: Suave, educada, de unos treinta y cinco años. Sonaba nervioso, no enfadado.
examples.trans: Soft, polite, around thirty-five. He sounded nervous, not angry.

examples.text: Hace un papel de enfermera.
examples.trans: She plays a nurse role.

examples.text: La enfermera trabaja de noche.
examples.trans: The nurse works at night.

meanings.note: Takes an accent in present boot forms: se enfría.

examples.text: El bizcocho se enfría en la rejilla.
examples.trans: The cake cools on the wire rack.

examples.text: Bebe el té antes de que se enfríe.
examples.trans: Drink your tea before it gets cold.

meanings.note: From gancho ('hook'); regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Engancha bien la contraventana para que no golpee.
examples.trans: Latch the shutter securely so it does not bang.

examples.text: Enganchamos los faroles en los soportes de hierro.
examples.trans: We hooked the lanterns onto the iron brackets.

meanings.en: deceitful woman, deceiver, trickster; deceptive, misleading
meanings.note: Feminine form of engañador, derived from engañar ('to deceive, to trick, to cheat on'). Used both as an adjective and a noun to reproach someone for dishonesty.

examples.text: Que si mentirosa, que si engañadora...
examples.trans: Calling me a liar, calling me a deceiver...

examples.text: Tiene fama de engañadora porque promete papeles que no existen.
examples.trans: She has a reputation as a deceiver because she promises roles that don't exist.

related.gloss: to deceive, to trick, to cheat

engañar.gloss: to deceive; to play tricks on

meanings.en: to deceive; to play tricks on
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: La luz baja a veces engaña la vista.
examples.trans: Dim light sometimes plays tricks on your eyes.

examples.text: El mapa viejo nos engañó un poco.
examples.trans: The old map misled us a bit.

examples.text: Sí, he adelgazado tres kilos porque para la película tuve que engordar diez.
examples.trans: Yes, I've lost three kilos because for the movie I had to put on ten.

examples.text: Hablamos de engordar en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about to gain weight at the office.

meanings.note: Used both for oiling hinges/locks and for buttering baking tins (engrasar el molde).

examples.text: Mateo engrasó los goznes del portón para quitar el ruido.
examples.trans: Mateo oiled the gate hinges to stop the noise.

examples.text: Antes de verter la masa, hay que engrasar bien la bandeja.
examples.trans: Before pouring the batter, you have to grease the tray well.

examples.text: Enhorabuena, estoy emocionadísimo.
examples.trans: Congratulations, I'm deeply moved.

examples.text: Yo enhorabuena
examples.trans: I enhorabuena

meanings.note: Used for music, theatre, or practising a piece from start to finish.

examples.text: Carmen ensaya el vals en la galería silenciosa.
examples.trans: Carmen rehearses the waltz in the quiet sunroom.

examples.text: Ensayamos dos veces la pieza entera antes del viernes.
examples.trans: We rehearsed the whole piece twice before Friday.

meanings.note: Written as one word in modern Spanish.

examples.text: Subo el desayuno enseguida.
examples.trans: I will bring breakfast up right away.

examples.text: Enseguida vuelvo con la llave.
examples.trans: I will be right back with the key.

meanings.note: Means both 'to show something' and 'to teach'.

examples.text: Te enseño el patio de la casa.
examples.trans: I will show you the house courtyard.

examples.text: La profesora enseñó piano durante muchos años.
examples.trans: La profesora taught piano for many years.

examples.text: ¿Me entiendes ahora?
examples.trans: Do you understand me now?

examples.text: Entiendo perfectamente el problema.
examples.trans: I understand the problem completely.

examples.text: ¿No te enteras? ¿Cómo vamos a ver ahora el videobook de la prima de tu novio?
examples.trans: Don't you get it? How are we supposed to watch your boyfriend's cousin's showreel right now?

examples.text: Hablamos de enterar en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about you get it / notice at the office.

meanings.note: Sigue entera = it is still in one piece.

examples.text: Es una pieza entera.
examples.trans: It is a whole piece.

examples.text: ¿Y su taza dentro? ¿Sigue entera?
examples.trans: And your cup inside? Is it still in one piece?

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: entierro).

examples.text: El perro entierra su hueso en el jardín.
examples.trans: The dog buries its bone in the garden.

examples.text: No entierres la esperanza tan pronto.
examples.trans: Do not bury hope so soon.

meanings.note: Desde entonces = since then.

examples.text: ¿Entonces nos vemos mañana a las ocho?
examples.trans: So shall we see each other tomorrow at eight?

examples.text: Desde entonces trabaja con nosotros.
examples.trans: Since then she works with us.

meanings.note: Doorway or entrance hall.

examples.text: La entrada está aquí.
examples.trans: The entrance is here.

examples.text: Vemos las entradas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the entrances from the door.

meanings.note: Past participle of entrar ('to enter, to go/come in'), used with haber to form compound tenses such as the present perfect (he entrado, hemos entrado), which Peninsular Spanish uses for recent past actions.
As an adjective, используется in idioms like entrado en años ('getting on in years') or entrado en carnes ('plump, heavyset').

examples.text: ¡Ya vale, hombre! ¿Por aquí hemos entrado?
examples.trans: That's enough, man! Did we come in this way?

examples.text: A ver, ¿yo qué he hecho cuando he entrado?
examples.trans: Let's see, what did I do when I walked in?

related.gloss: to enter, to come in, to fit

entrar.gloss: to come in; to go in; to enter

meanings.en: to come in; to go in; to enter
meanings.note: Pairs with en in Spain (entrar en la posada).

examples.text: Entra mucha luz por el balcón.
examples.trans: Plenty of light comes in through the balcony.

examples.text: Entramos en la tienda para resguardarnos.
examples.trans: We stepped into the shop to shelter.

meanings.note: Places something between two people or things.

examples.text: La mesita está entre las dos sillas.
examples.trans: The small table is between the two chairs.

examples.text: Entre todos arreglamos el patio.
examples.trans: Among all of us we tidied the courtyard.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells g -> gu: entregué.

examples.text: Entrego el paquete en recepción.
examples.trans: I hand the parcel over at reception.

examples.text: El cartero entregó una carta urgente.
examples.trans: The postman delivered an urgent letter.

entregarlo.gloss: to hand it in, to deliver it

meanings.en: to hand it in, to deliver it, to turn it over
meanings.note: Compound verb form consisting of the infinitive entregar ('to deliver, to hand over, to submit') plus the enclitic masculine/neuter direct object pronoun lo ('it/him'). In Spanish, object pronouns attach directly to the end of infinitives.

forms.title: Infinitive of entregar with Object Pronouns

examples.text: Hay que entregarlo esta tarde. Sí.
examples.trans: We have to hand it in this afternoon. Yes.

examples.text: Firma el contrato antes de entregarlo en la productora.
examples.trans: Sign the contract before delivering it to the production company.

related.gloss: to deliver, to hand in, to surrender

meanings.en: coaching, training (a team or athletes); practicing, working out
meanings.note: Gerund (present participle) of entrenar ('to train, to coach'), used with estar to form the progressive aspect (está entrenando). Can be transitive ('coaching a team') or intransitive/reflexive ('working out').

examples.text: Está entrenando a los niños en el fútbol.
examples.trans: He is coaching the kids in soccer.

examples.text: Ya me han dicho, ya, que estás entrenando un equipo de fútbol.
examples.trans: They have already told me, yeah, that you are coaching a soccer team.

related.gloss: to train, to coach, to practice

examples.text: Todo el año de entrevistas, alfombras rojas y los castings.
examples.trans: A whole year of interviews, red carpets, and castings.

examples.text: Hablamos de entrevista en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about interviews at the office.

envelope.gloss: envelope, paper letter cover (English audition word)

meanings.en: envelope (quoted English word from an audition script)
meanings.note: Unadapted English noun central to a classic comedic scene in Paquita Salas where an actress waiting in an English audition asks the room how to pronounce "envelope" ("¿Envelup?") in the line "It is very important to give this envelope to the emperor." In Spanish, 'envelope' is sobre.

examples.text: Eh, ¿alguien me puede decir cómo se dice "envelope"?
examples.trans: Uh, can someone tell me how you pronounce "envelope"?

examples.text: ¿"Envelup"? "Envelope". No tenía ni idea de qué significaba en el guion.
examples.trans: "Envelup"? "Envelope." She had no idea what it meant in the script.

examples.text: "Envelup".
examples.trans: "Envelup".

examples.text: Yo Envelup
examples.trans: I Envelup

meanings.note: Feminine singular past participle of enviar ('to send'). Used in passive and resultative constructions (quedar enviada, ser enviada) agreeing in gender and number with a feminine noun like la prueba ('the audition tape').

meanings.en: female envoy or special correspondent (enviada especial)
meanings.note: Used as a feminine noun in journalism and diplomacy.

forms.title: Participle and Adjective Forms of enviado

examples.text: Queda a tu cargo que esta prueba quede enviada hoy.
examples.trans: It is your responsibility to make sure this audition tape gets sent today.

examples.text: La solicitud ya fue enviada por correo electrónico a primera hora.
examples.trans: The application was already sent by email first thing in the morning.

meanings.note: Past participle of enviar ('to send'), invariable when forming compound perfect tenses with haber (ha enviado, habéis enviado) and inflected for gender/number as an adjective.
As a masculine noun, refers to an official representative or reporter sent on assignment.

forms.title: Participle and Adjective Forms of enviado

examples.text: Lo ha enviado Camilla Isola.
examples.trans: Camilla Isola sent it.

examples.text: Porque no me habéis enviado el guion ni el personaje.
examples.trans: Because you haven't sent me the script or the character breakdown.

meanings.note: Present boot forms carry an accent on í (envío, envías, envía).

examples.text: Envío una postal desde Valencia.
examples.trans: I am sending a postcard from Valencia.

examples.text: Ayer enviamos la confirmación por correo.
examples.trans: Yesterday we sent the confirmation by post.

meanings.note: Irregular past participle envuelto.

examples.text: Envuelvo el regalo en papel blanco.
examples.trans: I wrap the gift in white paper.

examples.text: Envolvió el pan en un paño limpio.
examples.trans: She wrapped the bread in a clean cloth.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from envolver.

examples.text: Es una pieza envuelta.
examples.trans: It is a wrapped piece.

examples.text: ¿Y qué es esto envuelto en papel blanco? ¡Un trenecito de madera!
examples.trans: And what is this wrapped in white paper? A little wooden train!

meanings.note: Buen equipo = good team.

examples.text: El equipo está aquí.
examples.trans: The team is here.

examples.text: Vemos los equipos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teams from the door.

meanings.note: La maleta equivocada = the wrong suitcase.

examples.text: Es una pieza equivocada.
examples.trans: It is a wrong piece.

examples.text: equivocada
examples.trans: wrong

equivocar.gloss: to get wrong; to make a mistake (equivocarse)

meanings.en: to get wrong; to make a mistake (equivocarse)
meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells c -> qu: me equivoqué.

examples.text: Perdón, me he equivocado de llave.
examples.trans: Sorry, I picked up the wrong key.

examples.text: Nos equivocamos de calle al girar.
examples.trans: We took the wrong street when turning.

meanings.note: Por error = by mistake.

examples.text: El error está aquí.
examples.trans: The mistake is here.

examples.text: Vemos los errores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the mistakes from the door.

meanings.note: Escala de fa mayor = F-major scale.

examples.text: La escala está aquí.
examples.trans: The musical scale is here.

examples.text: Vemos las escalas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the musical scales from the door.

meanings.note: Often singular (la escalera) or plural (las escaleras) for a staircase.

examples.text: La escalera está aquí.
examples.trans: The stairs is here.

examples.text: Vemos las escaleras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stairss from the door.

meanings.note: Single step of a staircase (plural: escalones).

examples.text: El escalón está aquí.
examples.trans: The step is here.

examples.text: Vemos los escalones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the steps from the door.

meanings.en: escapes, gets away, slips through one's fingers
meanings.note: Third-person singular present indicative (or second-person singular informal imperative) of escapar. Often used reflexively with an ethical/affected dative pronoun (se nos escapa = 'she gets away from us', se me escapa = 'it slips my mind / escapes me').

examples.text: Si no la agarro, se nos escapa.
examples.trans: If I don't grab hold of her, she'll get away from us.

examples.text: A Paquita no se le escapa ni un solo detalle del contrato.
examples.trans: Not a single detail of the contract slips past Paquita.

examples.text: Te doy mi tarjeta por si te escapas.
examples.trans: I'm giving you my card in case you slip away.

examples.text: Yo escapar
examples.trans: I escapar

examples.text: De un corto. Era un escaparate muy bueno.
examples.trans: For a short film. It was a really good showcase.

examples.text: Escaparate es el mandil. ¿Dónde tienes el mandil?
examples.trans: Your showcase is the apron. Where do you have your apron?

examples.text: Quería invitar al escenario a una persona muy importante.
examples.trans: I wanted to invite a very important person onto the stage.

examples.text: Yo escenario
examples.trans: I escenario

meanings.note: Esconderse detrás de = to hide behind.

examples.text: Escondo el regalo en el armario.
examples.trans: I hide the present in the wardrobe.

examples.text: El gato se escondió detrás de la maceta.
examples.trans: The cat hid behind the flowerpot.

meanings.note: From esconder, to hide.

examples.text: Hay un regalo escondido en el armario.
examples.trans: There is a present hidden in the wardrobe.

examples.text: El gato está escondido debajo de la cama.
examples.trans: The cat is hidden under the bed.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle escrito.

examples.text: Escribo la nota con lápiz azul.
examples.trans: I write the note in blue pencil.

examples.text: Mi hermano me escribió una postal corta.
examples.trans: My brother wrote me a short postcard.

meanings.note: Escrito a lápiz = written in pencil.

examples.text: Es una pieza escrita.
examples.trans: It is a written piece.

examples.text: Mira debajo de las ruedas: tu nombre y el mío siguen escritos a lápiz ahí.
examples.trans: Look underneath the wheels—your name and mine are still pencilled there.

meanings.note: Writing desk in a room or study.

examples.text: El escritorio está aquí.
examples.trans: The desk is here.

examples.text: Vemos los escritorios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the desks from the door.

meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'to' before things (escucha el agua).

examples.text: Escucho los pájaros desde mi cama.
examples.trans: I listen to the birds from my bed.

examples.text: Escuchamos la lluvia sobre las tejas.
examples.trans: We listened to the rain on the tiles.

meanings.note: Primary, music, or neighbourhood school.

examples.text: La escuela está aquí.
examples.trans: The school is here.

examples.text: Vemos las escuelas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the schools from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.text: Pásame ese cuaderno azul.
examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

meanings.note: Sin esfuerzo means 'effortlessly / without straining'.

examples.text: Con las bisagras nuevas la puerta abre sin esfuerzo.
examples.trans: With the new hinges the door opens effortlessly.

examples.text: Gracias a todos por el gran esfuerzo de esta semana.
examples.trans: Thank you everyone for this week's great effort.

examples.text: Practica esgrima los martes.
examples.trans: She practises fencing on Tuesdays.

examples.text: Es experta en esgrima.
examples.trans: She is an expert in fencing.

meanings.note: Cristal esmerilado is translucent frosted glass that softens bright light.

examples.text: La lámpara tiene una pantalla de cristal esmerilado.
examples.trans: The lamp has a frosted glass shade.

examples.text: El cristal esmerilado deja pasar una luz muy suave.
examples.trans: Frosted glass lets very soft light through.

meanings.note: Neuter pronoun; por eso = that is why.

examples.text: Por eso traje dos paraguas.
examples.trans: That is why I brought two umbrellas.

examples.text: ¿Qué significa eso exactamente?
examples.trans: What does that mean exactly?

meanings.en: those (masculine plural demonstrative determiner or pronoun)
meanings.note: Masculine plural of ese ('that'), indicating objects or people at a medium distance from the speaker or near the listener, or referring back to things just mentioned in conversation (uno de esos, 'one of those').

examples.text: Y dije: "¿Y si decimos que te han cogido para uno de esos?".
examples.trans: And I said: "What if we say you got cast in one of those?"

examples.text: Esos guiones nuevos que trajiste tienen muy buena pinta.
examples.trans: Those new scripts you brought look really promising.

meanings.note: Open room or physical space.

examples.text: El espacio está aquí.
examples.trans: The space is here.

examples.text: Vemos los espacios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the spaces from the door.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Lo vio toda España.
examples.trans: All of Spain saw it.

examples.text: Viajamos por toda España.
examples.trans: We travel all around Spain.

examples.text: Trabaja en el cine español.
examples.trans: He works in Spanish cinema.

examples.text: Es una actriz española.
examples.trans: She's a Spanish actress.

meanings.note: Same singular form for masculine and feminine; plural especiales.

examples.text: La tarta de limón es el postre especial de la casa.
examples.trans: Lemon tart is the house signature dessert.

examples.text: Viernes va a ser una noche muy especial aquí.
examples.trans: Friday is going to be a very special night here.

examples.text: ¡Estás espectacular con ese vestido!
examples.trans: You look spectacular in that dress!

examples.text: Tienen unas vistas espectaculares.
examples.trans: They have spectacular views.

meanings.note: Wall or bathroom mirror.

examples.text: El espejo está aquí.
examples.trans: The mirror is here.

examples.text: Vemos los espejos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the mirrors from the door.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.text: Espere un momento, por favor.
examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.

examples.text: Esperamos que descanse muy bien.
examples.trans: We hope you rest very well.

espeso.gloss: thick (of liquids, creams, soups, or fog)

meanings.en: thick (of liquids, creams, soups, or fog)
meanings.note: Describes dense liquids, sauces, and custards (crema espesa, chocolate espeso), whereas grueso describes solid objects.

examples.text: La crema de limón ha quedado espesa y muy brillante.
examples.trans: The lemon curd has turned out thick and very glossy.

examples.text: En los días fríos sirven un chocolate caliente muy espeso.
examples.trans: On cold days they serve a very thick hot chocolate.

meanings.note: Present boot forms carry í: espía.

examples.text: No espíes por detrás del visillo.
examples.trans: Do not peek from behind the net curtain.

examples.text: El niño espiaba la cocina con curiosidad.
examples.trans: The boy peeked curiously into the kitchen.

meanings.note: Often paired with weather or hospitality: un sol espléndido ('glorious sunshine'), una mañana espléndida.

examples.text: Esta mañana brilla un sol espléndido sobre Valencia.
examples.trans: This morning a glorious sun is shining over Valencia.

examples.text: Rocío preparó un desayuno espléndido para los huéspedes.
examples.trans: Rocío prepared a splendid breakfast for the guests.

meanings.note: Used for washing windows, dishes, and tiles.

examples.text: Escurre bien la esponja antes de limpiar el marco.
examples.trans: Squeeze the sponge out well before wiping the frame.

examples.text: Mojamos la esponja suave en agua con vinagre.
examples.trans: We dip the soft sponge in vinegar water.

examples.text: Busca una actriz espontánea.
examples.trans: He is looking for a spontaneous actress.

examples.text: Fue un gesto muy espontáneo.
examples.trans: It was a very spontaneous gesture.

meanings.en: wait, hold on a second, wait up!
meanings.note: Second-person singular informal affirmative imperative of esperar ('to wait') with the enclitic reflexive pronoun te (from pronominal esperarse). Extremely common in spoken Spanish to pause someone or change the subject mid-thought; the written accent preserves stress on the antepenultimate syllable -pé-.

examples.text: Yo me voy por aquí. No, espérate. ¿Y tú cómo estás?
examples.trans: I'm heading this way. No, wait a second. And how are you doing?

examples.text: La dirección, que te la dejas. Espérate, espérate.
examples.trans: The address—you're leaving it behind! Wait, wait up.

related.gloss: to wait, to hope, to expect

esquina.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

meanings.en: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)
meanings.note: Outer corner where two streets meet, or the crisp corner of a baking tray.

examples.text: La esquina está aquí.
examples.trans: The corner is here.

examples.text: Vemos las esquinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the corners from the door.

meanings.en: I was; he/she/it was; you (formal) were
meanings.note: First- and third-person singular imperfect indicative of the irregular verb 'estar'. Used to describe ongoing past states, locations, or temporary conditions.

examples.text: Y nosotros teníamos un chiquito que estaba en "Los Borgia".
examples.trans: And we had a young guy who was in "The Borgias".

examples.text: Me pasé a saludar porque estaba por el barrio.
examples.trans: I stopped by to say hello because I was in the neighborhood.

meanings.note: La estación de tren = the train station.

examples.text: La estación está aquí.
examples.trans: The station is here.

examples.text: Vemos las estaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stations from the door.

estancia.gloss: stay (at a hotel or inn); room

meanings.en: stay (at a hotel or inn); room
meanings.note: Polite hospitality word for a guest's stay (feliz estancia, ampliar la estancia).

examples.text: Le deseamos una estancia muy agradable en nuestra posada.
examples.trans: We wish you a very pleasant stay at our inn.

examples.text: Carmen decidió ampliar su estancia dos semanas más.
examples.trans: Carmen decided to extend her stay by two more weeks.

meanings.note: Wooden wall or cupboard shelf.

examples.text: El estante está aquí.
examples.trans: The shelf is here.

examples.text: Vemos los estantes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shelves from the door.

meanings.note: A piece of furniture with shelves for books or other items.

examples.text: Guardó el jarrón en la estantería.
examples.trans: She kept the vase on the shelf.

examples.text: Compró una nueva estantería.
examples.trans: He bought a new bookcase.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.

examples.text: ¿Dónde están las llaves de latón?
examples.trans: Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.text: Este patio es muy tranquilo.
examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.

examples.text: Esta mañana hace mucho sol.
examples.trans: This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Al estilo francés = French-style.

examples.text: El estilo está aquí.
examples.trans: The style is here.

examples.text: Vemos los estilos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the styles from the door.

meanings.note: Standard polite salutation in Spanish formal correspondence (Estimado señor / Estimada representante), more formal than querido.

examples.text: Estimada señora: le confirmamos su reserva para el viernes.
examples.trans: Dear Madam, we confirm your reservation for Friday.

examples.text: Es un vecino muy estimado por toda la gente del barrio.
examples.trans: He is a neighbour greatly esteemed by everyone in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Neuter pronoun used when not naming a gendered noun.

examples.text: He encontrado esto en el sótano.
examples.trans: I found this in the cellar.

examples.text: ¿Qué es esto encima de la mesa?
examples.trans: What is this on top of the table?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la estrategia'). Commonly used in business, PR, and talent representation contexts.

examples.text: Con Clara seguimos una estrategia un poquito arriesgada.
examples.trans: With Clara we followed a slightly risky strategy.

examples.text: Necesitamos diseñar una nueva estrategia para promocionar la película.
examples.trans: We need to design a new strategy to promote the movie.

meanings.note: Opposite of ancho (wide).

examples.text: Es una pieza estrecha.
examples.trans: It is a narrow piece.

examples.text: Coge la segunda calle, junto al puesto de flores, no el callejón estrecho.
examples.trans: Take the second street, beside the flower stall, not the narrow alley.

meanings.note: De cinco estrellas = five-star.

examples.text: La estrella está aquí.
examples.trans: The star is here.

examples.text: Vemos las estrellas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stars from the door.

meanings.note: From estrenar ('to debut / use for the first time').

examples.text: Todos los vecinos vendrán a la noche del estreno.
examples.trans: All the neighbours will come to opening night.

examples.text: Guardamos las flores frescas para la tarde del estreno.
examples.trans: We save the fresh flowers for opening afternoon.

meanings.note: Regular 4-form adjective.

examples.text: Rocío es muy estricta con los tiempos del horno.
examples.trans: Rocio is very strict about oven timings.

examples.text: Seguimos normas estrictas de limpieza en la cocina.
examples.trans: We follow strict cleanliness rules in the kitchen.

estuche.gloss: case (for an instrument, glasses, or pens)

meanings.en: case (for an instrument, glasses, or pens)
meanings.note: Used for fitted protective cases: estuche del violín, estuche de las gafas.

examples.text: Abrió con cuidado el estuche negro de su violín.
examples.trans: He carefully opened the black case of his violin.

examples.text: Siempre guardo las gafas de leer dentro de su estuche.
examples.trans: I always keep my reading glasses inside their case.

meanings.note: Past participle of the regular -ar verb 'estudiar', used with the auxiliary 'haber' to form compound tenses such as the present perfect ('he estudiado').
When used as an adjective ('estudiado/a'), describes a gesture or pose that is carefully rehearsed rather than spontaneous.

examples.text: Sí, yo he estudiado la FP. Ah, ¿sí?
examples.trans: Yes, I have studied vocational training. Oh, really?

examples.text: Ha estudiado arte dramático en una de las mejores escuelas de Madrid.
examples.trans: She has studied drama at one of the best schools in Madrid.

examples.text: Estudié mi carrera en Madrid.
examples.trans: I did my degree in Madrid.

examples.text: Ella estudia interpretación.
examples.trans: She studies acting.

meanings.note: Design or architecture studio, as well as academic study.

examples.text: Javier trabaja con su socio en un estudio de arquitectura.
examples.trans: Javier works with his partner at an architecture studio.

examples.text: Llamé al estudio para avisar del cambio de tren.
examples.trans: I called the studio to let them know about the train change.

meanings.note: Warm everyday enthusiasm in Spain.

examples.text: Es una pieza estupenda.
examples.trans: It is a great piece.

examples.text: Estupendo. ¿La ventana da a la calle o al patio?
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

meanings.note: Second-person plural ('vosotros/vosotras') present indicative of 'estar' in Peninsular Spanish. Also used with a gerund to form the present continuous ('estáis buscando').

examples.text: Tranquilas, que veo que estáis muy nerviosas.
examples.trans: Calm down, I can see that you all are very nervous.

examples.text: Mariona Terés, lo que estáis buscando.
examples.trans: Mariona Terés, just what you all are looking for.

meanings.note: Second-person singular ('tú') present subjunctive of 'estar'. Used after temporal conjunctions referring to future or indeterminate events ('siempre que lo estés viendo') and in negative commands ('no estés triste').

examples.text: Pues piensa que siempre que lo estés viendo, yo estoy ahí detrás de todo.
examples.trans: Well think that whenever you are watching it, I am right there behind everything.

examples.text: Llámame en cuanto estés lista para salir hacia el rodaje.
examples.trans: Call me as soon as you are ready to leave for the shoot.

meanings.note: Luggage tag or bottle label.

examples.text: La etiqueta está aquí.
examples.trans: The tag is here.

examples.text: Vemos las etiquetas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tags from the door.

meanings.note: Currency of Spain.

examples.text: Un café con leche y dos churros calientes cuestan apenas tres euros.
examples.trans: A coffee with milk and two hot churros cost barely three euros.

examples.text: El billete de autobús hasta el centro histórico cuesta solo dos euros.
examples.trans: The bus ticket to the historic center costs only two euros.

examples.text: Nos gusta la gente con personalidad, y para eso, Europa.
examples.trans: We like people with personality, and for that, Europe.

examples.text: Yo Europa
examples.trans: I Europa

meanings.note: Feminine plural form of the relational adjective 'europeo'. Note that nationality and geographic adjectives are not capitalized in Spanish.

examples.text: Buscamos actores bilingües para producciones europeas.
examples.trans: We are looking for bilingual actors for European productions.

examples.text: Varias capitales europeas acogen festivales de cine muy prestigiosos.
examples.trans: Several European capitals host very prestigious film festivals.

meanings.note: Masculine singular form of the adjective 'europeo', or a masculine noun referring to a person from Europe. Uncapitalized in Spanish.

examples.text: Se trata de una cosita de época que se va a hacer a nivel europeo.
examples.trans: It's about a little period piece that is going to be done at a European level.

examples.text: Nos gusta mucho el sistema europeo de ayudas al cine.
examples.trans: We really like the European system of film grants.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('el evento'). In Spanish entertainment and PR, frequently refers to a sponsored brand event or photocall where actors are paid to appear.

examples.text: En un evento de un champú... Cosas así, cosas simples.
examples.trans: At a shampoo event... Things like that, simple things.

examples.text: Te han invitado al evento de presentación de la nueva temporada.
examples.trans: They have invited you to the launch event for the new season.

meanings.note: Invariable in the plural: el/la ex, los/las ex.

examples.text: Paco es mi ex.
examples.trans: Paco is my ex.

examples.text: Una foto para tu ex.
examples.trans: A photo for your ex.

meanings.note: Formed from exacta + -mente.

examples.text: Sabe exactamente igual que antes.
examples.trans: It tastes exactly the same as before.

examples.text: Son las doce exactamente.
examples.trans: It is twelve o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Used alone as an enthusiastic 'Exactly!'.

examples.text: Es una pieza exacta.
examples.trans: It is an exact piece.

examples.text: ¡Exacto! Ya eres una más del equipo.
examples.trans: Exactly! You are already one of the team.

examples.text: Es un libro muy excitante.
examples.trans: It is a very exciting book.

examples.text: Qué viaje tan excitante.
examples.trans: What an exciting trip.

examples.text: Eso es falta de exfoliación.
examples.trans: That is a lack of exfoliation.

examples.text: La exfoliación cuida la piel.
examples.trans: Exfoliation takes care of the skin.

examples.text: ¿No existe Rusia?
examples.trans: Doesn't Russia exist?

examples.text: Ese problema no existe.
examples.trans: That problem doesn't exist.

examples.text: Son experiencias de la vida y hay que dejarlas marchar.
examples.trans: They are life experiences, and you have to let them move on.

examples.text: Hablamos de experiencia en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about experiences at the office.

meanings.note: Also used as a noun (un experto / una experta).

examples.text: Mateo es experto en arreglar tuberías.
examples.trans: Mateo is an expert at fixing pipes.

examples.text: Necesitamos una opinión experta.
examples.trans: We need an expert opinion.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells c -> qu: expliqué.

examples.text: Te explico el camino en un minuto.
examples.trans: I will explain the way to you in a minute.

examples.text: El arquitecto explicó toda la historia en el patio.
examples.trans: El arquitecto explained the whole story in the courtyard.

examples.text: ¿Sabes qué debes enseñarme? El vestido de los Goya, que me explotaba.
examples.trans: Do you know what you need to show me? My Goya dress, because it was bursting on me.

examples.text: Hablamos de explotar en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about was bursting (tight) at the office.

meanings.note: Recién exprimido = freshly squeezed.

examples.text: Es una pieza exprimida.
examples.trans: It is a squeezed piece.

examples.text: ¡Permítame servirle el zumo de naranja recién exprimido, señora!
examples.trans: Allow me to pour you the freshly squeezed orange juice, madam!

meanings.note: Invariable in everyday commercial names and phrases (envío exprés, café exprés).

examples.text: Pedimos un envío exprés para recibir las cajas hoy.
examples.trans: We ordered express delivery to receive the boxes today.

examples.text: Tomo un café exprés antes de abrir la recepción.
examples.trans: I drink an espresso before opening the front desk.

meanings.note: Invariable in singular (esquinas extra).

examples.text: Es una pieza extra.
examples.trans: It is an extra piece.

examples.text: Recién salido del horno: ¡bizcocho de limón de los viernes con esquinas extra!
examples.trans: Fresh from the oven: Friday lemon cake with extra corner pieces!

meanings.note: With the definite article ('el extranjero'), refers collectively to foreign countries ('abroad'). In Paquita Salas, Paquita humorously says 'el mundo del extranjero' ('the foreign world').
As an adjective ('extranjero/a'), modifies nouns to mean from another country.

examples.text: En PS tenemos muchos contactos con el mundo del extranjero.
examples.trans: At PS we have many contacts with the foreign world.

examples.text: Se fue a estudiar inglés al extranjero durante todo el verano.
examples.trans: She went to study English abroad for the whole summer.

meanings.note: ¡Qué extraño! = How strange!

examples.text: Es una pieza extraña.
examples.trans: It is a strange piece.

examples.text: ¡Qué extraño! Viajamos en el mismo tren de la mañana al mismo barrio.
examples.trans: How strange! We rode the same morning train to the same neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Fourth note of the solfege scale (fa mayor = F major).

examples.text: El fa es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The F is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el fa.
examples.trans: We talk about the F.

examples.text: Tengo facilidad para los idiomas.
examples.trans: I have a knack for languages.

examples.text: Habla en público con facilidad.
examples.trans: She speaks in public with ease.

meanings.note: Fallar una nota = to miss a musical note.

examples.text: Casi nunca falla esa cerradura.
examples.trans: That lock almost never fails.

examples.text: Falló una sola nota en toda la pieza.
examples.trans: He missed only a single note in the whole piece.

meanings.note: ¿Qué falta? = What is missing?

examples.text: La falta está aquí.
examples.trans: The lack is here.

examples.text: Vemos las faltas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lacks from the door.

faltar.gloss: to be missing; to remain until (time)

meanings.en: to be missing; to remain until (time)
meanings.note: Faltan cinco para las doce = it is five to twelve.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para el mediodía.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to noon.

examples.text: En esta mesa falta una cucharilla.
examples.trans: A teaspoon is missing at this table.

examples.text: Mis cinco minutos de fama.
examples.trans: My five minutes of fame.

examples.text: La fama cambia rápido.
examples.trans: Fame changes fast.

meanings.note: Takes singular verb agreement in Spanish (la familia vive aquí).

examples.text: La familia está aquí.
examples.trans: The family is here.

examples.text: Vemos las familias desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the families from the door.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza familiar.
examples.trans: It is a family piece.

examples.text: ¡Qué curioso! La letra de esa etiqueta me resultaba muy familiar.
examples.trans: How curious! The handwriting on that tag felt very familiar to me.

meanings.note: Common-gender noun ('el/la fan') borrowed from English. Its standard plural in Spanish is 'los/las fans' (or colloquially 'fanes').

examples.text: ¿Te acuerdas de esa que era tu fan número uno, la Macarena?
examples.trans: Do you remember that girl who was your number one fan, Macarena?

examples.text: Soy muy fan de todas las películas que hizo en los años noventa.
examples.trans: I am a huge fan of all the movies she made in the nineties.

examples.text: Habéis estado fantásticos.
examples.trans: You've been fantastic.

examples.text: Yo fantástico
examples.trans: I fantástico

meanings.note: Marked in Spain by a lit green cross.

examples.text: La farmacia está aquí.
examples.trans: The pharmacy is here.

examples.text: Vemos las farmacias desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pharmacys from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine form: la farmacéutica; works at la farmacia ('pharmacy').

examples.text: El farmacéutico de la esquina nos recomendó poner hielo.
examples.trans: The corner pharmacist recommended putting ice on it.

examples.text: La farmacéutica abre su tienda a las nueve en punto.
examples.trans: The pharmacist opens her shop at nine o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Plural faroles; classic wrought-iron courtyard lantern.

examples.text: Encendemos los faroles del patio al caer la tarde.
examples.trans: We light the courtyard lanterns at dusk.

examples.text: El farol de hierro alumbra toda la escalera.
examples.trans: The iron lantern lights up the whole staircase.

meanings.note: Festive hanging lantern strung across Spanish courtyards.

examples.text: El farolillo está aquí.
examples.trans: The paper lantern is here.

examples.text: Vemos los farolillos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the paper lanterns from the door.

meanings.note: Colloquial favourite in Spain: va fatal = it is running terribly.

examples.text: Es una pieza fatal.
examples.trans: It is a terrible piece.

examples.text: Un momento: ¡con mermelada va fatal, pero en los huevos revueltos queda riquísima!
examples.trans: Hold on: with jam it is terrible, yet in scrambled eggs it tastes delicious!

meanings.note: Por favor literally means 'as a favour'.

examples.text: El favor está aquí.
examples.trans: The favour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los favores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the favours from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with its noun.

examples.text: Es una pieza favorita.
examples.trans: It is a favourite piece.

examples.text: ¡Solo vestidos, partituras y mi taza favorita!
examples.trans: Only dresses, sheet music, and my favourite cup!

examples.text: Mariona tiene mucha fe.
examples.trans: Mariona has plenty of faith.

examples.text: Tengo fe en este proyecto.
examples.trans: I have faith in this project.

meanings.note: Calendar day, month, and year; distinct from cita ('appointment').

examples.text: Escribe la fecha de hoy arriba a la derecha.
examples.trans: Write today's date at the top right.

examples.text: La postal lleva una fecha de mayo muy clara.
examples.trans: The postcard bears a very clear May date.

examples.text: La carta del sol. Esto te va a dar felicidad con gente maravillosa.
examples.trans: The Sun card. This is going to bring you happiness with wonderful people.

examples.text: Hablamos de felicidad en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about happiness at the office.

meanings.note: Felicitar al cocinero = compliment the chef.

examples.text: Felicito a La panadera por sus bollos.
examples.trans: I compliment The baker on her sweet rolls.

examples.text: Todos felicitaron al equipo el viernes.
examples.trans: Everyone congratulated the team on Friday.

meanings.note: Invariable for gender ('un hombre feliz', 'una mujer feliz'). Forms its plural by changing -z to -ces ('felices').

examples.text: Es que trabajar en el teatro me hace muy feliz.
examples.trans: It is just that working in the theater makes me very happy.

examples.text: Estamos todos muy felices por el éxito de tu nueva serie.
examples.trans: We are all very happy about the success of your new series.

meanings.note: Invariable for gender ('fenomenal' in singular, 'fenomenales' in plural). Very common in Peninsular Spanish both as an adjective and adverbially ('todo me va fenomenal', 'me parece fenomenal').

examples.text: Ah, bueno. Todo fenomenal.
examples.trans: Oh, well. Everything is great.

examples.text: Paco en su casa, yo en la mía, fenomenal, mejor que él.
examples.trans: Paco in his house, me in mine, doing great, better than him.

examples.text: Uy, mira, Fernando Canelón.
examples.trans: Oh, look, Fernando Canelón.

examples.text: Yo Fernando
examples.trans: I Fernando

meanings.note: Built from hierro/ferro (iron).

examples.text: La ferretería está aquí.
examples.trans: The hardware shop is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ferreterías desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hardware shops from the door.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza fiable.
examples.trans: It is a reliable piece.

examples.text: ¡Caliente! ¿Oye eso, Clara? ¡Agua caliente moderna, fiable y de cinco estrellas!
examples.trans: Hot! Do you hear that, Clara? Modern, reliable, five-star hot water!

examples.text: Te voy a dar un consejo. Nunca te fíes de nadie.
examples.trans: I'm going to give you a piece of advice. Never trust anyone.

examples.text: Hablamos de fiar en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about trust (fiarse de) at the office.

examples.text: Tenemos que rellenar una fichita.
examples.trans: We need to fill in a little profile form.

examples.text: Guardo tus datos en esta fichita.
examples.trans: I keep your details on this card.

meanings.note: Dense wool fabric used on piano hammers and under chair legs.

examples.text: El fieltro blanco suaviza el golpe sobre la cuerda.
examples.trans: The white felt softens the strike on the string.

examples.text: Pegamos discos de fieltro debajo de las doce sillas.
examples.trans: We glued felt pads underneath all twelve chairs.

examples.text: Gracias a mi madre y a todas mis compañeras, que sois todas unas fieras.
examples.trans: Thank you to my mother and to all my fellow actresses—you are all fierce.

examples.text: Hablamos de fiera en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about powerhouses, fierce talents at the office.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la fiesta'). The idiomatic phrase 'estar/ir de fiesta' means to be out partying.

examples.text: Aquí, de fiesta, cuéntame.
examples.trans: Right here, out partying, tell me what's up.

examples.text: Después del estreno organizaron una fiesta privada para todo el equipo.
examples.trans: After the premiere they threw a private party for the whole crew.

examples.text: A ver, Paquita, las cartas. Fíjate, la carta de la torre.
examples.trans: Let me see the cards, Paquita. Look, the Tower card.

examples.text: Hablamos de fijar en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about look at the office.

meanings.note: Encargada fija = permanent manager.

examples.text: Es una pieza fija.
examples.trans: It is a permanent piece.

examples.text: Nadie mira fijo a los clientes. Entregamos la maleta y a lo nuestro.
examples.trans: Nobody stares at guests. We hand over the suitcase and mind our own business.

meanings.note: Primera fila = front row.

examples.text: La fila está aquí.
examples.trans: The row is here.

examples.text: Vemos las filas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rows from the door.

meanings.note: Por fin = finally.

examples.text: El fin está aquí.
examples.trans: The end is here.

examples.text: Vemos los fines desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ends from the door.

meanings.en: Fina (Spanish feminine given name, short for Josefina)
meanings.note: Used in Paquita Salas as the name of Fina, a character addressed in the salon scenes. As a common adjective ('fino/fina'), it also means 'fine', 'thin', or 'refined'.

examples.text: -Voy. Voy, voy, Fina.
examples.trans: -I'm coming. Coming, coming, Fina.

examples.text: Fina siempre tiene la tele puesta en la peluquería.
examples.trans: Fina always has the TV on at the hair salon.

meanings.note: As a masculine noun (el final), means the ending of a song, book, or day.

examples.text: El final del vals baja el ritmo poco a poco.
examples.trans: The ending of the waltz slows the tempo little by little.

examples.text: Al final de la tarde probamos las dos sopas.
examples.trans: At the end of the afternoon we tasted both soups.

meanings.note: Describes thin glass/fabric as well as fine quality.

examples.text: El cristal de estos vasos es demasiado fino para el té.
examples.trans: The glass of these cups is too thin for tea.

examples.text: Corta el limón en rodajas muy finas.
examples.trans: Cut the lemon into very thin slices.

meanings.note: Written signature on a receipt or delivery slip.

examples.text: La firma está aquí.
examples.trans: The signature is here.

examples.text: Vemos las firmas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the signatures from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Firmo el recibo en la esquina.
examples.trans: I sign the receipt in the corner.

examples.text: Firmaron el nuevo contrato esta mañana.
examples.trans: They signed the new contract this morning.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza firme.
examples.trans: It is a firm piece.

examples.text: Ahí suena la campana de la entrada. Un toque firme.
examples.trans: There goes the gate bell. One firm ring.

examples.text: El problema es la flacidez.
examples.trans: The problem is saggy skin.

examples.text: Esta crema combate la flacidez.
examples.trans: This cream fights sagginess.

meanings.note: Me flaquean las rodillas = my knees feel weak.

examples.text: Con el susto me flaquean las piernas.
examples.trans: From the fright my legs feel weak.

examples.text: Su ánimo nunca flaqueó aquel invierno.
examples.trans: Her spirits never faltered that winter.

meanings.note: An arrow on a sign or plan, or the arrow of a bow.

examples.text: Sigue la flecha verde.
examples.trans: Follow the green arrow.

examples.text: La flecha señala la salida.
examples.trans: The arrow points to the exit.

meanings.en: freaking out, tripping, being blown away
meanings.note: Gerund of the colloquial Peninsular Spanish verb 'flipar'. Commonly used in the progressive 'estar flipando' to express shock, disbelief, or amazement.

examples.text: Estoy flipando con todo lo que me acabas de contar.
examples.trans: I am freaking out over everything you just told me.

examples.text: Me quedé flipando cuando vi que le dieron el papel protagonista.
examples.trans: I was blown away when I saw they gave her the lead role.

related.gloss: to freak out, to be amazed

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la flor, las flores.

examples.text: La flor está aquí.
examples.trans: The flower is here.

examples.text: Vemos las flores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the flowers from the door.

flotar.gloss: to float; to drift in the air

meanings.en: to float; to drift in the air
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb used for floating on water or for music and scents drifting through the air.

examples.text: Las hojas amarillas de otoño flotan sobre el agua de la fuente.
examples.trans: The yellow autumn leaves float on the fountain water.

examples.text: Las notas del piano flotaban suaves por todo el patio.
examples.trans: The piano notes drifted softly across the whole courtyard.

meanings.note: Like construir, inserts -y- before a/e/o (fluyo, fluye, fluyó).

examples.text: La melodía del vals fluye con mucha naturalidad.
examples.trans: The waltz melody flows very naturally.

examples.text: Con las ventanas abiertas el aire fresco fluye por el pasillo.
examples.trans: With the windows open, fresh air flows down the hallway.

meanings.note: Drops the written accent in the plural: los fogones ('the kitchen stoves').

examples.text: La sopa de lentejas hierve suave en el fogón.
examples.trans: The lentil soup simmers gently on the burner.

examples.text: Apaga todos los fogones antes de cerrar la cocina.
examples.trans: Turn off all the burners before closing the kitchen.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('el fondo'). Used in photography/video for a backdrop ('un fondo blanco'), in audio/staging for 'in the background' ('de fondo'), and figuratively in 'en el fondo' ('deep down').

examples.text: Yo pondría un fondo blanco ahí. Tengo esta pared libre.
examples.trans: I would put a white backdrop there. I have this wall free.

examples.text: En el fondo es una buena persona, aunque tenga mucho carácter.
examples.trans: Deep down she is a good person, even if she has a strong temper.

examples.text: Una actriz se forma encima de las tablas.
examples.trans: An actress trains on the stage.

examples.text: Yo forma
examples.trans: I forma

meanings.note: Plural formales.

examples.text: Es una pieza formal.
examples.trans: It is a formal piece.

examples.text: ¡Cuando me pongo nervioso, mis frases se vuelven larguísimas y formales!
examples.trans: When I get nervous, my sentences grow very long and formal!

meanings.note: Costar una fortuna means 'to cost a fortune'; por fortuna means 'fortunately'.

examples.text: Las piedras antiguas del patio cuestan una fortuna.
examples.trans: The old courtyard flagstones cost a fortune.

examples.text: Por fortuna, no entró ni una gota de agua en la caja.
examples.trans: Fortunately, not a single drop of water got into the box.

meanings.note: Stem-changing o → ue verb when stressed (fuerzo, no fuerces), with a z → c spelling change before -e (forcé, fuerces).

examples.text: Nunca fuerces una tapa de lata antigua con un cuchillo.
examples.trans: Never force an old tin lid with a knife.

examples.text: No quiero forzar la cerradura de la puerta.
examples.trans: I do not want to force the door lock.

meanings.note: Short for la fotografía, so it is feminine even though it ends in -o.

examples.text: ¿Nos haces una foto, por favor?
examples.trans: Will you take a photo of us, please?

examples.text: Tengo una foto de mis padres en la cartera.
examples.trans: I have a photo of my parents in my wallet.

meanings.note: Plural of the feminine noun 'la foto' (clipped from 'la fotografía'). Despite ending in -o, it retains feminine gender ('las fotos', 'unas fotos').

examples.text: Cogimos y pusimos su cara en unas fotos de otra actriz.
examples.trans: We went and put her face onto some photos of another actress.

examples.text: Hace falta tener dos cosas: fe y fotos.
examples.trans: You need to have two things: faith and photos.

meanings.note: Initialism for 'Formación Profesional', Spain's official system of technical and vocational education. Treated as a feminine noun ('la FP') matching the head noun 'formación'.

examples.text: Sí, yo he estudiado la FP. Ah, ¿sí?
examples.trans: Yes, I have studied vocational training. Oh, really?

examples.text: Hizo un grado superior de FP en realización audiovisual.
examples.trans: She completed a higher vocational training degree in audiovisual production.

meanings.note: Forms: francés, francesa, franceses, francesas.

examples.text: Es una pieza francesa.
examples.trans: It is a French piece.

examples.text: al estilo francés
examples.trans: French-style

meanings.note: Feminine noun: una frase corta.

examples.text: La frase está aquí.
examples.trans: The sentence is here.

examples.text: Vemos las frases desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sentences from the door.

meanings.note: Means both braking a vehicle and stopping noise.

examples.text: El taxi frena suave junto a la acera.
examples.trans: The taxi brakes gently at the curb.

examples.text: Los muros gruesos frenan el ruido.
examples.trans: Thick walls block out the noise.

frente.gloss: forehead; front (frente a = in front of)

meanings.en: forehead; front (frente a = in front of)
meanings.note: La frente (f) = forehead; frente a frente = face to face.

examples.text: La frente está aquí.
examples.trans: The forehead is here.

examples.text: Vemos las frentes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the foreheads from the door.

meanings.note: Mermelada de fresa = strawberry jam.

examples.text: La fresa está aquí.
examples.trans: The strawberry is here.

examples.text: Vemos las fresas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the strawberries from the door.

meanings.note: Pintura fresca = wet paint; agua fresca = cool water.

examples.text: Es una pieza fresca.
examples.trans: It is a cool piece.

examples.text: Bien. Pon estas hierbas frescas por encima antes de servirlos.
examples.trans: Good. Put these fresh herbs on top before serving them.

meanings.note: Same singular form for masculine and feminine; plural frontales.

examples.text: Mateo limpia con cuidado la madera frontal del piano.
examples.trans: Mateo carefully cleans the front wood of the piano.

examples.text: Las ventanas frontales dan directamente a la calle.
examples.trans: The front windows look straight onto the street.

fruncir.gloss: to wrinkle; to furrow (fruncir el ceño = to frown)

meanings.en: to wrinkle; to furrow (fruncir el ceño = to frown)
meanings.note: Spelling changes c -> z before o (frunzo).

examples.text: Siempre frunces el ceño cuando lees.
examples.trans: You always wrinkle your brow when reading.

examples.text: Frunció el ceño al mirar la cuenta.
examples.trans: He frowned when looking at the bill.

meanings.note: While la fruta is everyday table fruit, masculine el fruto appears in culinary groupings like frutos rojos ('red summer berries') and frutos secos ('nuts and dried fruit').

examples.text: Horneamos un bizcocho de almendra y frutos rojos.
examples.trans: We baked an almond and summer berry sponge cake.

examples.text: El limonero da sus mejores frutos en primavera.
examples.trans: The lemon tree bears its finest fruit in spring.

meanings.note: As a masculine noun (el frío), means 'the cold'.

examples.text: Es una pieza fría.
examples.trans: It is a cold piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

fuego.gloss: fire; stove heat (a fuego suave = over gentle heat)

meanings.en: fire; stove heat (a fuego suave = over gentle heat)
meanings.note: In the kitchen, el fuego means the burner/heat and a fuego lento / suave means 'on low / gentle heat'.

examples.text: Cuece la crema a fuego suave para que no se pegue.
examples.trans: Cook the custard over gentle heat so it does not stick.

examples.text: Retira el cazo del fuego antes de mezclar la mantequilla.
examples.trans: Take the saucepan off the heat before mixing in the butter.

meanings.note: Means a stone water fountain in a square (una fuente de piedra), a large serving dish, or a source of information.

examples.text: La primera tarjeta muestra una fuente antigua de piedra.
examples.trans: The first card shows an old stone fountain.

examples.text: Nos sentamos a escuchar el agua junto a la fuente.
examples.trans: We sat listening to the water beside the fountain.

meanings.note: Diminutive of la fuente (fountain).

examples.text: La fuentecita está aquí.
examples.trans: The little fountain is here.

examples.text: Vemos las fuentecitas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the little fountains from the door.

meanings.note: Por fuera = on the outside.

examples.text: Hace frío fuera esta mañana.
examples.trans: It is cold outside this morning.

examples.text: La maleta es azul por fuera.
examples.trans: The suitcase is blue on the outside.

meanings.note: Also used adverbially (llover/discutir fuerte).

examples.text: Es una pieza fuerte.
examples.trans: It is a strong piece.

examples.text: ¡Rápido, ciérralo! Vamos a subirlo... esperad, ¿qué es ese golpe metálico tan fuerte?
examples.trans: Quick, close it! Let us take it upstairs... wait, what is that loud metallic bang?

meanings.note: Con fuerza = strongly / rushing hard.

examples.text: La fuerza es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The force is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la fuerza.
examples.trans: We talk about the force.

meanings.note: Feminine form of 'fugitivo' (noun and adjective). In the construction 'de fugitiva', it means 'as a fugitive' or 'in hiding'.

examples.text: La chica se agobió un poquillo y yo me la traje aquí de fugitiva.
examples.trans: The girl got a little overwhelmed and I brought her here as a runaway.

examples.text: En la película interpreta a una fugitiva que busca limpiar su nombre.
examples.trans: In the movie she plays a fugitive looking to clear her name.

meanings.note: Third-person singular present indicative (and second-person singular imperative) of 'funcionar'. Used for machines, systems, or figuratively for an actor's performance on screen.

examples.text: A ver, de verdad, niño, mira, ¿tú sabes cómo funciona esto?
examples.trans: Let's see, honestly, kid, look, do you know how this works?

examples.text: Funciona como un reloj. Es muy orgánica, muy natural.
examples.trans: She runs like clockwork. She's very organic, very natural.

meanings.note: Used for lamps, boilers, phones, and keys (never trabajar).

examples.text: La calefacción funciona de maravilla.
examples.trans: The heating works wonderfully.

examples.text: Ayer no funcionaba el timbre viejo.
examples.trans: Yesterday the old buzzer was not working.

fundir.gloss: to melt; to blow (a fuse or bulb)

meanings.en: to melt; to blow (a fuse or bulb)
meanings.note: Se ha fundido la bombilla = the bulb has blown.

examples.text: Se ha fundido la bombilla de la cocina.
examples.trans: The kitchen bulb has blown.

examples.text: El sol funde la nieve.
examples.trans: The sun melts the snow.

meanings.note: Small commercial van.

examples.text: La furgoneta está aquí.
examples.trans: The delivery van is here.

examples.text: Vemos las furgonetas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the delivery vans from the door.

meanings.note: The small safety part in an electrical panel.

examples.text: El fusible está en la caja de la entrada.
examples.trans: The fuse is in the box by the entrance.

examples.text: Necesito un fusible nuevo.
examples.trans: I need a new fuse.

examples.text: Mi amor, no pasa nada, tienes aquí un futuro muy bonito. Te lo prometo.
examples.trans: My love, it's alright, you have a lovely future right here. I promise you.

examples.text: Pues vamos a ver ese futuro. ¿Qué pasa con el trabajo?
examples.trans: Well let's see that future. What about work?

examples.text: Por el futuro.
examples.trans: To the future.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine; plural fáciles.

examples.text: La receta de la tarta de limón es muy fácil.
examples.trans: The lemon tart recipe is very easy.

examples.text: Esta cerradura nueva se abre muy fácil.
examples.trans: This new lock opens very easily.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for the science of physics; as an adjective (físico/física), it means 'physical'.

examples.text: Cortar verduras del mismo tamaño para que se hagan a la vez es física básica.
examples.trans: Cutting vegetables the same size so they cook at once is basic physics.

examples.text: Su hermano estudió física y diseño acústico en la universidad.
examples.trans: His brother studied physics and acoustic design at university.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('el fútbol') adapted from English 'football'. In Spain, pronounced with penultimate stress ('fútbol'), though 'futbol' without an accent also exists in parts of the Spanish-speaking world.

examples.text: Está entrenando a los niños en el fútbol.
examples.trans: He is coaching the kids in soccer.

examples.text: Ya me han dicho, ya, que estás entrenando un equipo de fútbol.
examples.trans: They have already told me, yeah, that you are coaching a soccer team.

examples.text: ¿La habrá adaptado una chiquita que se llama Hedda Gabler?
examples.trans: Could a young girl called Hedda Gabler have adapted it?

examples.text: Yo Gabler
examples.trans: I Gabler

meanings.note: Plural-only feminine noun in Spain: las gafas.

examples.text: ¿Dónde he dejado mis gafas?
examples.trans: Where did I leave my glasses?

examples.text: Lleva unas gafas redondas.
examples.trans: He wears round glasses.

meanings.en: gala, awards ceremony, special television broadcast
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la gala'). In Spain, refers both to red-carpet awards ceremonies (such as the Goyas or Oscars) and to live prime-time variety or talent show broadcasts.

examples.text: La pusimos como si estuviera en una gala de los Óscar o en un rodaje.
examples.trans: We edited her in as if she were at an Oscars gala or on a film shoot.

examples.text: Se compró un vestido espectacular para la gala de los premios Goya.
examples.trans: She bought a spectacular dress for the Goya Awards gala.

meanings.note: In a Spanish house, a long room or balcony closed in with windows; also an art gallery.

examples.text: Desayunamos en la galería por la mañana.
examples.trans: We have breakfast in the sunroom in the morning.

examples.text: La galería de arte abre a las diez.
examples.trans: The art gallery opens at ten.

meanings.note: Everyday word for sweet tea biscuits.

examples.text: Traje un plato de galletas caseras para la merienda.
examples.trans: I brought a plate of homemade biscuits for afternoon tea.

examples.text: Estas galletas de almendra acompañan muy bien el té.
examples.trans: These almond biscuits go very well with tea.

meanings.note: Used almost always in the plural ganas for keenness or enthusiasm.

examples.text: Tiene muchas ganas de trabajar.
examples.trans: She has lots of enthusiasm to work.

examples.text: Tengo ganas de ver la película.
examples.trans: I'm keen to see the film.

examples.text: Y la ganadora al Goya a la Mejor Actriz Revelación es Mariona Terés.
examples.trans: And the winner of the Goya for Best New Actress is Mariona Terés.

examples.text: Hablamos de ganadora en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about winner (female) at the office.

ganar.gloss: to win; to beat (ganar a); to earn

meanings.en: to win; to beat (ganar a); to earn
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Esta vista gana a cualquier postal.
examples.trans: This view beats any postcard.

examples.text: Con paciencia siempre ganamos tiempo.
examples.trans: With patience we always save time.

meanings.note: Metal hook for shutters, coats, or lanterns.

examples.text: Suelta el gancho de hierro para abrir la ventana.
examples.trans: Unhook the iron hook to open the window.

examples.text: Colgamos el farol grande en el gancho de la pared.
examples.trans: We hung the big lantern on the wall hook.

meanings.note: Source-attested name or surname. Name history is supplied separately with its own evidence and uncertainty; no unverified full name is inferred.

examples.text: Macarena García es actriz.
examples.trans: Macarena García is an actress.

examples.text: La agencia representa a Macarena García.
examples.trans: The agency represents Macarena García.

gas.gloss: gas; fizz (agua con gas = sparkling water)

meanings.en: gas; fizz (agua con gas = sparkling water)
meanings.note: Agua con gas = sparkling water; agua sin gas = still water.

examples.text: El gas es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The gas is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el gas.
examples.trans: We talk about the gas.

examples.text: Estamos en la gasolinera.
examples.trans: We're at the petrol station.

examples.text: Paramos en una gasolinera.
examples.trans: We stopped at a petrol station.

meanings.note: Used as both an adjective and a noun in Spanish. Its standard plural prescribed by the RAE is 'gais'.

examples.text: -Anda, qué tonterías. -Yo soy gay.
examples.trans: -Oh, come on, what nonsense. -I am gay.

examples.text: Pero ¿qué vas a ser gay? Están todas las niñas del colegio locas por ti.
examples.trans: But how could you be gay? All the girls at school are crazy about you.

meanings.note: La maleta gemela = the twin suitcase.

examples.text: Es una pieza gemela.
examples.trans: It is a twin piece.

examples.text: Oh, ¿esa es la maleta gemela del tren del lunes?
examples.trans: Oh, is that the twin suitcase from Monday's train?

examples.text: Es un móvil de última generación.
examples.trans: It is a next-generation phone.

examples.text: Somos de la misma generación.
examples.trans: We are from the same generation.

meanings.note: La llave general = the main shut-off tap.

examples.text: Es una pieza general.
examples.trans: It is a main piece.

examples.text: ¡Listo! ¿Ya has cerrado la llave general del agua?
