examples.trans: Got it! Did you turn off the main water tap already?

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: El nuevo café genera mucha ilusión en el barrio.
examples.trans: The new café creates great excitement in the neighbourhood.

examples.text: Las placas solares generan energía limpia.
examples.trans: Solar panels generate clean energy.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number.

examples.text: Es una pieza generosa.
examples.trans: It is a generous piece.

examples.text: ¡Qué generoso! ¿Habéis oído el timbre de la puerta del patio abajo?
examples.trans: How generous! Did you two hear the courtyard gate bell downstairs?

meanings.note: Everyday Peninsula exclamation of approval.

examples.text: Es una pieza genial.
examples.trans: It is a great piece.

examples.text: Genial. Dime todo lo que necesito saber.
examples.trans: Great. Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Grammatically singular feminine noun in Spanish: la gente es amable.

examples.text: La gente es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The people is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la gente.
examples.trans: We talk about the people.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Tenía la agencia en Getafe.
examples.trans: She had the agency in Getafe.

examples.text: Getafe está cerca de Madrid.
examples.trans: Getafe is near Madrid.

meanings.note: Anglicism fully naturalized in Peninsular Spanish (often spelled gintonic); Paquita's signature drink order alongside torreznos.

examples.text: Pues ponme un gin-tonic y unos torreznos.
examples.trans: Well, get me a gin and tonic and some crispy pork belly strips.

examples.text: Después del estreno nos tomamos un gin-tonic en el bar de la esquina.
examples.trans: After the premiere we had a gin and tonic at the corner bar.

examples.text: Hola, buenas, ¿qué tal? Mira, me pones unos torreznos y una ginebra.
examples.trans: Hello there, how are you? Look, could you get me some crispy pork belly and a gin?

examples.text: ¿Y de qué ginebra lo quieres?
examples.trans: And what kind of gin would you like?

meanings.note: Gira a la izquierda = turn left.

examples.text: Gira a la izquierda después del puente.
examples.trans: Turn left after the bridge.

examples.text: Giró la llave dos veces con cuidado.
examples.trans: She turned the key twice carefully.

examples.text: A ver un giro.
examples.trans: Let's see a twirl.

examples.text: Haz un giro despacio.
examples.trans: Do a slow twirl.

meanings.note: Quoted English verb appearing in a comedic *Paquita Salas* audition scene where characters struggle through an English script ("'give' this envelope..."), omitting 'to' and reading with heavy Spanish phonetics.

examples.text: En la prueba en inglés repetía: «But it's very important 'give' this envelope».
examples.trans: In the English audition she kept repeating: "But it's very important to give this envelope."

examples.text: Paquita intenta leer el guion en inglés y pronuncia «give» tal como suena en español.
examples.trans: Paquita tries to read the script in English and pronounces "give" just as it would sound in Spanish.

meanings.note: Invariable in azúcar glas ('icing sugar', from French glace).

examples.text: Pon azúcar glas sobre el bizcocho.
examples.trans: Put powdered sugar on the sponge cake.

examples.text: Me gusta el bizcocho con azúcar glas.
examples.trans: I like sponge cake with powdered sugar.

meanings.note: Sweet lemon or sugar glaze.

examples.text: El glaseado es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The glaze is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el glaseado.
examples.trans: We talk about the glaze.

meanings.note: De golpe = all of a sudden.

examples.text: El golpe está aquí.
examples.trans: The knock is here.

examples.text: Vemos los golpes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the knocks from the door.

golpear.gloss: to bump; to knock; to hit

meanings.en: to bump; to knock; to hit
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: No golpees la pared con la caja.
examples.trans: Do not bump the wall with the box.

examples.text: La rama golpeaba suavemente el cristal.
examples.trans: The branch tapped gently against the windowpane.

meanings.note: Diminutive of golpe ('blow, knock'); dar golpecitos = to tap lightly.

examples.text: Dio dos golpecitos suaves en la puerta antes de entrar.
examples.trans: She gave two gentle taps on the door before coming in.

examples.text: El músico dio unos golpecitos en el atril para pedir silencio.
examples.trans: The musician tapped the music stand lightly to ask for quiet.

meanings.note: Classic Spanish surname meaning 'son of Gonzalo'; in *Paquita Salas*, referenced in connection with popular Spanish TV actor Yon (spelled Jon in subtitles) González.

examples.text: Mira, la serie es con Jon González.
examples.trans: Look, the series stars Jon González.

examples.text: González es uno de los apellidos más frecuentes de toda España.
examples.trans: González is one of the most common surnames in all of Spain.

meanings.note: Feminine singular of adjective 'gordo'. Commonly used with 'hacer' ('hacer gorda a alguien', to make someone look fat/bulky in an outfit).
Used idiomatically in Peninsular Spanish for major trouble or a big fuss (e.g., 'liarse parda / armarse una gorda').

examples.text: Pero ¿me hace muy gorda?
examples.trans: But does it make me look really fat?

examples.text: Se armó una muy gorda en la agencia cuando se filtró el vídeo.
examples.trans: A huge scene broke out at the agency when the video leaked.

meanings.note: Ni una gota = not a single drop.

examples.text: La gota está aquí.
examples.trans: The drop is here.

examples.text: Vemos las gotas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the drops from the door.

meanings.note: Built from gota, a drop: el grifo gotea = the tap drips.

examples.text: El grifo del baño gotea toda la noche.
examples.trans: The bathroom tap drips all night.

examples.text: Cuando llueve, el techo gotea.
examples.trans: When it rains, the roof leaks.

meanings.note: Water dripping from a ceiling or roof.

examples.text: La gotera está aquí.
examples.trans: The roof leak is here.

examples.text: Vemos las goteras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the roof leaks from the door.

meanings.note: Diminutive of la gota ('drop') formed with -ita; used for a single drop of oil, lemon, or rain.

examples.text: Una gotita de aceite templado suelta cualquier borde.
examples.trans: One tiny drop of warm oil loosens any rim.

examples.text: Pon solo dos gotitas de limón en el té.
examples.trans: Put just two tiny drops of lemon in the tea.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Fui a los Goya por primera vez.
examples.trans: I went to the Goyas for the first time.

examples.text: Ganó un premio en los Goya.
examples.trans: She won an award at the Goyas.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from grabar.

examples.text: Es una pieza grabada.
examples.trans: It is a carved piece.

examples.text: Un momento... ¡Número doce de la calle del Limonero, y dos iniciales de infancia escritas en la esquina!
examples.trans: Wait a moment... Number twelve, Calle del Limonero, and two childhood initials written in the corner!

meanings.en: recording; filming; shooting (a TV show or video)
meanings.note: Gerund of base verb 'grabar'; frequently used with 'estar' ('estoy grabando') in Spanish TV/film industry parlance for shooting episodes or self-tapes.

examples.text: Nada, muy contenta porque estoy grabando una serie.
examples.trans: Nothing much, just really happy because I'm filming a series.

examples.text: Silencio en el pasillo, por favor, que están grabando la separata.
examples.trans: Quiet in the hallway, please—they're recording the audition sides.

grabar.gloss: to record; to film; to tape

meanings.en: to record; to film; to tape
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb standard in Peninsular television and casting for taping video auditions, voice notes, or TV episodes (whereas 'rodar' leans more toward cinema).

examples.text: Pero no me gusta grabar castings en la oficina.
examples.trans: But I don't like recording auditions in the office.

examples.text: Se ha grabado una cosa que no tenía que grabar.
examples.trans: Something got recorded that shouldn't have been recorded.

meanings.en: I recorded / were to record; he/she/it recorded (imperfect subjunctive)
meanings.note: 1st or 3rd person singular imperfect subjunctive (-se variant) of base verb 'grabar', used in counterfactual 'si' clauses; Peninsular Spanish uses '-se' forms more readily than Latin American Spanish.

examples.text: Si fuera una sala de casting y yo grabase aquí, pondría un foco bueno.
examples.trans: If this were an audition room and I recorded in here, I'd set up a proper spotlight.

examples.text: El director pidió que nadie grabase con el móvil durante el ensayo.
examples.trans: The director asked that nobody record with their phone during the rehearsal.

meanings.note: Plural gracias means thanks or thank you.

examples.text: Muchas gracias por todo.
examples.trans: Thank you very much for everything.

examples.text: Gracias por venir.
examples.trans: Thank you for coming.

meanings.note: Gracias por + noun/infinitive expresses 'thank you for...'.

examples.text: ¡Muchas gracias por su ayuda!
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your help!

examples.text: Gracias por venir hoy.
examples.trans: Thank you for coming today.

examples.text: Todas se van, estás sola. Es muy gracioso que eso me lo digas a mí.
examples.trans: They all leave, you're alone. It's funny you say that to me.

examples.text: Hablamos de gracioso en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about funny at the office.

meanings.note: Used for compass bearings (exacta al grado), oven or weather temperatures (veinte grados), and university degrees.

examples.text: La aguja de la brújula sigue exacta al grado.
examples.trans: The compass needle is still accurate to the degree.

examples.text: Hoy subirá la temperatura hasta los veintidós grados.
examples.trans: Today the temperature will rise to twenty-two degrees.

meanings.note: Standard metric weight unit in Spanish kitchen recipes (cien gramos de harina, doscientos gramos de almendra).

examples.text: Pesa doscientos gramos de almendra molida en la báscula.
examples.trans: Weigh out two hundred grams of ground almonds on the scale.

examples.text: Añade cincuenta gramos de azúcar al final.
examples.trans: Add fifty grams of sugar at the end.

grande.gloss: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)

meanings.en: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)
meanings.note: Shortens to gran before any singular noun (un gran libro, una gran idea).

examples.text: Tenemos una mesa grande en el patio.
examples.trans: We have a big table in the courtyard.

examples.text: Es una gran noticia para todos.
examples.trans: It is great news for everyone.

examples.text: Me salen granitos rojos aquí.
examples.trans: I get tiny red spots here.

examples.text: Tengo un granito en el brazo.
examples.trans: I have a tiny spot on my arm.

meanings.note: Invariable as adverb or adjective.

examples.text: El mapa de la ciudad es gratis.
examples.trans: The city map is free.

examples.text: Los niños entran gratis al museo.
examples.trans: Children enter the museum for free.

meanings.note: In music it means a deep, low sound; elsewhere it means serious.

examples.text: Tiene una voz grave y bonita.
examples.trans: He has a deep, lovely voice.

examples.text: No es nada grave, tranquila.
examples.trans: It's nothing serious, don't worry.

meanings.note: Crack in a wall, ceiling, or tile.

examples.text: La grieta está aquí.
examples.trans: The crack is here.

examples.text: Vemos las grietas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cracks from the door.

meanings.note: Water tap in a sink or shower.

examples.text: El grifo está aquí.
examples.trans: The tap is here.

examples.text: Vemos los grifos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the taps from the door.

meanings.note: Plural grises.

examples.text: Es una pieza gris.
examples.trans: It is a grey piece.

examples.text: Dos pares de zapatos marrones de hombre y jerséis grises.
examples.trans: Two pairs of men's brown shoes and grey sweaters.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Aquí nadie grita por las mañanas.
examples.trans: Nobody shouts here in the mornings.

examples.text: Gritó de alegría al ver a su hermana.
examples.trans: She shouted for joy on seeing her sister.

meanings.note: Dar un grito = to let out a shout.

examples.text: El grito está aquí.
examples.trans: The shout is here.

examples.text: Vemos los gritos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shouts from the door.

meanings.note: Describes thick envelopes, walls, or coats.

examples.text: Es una pieza gruesa.
examples.trans: It is a thick piece.

examples.text: este sobre grueso
examples.trans: this thick envelope

meanings.note: Covers a circle of friends (el grupo del té del viernes), a tour group, or a musical ensemble.

examples.text: El grupo del té del viernes se reúne en el patio.
examples.trans: The Friday tea crew meets in the courtyard.

examples.text: Un grupo de vecinos aplaudió desde la acera.
examples.trans: A group of neighbours applauded from the pavement.

examples.text: (Guantazo)
examples.trans: (Slap)

examples.text: Yo Guantazo
examples.trans: I Guantazo

examples.text: Estás muy guapa hoy.
examples.trans: You look very pretty today.

examples.text: ¡Qué guapa vas!
examples.trans: How gorgeous you look!

examples.text: Estás guapísima siempre.
examples.trans: You always look gorgeous.

examples.text: Salís guapísimas en la foto.
examples.trans: You look gorgeous in the photo.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from guardar.

examples.text: Es una pieza guardada.
examples.trans: It is a kept safe piece.

examples.text: De momento, su maleta sigue guardada bajo llave.
examples.trans: For now, his suitcase stays safe under lock and key.

guardar.gloss: to keep; to put away; to guard

meanings.en: to keep; to put away; to guard
meanings.note: Everyday verb for putting something safely away in a pocket or cupboard.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en este cajón.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in this drawer.

examples.text: Te guardé el último rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I saved the last cinnamon roll for you.

guardas.gloss: you keep; you save; you hold onto

meanings.en: you keep; you put away; you hold onto (for someone)
meanings.note: 2nd person singular ('tú') present indicative of base verb 'guardar'. Often used in polite spoken requests ('¿Me lo guardas?', 'Will you hold onto this for me?').

examples.text: Pero esto guárdamelo, ¿vale? ¿Me lo guardas? Venga.
examples.trans: But hold onto this for me, okay? Will you keep it safe for me? Come on.

examples.text: ¿Dónde guardas las carpetas con los currículums de las actrices?
examples.trans: Where do you keep the folders with the actresses' résumés?

guiar.gloss: to guide; to lead the way

meanings.en: to guide; to lead the way
meanings.note: Present forms stress the í (guío, guías, guía, guían).

examples.text: Rocío nos guía por los puestos del mercado.
examples.trans: Rocio guides us through the market stalls.

examples.text: Las farolas del patio guían a los huéspedes de noche.
examples.trans: The courtyard lanterns guide the guests at night.

examples.text: No me han enviado el guion.
examples.trans: They haven't sent me the script.

examples.text: Estoy leyendo un guion nuevo.
examples.trans: I am reading a new script.

meanings.note: Plural of masculine noun 'guion' (written without an accent mark in singular since the 2010 RAE spelling reform, though plural 'guiones' never carried one).

examples.text: No me han pasado guiones ni nada, solo sé que empiezo el lunes.
examples.trans: They haven't sent me any scripts or anything—I only know I start on Monday.

examples.text: Magüi tiene la mesa llena de guiones pendientes de leer.
examples.trans: Magüi's desk is covered with scripts waiting to be read.

gustar.gloss: to please; to like (me gusta / me gustan)

meanings.en: to please; to like (me gusta / me gustan)
meanings.note: Used with indirect object pronouns (me, te, le, nos, os, les); singular gusta + one noun/infinitive, plural gustan + plural noun.

examples.text: Me gusta mucho el olor a café recién hecho.
examples.trans: I really like the smell of freshly brewed coffee.

examples.text: ¿Te gustan las habitaciones con balcón?
examples.trans: Do you like rooms with a balcony?

meanings.note: ¡Mucho gusto! = Pleased to meet you!; estar a gusto = to feel comfortable.

examples.text: El gusto es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The pleasure is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el gusto.
examples.trans: We talk about the pleasure.

guárdamelo.gloss: keep it for me; save it for me

meanings.en: keep it for me; save it for me; hold onto it for me
meanings.note: 2nd person singular ('tú') affirmative imperative of base verb 'guardar' with enclitic indirect object 'me' and direct object 'lo', requiring a written accent to preserve stress on the first syllable.

examples.text: Pero esto guárdamelo, ¿vale? ¿Me lo guardas? Venga.
examples.trans: But hold onto this for me, okay? Will you keep it safe for me? Come on.

examples.text: Sobra medio bocadillo; guárdamelo en la nevera para luego.
examples.trans: There's half a sandwich left over; save it in the fridge for me for later.

meanings.note: La guía de viajes = the travel guidebook.

examples.text: La guía está aquí.
examples.trans: The guidebook is here.

examples.text: Vemos las guías desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the guidebooks from the door.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.

examples.text: Ya hemos preparado las habitaciones.
examples.trans: We have already prepared the rooms.

examples.text: ¿Qué habilidades tienes?
examples.trans: What skills do you have?

examples.text: Tiene mucha habilidad manual.
examples.trans: She has great manual skill.

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.text: La habitación está aquí.
examples.trans: The room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las habitaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rooms from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Hablo con mi familia cada domingo.
examples.trans: I speak with my family every Sunday.

examples.text: Hablamos largo rato bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We talked for a long while under the tree.

meanings.en: they spoke; they could speak (imperfect subjunctive)
meanings.note: 3rd person plural imperfect subjunctive (-ra form) of base verb 'hablar'; classic in wistful hypothetical clauses like 'si las paredes/piedras hablaran' ('if these walls/stones could talk').

examples.text: Ay, si las piedras de la plaza hablaran...
examples.trans: Oh, if the stones in the town square could speak...

examples.text: Les pedí a los representantes que hablaran directamente con dirección de casting.
examples.trans: I asked the agents to speak directly with the casting director's office.

hacer.gloss: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)

meanings.en: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)
meanings.note: Irregular: hago, hice, hecho; hace tres años = three years ago.

examples.text: La panadera hace pan fresco cada mañana.
examples.trans: The baker bakes fresh bread every morning.

examples.text: Llegó hace diez minutos.
examples.trans: She arrived ten minutes ago.

meanings.note: Indicates direction of movement or gaze.

examples.text: Camina hacia el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: Walk toward the stone bridge.

examples.text: Sigue mirando hacia la esquina.
examples.trans: Keep looking toward the corner.

hacían.gloss: they made / used to make; were made (se hacían)

meanings.en: they made / did; they used to make; (with 'se') were made / filmed
meanings.note: 3rd person plural imperfect indicative of irregular base verb 'hacer'; used with passive 'se' ('se hacían') for ongoing or habitual past productions.

examples.text: Se rodará muy cerquita de donde se hacían «Los Borgia».
examples.trans: It will be shot very close to where "The Borgias" used to be filmed.

examples.text: Antes se hacían las cosas con más cariño en esta profesión.
examples.trans: Things used to be done with more care in this profession.

examples.text: Hala, nos vemos.
examples.trans: Alright, see you.

examples.text: Yo Hala
examples.trans: I Hala

meanings.note: Feminine noun taking el in singular when article is used (tengo mucha hambre).

examples.text: El hambre es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The hunger is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el hambre.
examples.trans: We talk about the hunger.

examples.text: Estoy harta de que no me escuchéis y de que no me veáis.
examples.trans: I'm fed up with you all not listening to me and not seeing me.

examples.text: Yo harto
examples.trans: I harto

meanings.en: he/she/it will do; will make; will perform
meanings.note: 3rd person singular future indicative of irregular base verb 'hacer' (built on irregular stem 'har-').

examples.text: ¿En serio te vas? Te lo hace ella, lo hará perfecto.
examples.trans: Are you seriously leaving? She'll do it for you—she'll do it perfectly.

examples.text: Ya verás como este papel te hará famosa en toda España.
examples.trans: You'll see how this role will make you famous all across Spain.

meanings.note: 1st or 3rd person singular conditional of irregular base verb 'hacer'; very common in 'me haría ilusión / ilu' ('it would thrill me / I'd love that').

examples.text: La verdad que sí. Me haría ilu...
examples.trans: Honestly, yes. It would make me really excited...

examples.text: Yo por mis actrices haría cualquier cosa, y lo sabes.
examples.trans: I would do anything for my actresses, and you know it.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.en: there is / there are (present subjunctive of impersonal 'haber')
meanings.note: Impersonal present subjunctive corresponding to indicative 'hay', triggered after conjunctions like 'a no ser que', 'para que', or 'en cuanto'.
1st or 3rd person singular present subjunctive of auxiliary 'haber' used to form the present perfect subjunctive (e.g., 'que haya venido').

examples.text: A ver, para que nos organicemos bien y no haya líos, lo haremos por orden alfabético.
examples.trans: Alright, so we stay organized and there's no confusion, we'll go in alphabetical order.

examples.text: Avísame en cuanto haya novedades sobre el rodaje en Madrid.
examples.trans: Let me know as soon as there is any news about the shoot in Madrid.

related.gloss: to have / there to be (base lemma)

meanings.en: made; done; reduced to / in a state of (idiomatic fem.)
meanings.note: Feminine singular of irregular past participle 'hecho' (from 'hacer'); pervasive in Peninsular idioms describing someone's state: 'hecha un lío' (all confused/in a muddle), 'hecha polvo' (exhausted/devastated), 'hecha un cuadro' (looking a mess).

examples.text: Estoy hecha un lío con tantos cambios de última hora en el guion.
examples.trans: I'm all mixed up with so many last-minute changes to the script.

examples.text: Después de doce horas de rodaje llegó a casa hecha polvo.
examples.trans: After twelve hours of filming she got home completely wiped out.

meanings.note: Irregular past participle of hacer (recién hecho = freshly made).

examples.text: Es una pieza hecha.
examples.trans: It is a made piece.

examples.text: ¡Son bollos recién hechos! Toma uno, todavía está caliente.
examples.trans: They are freshly baked rolls! Take one, it is still warm.

examples.text: ¿La habrá adaptado una chiquita que se llama Hedda Gabler?
examples.trans: Could a young girl called Hedda Gabler have adapted it?

examples.text: Yo Hedda
examples.trans: I Hedda

meanings.note: As a noun (el helado), means 'ice cream'.

examples.text: Es una pieza helada.
examples.trans: It is a freezing piece.

examples.text: Para mañana por la mañana, el agua de la ducha estará helada.
examples.trans: By tomorrow morning, the shower water will be ice-cold.

examples.text: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old".
examples.trans: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old".

examples.text: Yo Hello
examples.trans: I Hello

examples.text: Vamos a ver una obra de Henrik Ibsen.
examples.trans: We're going to see a play by Henrik Ibsen.

examples.text: Yo Henrik
examples.trans: I Henrik

examples.text: Si es tu hermana, lo veo.
examples.trans: If she is your sister, I'll watch it.

examples.text: Mi hermana vive cerca.
examples.trans: My sister lives nearby.

meanings.note: Affectionate diminutive of hermano.

examples.text: El hermanito está aquí.
examples.trans: The little brother is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hermanitos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the little brothers from the door.

meanings.note: Hermano mayor = older brother; hermano pequeño = younger brother.

examples.text: El hermano está aquí.
examples.trans: The brother is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hermanos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the brothers from the door.

meanings.note: Caja de herramientas = toolbox.

examples.text: La herramienta está aquí.
examples.trans: The tool is here.

examples.text: Vemos las herramientas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tools from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing -ir verb (e -> ie in present: hierve, hierva; e -> i in 3rd preterite: hirvió).

examples.text: Cuando el agua empiece a hervir, apaga el fuego y prepara el té.
examples.trans: When the water starts to boil, turn off the heat and make the tea.

examples.text: La sopa de lentejas hierve despacio en la olla de barro.
examples.trans: The lentil soup simmers slowly in the clay pot.

examples.text: Hola, ¿Hiba Abouk?
examples.trans: Hello, Hiba Abouk?

examples.text: Yo Hiba
examples.trans: I Hiba

meanings.en: I/he/she/it did / made; were to do (imperfect subjunctive)
meanings.note: 1st or 3rd person singular imperfect subjunctive (-ra form) of irregular base verb 'hacer' (from preterite stem 'hic-'); used both in 'si' clauses and after volitional verbs like 'me gustaría que'.

examples.text: Y me gustaría que hiciera la prueba para una de tus películas.
examples.trans: And I'd like her to audition for one of your films.

examples.text: Si lo hiciera bien, dices: «Bueno, pues se ve una pared detrás».
examples.trans: If she did it well, you'd say: "Well, okay, there's a wall visible behind her."

meanings.note: Evergreen climbing plant common on shaded courtyard walls.

examples.text: La hiedra cubre la mitad del muro de piedra.
examples.trans: Ivy covers half of the stone wall.

examples.text: Apartamos la hiedra con cuidado sin romper ni una hoja.
examples.trans: We moved the ivy aside gently without breaking a single leaf.

meanings.note: Silent h-; diphthong ie- pronounced [ʝe].

examples.text: Pon un poco de hielo envuelto sobre el tobillo.
examples.trans: Put a little wrapped ice on your ankle.

examples.text: En verano servimos agua fresca con hielo y limón.
examples.trans: In summer we serve cool water with ice and lemon.

meanings.note: Garden herbs or meadow grass.

examples.text: La hierba está aquí.
examples.trans: The herb is here.

examples.text: Vemos las hierbas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the herbs from the door.

examples.text: Quiero los baños limpios, y por favor los rollitos con la hierbabuena y la lechuga.
examples.trans: I want the bathrooms clean, and please prepare the rolls with the mint and the lettuce.

examples.text: Hablamos de hierbabuena en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about mint, spearmint at the office.

meanings.note: De hierro = made of iron.

examples.text: El hierro es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The iron is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el hierro.
examples.trans: We talk about the iron.

meanings.note: Older speakers in Spain warmly call a young woman hija ('my dear').

examples.text: La hija está aquí.
examples.trans: The daughter is here.

examples.text: Vemos las hijas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the daughters from the door.

meanings.note: Core kinship noun; in the show's soundtrack cues, appears in the name of Madrid indie-pop band *El Buen Hijo* ("Pekín").

meanings.en: dear; honey; kid (affectionate or exasperated Peninsular vocative)
meanings.note: Very common in everyday Spain ('¡Ay, hijo!' / 'hijo mío') when addressing friends or younger colleagues regardless of actual kinship.

examples.text: Mientras recoge la oficina, suena «Pekín», del grupo El Buen Hijo.
examples.trans: While she tidies up the office, "Pekín" by the band El Buen Hijo plays.

examples.text: Ay, hijo mío, no te agobies, que seguro que te llaman para otro papel.
examples.trans: Oh, sweetheart, don't stress yourself out—they're bound to call you for another role.

meanings.note: Covers sewing thread, kitchen twine (hilo de cocina), and a thin stream of liquid (un hilo de aceite).

examples.text: Atamos las ramitas de tomillo y perejil con hilo de cocina.
examples.trans: We tied the sprigs of thyme and parsley with kitchen twine.

examples.text: Cose el botón suelto con aguja e hilo blanco.
examples.trans: Sew the loose button on with a needle and white thread.

meanings.note: Participle of hinchar ('to swell') used as a 4-form adjective.

examples.text: La madera húmeda estaba hinchada tras tanta lluvia.
examples.trans: The damp wood was swollen after so much rain.

examples.text: Mantén en alto el pie hinchado toda la noche.
examples.trans: Keep your swollen foot elevated all night.

meanings.note: Feminine noun derived from hinchar ('to swell'); drops the written accent in the plural (las hinchazones).

examples.text: Con el descanso y el cojín alto ya bajó la hinchazón del tobillo.
examples.trans: With rest and the high cushion, the ankle swelling has already gone down.

examples.text: Un paño frío ayuda mucho a aliviar la hinchazón.
examples.trans: A cold cloth helps a great deal to relieve the swelling.

meanings.note: Covers both a personal story and historical past.

examples.text: La historia está aquí.
examples.trans: The story is here.

examples.text: Vemos las historias desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stories from the door.

meanings.note: Describes heritage buildings and old quarters.

examples.text: Es una pieza histórica.
examples.trans: It is a historic piece.

examples.text: ¡Un arquitecto que trabaja con patios históricos por toda Valencia!
examples.trans: An architect who works with historic courtyard buildings all over Valencia!

meanings.note: Traditional large crusty round loaf of bread in Spain.

examples.text: Sacamos seis hogazas doradas y crujientes del horno.
examples.trans: We pulled six golden, crusty loaves from the oven.

examples.text: Corta rebanadas gruesas de la hogaza para la sopa.
examples.trans: Cut thick slices from the country loaf for the soup.

meanings.note: Means both a tree leaf and a single sheet of paper.

examples.text: La hoja está aquí.
examples.trans: The leaf is here.

examples.text: Vemos las hojas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the leaves from the door.

meanings.note: Universal friendly greeting at any hour of the day.

examples.text: ¡Hola, pasa y siéntate!
examples.trans: Hello, come in and sit down!

examples.text: Hola, ¿qué tal estás hoy?
examples.trans: Hi, how are you doing today?

examples.text: O sea, hay casting en inglés para producciones de Hollywood
examples.trans: I mean, there are castings in English for Hollywood productions

examples.text: Yo Hollywood
examples.trans: I Hollywood

meanings.note: Plural los hombres.

examples.text: El hombre está aquí.
examples.trans: The man is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hombres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the men from the door.

meanings.note: Hombros atrás = shoulders back.

examples.text: El hombro está aquí.
examples.trans: The shoulder is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hombros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shoulders from the door.

meanings.note: Respire hondo = take a deep breath.

examples.text: Es una pieza honda.
examples.trans: It is a deep piece.

examples.text: Respire hondo, Ernesto. Todavía nadie ha escrito nada.
examples.trans: Take a deep breath, Ernesto. Nobody has written anything yet.

meanings.note: ¡Palabra de honor! ('word of honour! / honour system!') is the classic Spanish pledge to play fair.

examples.text: ¡Palabra de honor: nadie abrirá el sobre antes de tiempo!
examples.trans: Word of honour: nobody will open the envelope early!

examples.text: Es un gran honor recibir a su familia en la posada.
examples.trans: It is a great honour to welcome your family to the inn.

meanings.note: ¿Qué hora es? asks the clock time.

examples.text: La hora está aquí.
examples.trans: The hour is here.

examples.text: Vemos las horas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hours from the door.

meanings.note: Train timetable or shop hours.

examples.text: El horario está aquí.
examples.trans: The timetable is here.

examples.text: Vemos los horarios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the timetables from the door.

meanings.note: Built from horno (oven).

examples.text: La panadera hornea bizcochos cada viernes.
examples.trans: The baker bakes sponge cakes every Friday.

examples.text: Esta mañana horneamos pan crujiente.
examples.trans: This morning we baked crusty bread.

meanings.note: Del horno = out of the oven.

examples.text: El horno está aquí.
examples.trans: The oven is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hornos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ovens from the door.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza horrible.
examples.trans: It is a horrible piece.

examples.text: ¡Treinta y cinco minutos! ¡Va a escribir una reseña horrible de una estrella!
examples.trans: Thirty-five minutes! He is going to write a terrible one-star review!

meanings.note: Nouns ending in -dad are always feminine in Spanish.

examples.text: Muchas gracias por su cálida hospitalidad en esta posada.
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your warm hospitality at this inn.

examples.text: La buena hospitalidad empieza con una sonrisa y una taza caliente.
examples.trans: Good hospitality begins with a smile and a hot cup.

meanings.note: Covers inns, hotels, and catering in Spain.

examples.text: La hostelería es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The hospitality trade is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la hostelería.
examples.trans: We talk about the hospitality trade.

meanings.note: Plural los hoteles.

examples.text: El hotel está aquí.
examples.trans: The hotel is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hoteles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hotels from the door.

meanings.en: House (proper title element in *House of Cards*)
meanings.note: Appears in *Paquita Salas* as part of the English TV series title *House of Cards*, referenced humorously to highlight Paquita's late discovery of prestige streaming shows.

examples.text: He empezado una serie americana que se llama «House of Cards», no sé si la conocéis.
examples.trans: I've started an American series called "House of Cards"—I don't know if you're familiar with it.

examples.text: ¿Que si «House of Cards»? No sabía que eso lo veía nadie aquí.
examples.trans: "House of Cards," you say? I had no idea anybody around here watched that.

meanings.note: El día de hoy = today.

examples.text: Hoy es viernes por fin.
examples.trans: Today is finally Friday.

examples.text: ¿Qué desayunamos hoy?
examples.trans: What are we having for breakfast today?

hubiéramos.gloss: we had / would have (imperfect subjunctive aux.)

meanings.en: we had; we would have (imperfect subjunctive auxiliary)
meanings.note: 1st person plural imperfect subjunctive (-ra form) of auxiliary 'haber'; forms the pluperfect subjunctive ('hubiéramos llegado') and in spoken Spanish often substitutes for conditional perfect 'habríamos' in the result clause.

examples.text: Quién nos iba a decir que hubiéramos llegado tan lejos juntas.
examples.trans: Who would have told us that we would have come so far together.

examples.text: Si hubiéramos salido diez minutos antes, no habríamos pillado atasco en la M-30.
examples.trans: If we had left ten minutes earlier, we wouldn't have hit traffic on the M-30.

meanings.en: we had (1st person plural imperfect subjunctive auxiliary)
meanings.note: 1st person plural imperfect subjunctive (-se variant) of auxiliary 'haber', fully interchangeable with 'hubiéramos' in counterfactual 'si' clauses and 'ojalá' wishes, and especially natural in Peninsular speech.

examples.text: Si tú y yo lo hubiésemos hecho un poquito mejor, otro gallo cantaría.
examples.trans: If you and I had done it a little bit better, things would be very different now.

examples.text: Ojalá hubiésemos grabado otra toma por si acaso.
examples.trans: I wish we had recorded another take just in case.

meanings.note: Sonar hueco means 'to sound hollow' when tapped; as a noun (el hueco), it means 'gap, space, or free slot'.

examples.text: Ese tronco viejo está hueco por dentro.
examples.trans: That old tree trunk is hollow inside.

examples.text: Al pisar la tercera piedra del patio, sonó hueca.
examples.trans: When stepping on the third courtyard stone, it sounded hollow.

meanings.en: it smells (bad or noticeable); he/she/it smells
meanings.note: 3rd person singular present indicative of stem-changing verb 'oler' (o -> hue- with orthographic initial 'h-' when stressed). Used alone ('huele un poquito'), it implies an unpleasant odor; figuratively 'oler a' means to suspect something is afoot.

examples.text: Huele quizá un poquito, ¿no? Abre la ventana un momento.
examples.trans: It smells maybe a little bit, doesn't it? Open the window for a moment.

examples.text: Aquí huele a que le van a dar el papel protagonista a ella.
examples.trans: Something tells me they're going to give her the lead role.

meanings.note: Huevos revueltos = scrambled eggs.

examples.text: El huevo está aquí.
examples.trans: The egg is here.

examples.text: Vemos los huevos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the eggs from the door.

meanings.en: hmm; um; huh? (hesitation, skepticism, or prompt to repeat)
meanings.note: Conversational interjection representing a closed-lip nasal murmur, expressing doubt, reluctant realization ('Hum... Vamos, que...'), or a quick question ('¿Hum?').

examples.text: Hum... Vamos, que no me han cogido en el casting, ¿verdad?
examples.trans: Hmm... Basically, they didn't pick me at the audition, right?

examples.text: ¿Hum? Perdona, estaba mirando el móvil y no te he oído.
examples.trans: Hmm? Sorry, I was looking at my phone and didn't hear you.

meanings.note: Feminine abstract noun ending in '-dad' (always feminine in Spanish); in plural ('las humanidades'), refers to the humanities as academic disciplines.

examples.text: Ha habido maricones toda la historia de la humanidad.
examples.trans: There have been gay men throughout the entire history of humanity.

examples.text: Estos torreznos deberían ser patrimonio de la humanidad.
examples.trans: These crispy pork belly strips ought to be a World Heritage treasure.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun in -dad related to húmedo ('damp, humid').

examples.text: Ni una gota de humedad entró dentro del paquete.
examples.trans: Not a single drop of moisture got inside the parcel.

examples.text: La brisa del mar trae mucha humedad por la noche.
examples.trans: The sea breeze brings a lot of humidity at night.

meanings.note: Plural los huéspedes.

examples.text: El huésped está aquí.
examples.trans: The overnight guest is here.

examples.text: Vemos los huéspedes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the overnight guests from the door.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: No llamaron de Hyundai.
examples.trans: They didn't call from Hyundai.

examples.text: Hizo una prueba para Hyundai.
examples.trans: He did an audition for Hyundai.

meanings.note: Proparoxytone (esdrújula), so it always keeps its written accent.

examples.text: El aire húmedo del mar entra por el balcón.
examples.trans: Damp sea air comes in through the balcony.

examples.text: Pasa primero un paño húmedo sobre la pizarra.
examples.trans: Run a damp cloth across the board first.

examples.text: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old".
examples.trans: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old".

examples.text: Yo I
examples.trans: I I

examples.text: Vamos a ver una obra de Henrik Ibsen.
examples.trans: We're going to see a play by Henrik Ibsen.

examples.text: Yo Ibsen
examples.trans: I Ibsen

meanings.note: ¡Buena idea! = Good idea!

examples.text: Abrir las ventanas al patio fue una excelente idea para refrescar el salón.
examples.trans: Opening the windows onto the courtyard was an excellent idea to air out the lounge.

examples.text: No tenía ni idea de que esta posada tuviera más de cien años.
examples.trans: I had no idea that this inn was more than a hundred years old.

meanings.note: Plural ideales.

examples.text: Es una pieza ideal.
examples.trans: It is an ideal piece.

examples.text: ¡En absoluto! Y este escritorio amplio bajo la ventana es ideal para mi trabajo.
examples.trans: Not at all! And this wide desk under the window is ideal for my work.

examples.text: ¿Qué idiomas hablas?
examples.trans: What languages do you speak?

examples.text: Habla tres idiomas muy bien.
examples.trans: She speaks three languages very well.

meanings.note: Exact match in appearance.

examples.text: Es una pieza idéntica.
examples.trans: It is an identical piece.

examples.text: ¡Por fuera es idéntica, sí! ¡Pero mire por dentro!
examples.trans: On the outside it is identical, yes! Yet look on the inside!

meanings.note: Town or parish church.

examples.text: La iglesia está aquí.
examples.trans: The church is here.

examples.text: Vemos las iglesias desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the churchs from the door.

meanings.note: Igual que = just like / the same as.

examples.text: Es una pieza igual.
examples.trans: It is a same piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Polite reply meaning 'likewise / same to you', or 'anyway'.

examples.text: —¡Buen fin de semana! —¡Igualmente!
examples.trans: 'Have a nice weekend!' 'Likewise!'

examples.text: Sabía quién era y vino igualmente.
examples.trans: He knew who it was and came anyway.

meanings.en: excitement; happy anticipation; thrill (colloquial Peninsular clipping)
meanings.note: Informal apocope of feminine noun 'ilusión', ubiquitous in Madrid/Peninsular casual speech in the expression 'hacer ilu' ('me hace mucha ilu' / '¡qué ilu!', 'that makes me so excited!').

examples.text: La verdad que sí. Me haría ilu...
examples.trans: Honestly, yes. It would make me really excited...

examples.text: ¡Qué ilu me hace verte en el cartel de la obra!
examples.trans: I'm so thrilled to see you on the poster for the play!

examples.text: Veamos. Te veo muy ilusionada.
examples.trans: Let's see. I can tell you're very excited.

examples.text: Hablamos de ilusionado en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about excited, hopeful at the office.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la imagen'). Note that the plural gains a written accent mark to preserve stress on the 'a': 'las imágenes'. In the show, 'Imagen y sonido' refers to the vocational training track in audiovisual media.

examples.text: Estudié el módulo de Imagen y sonido, sí.
examples.trans: I studied the Image and Sound vocational program, yes.

examples.text: Como actriz, tienes que cuidar mucho tu imagen pública en las redes.
examples.trans: As an actress, you have to take great care of your public image on social media.

examples.text: Imagínate la sorpresa.
examples.trans: Imagine the surprise.

examples.text: No me imagino otra vida.
examples.trans: I can't imagine another life.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza impecable.
examples.trans: It is a spotless piece.

examples.text: ¡Impecable, Ernesto! Hasta lleva las gafas en la nariz en vez de en la frente.
examples.trans: Sharp and spotless, Ernesto! Even your glasses are on your nose instead of your forehead.

meanings.note: English adjective ('important', Spanish 'importante') used in Paquita Salas during the comedic English-language audition scene where Macarena and Paquita struggle through broken English lines ('It's easy, but it's very important').

examples.text: En el casting en inglés repetía: "But it's very important 'give' this".
examples.trans: In the English audition she kept repeating: "But it's very important 'give' this".

examples.text: Paquita le leía la réplica diciendo: "It's easy, but it's very important".
examples.trans: Paquita read her the cue line saying: "It's easy, but it's very important".

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza importante.
examples.trans: It is an important piece.

examples.text: A dos calles de aquí, cuando yo era pequeño. El viernes es... un día importante para mí.
examples.trans: Two streets from here, when I was little. Friday is... an important day for me.

importar.gloss: to matter; to mind (importarle a alguien)

meanings.en: to matter; to mind (importarle a alguien)
meanings.note: ¿Le importa esperar? = Do you mind waiting?

examples.text: ¿Te importa abrir un poco la ventana?
examples.trans: Do you mind opening the window a little?

examples.text: No me importa esperar cinco minutos.
examples.trans: I do not mind waiting five minutes.

imprenta.gloss: printing press; block capitals (letra de imprenta)

meanings.en: printing press; block capitals (letra de imprenta)
meanings.note: Letra de imprenta means neat printed block letters.

examples.text: La imprenta es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The printing press is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la imprenta.
examples.trans: We talk about the printing press.

meanings.note: Irregular participle of imprimir used as an adjective (carta impresa, libro impreso).

examples.text: Dejamos veinte cartas impresas del menú sobre el mostrador.
examples.trans: We left twenty printed menu cards on the counter.

examples.text: Prefiero leer en una página impresa antes de dormir.
examples.trans: I prefer reading on a printed page before going to sleep.

meanings.note: Often used in the plural (los impuestos); manual de impuestos = tax handbook.

examples.text: El contable revisó todos los recibos y los impuestos del trimestre.
examples.trans: The accountant reviewed all the receipts and taxes for the quarter.

examples.text: El precio del menú ya incluye todos los impuestos.
examples.trans: The menu price already includes all taxes.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Inclino la jarra para servir el agua.
examples.trans: I tilt the pitcher to pour the water.

examples.text: Inclinó la caja y oyó una llave.
examples.trans: He tilted the box and heard a key.

meanings.note: Con desayuno incluido = with breakfast included.

examples.text: Es una pieza incluida.
examples.trans: It is an included piece.

examples.text: con desayuno incluido
examples.trans: with breakfast included

meanings.note: Adds an unexpected or emphatic item.

examples.text: Incluso el timbre estuvo callado hoy.
examples.trans: Even the buzzer stayed quiet today.

examples.text: Trabaja incluso los domingos.
examples.trans: He works even on Sundays.

examples.text: Y tiene la reciente incorporación de Macarena García.
examples.trans: And he has the recent addition of Macarena García.

examples.text: Yo incorporación
examples.trans: I incorporación

examples.text: Tenía una trama increíble.
examples.trans: She had an incredible storyline.

examples.text: Es una actriz increíble.
examples.trans: She's an incredible actress.

meanings.note: Often refers to the entertainment or television industry ("la industria audiovisual") in showbiz contexts, or manufacturing and commerce in general.
Used in the older or colloquial sense of diligence and productive activity, as in "mucha industria".

examples.text: Gente muy trabajadora, mucha industria.
examples.trans: Very hardworking people, lots of industry.

examples.text: Lleva más de veinte años trabajando en la industria del cine español.
examples.trans: She has been working in the Spanish film industry for over twenty years.

meanings.note: The state or period of being a child.

examples.text: Fueron muy buenos amigos en la infancia.
examples.trans: They were very good friends in childhood.

examples.text: Tuvo una infancia feliz.
examples.trans: She had a happy childhood.

meanings.note: Plural infantiles.

examples.text: Es una pieza infantil.
examples.trans: It is a childhood piece.

examples.text: Un momento... ¡Número doce de la calle del Limonero, y dos iniciales de infancia escritas en la esquina!
examples.trans: Wait a moment... Number twelve, Calle del Limonero, and two childhood initials written in the corner!

meanings.note: Invariable for masculine and feminine singular; contrasts with superior ('upper, top').

examples.text: Hay una estrella en el borde inferior derecho de la tarjeta.
examples.trans: There is a star in the bottom right border of the card.

examples.text: Guardamos las ollas grandes en el estante inferior.
examples.trans: We keep the large pots on the bottom shelf.

meanings.note: Describes both a quick-thinking person (un amigo ingenioso) and a clever design or puzzle (una idea ingeniosa).

examples.text: Dos amigos ingeniosos partieron la receta en dos mitades.
examples.trans: Two clever friends split the recipe into two halves.

examples.text: El carpintero encontró una solución muy ingeniosa.
examples.trans: The carpenter found a very ingenious solution.

meanings.note: La llave inglesa ('the English key') is an adjustable wrench in Spain.

examples.text: Es una pieza inglesa.
examples.trans: It is an English piece.

examples.text: Cerrada y vaciada. Pásame la llave inglesa pesada de tu izquierda.
examples.trans: Off and drained. Pass me the heavy wrench on your left.

examples.text: ¡Es inhumano!
examples.trans: It's inhumane!

examples.text: Yo inhumano
examples.trans: I inhumano

meanings.note: Plural las iniciales.

examples.text: La inicial está aquí.
examples.trans: The initial is here.

examples.text: Vemos las iniciales desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the initials from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: El técnico inspecciona la caldera anual.
examples.trans: The technician inspects the boiler yearly.

examples.text: Inspeccionaron el tejado tras la lluvia.
examples.trans: They inspected the roof after the rain.

meanings.note: Feminine: la inspectora.

examples.text: El inspector municipal revisó la fachada histórica con mucha atención.
examples.trans: The municipal inspector examined the historic facade with great care.

examples.text: El inspector felicitó a Mateo por el buen estado del edificio.
examples.trans: The inspector congratulated Mateo on the building's fine condition.

meanings.note: Feminine form of inspector.

examples.text: La inspectora revisó los planos y la salida al patio.
examples.trans: The inspector checked the plans and the courtyard exit.

examples.text: Ofrecimos un vaso de agua fresca a la inspectora.
examples.trans: We offered a glass of cool water to the inspector.

meanings.note: Un instante = just a moment.

examples.text: El instante está aquí.
examples.trans: The instant is here.

examples.text: Vemos los instantes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the instants from the door.

examples.text: ¿Tocas algún instrumento musical?
examples.trans: Do you play any musical instrument?

examples.text: El piano es mi instrumento favorito.
examples.trans: The piano is my favourite instrument.

meanings.note: Same singular form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: El aroma del pan recién horneado es insuperable.
examples.trans: The aroma of freshly baked bread is unbeatable.

examples.text: Rocío prepara una sopa de lentejas insuperable.
examples.trans: Rocio makes an unbeatable lentil soup.

examples.text: Lee algo más intelectual.
examples.trans: Read something more intellectual.

examples.text: Es una revista cultural e intelectual.
examples.trans: It is a cultural, intellectual magazine.

meanings.note: Followed directly by an infinitive (intenté sonreír).

examples.text: Intento aprender diez palabras al día.
examples.trans: I try to learn ten words a day.

examples.text: Intenté llamarte ayer por la tarde.
examples.trans: I tried calling you yesterday afternoon.

meanings.note: Plural interiores.

examples.text: Es una pieza interior.
examples.trans: It is an inner piece.

examples.text: Asegúrate de que el anillo interior de latón mide veinte milímetros.
examples.trans: Make sure the inner brass ring measures twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Invariable in gender in the singular ("el mundo internacional", "la fama internacional"); forms the plural "internacionales".

examples.text: Quiere dar el salto al mundo internacional con una serie en inglés.
examples.trans: She wants to make the leap to the international world with a series in English.

examples.text: Esa actriz tiene mucha proyección internacional.
examples.trans: That actress has great international reach.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Antes no había Internet.
examples.trans: Before there was no Internet.

examples.text: Busco el billete en Internet.
examples.trans: I look for the ticket on the Internet.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb.

examples.text: Perdone que interrumpa su conversación un momento.
examples.trans: Forgive me for interrupting your conversation for a moment.

examples.text: Un chaparrón de mayo interrumpió la fiesta del jardín.
examples.trans: A May downpour interrupted the garden party.

meanings.note: A light switch on the wall.

examples.text: El interruptor está al lado de la puerta.
examples.trans: The switch is next to the door.

examples.text: No encuentro el interruptor de la luz.
examples.trans: I can't find the light switch.

examples.text: Gracias. Perdón por la intrusión.
examples.trans: Thank you. Sorry for the intrusion.

examples.text: Yo intrusión
examples.trans: I intrusión

meanings.note: Coldest season of the year.

examples.text: El invierno está aquí.
examples.trans: The winter is here.

examples.text: Vemos los inviernos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the winters from the door.

examples.text: No tengo invitación para la fiesta.
examples.trans: I don't have an invitation to the party.

examples.text: Mandaron las invitaciones ayer.
examples.trans: They sent the invitations yesterday.

invitar.gloss: to invite; to treat (pick up the bill)

meanings.en: to invite; to treat (pick up the bill)
meanings.note: Invita la casa means 'it is on the house'.

examples.text: Hoy invito yo al café de la mañana.
examples.trans: Today morning coffee is my treat.

examples.text: Nos invitaron a cenar el sábado.
examples.trans: They invited us to dinner on Saturday.

examples.text: Mira, la niña. La hemos invocado. A ver qué dice.
examples.trans: Look, it's the girl calling. We summoned her. Let's see what she says.

examples.text: Hablamos de invocar en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about summoned at the office.

meanings.note: Describes a manuscript, musical score, or story that has never been published or performed in public.

examples.text: Encontraron un vals inédito escrito a lápiz dentro del cuaderno.
examples.trans: They found an unpublished waltz written in pencil inside the notebook.

examples.text: La librería presentó una carta inédita de un poeta del barrio.
examples.trans: The bookshop presented an unpublished letter by a neighbourhood poet.

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.

examples.text: ¿Cómo va todo esta mañana?
examples.trans: How is everything going this morning?

meanings.en: is (third-person singular present of English "to be")
meanings.note: Quoted English verb featured in *Paquita Salas* during self-tape introductions ("My name is...") and English audition scenes ("It is very important...").

examples.text: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old", dijo mirando a cámara.
examples.trans: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old," she said looking at the camera.

examples.text: "It is very important to give this envelope to the emperor", repitió en el casting.
examples.trans: "It is very important to give this envelope to the emperor," she repeated at the audition.

examples.text: Lo ha enviado Camilla Isola,
examples.trans: Camilla Isola sent it,

examples.text: Yo Isola
examples.trans: I Isola

meanings.note: Quoted English pronoun used in *Paquita Salas* in the recurring audition line "It is very important to give this envelope to the emperor".

examples.text: "It is very important to give this envelope to the emperor", leyó con acento español.
examples.trans: "It is very important to give this envelope to the emperor," she read with a Spanish accent.

examples.text: No sabía ni pronunciar "It is very important" en la prueba de inglés.
examples.trans: She didn't even know how to pronounce "It is very important" in the English audition.

examples.text: "It's easy".
examples.trans: "It's easy".

examples.text: Yo It's
examples.trans: I It's

meanings.note: A la izquierda = on/to the left.

examples.text: La izquierda está aquí.
examples.trans: The left is here.

examples.text: Vemos las izquierdas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lefts from the door.

meanings.note: a la izquierda = on the left; la mano izquierda = the left hand.

examples.text: Me duele el pie izquierdo.
examples.trans: My left foot hurts.

examples.text: Escribe con la mano izquierda.
examples.trans: She writes with her left hand.

meanings.note: Spoken laugh or triumphant exclamation (¡ja! / ¡ja, ja!).

examples.text: ¡Ja, sabía que cabrían las ocho mesas en el plano!
examples.trans: Ha, I knew all eight tables would fit on the plan!

examples.text: Ernesto soltó un «¡ja!» alegre al terminar la lama.
examples.trans: Ernesto let out a cheerful 'ha!' upon finishing the slat.

meanings.note: Plural jabones.

examples.text: El jabón está aquí.
examples.trans: The soap is here.

examples.text: Vemos los jabones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the soaps from the door.

examples.text: Estamos muy liados, mucho jaleo en la oficina.
examples.trans: We're really swamped, lots of chaos at the office.

examples.text: Yo jaleo
examples.trans: I jaleo

meanings.note: Stronger, more emphatic counterpart of nunca.

examples.text: Jamás he visto una caja igual.
examples.trans: I have never ever seen a box like it.

examples.text: Nunca jamás olvides esta receta.
examples.trans: Never ever forget this recipe.

meanings.note: Plural jardines, without the written accent.

examples.text: Mi madre tiene flores en el jardín.
examples.trans: My mother has flowers in the garden.

examples.text: Los niños juegan en el jardín.
examples.trans: The children play in the garden.

meanings.note: Glass or ceramic pitcher for water or juice.

examples.text: La jarra está aquí.
examples.trans: The jug is here.

examples.text: Vemos las jarras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the jugs from the door.

meanings.note: Diminutive of jarra ('jug / pitcher').

examples.text: Sirvo la leche caliente en una jarrita blanca.
examples.trans: I serve the warm milk in a small white jug.

examples.text: Hay dos jarritas azules en la bandeja del desayuno.
examples.trans: There are two small blue jugs on the breakfast tray.

meanings.note: Augmentative of jarra ('pitcher/jug') that specialized to mean a flower vase.

examples.text: Pusimos un pequeño jarrón con hojas de limonero en cada mesa.
examples.trans: We put a small vase with lemon leaves on every table.

examples.text: Llenó el jarrón de cristal con agua fresca y flores blancas.
examples.trans: She filled the glass vase with fresh water and white flowers.

meanings.note: Feminine form of jefe.

examples.text: En la cocina manda siempre nuestra jefa Rocío.
examples.trans: In the kitchen our head chef Rocio is always in charge.

examples.text: La jefa probó el caldo con una cuchara limpia.
examples.trans: The boss tasted the broth with a clean spoon.

meanings.note: Feminine: la jefa.

examples.text: El jefe está aquí.
examples.trans: The boss is here.

examples.text: Vemos los jefes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bosss from the door.

meanings.note: Plural in Spain: los jerséis.

examples.text: El jersey está aquí.
examples.trans: The jumper is here.

examples.text: Vemos los jerséis desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the jumpers from the door.

meanings.note: English loanword used in Peninsular Spanish mainly in the compound "jet lag" (desfase horario), "jet privado" (private jet), and "la jet set" (high society).

examples.text: Acabo de volver de viaje, así que tengo un poquito de "jet lag" aún.
examples.trans: I just got back from a trip, so I still have a little bit of jet lag.

examples.text: Los actores de Hollywood viajan en jet privado a los festivales de cine.
examples.trans: Hollywood actors travel by private jet to film festivals.

meanings.note: Very frequent Peninsular Spanish vulgar interjection (from the verb "joder") used to express annoyance, shock, frustration, or strong emphasis.

meanings.en: to fuck up, to ruin, to annoy
meanings.note: As a verb, used transitively ("joder algo") to spoil or ruin something, or pronominally ("joderse") to put up with bad luck.

examples.text: ¡Joder, tronca! ¿Por qué no me avisaste antes?
examples.trans: Fuck, girl! Why didn't you warn me earlier?

examples.text: "-¡Esto! -Joder, vaya leche".
examples.trans: "-This! -Fuck, what a slap."

meanings.en: ruined, screwed up, messed up (past participle of "joder")
meanings.note: Past participle of the vulgar verb "joder", used in compound tenses such as "me has jodido toda la prueba" (you've ruined the whole audition for me).
Inflects for gender and number (jodido/jodida) to describe a person in a bad state or a very difficult situation.

examples.text: Lidia San José, encantada. Pues me has jodido toda la prueba.
examples.trans: Lidia San José, nice to meet you. Well, you've ruined the whole audition for me.

examples.text: Está la cosa muy jodida para conseguir papeles protagonistas este año.
examples.trans: Things are really tough for landing leading roles this year.

meanings.note: Masculine given name; in *Paquita Salas*, refers to the popular Spanish television actor Yon/Jon González.

examples.text: Mira, la serie es con Jon González.
examples.trans: Look, the series is with Jon González.

examples.text: Jon protagonizó varias series juveniles de mucho éxito en televisión.
examples.trans: Jon starred in several very successful teen drama series on television.

examples.text: Traigo un paquete para Jorge Roelas. ¿Me firmas aquí?
examples.trans: I have a parcel for Jorge Roelas. Will you sign here for me?

examples.text: Yo Jorge
examples.trans: I Jorge

meanings.note: A jornada completa = full-time.

examples.text: La jornada está aquí.
examples.trans: The workday is here.

examples.text: Vemos las jornadas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the workdays from the door.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Viene Lidia San José.
examples.trans: Lidia San José is coming.

examples.text: Te mando a Lidia San José.
examples.trans: I'm sending you Lidia San José.

meanings.note: Plural lleva tilde: jóvenes; also used as a noun (el/la joven).

examples.text: Es una pieza joven.
examples.trans: It is a young piece.

examples.text: ¿Voz educada? ¿Joven o mayor?
examples.trans: Polite voice? Young or older?

examples.text: Igual aquí hay una joya por descubrir.
examples.trans: Maybe there is a gem to discover here.

examples.text: Yo joya
examples.trans: I joya

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Juanfran mandó un correo urgente.
examples.trans: Juanfran sent an urgent email.

examples.text: Paquita llama a Juanfran.
examples.trans: Paquita calls Juanfran.

meanings.note: Used with estar when stating someone is retired (está jubilado) or directly after a profession (un cartógrafo jubilado); also used as a noun.

examples.text: El cartógrafo jubilado envió una postal desde la costa.
examples.trans: The retired mapmaker sent a postcard from the coast.

examples.text: Mi tío está jubilado y pasea cada mañana por el parque.
examples.trans: My uncle is retired and walks through the park every morning.

meanings.note: Second-person singular (tú) present indicative of the stem-changing verb "jugar" (u -> ue). Used figuratively in "juegas en primera división" (you're playing in the big leagues now).

examples.text: Claro, como ahora juegas en primera división.
examples.trans: Of course, since now you play in the first division.

examples.text: Si juegas bien tus cartas, conseguirás el papel en la película.
examples.trans: If you play your cards right, you'll get the role in the movie.

examples.text: Mira, te voy a proponer un juego. Es un juego muy sencillo.
examples.trans: Look, I'm going to propose a game to you. It's a very simple game.

examples.text: Pues porque es un juego, ya te lo he dicho.
examples.trans: Because it's a game, like I just told you.

meanings.en: I play / he, she, or it plays (subjunctive)
meanings.note: First- or third-person singular present subjunctive of the stem-changing verb "jugar" (with spelling change g -> gu before e). Used after concessive clauses like "por mucho que juegue" (however much I/she may play).

examples.text: Pues por mucho que juegue en primera división, sigue siendo mi amiga.
examples.trans: Well, as much as she plays in the first division, she is still my friend.

examples.text: Espero que el equipo juegue mejor en el próximo partido.
examples.trans: I hope the team plays better in the next match.

meanings.note: Invariable in the plural: el jueves ('on Thursday'), los jueves ('on Thursdays').

examples.text: El repartidor viene el jueves por la tarde.
examples.trans: The delivery driver comes on Thursday afternoon.

examples.text: Los jueves limpiamos todas las lámparas del patio.
examples.trans: On Thursdays we clean all the courtyard lamps.

meanings.en: we play, we are playing / we played
meanings.note: First-person plural (nosotros) present indicative and preterite indicative of "jugar". In Spanish, "jugar" takes the preposition "a" before the game ("jugamos a un montón de cosas").

examples.text: Cuido de tu madre y jugamos a un montón de cosas.
examples.trans: I take care of your mother and we play a lot of things.

examples.text: Todos los domingos jugamos a las cartas después de comer.
examples.trans: Every Sunday we play cards after lunch.

meanings.en: to play (a game, sport, or match)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (u -> ue in stressed forms: juego, juegas, juega, juegan). Takes the preposition "a" before the name of a sport or game ("jugar al fútbol").

meanings.en: to toy with, to take risks with
meanings.note: Followed by "con" ("jugar con fuego", "jugar con los sentimientos"), means to trifle or gamble with something.

examples.text: Yo estoy dispuesto a jugar un partido amistoso.
examples.trans: I am willing to play a friendly match.

examples.text: ¿Te apetece jugar una partida de cartas esta tarde?
examples.trans: Do you feel like playing a game of cards this afternoon?

meanings.note: Plumbing joint where two pipes meet.

examples.text: La junta está aquí.
examples.trans: The pipe joint is here.

examples.text: Vemos las juntas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pipe joints from the door.

juntar.gloss: to put together; to join (juntarse = to meet, gather)

meanings.en: to put together; to join (juntarse = to meet, gather)
meanings.note: Reflexive juntarse means 'to get together, meet up, or combine'.

examples.text: Juntamos dos mesas pequeñas para sentarnos todos.
examples.trans: We pushed two small tables together so we could all sit.

examples.text: Los viernes por la tarde se juntan los vecinos en el patio.
examples.trans: On Friday afternoons the neighbours gather in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Junto a + noun works like a preposition meaning 'beside / next to'.

examples.text: Siéntate junto a la ventana.
examples.trans: Sit next to the window.

examples.text: Trabajamos juntos en la posada.
examples.trans: We work together at the guesthouse.

meanings.note: Justo aquí = right here; justo al lado = right next door.

examples.text: La llave está justo aquí.
examples.trans: The key is right here.

examples.text: La panadería queda justo al lado.
examples.trans: The bakery is right next door.

examples.text: ¿Cómo va a ir en kayak?
examples.trans: How is she going to go by kayak?

examples.text: Alquilamos un kayak en el río.
examples.trans: We rented a kayak on the river.

meanings.note: Masculine noun used in Spain for both the popular takeaway pita/wrap filled with spit-roasted meat and the fast-food shop that sells it.

examples.text: Anda, por favor, vete o súbeme un kebab.
examples.trans: Go on, please, either leave or bring me up a kebab.

examples.text: Después de salir de fiesta nos comimos un kebab de pollo con salsa blanca.
examples.trans: After going out partying, we ate a chicken kebab with white sauce.

meanings.note: Spanish onomatopoeic interjection and masculine noun ("el kikirikí") imitating the crow of a rooster; featured in *Paquita Salas* as a humorous cellphone ringtone.

examples.text: (Kikirikí como tono de móvil)
examples.trans: (Cock-a-doodle-doo as a cellphone ringtone)

examples.text: El gallo nos despertó al amanecer con su kikirikí.
examples.trans: The rooster woke us up at dawn with its cock-a-doodle-doo.

meanings.note: Everyday shortening of kilogramo.

examples.text: Compramos tres kilos de limones amarillos.
examples.trans: We bought three kilos of yellow lemons.

examples.text: Medio kilo de harina basta para dos panes.
examples.trans: Half a kilo of flour is enough for two loaves.

examples.text: Me gusta con mucho kétchup.
examples.trans: I like it with lots of ketchup.

examples.text: Pon un poco de kétchup.
examples.trans: Put a little ketchup on it.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Al lado = on the side / next door.

examples.text: El lado está aquí.
examples.trans: The side is here.

examples.text: Vemos los lados desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sides from the door.

meanings.note: Masculine plural of "ladrido" (from "ladrar", to bark). Frequently used in the plural to denote continuous dog barking, including in script and subtitle sound cues.

examples.text: Se oyeron ladridos en el jardín cuando tocaron el timbre.
examples.trans: Barking was heard in the garden when they rang the doorbell.

examples.text: Los ladridos del perro del vecino no me dejaron dormir en toda la noche.
examples.trans: The barking of the neighbor's dog didn't let me sleep all night.

meanings.note: De ladrillo = made of brick.

examples.text: El ladrillo está aquí.
examples.trans: The brick is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ladrillos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bricks from the door.

meanings.note: English loanword used in Spanish primarily as part of the expression "jet lag" (desfase horario) or by gamers to refer to connection delay.

examples.text: Acabo de volver de América, así que tengo un poquito de "jet lag" aún.
examples.trans: I just got back from America, so I still have a little bit of jet lag.

examples.text: El "jet lag" me tiene despierta a las cuatro de la mañana.
examples.trans: The jet lag has me wide awake at four in the morning.

meanings.note: Angled wooden slat in a shutter (contraventana de lamas).

examples.text: Pintamos despacio cada lama de madera por ambos lados.
examples.trans: We slowly paint each wooden slat on both sides.

examples.text: El aire fresco pasa suave entre las lamas verdes.
examples.trans: Cool air passes gently between the green louvres.

meanings.note: De lana = woollen.

examples.text: La lana es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The wool is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la lana.
examples.trans: We talk about the wool.

meanings.note: Superlative larguísimo = very long.

examples.text: ¡Qué día tan largo en la posada!
examples.trans: What a long day at the inn!

examples.text: El pasillo es largo y oscuro.
examples.trans: The hallway is long and dark.

meanings.note: Absolute superlative of largo (spelled gu before í to keep the /g/ sound).

examples.text: Es una pieza larguísima.
examples.trans: It is a very long piece.

examples.text: ¡Cuando me pongo nervioso, mis frases se vuelven larguísimas y formales!
examples.trans: When I get nervous, my sentences grow very long and formal!

examples.text: Muy bien, de Larios, ¿verdad?
examples.trans: Very good, Larios brand, right?

examples.text: Yo Larios
examples.trans: I Larios

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: De lata means 'made of tin / tinplate' (una caja de lata); una lata also means a food can.

examples.text: Mi abuela guardaba los botones en una caja redonda de lata.
examples.trans: My grandmother kept buttons in a round tin box.

examples.text: Abrimos una lata de aceitunas para el aperitivo.
examples.trans: We opened a tin of olives for the snack.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine singular; plural laterales.

examples.text: La puerta lateral da directamente al jardín.
examples.trans: The side door opens straight onto the garden.

examples.text: Aprieta el cierre lateral para doblar la silla.
examples.trans: Press the side latch to fold the chair.

examples.text: Trabajamos con el mercado latino.
examples.trans: We work with the Latin American market.

examples.text: Me encanta la música latina.
examples.trans: I love Latin music.

meanings.note: El corazón me late rápido = my heart is beating fast.

examples.text: El corazón me late rápido de alegría.
examples.trans: My heart beats fast with joy.

examples.text: Sentía latir el pulso tras correr.
examples.trans: She felt her pulse beating after running.

meanings.note: Yellow copper-zinc alloy used for keys, lamps, and valves.

examples.text: El latón es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The brass is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el latón.
examples.trans: We talk about the brass.

meanings.note: Third-person singular indirect object pronoun.

examples.text: Le llevo una taza de té caliente.
examples.trans: I am bringing you/her a cup of hot tea.

examples.text: ¿Le gusta la habitación del patio?
examples.trans: Do you like the courtyard room?

meanings.note: Café con leche = white coffee.

examples.text: La leche es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The milk is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la leche.
examples.trans: We talk about the milk.

examples.text: Quiero los baños limpios, y por favor los rollitos con la hierbabuena y la lechuga.
examples.trans: I want the bathrooms clean, and please prepare the rolls with the mint and the lettuce.

examples.text: Hablamos de lechuga en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about lettuce at the office.

meanings.note: Lámpara de lectura = reading lamp.

examples.text: La lectura es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The reading is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la lectura.
examples.trans: We talk about the reading.

meanings.note: Preterite 3rd sg/pl spells y: leyó, leyeron; past participle leído.

examples.text: Leo el periódico con el primer café.
examples.trans: I read the newspaper with my first coffee.

examples.text: Anoche leímos toda la carta juntos.
examples.trans: Last night we read the whole letter together.

meanings.note: Plural legales.

examples.text: Todo el trámite legal de la posada quedó resuelto antes del viernes.
examples.trans: All the legal paperwork for the inn was settled before Friday.

examples.text: ¡Los párrafos legales me dan dolor de cabeza incluso con dos pares de gafas!
examples.trans: Legal paragraphs give me a headache even with two pairs of glasses!

lejos.gloss: far; far away (lejos de = away from)

meanings.en: far; far away (lejos de = away from)
meanings.note: Opposite of cerca.

examples.text: La estación no está lejos.
examples.trans: The station is not far.

examples.text: Pon la mesa lejos de la puerta.
examples.trans: Put the table away from the door.

meanings.note: Usually plural (lentejas) when referring to lentil soup or stew.

examples.text: Una sopa caliente de lentejas reconforta en invierno.
examples.trans: A hot lentil soup is comforting in winter.

examples.text: Cocemos las lentejas a fuego lento con verduras frescas.
examples.trans: We simmer the lentils slowly with fresh vegetables.

meanings.note: Opposite of rápido.

examples.text: Es una pieza lenta.
examples.trans: It is a slow piece.

examples.text: Dele unos minutos, Javier. El tráfico del centro al mediodía siempre va lento.
examples.trans: Give it a few minutes, Javier. City traffic at noon is always slow.

meanings.note: Plural indirect object pronoun.

examples.text: Les preparo el desayuno enseguida.
examples.trans: I will prepare breakfast for you all right away.

examples.text: Les debo toda la verdad.
examples.trans: I owe you both the whole truth.

examples.text: Es que ahora soy lesbiana. No lo sabías, ¿no?
examples.trans: The thing is, I'm a lesbian now. You didn't know, did you?

examples.text: Hablamos de lesbiana en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about lesbian at the office.

meanings.note: Tu letra means 'your handwriting'.

examples.text: La letra está aquí.
examples.trans: The handwriting is here.

examples.text: Vemos las letras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the handwritings from the door.

levantar.gloss: to lift; to raise; to get up (levantarse)

meanings.en: to lift; to raise; to get up (levantarse)
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Levanta esa esquina de la alfombra.
examples.trans: Lift that corner of the rug.

examples.text: Nos levantamos a las seis y media.
examples.trans: We get up at six thirty.

meanings.note: Plural las leyes.

examples.text: La ley está aquí.
examples.trans: The law is here.

examples.text: Vemos las leyes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the laws from the door.

examples.text: Estamos muy liados, mucho jaleo en la oficina.
examples.trans: We're really swamped, lots of chaos at the office.

examples.text: Yo liado
examples.trans: I liado
