meanings.note: Está libre = it is vacant / available.

examples.text: Es una pieza libre.
examples.trans: It is a free piece.

examples.text: está libre
examples.trans: is free

meanings.note: In Spain both a bookshop and a piece of furniture full of shelves for books. Not a library (biblioteca).

examples.text: Compro el libro en la librería de la esquina.
examples.trans: I buy the book at the bookshop on the corner.

examples.text: Tenemos una librería grande en el salón.
examples.trans: We have a big bookcase in the living room.

meanings.note: Handy pocket or desk notepad for lists and phone notes.

examples.text: Apunto todos los pedidos en una libreta pequeña.
examples.trans: I write down all the orders in a small notepad.

examples.text: Ernesto dejó su libreta abierta junto al teléfono.
examples.trans: Ernesto left his notepad open beside the telephone.

meanings.note: Libro de reservas = reservation ledger.

examples.text: El libro está aquí.
examples.trans: The book is here.

examples.text: Vemos los libros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the books from the door.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: ¡Madre mía, Lidi!
examples.trans: Goodness me, Lidi!

examples.text: Lidi ha trabajado mucho.
examples.trans: Lidi has worked a lot.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: ¿Quieres un chupito, Lidia?
examples.trans: Do you want a shot, Lidia?

examples.text: Lidia no bebe alcohol.
examples.trans: Lidia doesn't drink alcohol.

meanings.note: Opposite of pesado ('heavy').

examples.text: Las sillas de madera nueva son firmes pero ligeras.
examples.trans: The new wooden chairs are sturdy yet light.

examples.text: Entra una brisa ligera desde el jardín interior.
examples.trans: A light breeze comes in from the inner garden.

meanings.note: Colloquial Peninsular Spanish noun and adjective derived from "ligar" (to flirt/hook up), describing someone who flirts constantly or easily attracts romantic partners.

examples.text: Como su padre, es un ligón. Ya...
examples.trans: Just like his father, he's a total flirt. Yeah...

examples.text: De joven tenía fama de ser el más ligón de todo el barrio.
examples.trans: When he was young, he had a reputation for being the biggest flirt in the whole neighborhood.

meanings.note: Used alone (la lija) or in papel de lija ('sandpaper').

examples.text: Compra dos hojas de papel de lija fina.
examples.trans: Buy two sheets of fine sandpaper.

examples.text: Pasamos la lija por los bordes secos de la madera.
examples.trans: We rub sandpaper along the dry edges of the wood.

meanings.note: To smooth wood with sandpaper (la lija).

examples.text: Hoy vamos a lijar la mesa vieja.
examples.trans: Today we are going to sand the old table.

examples.text: Primero lijo la puerta y luego la pinto.
examples.trans: First I sand the door and then I paint it.

meanings.note: Fruit tree bearing lemons (el limón -> el limonero).

examples.text: El limonero está aquí.
examples.trans: The lemon tree is here.

examples.text: Vemos los limoneros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lemon trees from the door.

limpiar.gloss: to clean; to polish; to wipe

meanings.en: to clean; to polish; to wipe
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Limpio el mostrador con un paño seco.
examples.trans: I wipe the counter with a dry cloth.

examples.text: Limpiamos los farolillos para la fiesta.
examples.trans: We polished the lanterns for the party.

meanings.note: Opposite of sucio (dirty).

examples.text: Es una pieza limpia.
examples.trans: It is a clean piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

meanings.note: Plural limones.

examples.text: El limón está aquí.
examples.trans: The lemon is here.

examples.text: Vemos los limones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lemons from the door.

examples.text: Paquita, ahora todo va vía link.
examples.trans: Paquita, everything goes by link nowadays.

examples.text: Yo link
examples.trans: I link

meanings.note: De lino means 'made of linen' (manteles blancos de lino).

examples.text: Planchamos cuatro manteles blancos de lino para las mesas del patio.
examples.trans: We ironed four white linen tablecloths for the courtyard tables.

examples.text: Una camisa de lino es muy fresca para los días de verano.
examples.trans: A linen shirt is very cool for summer days.

meanings.note: Hand-held electric torch in Spain.

examples.text: La linterna está aquí.
examples.trans: The flashlight is here.

examples.text: Vemos las linternas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the flashlights from the door.

meanings.note: Describes smooth wood, flat surfaces, or unpatterned fabric.

examples.text: La madera queda suave y lisa después de lijar.
examples.trans: The wood turns out soft and smooth after sanding.

examples.text: Doblada así, la silla queda completamente lisa.
examples.trans: Folded like this, the chair lies completely flat.

meanings.note: A shopping list is la lista de la compra.

examples.text: Hago la lista de la compra.
examples.trans: I'm making the shopping list.

examples.text: Tu nombre no está en la lista.
examples.trans: Your name isn't on the list.

meanings.note: With estar, means 'ready / all set'; with ser, means 'smart'.

examples.text: El té caliente ya está listo.
examples.trans: The hot tea is ready now.

examples.text: Es una arquitecta muy lista.
examples.trans: She is a very smart architect.

meanings.note: Burner or candle flame (homograph of 3rd sg llama from llamar).

examples.text: La llama está aquí.
examples.trans: The flame is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llamas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the flames from the door.

meanings.note: First- or third-person singular imperfect indicative of "llamar". Used reflexively ("se llamaba") to state someone's name in the past.
Used transitively to describe habitual or ongoing phone calls in the past.

examples.text: Conocí a un chico que se llamaba Carlos...
examples.trans: I met a guy whose name was Carlos...

examples.text: Antes nos llamaba por teléfono todas las semanas para contarnos sus proyectos.
examples.trans: She used to call us on the phone every week to tell us about her projects.

meanings.en: they called, they used to call
meanings.note: Third-person plural imperfect indicative of "llamar". Often used with an impersonal plural subject ("la llamaban" = she used to get called/offered work).

examples.text: Hacía muchas cosas y la llamaban para muchos asuntos.
examples.trans: She did many things and they used to call her for lots of matters.

examples.text: En los años noventa la llamaban de todas las cadenas de televisión.
examples.trans: In the nineties they used to call her from every television network.

meanings.note: Hacer una llamada = to make a phone call.

examples.text: La llamada está aquí.
examples.trans: The phone call is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llamadas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the phone calls from the door.

llamar.gloss: to call; to ring; to be named (llamarse)

meanings.en: to call; to ring; to be named (llamarse)
meanings.note: ¿Cómo se llama? asks someone's name.

examples.text: Soy de aquí, mucho gusto.
examples.trans: I am from here, pleased to meet you.

examples.text: Alguien llamó por teléfono ayer.
examples.trans: Someone called by phone yesterday.

meanings.note: Versatile everyday noun for door keys, shut-off valves, and spanners.

examples.text: La llave está aquí.
examples.trans: The key is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llaves desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the keys from the door.

meanings.note: Diminutive of la llave.

examples.text: La llavecita está aquí.
examples.trans: The little key is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llavecitas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the little keys from the door.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells g -> gu: llegué.

examples.text: Siempre llego diez minutos temprano.
examples.trans: I always arrive ten minutes early.

examples.text: El tren de Madrid llegó en punto.
examples.trans: The train from Madrid arrived on the dot.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; llenarse de means 'to fill up with'.

examples.text: El sol de la mañana llena toda la galería.
examples.trans: Morning sunlight fills the whole sunroom.

examples.text: Llenamos las jarras de cristal con agua fresca.
examples.trans: We fill the glass jugs with cool water.

meanings.note: Opposite of vacío (empty).

examples.text: Es una pieza llena.
examples.trans: It is a full piece.

examples.text: Vaya... ¿con esta lluvia? Todos los hoteles cerca de la estación parecían llenos.
examples.trans: Oh dear... in this rain? Every hotel near the station looked full.

llevar.gloss: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)

meanings.en: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)
meanings.note: Versatile verb for carrying items, wearing clothes/glasses, or duration.

examples.text: Llevo dos tazas calientes al jardín.
examples.trans: I carry two hot cups to the garden.

examples.text: Hoy lleva un abrigo gris oscuro.
examples.trans: Today he is wearing a dark grey coat.

meanings.note: A punto de llorar = ready to cry.

examples.text: Casi lloro de risa con tu historia.
examples.trans: I nearly cried laughing at your story.

examples.text: El niño lloró un segundo nada más.
examples.trans: The child cried for just a second.

meanings.note: Impersonal stem-changing verb (o -> ue: llueve).

examples.text: Hoy llueve mucho en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is raining heavily in Valencia.

examples.text: Anoche llovió hasta las diez.
examples.trans: Last night it rained until ten.

meanings.note: Weather verb mostly used in 3rd-person singular (llovizna, lloviznó).

examples.text: Afuera llovizna suave sobre las baldosas del jardín.
examples.trans: Outside it is drizzling gently on the garden tiles.

examples.text: Aunque lloviznó por la mañana, la tarde abrió clara.
examples.trans: Although it drizzled in the morning, the afternoon cleared up.

meanings.note: Bajo la lluvia = in the rain.

examples.text: La lluvia es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The rain is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la lluvia.
examples.trans: We talk about the rain.

meanings.note: From lluvia, rain: un día lluvioso.

examples.text: Mañana va a ser un día lluvioso.
examples.trans: Tomorrow is going to be a rainy day.

examples.text: El otoño aquí es muy lluvioso.
examples.trans: Autumn here is very rainy.

examples.text: Llévame a Madrid.
examples.trans: Take me to Madrid.

examples.text: Yo Llévame
examples.trans: I Llévame

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)
meanings.note: Direct object pronoun before verbs (lo veo), and neuter article in lo que ('what') or lo mejor ('the best').

examples.text: Ya lo veo encima del estante.
examples.trans: I see it now on the shelf.

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

examples.text: No localizo a Maqui esta tarde.
examples.trans: I can't reach Maqui this afternoon.

examples.text: No consigo localizarte.
examples.trans: I can't manage to reach you.

meanings.note: Feminine plural of "loco". Used both for infatuation ("volver locas a las niñas") and in the colloquial Peninsular idiom "ir como las locas" (to rush around frantically).

examples.text: -Pero ¿qué vas a ser gay? Están todas las niñas del colegio locas.
examples.trans: -What do you mean you're gay? All the girls at school are crazy about you.

examples.text: Paquita, amor, hola. Voy como las locas en medio de las fotos.
examples.trans: Paquita, honey, hi. I'm rushing like crazy in the middle of the photo shoot.

examples.text: Perdonad un momento. Quiero decir que Paquita no está loca.
examples.trans: Excuse me a moment. I want to say that Paquita isn't crazy.

examples.text: Yo loco
examples.trans: I loco

meanings.note: Engine car at the front of a train.

examples.text: La locomotora está aquí.
examples.trans: The locomotive is here.

examples.text: Vemos las locomotoras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the locomotives from the door.

examples.text: Bueno, perdonad este momento de locura entre representantes.
examples.trans: Well, forgive this moment of madness between agents.

examples.text: Yo locura
examples.trans: I locura

examples.text: Vivir la vida es magia. Todos podemos lograr el éxito en la vida.
examples.trans: Living life is magic. All of us can achieve success in life.

examples.text: Hablamos de lograr en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about to achieve at the office.

examples.text: ¿Tienes look para esta noche?
examples.trans: Do you have an outfit for tonight?

examples.text: Me encanta ese look.
examples.trans: I love that outfit.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.text: Los vecinos vienen a desayunar.
examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

examples.text: Chicos, valéis mucho. De verdad, luchad por vuestros sueños.
examples.trans: Guys, you're worth so much. Truly, fight for your dreams.

examples.text: Yo luchar
examples.trans: I luchar

examples.text: Lucía.
examples.trans: Lucía.

examples.text: Yo Lucía
examples.trans: I Lucía

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.

examples.text: ¡Hasta luego, que tengas buen día!
examples.trans: See you later, have a good day!

meanings.note: Un lugar tranquilo = a quiet place.

examples.text: El lugar está aquí.
examples.trans: The place is here.

examples.text: Vemos los lugares desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the place from the door.

meanings.en: Luisito (diminutive of the given name Luis)
meanings.note: Affectionate masculine proper name formed from "Luis" + "-ito". In colloquial and rural Peninsular Spanish, proper names are often preceded by the definite article ("el Luisito").

examples.text: ¿Te acuerdas del Luisito? Claro.
examples.trans: Do you remember Luisito? Of course.

examples.text: Luisito siempre venía a pasar los veranos al pueblo con sus abuelos.
examples.trans: Luisito always used to come spend the summers in the village with his grandparents.

meanings.note: Describes a sunny morning or airy room.

examples.text: Es una pieza luminosa.
examples.trans: It is a bright piece.

examples.text: Qué mañana tan luminosa
examples.trans: What a bright morning

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el lunes, los lunes.

examples.text: El lunes está aquí.
examples.trans: The Monday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los lunes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Mondays from the door.

meanings.note: Plural las luces; a plena luz del sol = in bright sunlight.

examples.text: La luz está aquí.
examples.trans: The light is here.

examples.text: Vemos las luces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lights from the door.

meanings.note: Antepenultimate stress (esdrújula); tener lágrimas en los ojos = to have tears in one's eyes.

examples.text: Al oír el viejo vals, el vecino tenía lágrimas de emoción en los ojos.
examples.trans: On hearing the old waltz, the neighbour had tears of emotion in his eyes.

examples.text: Cortar cebolla siempre me saca alguna lágrima.
examples.trans: Chopping onions always brings a tear to my eye.

meanings.note: Table, ceiling, or reading lamp.

examples.text: La lámpara está aquí.
examples.trans: The lamp is here.

examples.text: Vemos las lámparas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lamps from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los lápices; a lápiz = in pencil.

examples.text: El lápiz está aquí.
examples.trans: The pencil is here.

examples.text: Vemos los lápices desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pencils from the door.

meanings.note: La primera línea = the top line.

examples.text: La línea está aquí.
examples.trans: The line is here.

examples.text: Vemos las líneas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lines from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Vaya lío! = What a mess!

examples.text: El lío está aquí.
examples.trans: The mess is here.

examples.text: Vemos los líos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the messs from the door.

meanings.note: Source-attested name or surname. Name history is supplied separately with its own evidence and uncertainty; no unverified full name is inferred.

examples.text: ¿Ha llamado Maca?
examples.trans: Has Maca called?

examples.text: Maca no ha llamado.
examples.trans: Maca hasn't called.

meanings.note: Source-attested name or surname. Name history is supplied separately with its own evidence and uncertainty; no unverified full name is inferred.

examples.text: Llevamos a Macarena García.
examples.trans: We represent Macarena García.

examples.text: Maca es Macarena.
examples.trans: Maca is Macarena's short name.

meanings.note: Terracotta or ceramic pot for courtyard plants and herbs.

examples.text: Regamos las macetas de hierbas cada mañana.
examples.trans: We water the herb pots every morning.

examples.text: Hay una maceta grande junto a la escalera de piedra.
examples.trans: There is a big plant pot beside the stone stairs.

meanings.note: Diminutive of mazo ('mallet'); standard Spanish term for a felt piano hammer.

examples.text: Cada tecla levanta su propio macillo cubierto de fieltro.
examples.trans: Each key lifts its own felt-covered hammer.

examples.text: El macillo vuelve recto a su sitio después del arreglo.
examples.trans: The hammer returns straight to its place after the repair.

meanings.note: Roble macizo = solid oak.

examples.text: Es una pieza maciza.
examples.trans: It is a solid piece.

examples.text: Roble macizo, de ochenta años. Ni una sola gotera.
examples.trans: Solid oak, eighty years old. Not a single leak.

meanings.note: De madera = wooden.

examples.text: La madera está aquí.
examples.trans: The wood is here.

examples.text: Vemos las maderas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the woods from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Madre mía! is a mild, warm everyday exclamation across Spain.

examples.text: La madre está aquí.
examples.trans: The mother is here.

examples.text: Vemos las madres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the mothers from the door.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Mejor me vuelvo a Madrid.
examples.trans: I'd better head back to Madrid.

examples.text: La agencia está en Madrid.
examples.trans: The agency is in Madrid.

examples.text: Ella sabe mucho de magia. Es la mejor.
examples.trans: She knows a lot about magic. She's the best.

examples.text: Tengo un libro que se titula La magia que hay en ti.
examples.trans: I have a book titled The Magic Within You.

examples.text: Vivir la vida es magia. Todos podemos lograr el éxito en la vida.
examples.trans: Living life is magic. All of us can achieve success in life.

meanings.note: Carries a written accent on í.

examples.text: Es una pieza magnífica.
examples.trans: It is a wonderful piece.

examples.text: ¡Magnífica elección! ¿Quiere miel o mermelada de manzana al lado?
examples.trans: Wonderful choice! Would you like honey or apple jam on the side?

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Magüi trabaja con Paquita.
examples.trans: Magüi works with Paquita.

examples.text: Qué guapa vas, Magüi.
examples.trans: How gorgeous you look, Magüi.

examples.text: No llegó ningún mail.
examples.trans: No email arrived.

examples.text: ¿Has recibido mi mail?
examples.trans: Did you get my email?

meanings.note: Quintessential colloquial Peninsular Spanish adjective ("majo/maja") used to describe someone who is warm, pleasant, and easy to get along with.

examples.text: Es majica la chica, ¿verdad? Sí, muy maja. A ver.
examples.trans: The girl is really sweet, isn't she? Yes, very nice. Let's see.

examples.text: Tu nueva representante parece una mujer muy maja y cercana.
examples.trans: Your new talent agent seems like a very nice and approachable woman.

meanings.note: Feminine diminutive of "majo/maja" formed with the regional suffix "-ico/-ica", typical of La Rioja, Navarre, and Aragon (reflecting Paquita Salas's roots in Navarrete).

examples.text: Es majica la chica, ¿verdad? Sí, muy maja. A ver.
examples.trans: The girl is really sweet, isn't she? Yes, very nice. Let's see.

examples.text: Qué majica es tu sobrina, siempre saluda con una sonrisa.
examples.trans: How sweet your niece is, she always says hello with a smile.

meanings.note: Nada mal = not bad at all; menos mal = thank goodness.

examples.text: Nada mal para el primer día.
examples.trans: Not bad at all for the first day.

examples.text: ¡Menos mal que trajiste paraguas!
examples.trans: Thank goodness you brought an umbrella!

meanings.note: Hacer la maleta = to pack one's suitcase.

examples.text: Esta maleta azul pesa mucho.
examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en la maleta.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in the suitcase.

meanings.note: Shortens to mal before masculine singular nouns (mal tiempo); malas noticias = bad news.

examples.text: Es una pieza mala.
examples.trans: It is a bad piece.

examples.text: Malas noticias
examples.trans: Bad news

meanings.note: Affectionate everyday word for madre; stressed on the final syllable.

examples.text: Mamá abría todas las ventanas los sábados de primavera.
examples.trans: Mom used to open every window on spring Saturdays.

examples.text: Llamaré a mamá esta noche para contarle la noticia.
examples.trans: I will call mom tonight to tell her the news.

examples.text: Mira, soy Paquita Salas, de PS Management.
examples.trans: Look, I'm Paquita Salas, from PS Management.

examples.text: Yo Management
examples.trans: I Management

meanings.note: Everyday noun related to manchar ('to stain').

examples.text: Esa mancha fresca de pintura sale con agua templada.
examples.trans: That fresh smudge of paint comes out with warm water.

examples.text: Revisa que los manteles blancos no tengan ninguna mancha.
examples.trans: Check that the white tablecloths do not have a single stain.

meanings.note: Everyday synonym of enviar.

examples.text: Te mando un mensaje cuando llegue.
examples.trans: I will send you a message when I arrive.

examples.text: Mi primo me mandó naranjas de Valencia.
examples.trans: My cousin sent me oranges from Valencia.

examples.text: Escaparate es el mandil. ¿Dónde tienes el mandil?
examples.trans: Your showcase is the apron. Where do you have your apron?

examples.text: Hablamos de mandil en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about apron at the office.

meanings.note: Third-person singular (él/ella/usted) present indicative of "manejar". Featured prominently in the *Paquita Salas* theme song ("maneja la ciudad", "maneja su suerte").

examples.text: Con el mundo por montera, maneja la ciudad.
examples.trans: Taking the world in her stride, she runs the city.

examples.text: Paquita maneja su agencia de representantes a su manera tradicional.
examples.trans: Paquita runs her talent agency in her own traditional way.

examples.text: Lo preparo a mi manera.
examples.trans: I prepare it my own way.

examples.text: De ninguna manera.
examples.trans: No way at all.

meanings.note: Subirse las mangas means 'to roll up one's sleeves'.

examples.text: Súbete las mangas de la camisa antes de fregar.
examples.trans: Roll up your shirt sleeves before scrubbing.

examples.text: La lluvia repentina me mojó las dos mangas.
examples.trans: The sudden rain got both my sleeves wet.

mango.gloss: handle (of a tool or pan); mango

meanings.en: handle (of a tool or pan); mango
meanings.note: Watch the gender contrast: masculine el mango is a tool handle (or tropical mango fruit), whereas feminine la manga is a shirt or coat sleeve.

examples.text: Golpee la piedra suavemente con el mango de madera.
examples.trans: Tap the stone gently with the wooden handle.

examples.text: Coge la sartén caliente siempre por el mango.
examples.trans: Always hold the hot frying pan by the handle.

meanings.note: Feminine despite ending in -o: la mano, las manos; a mano derecha = on your right-hand side.

examples.text: Gira después de la farmacia a mano derecha.
examples.trans: Turn past the pharmacy on your right-hand side.

examples.text: Tengo las manos limpias.
examples.trans: My hands are clean.

meanings.note: Built from mano ('hand'); in the kitchen, las manoplas are padded oven mitts.

examples.text: Ponte las manoplas gruesas antes de sacar la bandeja del horno.
examples.trans: Put on the thick oven mitts before taking the tray out of the oven.

examples.text: Colgó las manoplas de tela junto a los delantales.
examples.trans: He hung the cloth oven mitts next to the aprons.

meanings.note: Warm wool or cotton bed blanket.

examples.text: La manta está aquí.
examples.trans: The blanket is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mantas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the blankets from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los manteles.

examples.text: El mantel está aquí.
examples.trans: The tablecloth is here.

examples.text: Vemos los manteles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tablecloths from the door.

meanings.note: Conjugates like tener (mantengo, mantienes, mantén, mantuvo).

examples.text: Las tazas gruesas mantienen caliente el té.
examples.trans: Thick cups keep the tea hot.

examples.text: Mantén cerrada la puerta para guardar el calor.
examples.trans: Keep the door closed to hold in the warmth.

meanings.note: Building maintenance and repairs.

examples.text: El mantenimiento es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The maintenance is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el mantenimiento.
examples.trans: We talk about the maintenance.

meanings.note: Spread on warm morning toast.

examples.text: La mantequilla es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The butter is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la mantequilla.
examples.trans: We talk about the butter.

meanings.note: As a masculine noun (el manual) it means a handbook or instruction manual; as an adjective it means 'manual / by hand'.

examples.text: Lee el manual de instrucciones antes de tocar la caldera.
examples.trans: Read the instruction manual before touching the boiler.

examples.text: Nadie quiere que un anfitrión hable como un aburrido manual.
examples.trans: Nobody wants a host to speak like a dry handbook.

meanings.note: Means both 'apple' and a square block of city buildings.

examples.text: La manzana está aquí.
examples.trans: The apple is here.

examples.text: Vemos las manzanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the apples from the door.

meanings.note: Soothing herbal infusion (una manzanilla caliente) popular across Spain.

examples.text: Te preparo una taza caliente de manzanilla para descansar.
examples.trans: I will make you a hot cup of chamomile tea to rest.

examples.text: Las flores secas de manzanilla huelen a campo limpio.
examples.trans: Dried chamomile flowers smell like clean countryside.

meanings.note: Masculine noun despite ending in -a: el mapa antiguo, estos mapas mojados.

examples.text: Mateo dibujó un mapa sencillo para llegar a la ferretería.
examples.trans: Mateo drew a simple map to get to the hardware shop.

examples.text: Extendimos el mapa de Valencia sobre la mesa de madera.
examples.trans: We spread the map of Valencia out on the wooden table.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: ¡Maqui, qué alegría verte!
examples.trans: Maqui, how lovely to see you!

examples.text: No localizo a Maqui esta tarde.
examples.trans: I can't reach Maqui this afternoon.

maquillar.gloss: to put makeup on, to sugarcoat

meanings.en: to sugarcoat, to gloss over, to dress up (figurative)
meanings.note: Figuratively, to soften or disguise an awkward truth, crisis, or bad numbers ("maquillar la realidad").
Literally, to put cosmetics on an actor or oneself ("maquillarse") for stage, film, or daily life.

examples.text: Maquillar un poquito lo que está pasando, ¿no?
examples.trans: Sugarcoat what's going on a little bit, right?

examples.text: Antes de salir al plató tienen que maquillar a todos los actores.
examples.trans: Before going out onto the set, they have to put makeup on all the actors.

meanings.note: Ordinarily masculine in everyday speech (el mar Mediterráneo, salado como el mar), though poetic/seafaring Spanish also uses la mar.

examples.text: Esta cucharada del tarro blanco sabe salada como el mar.
examples.trans: This spoonful from the white jar tastes as salty as the sea.

examples.text: Desde la colina del parque se ve brillar el mar a lo lejos.
examples.trans: From the park hill you can see the sea shining in the distance.

meanings.note: ¡Qué maravilla! = How wonderful!

examples.text: La maravilla está aquí.
examples.trans: The wonder is here.

examples.text: Vemos las maravillas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the wonders from the door.

meanings.note: Warm praise.

examples.text: Es una pieza maravillosa.
examples.trans: It is a wonderful piece.

examples.text: ¡Maravilloso! Ahora estoy lista para un gran desayuno.
examples.trans: Wonderful! Now I am ready for a big breakfast.

meanings.note: On glass or wood, sin marcas means 'streak-free / without marks'.

examples.text: El agua con vinagre no deja marcas en el espejo.
examples.trans: Vinegar water leaves no streaks on the mirror.

examples.text: Haz una marca suave con lápiz junto a la bisagra.
examples.trans: Make a light pencil mark next to the hinge.

marcar.gloss: to show (the time); to dial; to mark

meanings.en: to show (the time); to dial; to mark
meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells c -> qu: marqué.

examples.text: El reloj de la torre marca las doce.
examples.trans: The tower clock shows twelve.

examples.text: Marqué el número de la estación.
examples.trans: I dialled the station number.

meanings.note: Marcharse is everyday Peninsula Spanish for leaving a place.

examples.text: Me marcho pronto para coger el tren.
examples.trans: I am leaving early to catch the train.

examples.text: Los clientes se marcharon muy contentos.
examples.trans: The guests left very happy.

meanings.note: El marco de la puerta = the doorframe.

examples.text: El marco está aquí.
examples.trans: The doorframe is here.

examples.text: Vemos los marcos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doorframes from the door.

meanings.note: Masculine plural of the base lemma 'maricón'. Historically a derogatory slur, in contemporary Peninsular Spanish and throughout Paquita Salas it is frequently used colloquially, affectionately, or as a reclaimed term in entertainment and LGBTQ+ circles.

examples.text: Ha habido maricones toda la historia de la humanidad.
examples.trans: There have been gay men throughout the entire history of humanity.

examples.text: En el mundo del teatro tenemos muchísimos amigos maricones que son como de la familia.
examples.trans: In the theater world we have lots of gay friends who are like family.

meanings.note: Augmentative of 'marica'. While traditionally pejorative, in Peninsular Spanish (and when Paquita Salas argues bluntly for LGBTQ+ representation in period dramas) it is often used either as a reclaimed identity noun or as unvarnished colloquial speech.
Also used in informal slang to call someone timid or hesitant.

examples.text: ¡Toda la historia! ¿No puede haber un maricón en "Puente Viejo"?
examples.trans: All throughout history! Can't there be a gay man in "Puente Viejo"?

examples.text: Él se define como maricón con mucho orgullo delante de todo el mundo.
examples.trans: He defines himself as a gay man with great pride in front of everyone.

meanings.note: In azul marino, invariable or agreeing depending on style.

examples.text: Es una pieza marina.
examples.trans: It is a marine piece.

examples.text: ¿Esa es la vieja maleta azul marino del taller del abuelo?
examples.trans: Is that the old dark-blue bag from Grandfather's workshop?

examples.text: Mariola, por favor.
examples.trans: Mariola, please.

examples.text: Yo Mariola
examples.trans: I Mariola

examples.text: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old".
examples.trans: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old".

examples.text: Yo Mariona
examples.trans: I Mariona

meanings.note: Plural marrones.

examples.text: Es una pieza marrón.
examples.trans: It is a brown piece.

examples.text: Dos pares de zapatos marrones de hombre y jerséis grises.
examples.trans: Two pairs of men's brown shoes and grey sweaters.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el martes, los martes.

examples.text: El martes está aquí.
examples.trans: The Tuesday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los martes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Tuesdays from the door.

meanings.note: Bread or pastry dough.

examples.text: La masa es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The dough is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la masa.
examples.trans: We talk about the dough.

meanings.note: Compound masculine noun (matar + sellos, literally 'stamp-killer'); singular and plural have the exact same form.

examples.text: El matasellos de la postal lleva la fecha del diez de mayo.
examples.trans: The postmark on the postcard bears the date of May tenth.

examples.text: Apenas puedo leer la ciudad bajo la tinta del matasellos.
examples.trans: I can barely read the city name beneath the postmark ink.

meanings.note: In Spanish casting and talent agency jargon (such as at PS Management), 'el material' refers specifically to an actor's videobook, headshots, and recorded scenes sent to casting directors.
General masculine noun referring to raw matter or professional supplies.

examples.text: Hemos visto tu material y nos ha gustado muchísimo.
examples.trans: We've seen your portfolio, and we really liked it.

examples.text: He visto tu material y me ha encantado. Tu primo Álex es muy amigo mío.
examples.trans: I've seen your showreel and loved it. Your cousin Álex is a close friend of mine.

meanings.note: Months are written with a small letter in Spanish: el diez de mayo.

examples.text: Mi cumpleaños es en mayo.
examples.trans: My birthday is in May.

examples.text: Llegamos el tres de mayo.
examples.trans: We arrive on the third of May.

meanings.note: Hermano mayor = older brother; plural mayores.

examples.text: Es una pieza mayor.
examples.trans: It is an older piece.

examples.text: Conoces bien a los hermanos mayores, Mateo.
examples.trans: You know older brothers well, Mateo.

meanings.note: La mañana = the morning; mañana (without article) = tomorrow.

examples.text: Por la mañana servimos café caliente.
examples.trans: In the morning we serve hot coffee.

examples.text: ¡Hasta mañana a las ocho!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow at eight!

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.text: ¿Me pasas la sal, por favor?
examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?

examples.text: Vivo aquí y trabajo aquí.
examples.trans: I live here and I work here.

meanings.note: A medianoche means 'at midnight'.

examples.text: La tormenta de verano empezó justo a medianoche.
examples.trans: The summer storm started right at midnight.

examples.text: A medianoche todo el barrio queda en completo silencio.
examples.trans: At midnight the whole neighbourhood falls completely quiet.

meanings.note: Feminine plural of the base lemma 'media'. In Peninsular Spanish, 'las medias' commonly denotes sheer stockings or tights.

meanings.en: halves; averages (used in idioms like 'a medias')
meanings.note: In the phrase 'a medias', it means 'halfway' or 'fifty-fifty'.

examples.text: Cuidado con las medias, que son caras.
examples.trans: Careful with the stockings, they are expensive.

examples.text: Se me ha hecho una carrera en las medias justo antes de entrar al estreno.
examples.trans: I got a run in my stockings right before walking into the premiere.

meanings.note: Exact measurement or step.

examples.text: La medida está aquí.
examples.trans: The measurement is here.

examples.text: Vemos las medidas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the measurements from the door.

meanings.note: Media vuelta = half-turn (turn around); medio vaso = half a glass.

examples.text: Es una pieza media.
examples.trans: It is a half piece.

examples.text: Oh, qué amable es usted, señor. Solo medio vaso.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

meanings.note: Al mediodía = at noon.

examples.text: El mediodía es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The noon is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el mediodía.
examples.trans: We talk about the noon.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: mido, midió).

examples.text: Mido el ancho de la mesa nueva.
examples.trans: I measure the width of the new table.

examples.text: El carpintero midió la tabla dos veces.
examples.trans: The carpenter measured the plank twice.

meanings.note: Irregular comparative/superlative of bueno; plural mejores.

examples.text: Esta ventana tiene la mejor vista.
examples.trans: This window has the best view.

examples.text: Hoy el radiador calienta mejor.
examples.trans: Today the radiator heats better.

meanings.note: The standard Peninsular Spanish word for 'peach' (whereas Latin American Spanish predominantly uses 'durazno'). Often used in the singular in Spanish to refer collectively to the crop or fruit variety ('hay melocotón').

examples.text: En Navarrete hay mucha alcachofa, mucho pimiento, hay melocotón...
examples.trans: In Navarrete there are lots of artichokes, lots of peppers, there are peaches...

examples.text: De postre nos sacaron melocotón en almíbar bien fresquito.
examples.trans: For dessert they brought us nicely chilled peaches in syrup.

meanings.note: Written accent on í marks hiatus.

examples.text: Carmen toca una melodía suave en el piano de nogal.
examples.trans: Carmen plays a gentle melody on the walnut piano.

examples.text: Todavía recuerdo la melodía de aquella canción.
examples.trans: I still remember the melody of that song.

examples.text: Lo sé de memoria.
examples.trans: I know it by heart.

examples.text: Tiene muy buena memoria.
examples.trans: She has a very good memory.

meanings.note: Por lo menos = at least; echar de menos = to miss; a menos que = unless.

examples.text: Son las ocho menos diez.
examples.trans: It is ten to eight.

examples.text: Por lo menos ya no llueve.
examples.trans: At least it is no longer raining.

meanings.note: Mensaje de voz means 'voice message / voicemail'.

examples.text: Tienes un mensaje nuevo en el teléfono de recepción.
examples.trans: You have a new message on the front desk phone.

examples.text: Dejé un mensaje corto para confirmar la hora.
examples.trans: I left a short message to confirm the time.

examples.text: Vienen a veces a dejarlos por mensajería.
examples.trans: Sometimes people come to drop them off by courier.

examples.text: Yo mensajería
examples.trans: I mensajería

examples.text: Mándame un mensajito luego.
examples.trans: Send me a quick message later.

examples.text: Te dejé dos mensajitos.
examples.trans: I left you two quick messages.

meanings.note: Té de menta = mint tea.

examples.text: La menta es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The mint is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la menta.
examples.trans: We talk about the mint.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la mente'). Featured prominently in the opening theme song of Paquita Salas ('¡Ay, Paquita!', sung by Rosalía): 'que maneja su suerte, un prodigio su mente'.

examples.text: # que maneja su suerte, un prodigio su mente
examples.trans: # that she manages her luck, her mind is a prodigy

examples.text: Tienes que dejar la mente en blanco y concentrarte en el personaje.
examples.trans: You have to clear your mind and focus on the character.

examples.text: Te prometo que hay Goya. Las cartas no mienten.
examples.trans: I promise you there's a Goya. The cards don't lie.

examples.text: Se viene todo abajo. La torre no miente, mi vida. Sí que se te va.
examples.trans: Everything comes crashing down. The Tower doesn't lie, darling. She really is leaving you.

meanings.note: Feminine singular of the base lemma 'mentiroso'. Used both as an adjective ('una persona mentirosa') and as a noun ('una mentirosa'). In conversational Peninsular Spanish, 'que si mentirosa...' reports a string of accusations ('saying I'm a liar...').

examples.text: Que si mentirosa... Que si embustera...
examples.trans: Calling me a liar... Calling me a fraud...

examples.text: No le creas ni una palabra de lo que dice, que es muy mentirosa.
examples.trans: Don't believe a single word of what she says, she is such a liar.

meanings.note: Plural menús; menú del día is Spain's classic midday set menu.

examples.text: Escribimos el menú del miércoles en la pizarra.
examples.trans: We write Wednesday's menu on the board.

examples.text: El menú incluye sopa caliente, pan crujiente y té.
examples.trans: The menu includes hot soup, crusty bread, and tea.

meanings.note: Covered food market in a Spanish neighbourhood.

examples.text: El mercado está aquí.
examples.trans: The market is here.

examples.text: Vemos los mercados desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the markets from the door.

meanings.en: he/she/it deserves, merits; it is worth
meanings.note: Third-person singular present indicative of the base verb 'merecer' (to deserve). Commonly used in phrases like 'lo merece' (it's worth it) and 'merece la pena' (it's worthwhile).

examples.text: pero he dicho: mira, me hago el viaje, que la noticia lo merece.
examples.trans: but I said to myself: look, I'll make the trip, because the news is worth it.

examples.text: Esa actriz se merece un premio por todo el esfuerzo que ha hecho.
examples.trans: That actress deserves an award for all the effort she has put in.

meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg merezco.

examples.text: Este café merece cinco estrellas.
examples.trans: This coffee deserves five stars.

examples.text: Después de correr, mereces un descanso.
examples.trans: After running, you deserve a rest.

examples.text: En esta agencia creemos en la meritocracia.
examples.trans: At this agency we believe in meritocracy.

examples.text: Aquí todo funciona por meritocracia.
examples.trans: Here everything works by meritocracy.

meanings.note: Fruit preserve eaten at breakfast.

examples.text: La mermelada está aquí.
examples.trans: The jam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mermeladas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the jams from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los meses.

examples.text: El mes está aquí.
examples.trans: The month is here.

examples.text: Vemos los meses desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the months from the door.

meanings.note: Dining, cafe, or courtyard table.

examples.text: La mesa está aquí.
examples.trans: The table is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mesas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tables from the door.

meanings.note: Diminutive of la mesa.

examples.text: La mesita está aquí.
examples.trans: The small table is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mesitas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the small tables from the door.

meanings.note: With de, algo de metal or una caja de metal describes something made of metal.

examples.text: Algo de metal acaba de moverse dentro del paquete.
examples.trans: Something metal just moved inside the parcel.

examples.text: Limpiamos el tirador de metal de la puerta principal.
examples.trans: We polished the metal handle on the front door.

meter.gloss: to put in; to tuck in

meanings.en: to put in; to tuck in
meanings.note: Everyday Spanish verb specifically for putting something inside a pocket, bag, or drawer.

examples.text: Meto las llaves en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: I put the keys in my pocket.

examples.text: Metimos las sillas dentro por la lluvia.
examples.trans: We brought the chairs inside because of the rain.

meanings.note: Unit of length (diez metros) or city metro.

examples.text: El metro está aquí.
examples.trans: The metre is here.

examples.text: Vemos los metros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the metres from the door.

meanings.note: La persiana metálica = the metal shop shutter.

examples.text: Es una pieza metálica.
examples.trans: It is a metal piece.

examples.text: ¡Bien! ¿Está abierta la persiana metálica?
examples.trans: Good! Is the metal shutter open?

mezclar.gloss: to mix; to stir in; to blend

meanings.en: to mix; to stir in; to blend
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; la mezcla is the noun 'mixture'.

examples.text: Mezcla un dado frío de mantequilla en la crema caliente.
examples.trans: Stir a cold cube of butter into the hot curd.

examples.text: En un bol grande mezclamos la harina con la almendra molida.
examples.trans: In a large bowl we mixed the flour with the ground almond.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.text: Mi maleta es azul marino.
examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

examples.text: Perdón, una cosita. ¿Puedo coger el micro un momento?
examples.trans: Excuse me, just one little thing. Can I borrow the mic for a moment?

examples.text: Yo micro
examples.trans: I micro

examples.text: Hice teatro y microteatro.
examples.trans: I did theatre and micro-theatre.

examples.text: Vamos al microteatro en Madrid.
examples.trans: We're going to micro-theatre in Madrid.

meanings.note: Tener miedo = be afraid; entrarle miedo = to panic.

examples.text: El miedo es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The fear is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el miedo.
examples.trans: We talk about the fear.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la miel.

examples.text: La miel es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The honey is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la miel.
examples.trans: We talk about the honey.

meanings.note: Links two simultaneous actions.

examples.text: Espera aquí mientras abro la puerta.
examples.trans: Wait here while I open the door.

examples.text: Preparo el té mientras sale el pan.
examples.trans: I make the tea while the bread comes out.

meanings.note: Singular la miga refers to a single crumb or the soft interior of a loaf (opposite of la corteza); plural las migas means crumbs.

examples.text: La hogaza recién hecha tiene la corteza crujiente y la miga tierna.
examples.trans: The freshly baked loaf has a crisp crust and a tender crumb.

examples.text: Le gustó tanto la tarta de limón que no dejó ni una miga.
examples.trans: She liked the lemon tart so much that she did not leave a single crumb.

examples.text: Mira el de Miguel Ángel Muñoz.
examples.trans: Look at Miguel Ángel Muñoz's one.

examples.text: Yo Miguel
examples.trans: I Miguel

meanings.note: A mil = racing at a thousand an hour.

examples.text: Gracias mil veces por tu ayuda.
examples.trans: Thanks a thousand times for your help.

examples.text: El corazón me va a mil.
examples.trans: My heart is racing at a thousand an hour.

meanings.note: Hacer milagros / obrar milagros = 'to work miracles / work wonders'.

examples.text: Dormir ocho horas seguidas hace milagros cuando estás cansado.
examples.trans: Sleeping eight hours straight works wonders when you are tired.

examples.text: Es un milagro que quedaran tres trozos de tarta para nosotros.
examples.trans: It is a miracle that three slices of tart were left for us.

examples.text: Hombre, como seis millones de personas.
examples.trans: Come on, around six million people.

examples.text: Yo millón
examples.trans: I millón

meanings.note: Veinte milímetros = twenty millimetres.

examples.text: El milímetro está aquí.
examples.trans: The millimetre is here.

examples.text: Vemos los milímetros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the millimetres from the door.

examples.text: ¿Tenéis cinco minutitos para mí?
examples.trans: Do you have five quick minutes for me?

examples.text: Va a ser solo un minutito.
examples.trans: It will only be one quick minute.

meanings.note: En cinco minutos = in five minutes.

examples.text: El minuto está aquí.
examples.trans: The minute is here.

examples.text: Vemos los minutos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the minutes from the door.

miraban.gloss: they were looking at, they watched

meanings.en: they were looking at, they watched, they used to look
meanings.note: Third-person plural imperfect indicative of the base verb 'mirar' (to look at, to watch), describing an ongoing or habitual action in the past.

examples.text: Es que me miraban como si fuera una estrella.
examples.trans: They were looking at me as if I were a star.

examples.text: En la sala de espera todas las candidatas se miraban de reojo.
examples.trans: In the waiting room all the candidates were looking at each other out of the corner of their eye.

meanings.note: Feminine noun derived from 'mirar'. In acting, headshots, and camera direction, 'la mirada' refers to the angle, intensity, and expression of an actor's eyes.

examples.text: La mirada queda mejor así.
examples.trans: The gaze looks better like this.

examples.text: Tiene una mirada muy expresiva que enamora a la cámara desde el primer plano.
examples.trans: She has a very expressive gaze that makes the camera fall in love from the first close-up.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.en: I look at, I check, I'll take a look
meanings.note: First-person singular present indicative of the base verb 'mirar' (to look at, to check). In colloquial Peninsular Spanish, the present tense ('lo miro') is routinely used with immediate future force ('I'll check it right now').

examples.text: Lo miro, pero que no tengo apuntado
examples.trans: I'll check it, though I don't have it written down.

examples.text: Espera un momento que miro en el bolso a ver si llevo las llaves.
examples.trans: Wait a moment while I check my bag to see if I have the keys.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, meaning right now, mismo strengthens the time word ahora. Now comes from ahora; mismo supplies emphasis without agreeing with a person in this expression.

examples.text: Tenemos el mismo trabajo.
examples.trans: We have the same job.

examples.text: Ahora mismo estoy ocupada.
examples.trans: I am busy right now.

meanings.note: Resolver un misterio = to solve a mystery.

examples.text: La llave escondida abrió el misterio de la habitación nueve.
examples.trans: The hidden key unlocked the mystery of Room Nine.

examples.text: Todavía es un misterio qué guardaron dentro de aquella lata.
examples.trans: It is still a mystery what they put inside that tin.

meanings.note: Describes a mystery caller or note.

examples.text: Es una pieza misteriosa.
examples.trans: It is a mysterious piece.

examples.text: Pues claro que vine. ¿Por qué te escondiste detrás de una nota misteriosa?
examples.trans: Of course I came. Why did you hide behind a mystery note?

meanings.note: A mitad de precio = at half price.

examples.text: La mitad está aquí.
examples.trans: The half is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mitades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the halves from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el miércoles, los miércoles.

examples.text: El miércoles está aquí.
examples.trans: The Wednesday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los miércoles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Wednesdays from the door.

examples.text: Primero has dejado la mochila.
examples.trans: First you put down your backpack.

examples.text: Llevo el guion en la mochila.
examples.trans: I carry the script in my backpack.

examples.text: Muy de moda ese papel. ¿Y por qué lloras, corazón?
examples.trans: That kind of role is very in style. And why are you crying, sweetheart?

examples.text: Todos me han dicho que tú estás muy pasada de moda, que necesito un cambio.
examples.trans: Everyone has told me you're really out of date, and that I need a change.

examples.text: Poniéndome al día con esto. Está muy de moda.
examples.trans: Catching up with this trend. It's very fashionable.

meanings.note: Refers to a design model or example; as a person (el/la modelo), takes common gender.

examples.text: El modelo está aquí.
examples.trans: The model is here.

examples.text: Vemos los modelos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the models from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of antiguo.

examples.text: Es una pieza moderna.
examples.trans: It is a modern piece.

examples.text: ¡Caliente! ¿Oye eso, Clara? ¡Agua caliente moderna, fiable y de cinco estrellas!
examples.trans: Hot! Do you hear that, Clara? Modern, reliable, five-star hot water!

meanings.note: Opposite of seco (dry).

examples.text: Es una pieza mojada.
examples.trans: It is a wet piece.

examples.text: Porque las contraventanas de madera mojadas suavizan el eco de los adoquines...
examples.trans: Because wet wooden shutters soften the echo from the cobblestones...

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: La lluvia moja los adoquines grises.
examples.trans: The rain wets the grey cobblestones.

examples.text: Perdón por mojar la entrada con el paraguas.
examples.trans: Sorry for wetting the entrance with my umbrella.

meanings.note: Siento molestarle = sorry to bother you.

examples.text: Perdona, ¿te molesto un segundo?
examples.trans: Excuse me, am I bothering you for a second?

examples.text: Aquí el ruido de los coches no molesta.
examples.trans: Here car noise does not bother anyone.

meanings.note: Past participle of moler ('to grind') used as a culinary adjective: almendra molida ('ground almonds'), café molido ('ground coffee').

examples.text: Mezcla doscientos gramos de almendra molida con mantequilla.
examples.trans: Mix two hundred grams of ground almonds with butter.

examples.text: Me encanta el aroma del café recién molido por la mañana.
examples.trans: I love the aroma of freshly ground coffee in the morning.

meanings.note: De momento = for now.

examples.text: El momento está aquí.
examples.trans: The moment is here.

examples.text: Vemos los momentos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the moments from the door.

meanings.note: Metal coin.

examples.text: La moneda está aquí.
examples.trans: The coin is here.

examples.text: Vemos las monedas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coins from the door.

meanings.note: Small hinged window pane set above a door to let air circulate.

examples.text: Abre un poco el montante alto para ventilar el pasillo.
examples.trans: Open the high transom window slightly to air the hallway.

examples.text: La luz de la mañana entra por el montante de cristal.
examples.trans: Morning light comes in through the glass fanlight.

examples.text: Pues he montado una banda. ¡Estoy supercontenta!
examples.trans: Well, I've put together a band. I'm super happy!

examples.text: Hablamos de montar en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about put together, formed at the office.

meanings.note: Used literally for mountains and figuratively for a huge heap.

examples.text: Esta miel oscura viene de las flores de montaña.
examples.trans: This dark honey comes from mountain flowers.

examples.text: Tenemos una montaña de ropa blanca para doblar.
examples.trans: We have a mountain of white linen to fold.

meanings.en: montera (traditional bullfighter's cap); fearless stride (in 'por montera')
meanings.note: Feminine noun designating the traditional black cap worn by a bullfighter. Today it is most frequently encountered in the idiom 'ponerse el mundo por montera' (literally 'to wear the world as one's hat', meaning to disregard convention and take on the world boldly), as heard in the Paquita Salas theme song.

examples.text: # Con el mundo por montera, maneja la ciudad.
examples.trans: # Taking the world in her stride, she manages the city.

examples.text: Paquita se puso el mundo por montera y montó su propia agencia de representación.
examples.trans: Paquita took on the world fearlessly and set up her own talent agency.

meanings.en: a lot, tons, loads (in 'un montón' / 'un montón de')
meanings.note: Masculine noun literally meaning 'heap' or 'pile', used ubiquitously in colloquial Peninsular Spanish as a quantifier ('un montón de cosas' = 'loads of things') or adverbial intensifier ('me gusta un montón' = 'I like him a lot').
In the expression 'ser del montón', it means to be average, unremarkable, or run-of-the-mill.

examples.text: Cuido de tu madre y jugamos a un montón de cosas:
examples.trans: I take care of your mother and we play a lot of things:

examples.text: Para todo. Desde luego me gusta un montón y hace reír.
examples.trans: For everything. I definitely like him a lot and he makes people laugh.

examples.text: Tranquilas, que no muerdo.
examples.trans: Relax, I don't bite.

examples.text: El perro no muerde nunca.
examples.trans: The dog never bites.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue in present: muere; o -> u in preterite 3rd: murió).

examples.text: Las flores sin agua mueren pronto.
examples.trans: Flowers without water die quickly.

examples.text: Su abuelo murió hace tres inviernos.
examples.trans: His grandfather died three winters ago.

examples.text: Quiero kétchup y mucha mostaza.
examples.trans: I want ketchup and lots of mustard.

examples.text: La salsa lleva un poco de mostaza.
examples.trans: The sauce has a bit of mustard.

meanings.note: Reception desk or shop counter.

examples.text: El mostrador está aquí.
examples.trans: The counter is here.

examples.text: Vemos los mostradores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the counters from the door.

examples.text: Hay que mostrar el producto.
examples.trans: You have to show the product.

examples.text: Te muestro las fotos nuevas.
examples.trans: I'll show you the new photos.

meanings.note: Un viejo motivo familiar = an old family reason.

examples.text: El motivo está aquí.
examples.trans: The reason is here.

examples.text: Vemos los motivos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the reasons from the door.

examples.text: ¿No conduces ni moto?
examples.trans: Don't you even ride a motorbike?

examples.text: Viene al trabajo en moto.
examples.trans: He comes to work by motorbike.

meanings.note: Plural motores.

examples.text: El motor está aquí.
examples.trans: The engine is here.

examples.text: Vemos los motores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the engines from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: muevo).

examples.text: Movemos la mesa bajo la sombra.
examples.trans: We move the table into the shade.

examples.text: El viento suave movió las hojas.
examples.trans: The gentle breeze stirred the leaves.

meanings.note: Agrees before nouns (mucha agua, muchos años); invariable after verbs (llueve mucho).

examples.text: Hoy tenemos mucho trabajo.
examples.trans: Today we have a lot of work.

examples.text: Muchas gracias por el café.
examples.trans: Thank you very much for the coffee.

meanings.note: Superlative degree of mucho.

examples.text: Lo siento muchísimo, señora.
examples.trans: I am terribly sorry, madam.

examples.text: Me alegro muchísimo por ti.
examples.trans: I am so happy for you.

meanings.note: Hacer la mudanza = to move house.

examples.text: La mudanza está aquí.
examples.trans: The house move is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mudanzas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the house moves from the door.

meanings.note: Describes a piano key that makes no sound or a silent letter (la hache muda).

examples.text: Mañana arreglaremos la única tecla muda del teclado.
examples.trans: Tomorrow we will fix the single silent key on the keyboard.

examples.text: Todos se quedaron mudos al ver la sala iluminada.
examples.trans: Everyone was left speechless seeing the lit room.

meanings.note: The plural los muebles means furniture in general.

examples.text: Este mueble es de mi abuelo.
examples.trans: This piece of furniture is my grandfather's.

examples.text: Necesitamos muebles para el piso nuevo.
examples.trans: We need furniture for the new flat.

meanings.note: First-person singular present indicative of the stem-changing base verb 'morir' (o > ue). Very commonly used reflexively ('me muero') both literally and for dramatic exaggeration ('me muero de hambre/vergüenza').

examples.text: Un día me muero y no estás.
examples.trans: One day I die and you are not here.

examples.text: Ay, que me muero de vergüenza si tengo que cantar en directo.
examples.trans: Oh, I'll die of embarrassment if I have to sing live.

examples.text: (Mugido)
examples.trans: Moo.

examples.text: Yo Mugido
examples.trans: I Mugido

meanings.note: Plural las mujeres.

examples.text: Una mujer con paraguas azul preguntó por el café.
examples.trans: A woman with a blue umbrella asked about the café.

examples.text: Dos mujeres del barrio leen juntas junto al piano.
examples.trans: Two women from the neighbourhood read together by the piano.

examples.text: Yo le enseñé a moverse en este mundillo.
examples.trans: I taught him how to get around in this little world.

examples.text: Yo mundillo
examples.trans: I mundillo

meanings.note: Todo el mundo literally 'all the world' means 'everyone'.

examples.text: El mundo está aquí.
examples.trans: The world is here.

examples.text: Vemos los mundos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the worlds from the door.

meanings.note: Plural municipales.

examples.text: Es una pieza municipal.
examples.trans: It is a municipal piece.

examples.text: Bien pensado, Clara. Javier lee normas municipales de edificios cada semana.
examples.trans: Smart thinking, Clara. Javier reads city building rules every single week.

meanings.note: Third-person singular preterite indicative of the stem-changing base verb 'morir' (which undergoes o > u vowel raising in third-person preterite forms: 'murió', 'murieron'). Often used pronominally as 'se murió'.

examples.text: que yo creo que se murió.
examples.trans: who I think died.

examples.text: ¿Se murió Carlos?
examples.trans: Did Carlos die?

meanings.note: Exterior or structural masonry wall.

examples.text: El muro está aquí.
examples.trans: The thick wall is here.

examples.text: Vemos los muros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the thick walls from the door.

examples.text: Tele de momento no. Teatro, musical, cabaret.
examples.trans: Not television for now. Theatre, musicals, cabaret.

examples.text: Hablamos de musical en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about musical at the office.

meanings.note: Shortened form of mucho used before adjectives and adverbs.

examples.text: El bizcocho está muy rico.
examples.trans: The sponge cake is very tasty.

examples.text: Camina muy rápido por el puente.
examples.trans: She walks very fast across the bridge.

examples.text: Mira el de Miguel Ángel Muñoz.
examples.trans: Look at Miguel Ángel Muñoz's one.

examples.text: Yo Muñoz
examples.trans: I Muñoz

meanings.en: my (quoted English first-person singular possessive determiner; Spanish equivalent: mi / mis)
meanings.note: Quoted English audition word from Mariona Terés's self-tape and casting slate in Paquita Salas ("Hello, my name is Mariona Terés..."), showcasing the comedic recurring trope of Spanish actors tackling English-language auditions with rudimentary textbook phrases.

examples.text: En la prueba en inglés se presentó diciendo: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old".
examples.trans: At the English audition she introduced herself by saying: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old".

examples.text: Paquita repite "my darling" con acento de La Rioja cuando intenta impresionar a los productores extranjeros.
examples.trans: Paquita repeats "my darling" with a La Rioja accent when she tries to impress foreign producers.

meanings.note: Carries a written accent on á.

examples.text: Es una pieza mágica.
examples.trans: It is a magical piece.

examples.text: ¿En qué posada mágica has venido a parar, hermanito?
examples.trans: What kind of magical guesthouse did you stumble into, little brother?

meanings.note: Accented más means 'more / most'; de más = extra.

examples.text: ¿Quiere un poco más de té?
examples.trans: Would you like a little more tea?

examples.text: Es la habitación más tranquila.
examples.trans: It is the quietest room.

examples.text: Esta aplicación tiene un máximo de palabras.
examples.trans: This app has a word limit.

examples.text: Yo máximo
examples.trans: I máximo

examples.text: Métete más.
examples.trans: Get further in.

examples.text: Yo Métete
examples.trans: I Métete

meanings.note: Mostly heard in la cinta métrica, the tape measure.

examples.text: ¿Tienes una cinta métrica?
examples.trans: Do you have a tape measure?

examples.text: Usamos el sistema métrico.
examples.trans: We use the metric system.

meanings.note: Accented pronoun after para, por, a, de, sin (distinct from possessive mi).

examples.text: Esta taza de té es para mí.
examples.trans: This cup of tea is for me.

examples.text: Déjemelo a mí, por favor.
examples.trans: Leave it to me, please.

meanings.note: Stressed possessive (el mío, la mía, los míos, las mías); ¡Madre mía! = Goodness me!

examples.text: Esa maleta azul es mía.
examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

examples.text: Un amigo mío vive en esta calle.
examples.trans: A friend of mine lives on this street.

míralo.gloss: look at it, check it; look at him

meanings.en: look at it, check it; look at him
meanings.note: Second-person singular (tú) affirmative imperative of the base verb 'mirar' ('mira') fused with the masculine/neuter direct object enclitic pronoun 'lo'. The written acute accent is added to maintain stress on the stem syllable ('mí-ra-lo').

examples.text: Sí, míralo en la agenda, Paquita, que sí.
examples.trans: Yes, check it in the planner, Paquita, really.

examples.text: Míralo bien antes de firmar el contrato con la productora.
examples.trans: Look it over carefully before signing the contract with the production company.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (short for 'teléfono móvil'). It is the standard Peninsular Spanish word for a cell phone (contrasting with 'celular' in Latin America). Paquita's loud rooster ringtone on her 'móvil' is a signature running gag in the series.

meanings.en: motive (for an action or crime); mobile (adjective)
meanings.note: Also used as a noun meaning 'motive' ('el móvil del crimen') and as an adjective meaning 'movable, mobile'.

examples.text: (Kikirikí como tono de móvil)
examples.trans: (Cock-a-doodle-doo as a mobile phone ringtone)

examples.text: No me apagues el móvil, que nos tienen que llamar los del casting hoy mismo.
examples.trans: Don't turn off your cell phone on me, the casting people are supposed to call us today.

meanings.note: Clases de música = music lessons.

examples.text: La música es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The music is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la música.
examples.trans: We talk about the music.

nada.gloss: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)

meanings.en: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)
meanings.note: No pasa nada = no problem; nada de... = no ... at all.

examples.text: Tranquilo, no pasa nada.
examples.trans: Easy now, there is no problem at all.

examples.text: No queda nada de mantequilla.
examples.trans: There is no butter left at all.

meanings.note: Requires no before the verb when nadie follows (no hay nadie).

examples.text: Todavía no hay nadie en el patio.
examples.trans: There is nobody in the courtyard yet.

examples.text: Nadie conoce mejor este edificio.
examples.trans: Nobody knows this building better.

meanings.en: name (quoted English noun; Spanish equivalent: el nombre)
meanings.note: Quoted English audition word from Mariona Terés's English presentation ("Hello, my name is Mariona Terés...") in Paquita Salas, illustrating how actors at PS Management rely on memorized schoolbook English lines during international castings.

examples.text: Empezó su presentación en inglés con la frase: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old".
examples.trans: She began her introduction in English with the sentence: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old".

examples.text: En cuanto el director de casting le dijo "tell me your name", se puso nerviosísima.
examples.trans: As soon as the casting director told her "tell me your name", she got terribly nervous.

meanings.note: Zumo de naranja = orange juice.

examples.text: La naranja está aquí.
examples.trans: The orange is here.

examples.text: Vemos las naranjas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the oranges from the door.

meanings.note: Plural las narices.

examples.text: La nariz está aquí.
examples.trans: The nose is here.

examples.text: Vemos las narices desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the noses from the door.

meanings.en: swimming (as a sport, exercise, or scheduled class)
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la natación'). In everyday Peninsular Spanish, 'tener natación' means to have swimming class or practice, while casual recreational swimming is usually expressed with the verb 'nadar' or 'bañarse'.

examples.text: Oye, que nos vamos, que tenemos natación, ¿verdad, Luisito?
examples.trans: Hey, we're leaving, we have swimming lessons, right, Luisito?

examples.text: El médico le recomendó hacer natación dos veces por semana para la espalda.
examples.trans: The doctor recommended she go swimming twice a week for her back.

examples.text: Natalie Portman es un ejemplo perfecto.
examples.trans: Natalie Portman is a perfect example.

examples.text: Yo Natalie
examples.trans: I Natalie

examples.text: Es una actriz muy natural.
examples.trans: She is a very natural actress.

examples.text: Prefiero zumo de naranja natural.
examples.trans: I prefer fresh orange juice.

meanings.en: Navarrete (historic town and municipality in La Rioja, northern Spain)
meanings.note: Proper place name (capitalized 'Navarrete'), located near Logroño on the Camino de Santiago and renowned for its pottery and wine. In Paquita Salas, it is Paquita's cherished hometown and a symbol of her down-to-earth provincial roots.

examples.text: Bienvenidos a Navarrete.
examples.trans: Welcome to Navarrete.

examples.text: Navarrete... Navarrete para mí lo es todo. Es conocida por su alfarería.
examples.trans: Navarrete... Navarrete is everything to me. It is known for its pottery.

meanings.en: of or from Navarrete; a native or inhabitant of Navarrete
meanings.note: Formal demonym (gentilicio) for the municipality of Navarrete in La Rioja. Like other Spanish demonyms ending in '-ense', it has the same form for both masculine and feminine singular ('el/la navarretense').

examples.text: Yo soy navarreteña de corazón o navarretense.
examples.trans: I am a Navarrete local at heart, or a Navarretan.

examples.text: La tradición alfarera navarretense es famosa en toda La Rioja.
examples.trans: The Navarrete pottery tradition is famous throughout La Rioja.

meanings.en: female native of Navarrete; of or from Navarrete (feminine)
meanings.note: Feminine singular form of the base lemma 'navarreteño', an affectionate alternative demonym for someone from Navarrete (La Rioja), used by Paquita alongside the standard 'navarretense'.

examples.text: Yo soy navarreteña de corazón o navarretense.
examples.trans: I am a Navarrete woman at heart, or a Navarretan.

examples.text: Como buena navarreteña, Paquita siempre lleva productos de su tierra a la oficina.
examples.trans: Like a good woman from Navarrete, Paquita always brings produce from her homeland to the office.

meanings.note: Feminine noun (capitalized as 'Navidad' or 'Navidades' when referring to the holiday period). In Peninsular Spanish, both the singular ('en Navidad') and the plural ('en Navidades', 'felices Navidades') are widely used for the festive season from Christmas Eve through Epiphany (Reyes).

examples.text: Ay, pero que me digo: "¿Ya es Navidad?".
examples.trans: Oh, and I say to myself: "Is it Christmas already?".

examples.text: En Navidad siempre nos juntamos toda la familia en el pueblo para cenar.
examples.trans: At Christmas the whole family always gets together in the village for dinner.

examples.text: Aakif Ndel.
examples.trans: Aakif Ndel.

examples.text: Yo Ndel
examples.trans: I Ndel

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Necesito un bolígrafo para firmar.
examples.trans: I need a pen to sign.

examples.text: ¿Necesitan ustedes alguna toalla más?
examples.trans: Do you all need another towel?

meanings.note: Feminine singular of the base adjective 'negro'. In addition to literal color (such as a phone or camera screen going black: 'se me ha puesto negra'), it appears in idiomatic Peninsular expressions like 'ponerse negra' (to get furious or exasperated) and 'tener la negra' (to have a streak of bad luck).

examples.text: ¿Ves? ¡Es que yo no sé hacer "zoom"! ¡Uy! Se me ha puesto negra y todo.
examples.trans: See? I just do not know how to zoom! Oops! It has gone completely black.

examples.text: Me pongo negra cada vez que no me cogen el teléfono en la cadena.
examples.trans: I get furious every time they don't pick up my call at the network.

meanings.en: little black ones (diminutive plural of negro); used in Spanish titles of Agatha Christie's 'And Then There Were None' ('Diez negritos')
meanings.note: Masculine plural diminutive of 'negro' ('negrito'). In 'Paquita Salas', a character comically inflates the title of the classic mystery play 'Diez negritos' into 'Cien negritos'.
Also used colloquially to refer to shots or small cups of black coffee ('cafés solos').

examples.text: Oye, que mañana voy al estreno de "Cien negritos".
examples.trans: Hey, tomorrow I'm going to the premiere of "A Hundred Little Indians".

examples.text: ¿La obra de Agatha Christie no se llamaba "Diez negritos" en vez de cien?
examples.trans: Wasn't the Agatha Christie play called "Ten Little Indians" instead of a hundred?

meanings.note: Café solo / negro = black coffee.

examples.text: Es una pieza negra.
examples.trans: It is a black piece.

examples.text: ¡Buenos días de nuevo, señora Carmen! ¿Quiere café o té negro?
examples.trans: Good morning again, Madam Carmen! Would you like coffee or black tea?

examples.text: Llevas a esta nena al casting.
examples.trans: You take this girl to the audition.

examples.text: Ven aquí, nena.
examples.trans: Come here, kiddo.

examples.text: En nuestra oficina decimos no al nepotismo.
examples.trans: In our office we say no to nepotism.

examples.text: Entró por su talento, sin nepotismo.
examples.trans: She got in on her talent, without nepotism.

examples.text: Qué nervios.
examples.trans: What nerves.

examples.text: Yo nervio
examples.trans: I nervio

meanings.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective 'nervioso'. Takes 'estar' ('estoy muy nerviosa') or 'ponerse' for temporary jitters and stage fright, and 'ser' for an inherently high-strung temperament.

examples.text: Estoy muy nerviosa. Cariño, está muy bien.
examples.trans: I am very nervous. Honey, it's very good.

examples.text: Siempre me pongo muy nerviosa justo antes de entrar a una prueba de cámara.
examples.trans: I always get very nervous right before going into a screen test.

meanings.note: Feminine plural form of the adjective 'nervioso'. Used with 'estar' ('estáis muy nerviosas') to describe a group of women experiencing temporary anxiety or pre-audition jitters.

examples.text: que estáis muy nerviosas.
examples.trans: that you girls are very nervous.

examples.text: Las actrices estaban muy nerviosas en el camerino antes de salir al escenario.
examples.trans: The actresses were very nervous in the dressing room before going out on stage.

meanings.note: Ponerse nervioso = to get nervous.

examples.text: Es una pieza nerviosa.
examples.trans: It is a nervous piece.

examples.text: ¿Nervioso por un tren de madera? Esta historia es cada hora más rara.
examples.trans: Nervous about a wooden train? This story gets stranger every hour.

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for the kitchen refrigerator.

examples.text: La nevera está aquí.
examples.trans: The fridge is here.

examples.text: Vemos las neveras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the fridges from the door.

meanings.note: Ni... ni... = neither... nor...; ni una gota = not a single drop.

examples.text: No cae ni una sola gota.
examples.trans: Not a single drop is falling.

examples.text: No tengo ni papel ni bolígrafo.
examples.trans: I have neither paper nor pen.

meanings.note: Feminine: la nieta; los nietos = grandchildren / grandsons.

examples.text: El nieto está aquí.
examples.trans: The grandson is here.

examples.text: Vemos los nietos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the grandsons from the door.

meanings.note: Blanco como la nieve ('white as snow') is a classic idiom for spotless white.

examples.text: Los manteles planchados quedaron blancos como la nieve.
examples.trans: The ironed tablecloths came out white as snow.

examples.text: En invierno se ve nieve limpia en las cumbres lejanas.
examples.trans: In winter you can see clean snow on the distant peaks.

ninguno.gloss: no; none; neither (ninguno de los dos)

meanings.en: no; none; neither (ninguno de los dos)
meanings.note: Shortens to ningún before masculine singular nouns (ningún edificio).

examples.text: Ningún edificio antiguo se derriba aquí.
examples.trans: No historic building is torn down here.

examples.text: Ninguno de los dos se marchó.
examples.trans: Neither of the two walked away.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural 'niveles'). Frequently used in the prepositional construction 'a nivel + [adjective]' ('a nivel europeo' = 'at a European level / across Europe', 'a nivel nacional' = 'nationwide').
Often used to assess professional skill or prestige ('una actriz de mucho nivel').

examples.text: de una cosita de época que se va a hacer a nivel europeo.
examples.trans: for a little period piece that is going to be done at a European level.

examples.text: Necesitamos que tu nivel de inglés sea alto para este rodaje internacional.
examples.trans: We need your level of English to be high for this international shoot.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb built from nivel ('level'); used for levelling wobbly tables, floors, or shelves.

examples.text: Mateo niveló la mesa del jardín con una cuña de madera.
examples.trans: Mateo levelled the garden table with a wooden wedge.

examples.text: Hay que nivelar bien el estante antes de poner las tazas.
examples.trans: We must level the shelf properly before putting the cups on it.

meanings.note: Feminine form of 'niño'. Frequently used in temporal expressions like 'de niña' or 'cuando era niña' ('as a little girl / when I was a child').
Commonly used in colloquial Peninsular Spanish as an affectionate or emphatic form of address among adult women ('Niña, escúchame').

examples.text: Niña, el pico. Es Lidia San José, la niña de "¡Ala... Dina!".
examples.trans: Girl, watch your mouth. She's Lidia San José, the girl from "¡Ala... Dina!".

examples.text: # señora, niña bonita.
