examples.trans: # lady, pretty girl.

meanings.en: girls, female children, schoolgirls (plural of niña)
meanings.note: Feminine plural of 'niña' (base lemma 'niño'). In informal Peninsular Spanish, it is also affectionately used for young women ('mis niñas' = 'my girls', how Paquita refers to the actresses she represents).

examples.text: -Pero ¿qué vas a ser gay? Están todas las niñas del colegio locas.
examples.trans: -How could you possibly be gay? All the girls at school are crazy about you.

examples.text: Siempre está rodeado de niñas que le piden fotos y autógrafos.
examples.trans: He is always surrounded by girls asking him for photos and autographs.

meanings.note: Feminine: la niña.

examples.text: El niño está aquí.
examples.trans: The boy is here.

examples.text: Vemos los niños desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the boys from the door.

meanings.note: Masculine plural of 'niño'. In Spanish grammar, the masculine plural 'los niños' denotes either a group of boys specifically or a mixed-gender group of children generally.

examples.text: Está entrenando a los niños en el fútbol.
examples.trans: He is coaching the kids in soccer.

examples.text: Estoy dando un taller-teatro para niños.
examples.trans: I am giving a theater workshop for children.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.text: Hoy no llueve en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: ¡Buenas noches! = Good evening / Good night; esta noche = tonight.

examples.text: La noche está aquí.
examples.trans: The night is here.

examples.text: Vemos las noches desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the nights from the door.

meanings.note: The nut itself is la nuez; de nogal = made of walnut wood.

examples.text: La mesa del comedor es de nogal.
examples.trans: The dining table is made of walnut.

examples.text: Hay un nogal muy viejo en el pueblo.
examples.trans: There is a very old walnut tree in the village.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Te nombramos encargado oficial de las luces del patio.
examples.trans: We appoint you officially in charge of the courtyard lights.

examples.text: El libro antiguo nombra a cada huésped por su apellido.
examples.trans: The old book names each guest by surname.

meanings.note: Nombre y apellidos = full name.

examples.text: El nombre está aquí.
examples.trans: The name is here.

examples.text: Vemos los nombres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the names from the door.

examples.text: Cariño, ¿cómo voy a ir si tenemos lo de los Goya y está la niña nominada?
examples.trans: Darling, how can I go when we have the Goyas and my girl is nominated?

examples.text: Pues claro. Mariona está nominada al Goya a Mejor Actriz Revelación.
examples.trans: Of course. Mariona is nominated for the Goya for Best New Actress.

examples.text: Era una desconocida y ahora estoy nominada a Actriz Revelación.
examples.trans: I was an unknown and now I'm nominated for Best New Actress.

meanings.note: Normas municipales = city regulations.

examples.text: La norma está aquí.
examples.trans: The rule is here.

examples.text: Vemos las normas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rules from the door.

meanings.note: Al norte de = 'north of / to the north of'.

examples.text: Las ventanas frescas miran hacia el norte del jardín.
examples.trans: The cool windows face toward the north of the garden.

examples.text: Su familia vive en un pueblo verde del norte de España.
examples.trans: His family lives in a green village in northern Spain.

nos.gloss: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)

meanings.en: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)
meanings.note: First-person plural object/reflexive/reciprocal pronoun.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos mañana por la mañana!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow morning!

examples.text: Nos alegra mucho la noticia.
examples.trans: The news makes us very glad.

meanings.note: Feminine all-female plural: nosotras.

examples.text: Nosotros abrimos la posada a las siete.
examples.trans: We open the guesthouse at seven.

examples.text: Siéntese a tomar té con nosotros.
examples.trans: Sit down and have tea with us.

meanings.note: Covers jotted notes, musical notes, and review scores.

examples.text: La nota está aquí.
examples.trans: The note is here.

examples.text: Vemos las notas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notes from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Buena noticia! = Good news!

examples.text: La noticia está aquí.
examples.trans: The piece of news is here.

examples.text: Vemos las noticias desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the piece of newss from the door.

meanings.note: Friendly teasing word for a new team member (masculine: el novato).

examples.text: La novata está aquí.
examples.trans: The rookie is here.

examples.text: Vemos las novatas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rookies from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees with its noun: la novena llave.

examples.text: Es una pieza novena.
examples.trans: It is a ninth piece.

examples.text: ¡¿Una novena llave de latón?! ¡¿La abrimos esta noche o esperamos a mañana?!
examples.trans: A ninth brass key?! Do we open it tonight or wait until morning?!

examples.text: No eres la novia.
examples.trans: You're not the bride.

examples.text: La novia lleva un vestido blanco.
examples.trans: The bride is wearing a white dress.

examples.text: ¿No te enteras? ¿Cómo vamos a ver ahora el videobook de la prima de tu novio?
examples.trans: Don't you get it? How are we supposed to watch your boyfriend's cousin's showreel right now?

examples.text: Hablamos de novio en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about boyfriend at the office.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.text: Nuestra posada tiene ocho habitaciones.
examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.

examples.text: Nuestros vecinos toman café aquí.
examples.trans: Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Las nueve = nine o'clock.

examples.text: El tren llega a las nueve en punto.
examples.trans: The train arrives at nine on the dot.

examples.text: Vimos un nueve sobre diez.
examples.trans: We saw a nine out of ten.

meanings.note: De nuevo is an idiom meaning 'again'.

examples.text: Es una pieza nueva.
examples.trans: It is a new piece.

examples.text: ¡Ah, se abre! Gracias. Soy Clara, la nueva recepcionista.
examples.trans: Oh, it opens! Thank you. I am Clara, the new receptionist.

meanings.note: Diminutive of número.

examples.text: El numerito está aquí.
examples.trans: The tiny number is here.

examples.text: Vemos los numeritos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tiny numbers from the door.

meanings.note: Precede the verb alone (nunca llega tarde) or follow no.

examples.text: Nunca he visto ese cofre antes.
examples.trans: I have never seen that chest before.

examples.text: El tren de la mañana nunca llega tarde.
examples.trans: The morning train never arrives late.

meanings.note: Written after street names in Spanish addresses (Calle Mayor número ocho).

examples.text: El número está aquí.
examples.trans: The number is here.

examples.text: Vemos los números desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the numbers from the door.

meanings.note: Becomes u before words starting with o- or ho-.

examples.text: ¿Prefieres café o té caliente?
examples.trans: Do you prefer coffee or hot tea?

examples.text: ¿Abrimos hoy o esperamos a mañana?
examples.trans: Do we open today or wait until tomorrow?

meanings.note: Objetos perdidos is the standard Spanish phrase for lost-and-found.

examples.text: El objeto está aquí.
examples.trans: The object is here.

examples.text: Vemos los objetos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the objects from the door.

examples.text: Vamos a ver una obra de Henrik Ibsen.
examples.trans: We're going to see a play by Henrik Ibsen.

examples.text: Yo obra
examples.trans: I obra

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Esta casa tiene más de ochenta años.
examples.trans: This house is over eighty years old.

examples.text: Conté ochenta escalones de piedra.
examples.trans: I counted eighty stone steps.

meanings.note: Las ocho = eight o'clock.

examples.text: Abrimos la puerta a las ocho.
examples.trans: We open the door at eight.

examples.text: La posada tiene ocho habitaciones.
examples.trans: The guesthouse has eight rooms.

meanings.note: Eight-note musical interval from one note to the next of the same name.

examples.text: Toca la misma melodía una octava más arriba.
examples.trans: Play the same melody one octave higher.

examples.text: Ya hemos afinado toda la octava central del piano.
examples.trans: We have already tuned the piano's entire middle octave.

meanings.note: Used for hidden architectural features, secret doors, or tucked-away courtyards.

examples.text: Detrás del tabique viejo descubrieron una galería oculta.
examples.trans: Behind the old partition wall they discovered a hidden gallery.

examples.text: La llave estaba en un cajón oculto debajo del mostrador.
examples.trans: The key was in a hidden drawer underneath the counter.

meanings.note: Describes a busy person or an occupied room/table.

examples.text: Es una pieza ocupada.
examples.trans: It is a busy piece.

examples.text: Todas las llaves de la uno a la siete están ocupadas, y la ocho tiene pintura fresca.
examples.trans: Every key from one to seven is occupied, and room eight has wet paint.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; ocupar poco espacio means 'to take up little room'.

examples.text: Las mesas plegadas ocupan muy poco sitio.
examples.trans: The folded tables take up very little room.

examples.text: Los huéspedes nuevos ocupan la habitación cuatro.
examples.trans: The new guests occupy Room Four.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb (odio = I hate).

examples.text: Odio llegar tarde a una cita.
examples.trans: I hate arriving late for an appointment.

examples.text: De pequeño odiaba madrugar en invierno.
examples.trans: As a boy he hated getting up early in winter.

meanings.en: of (English preposition used in quoted phrases and titles)
meanings.note: Quoted English preposition in 'Paquita Salas'. Appears when characters claim to speak English by tossing out basic set phrases like 'Of course', or when referencing English-language TV titles such as 'House of Cards'. Its native Spanish equivalent is 'de'.

examples.text: Lidia, ¿sabes inglés? "Of course".
examples.trans: Lidia, do you know English? "Of course".

examples.text: Es una serie americana que se llama "House of Cards", no sé si lo conocéis.
examples.trans: It's an American series called "House of Cards", I don't know if you're familiar with it.

oferta.gloss: special offer; sale; bargain (de oferta = on sale)

meanings.en: special offer; sale; bargain (de oferta = on sale)
meanings.note: De oferta means 'on sale / at a bargain price'.

examples.text: Encontré estas sillas plegables de oferta a mitad de precio.
examples.trans: I found these folding chairs on sale at half price.

examples.text: En el mercado había una buena oferta de limones frescos.
examples.trans: At the market there was a great deal on fresh lemons.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine singular; plural oficiales.

examples.text: Mañana recibimos la carta oficial del ayuntamiento.
examples.trans: Tomorrow we receive the official letter from City Hall.

examples.text: Hoy es la apertura oficial de nuestra sala de té.
examples.trans: Today is the official opening of our tea room.

meanings.note: Workplace or municipal desk.

examples.text: La oficina está aquí.
examples.trans: The office is here.

examples.text: Vemos las oficinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the offices from the door.

meanings.note: Skilled craft or trade learned through practice.

examples.text: El oficio está aquí.
examples.trans: The trade is here.

examples.text: Vemos los oficios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the trades from the door.

meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg ofrezco.

examples.text: Ofrecemos té caliente y fruta fresca.
examples.trans: We offer hot tea and fresh fruit.

examples.text: El vecino nos ofreció su escalera.
examples.trans: The neighbour offered us his ladder.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise or realization.

examples.text: ¡Oh, ahí está la puerta azul!
examples.trans: Oh, there is the blue door!

examples.text: Oh, perdona, no te había visto.
examples.trans: Oh, sorry, I had not seen you.

meanings.note: Plural los ojos.

examples.text: El ojo está aquí.
examples.trans: The eye is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ojos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the eyes from the door.

meanings.en: old, years old (quoted English adjective in audition self-tapes)
meanings.note: Quoted English adjective used in 'Paquita Salas' when Mariona Terés records a stiff, textbook-style English audition tape ('I am 25 years old'). In Spanish, age is expressed with the verb 'tener' + 'años' ('Tengo veinticinco años'), whereas the literal adjective 'viejo' means 'elderly / aged'.

examples.text: Mariona dice en su vídeo de presentación: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old".
examples.trans: Mariona says in her introduction video: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old".

examples.text: En los castings en inglés todas las actrices terminan la frase diciendo "years old".
examples.trans: In English auditions all the actresses end the sentence by saying "years old".

oler.gloss: to smell (oler a = to smell of/like)

meanings.en: to smell (oler a = to smell of/like)
meanings.note: Irregular boot stem hue- (huelo, hueles, huele, huelen).

examples.text: La cocina huele a canela caliente.
examples.trans: The kitchen smells like warm cinnamon.

examples.text: El jardín huele a flores frescas.
examples.trans: The garden smells of fresh flowers.

meanings.note: In Valencia and eastern Spain, oliva is used alongside aceituna for the olive fruit.

examples.text: Un chorrito de aceite de oliva realza las lentejas.
examples.trans: A drizzle of olive oil brings out the lentils.

examples.text: Traemos aceite de oliva virgen del mercado local.
examples.trans: We bring virgin olive oil from the local market.

meanings.note: Standard word for a deep cooking pot with two handles used for soups, stews, and broths.

examples.text: La olla grande ya está al fuego con un chorrito de aceite de oliva.
examples.trans: The big pot is already on the stove with a drizzle of olive oil.

examples.text: Destapó la olla y toda la cocina olió a tomillo y verduras.
examples.trans: He lifted the lid off the pot and the whole kitchen smelled of thyme and vegetables.

meanings.en: he/she/it forgets; slips one's mind (se + indirect object + olvida)
meanings.note: Third-person singular present indicative (and affirmative 'tú' imperative) of 'olvidar'. In conversational Spanish, unintentional forgetting is most often framed with the accidental reflexive construction 'olvidársele algo a alguien' ('no se te olvida' = 'it doesn't slip your mind / you don't forget').

examples.text: Pero no se te olvida, ¿eh?
examples.trans: But you do not forget, huh?

examples.text: A Magüi nunca se le olvida apuntar los recados importantes en la agenda.
examples.trans: Magüi never forgets to write down important messages in the planner.

meanings.note: Used directly (olvidé la llave) or pronominally with de (me olvidé de...).

examples.text: Nunca olvido una cara amable.
examples.trans: I never forget a friendly face.

examples.text: Olvidé mi paraguas junto al mostrador.
examples.trans: I left my umbrella beside the counter.

meanings.note: Las once = eleven o'clock.

examples.text: Son las once y veinte de la mañana.
examples.trans: It is eleven twenty in the morning.

examples.text: Quedan once sillas limpias.
examples.trans: Eleven clean chairs remain.

examples.text: Aprovecha esa oportunidad.
examples.trans: Take that opportunity.

examples.text: Es una buena oportunidad.
examples.trans: It's a good opportunity.

meanings.note: Feminine (la orden / las órdenes) when meaning a command or rule; masculine (el orden) for tidiness.

examples.text: Tenemos orden de no abrir el horno antes de tiempo.
examples.trans: We have strict orders not to open the oven early.

examples.text: Todo el equipo siguió las órdenes claras de Rocío.
examples.trans: The whole team followed Rocio's clear instructions.

meanings.note: Letra ordenada = neat handwriting.

examples.text: Es una pieza ordenada.
examples.trans: It is a neat piece.

examples.text: Reconocí tu letra ordenada de imprenta en esa postal en dos segundos.
examples.trans: I recognized your neat block handwriting on that postcard in two seconds.

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for a computer.

examples.text: El ordenador está aquí.
examples.trans: The computer is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ordenadores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the computers from the door.

oreja.gloss: ear (de oreja a oreja = ear to ear)

meanings.en: ear (de oreja a oreja = ear to ear)
meanings.note: Oreja is the outer ear; sonreír de oreja a oreja means 'to grin from ear to ear'.

examples.text: Clara sonrió de oreja a oreja al ver el cartel puesto.
examples.trans: Clara grinned from ear to ear on seeing the sign up.

examples.text: El gorro de lana te abriga muy bien las orejas.
examples.trans: The wool hat keeps your ears nice and warm.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells z -> c: organicé.

examples.text: Organizamos desayunos en el patio.
examples.trans: We organize breakfasts in the courtyard.

examples.text: La encargada organizó las llaves por número.
examples.trans: La encargada organized the keys by number.

meanings.note: Dar orgullo / sentir orgullo means 'to make proud / feel proud'.

examples.text: A Carmen le da mucho orgullo tocar el vals familiar.
examples.trans: It fills Carmen with pride to play the family waltz.

examples.text: Este patio cuidado es el orgullo de toda la posada.
examples.trans: This well-kept courtyard is the pride of the whole inn.

meanings.note: Estar orgulloso de... expresses feeling proud of someone or something.

examples.text: Rocío miraba orgullosa cómo sus aprendices sacaban el pan del horno.
examples.trans: Rocio watched proudly as her apprentices took the bread out of the oven.

examples.text: Estamos muy orgullosos de haber recuperado la sala histórica.
examples.trans: We are very proud to have restored the historic room.

examples.text: Su actuación es muy orgánica.
examples.trans: Her performance is very organic.

examples.text: Compramos fruta orgánica.
examples.trans: We buy organic fruit.

meanings.en: gold (precious metal, color, or something of great value)
meanings.note: Masculine noun. Frequently used figuratively in the idiom 'valer oro' ('to be worth its weight in gold / to be priceless'), as when Paquita savors the fresh country air of her hometown.

meanings.en: oros (suit of golden coins in the Spanish card deck)
meanings.note: In the plural ('los oros'), refers to the suit of coins in the traditional Spanish deck of cards ('la baraja española').

examples.text: Este aire... (ASPIRA) Este aire vale oro.
examples.trans: This air... (INHALES) This air is worth its weight in gold.

examples.text: Esa representante tiene un corazón de oro aunque a veces pierda los nervios.
examples.trans: That talent agent has a heart of gold even though she loses her temper sometimes.

examples.text: Que no os engañen.
examples.trans: Don't let them fool you.

examples.text: Yo os
examples.trans: I os

meanings.note: Azul oscuro = dark blue; gris oscuro = dark grey.

examples.text: Es una pieza oscura.
examples.trans: It is a dark piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: En otoño means 'in autumn'.

examples.text: En otoño las hojas del patio se vuelven doradas.
examples.trans: In autumn the courtyard leaves turn golden.

examples.text: El aire fresco de otoño huele a lluvia limpia.
examples.trans: The crisp autumn air smells of clean rain.

meanings.note: Spanish never puts un/una before otro (otra taza = another cup; otra vez = again).

examples.text: ¿Quiere otra taza de café?
examples.trans: Would you like another cup of coffee?

examples.text: Míralo otra vez a la luz.
examples.trans: Look at it again in the light.

meanings.note: Feminine plural of 'oveja'. Unlike English 'sheep' (which has an unchanged plural), Spanish inflects regularly from singular 'la oveja' to plural 'las ovejas'. Also heard in the idiom 'la oveja negra' ('the black sheep').

examples.text: pasábamos las horas en el campo dando paseos con las ovejas.
examples.trans: we used to spend hours in the countryside taking walks with the sheep.

examples.text: ¿Sí? Ya no vamos con las ovejas, pero nos seguimos viendo por el pueblo.
examples.trans: Yeah? We don't go out with the sheep anymore, but we still see each other around the village.

meanings.note: Oído refers to inner hearing and musical pitch (tener buen oído = to have a good ear).

examples.text: Carmen afina las cuerdas centrales con muy buen oído.
examples.trans: Carmen tunes the middle strings with a very keen ear.

examples.text: Esa melodía suave es un regalo para los oídos.
examples.trans: That gentle melody is a treat for the ears.

meanings.note: Irregular: oigo, oyes, oye, oímos, oís, oyen; ¡Oiga! / ¡Oye! gets someone's attention.

examples.text: ¿Me oyes bien por teléfono?
examples.trans: Can you hear me clearly on the phone?

examples.text: Acabo de oír pasos en la escalera.
examples.trans: I just heard footsteps on the stairs.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Pocas personas me llaman Paca.
examples.trans: Few people call me Paca.

examples.text: Paca conoce a todo el mundo.
examples.trans: Paca knows everyone.

meanings.note: Tener paciencia = to be patient.

examples.text: La paciencia es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The patience is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la paciencia.
examples.trans: We talk about the patience.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Vamos a la boda de Paco.
examples.trans: We're going to Paco's wedding.

examples.text: Paco es productor de cine.
examples.trans: Paco is a film producer.

meanings.note: Masculine noun. Used affectionately in 'ser como un padre para alguien' ('to be like a father to someone'). In the plural, 'los padres' means 'parents' (mother and father together).
In colloquial Peninsular Spanish, 'padre' can follow a noun as an invariable adjective meaning 'tremendous / one hell of a' ('un lío padre' = 'a massive mess', 'un susto padre' = 'a huge scare').

examples.text: Es como un padre para mí.
examples.trans: He is like a father to me.

examples.text: Mi padre siempre venía a verme actuar en las obras del colegio.
examples.trans: My father always used to come see me perform in the school plays.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from pagar.

examples.text: Es una pieza pagada.
examples.trans: It is a paid piece.

examples.text: ¡Pagado en efectivo! Deja abierta tu caja de herramientas, ¡vuelvo corriendo por el puente!
examples.trans: Paid in cash! Keep your toolbox open, I am running back across the bridge!

meanings.note: Preterite yo pagué keeps the hard g sound with gu; pagar en efectivo = pay in cash.

examples.text: ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?
examples.trans: Can I pay by card?

examples.text: Ayer pagué la cena yo.
examples.trans: Yesterday I paid for dinner.

meanings.note: Ni una palabra = not a word.

examples.text: La palabra está aquí.
examples.trans: The word is here.

examples.text: Vemos las palabras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the words from the door.

meanings.note: La palma de la mano is the palm of your hand; batir / tocar las palmas means to clap.

examples.text: Empuja la masa hacia delante con la palma de la mano.
examples.trans: Push the dough forward with the palm of your hand.

examples.text: Se conoce todas las calles del barrio como la palma de su mano.
examples.trans: She knows every street in the neighbourhood like the palm of her hand.

meanings.note: From palma, the palm of the hand: dar una palmada = to clap once.

examples.text: El profesor da una palmada y todos callan.
examples.trans: The teacher claps once and everyone goes quiet.

examples.text: Le da una palmada en la espalda.
examples.trans: He gives him a pat on the back.

meanings.note: Plural los panes; pan recién hecho = freshly baked bread.

examples.text: El pan es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The bread is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el pan.
examples.trans: We talk about the bread.

meanings.note: A woman baker is la panadera; the shop is la panadería.

examples.text: El panadero empieza a trabajar a las cuatro.
examples.trans: The baker starts work at four.

examples.text: La panadera nos guarda dos barras de pan.
examples.trans: The baker keeps two loaves of bread for us.

meanings.note: Built from pan ('bread') + shop suffix -ería; the baker is el panadero / la panadera.

examples.text: Toda la calle huele a gloria cuando abre la panadería.
examples.trans: The whole street smells heavenly when the bakery opens.

examples.text: Compré dos barras crujientes en la panadería de la esquina.
examples.trans: I bought two crusty loaves at the corner bakery.

meanings.note: Plural adds -es: los paneles (paneles de madera, paneles acústicos).

examples.text: Colocaron paneles de madera para suavizar el eco de la sala.
examples.trans: They installed wooden panels to soften the echo in the room.

examples.text: El aviso del concierto está colgado en el panel de la entrada.
examples.trans: The concert notice is pinned to the entrance board.

meanings.note: Computer or phone screen.

examples.text: La pantalla está aquí.
examples.trans: The screen is here.

examples.text: Vemos las pantallas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the screens from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los papeles.

examples.text: El papel está aquí.
examples.trans: The paper is here.

examples.text: Vemos los papeles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the papers from the door.

meanings.note: Built from papel.

examples.text: El papeleo es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The paperwork is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el papeleo.
examples.trans: We talk about the paperwork.

meanings.note: Wrapped package or parcel.

examples.text: El paquete está aquí.
examples.trans: The parcel is here.

examples.text: Vemos los paquetes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the parcels from the door.

examples.text: ¿Qué pasa, Paqui?
examples.trans: What is up, Paqui?

examples.text: Yo Paqui
examples.trans: I Paqui

meanings.note: Source-attested name or surname. Name history is supplied separately with its own evidence and uncertainty; no unverified full name is inferred.

examples.text: Paquita es representante.
examples.trans: Paquita is an agent.

examples.text: Todo el mundo quiere a Paquita.
examples.trans: Everyone loves Paquita.

meanings.note: Plural los pares (dos pares de gafas = two pairs of glasses).

examples.text: El par está aquí.
examples.trans: The pair is here.

examples.text: Vemos los pares desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pairs from the door.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

parada.gloss: stop (bus/tram stop or stop along an errand)

meanings.en: stop (bus/tram stop or stop along an errand)
meanings.note: Siguiente parada means 'next stop'.

examples.text: La parada del autobús está en la esquina de la plaza.
examples.trans: The bus stop is at the corner of the square.

examples.text: Hacemos una última parada en la panadería.
examples.trans: We make one last stop at the bakery.

meanings.note: Venir a parar = to end up / stumble into.

examples.text: El autobús para frente al mercado.
examples.trans: The bus stops opposite the market.

examples.text: Un taxi amarillo paró en la puerta.
examples.trans: A yellow taxi pulled up at the gate.

pare.gloss: I stop / he or she stops (subjunctive)

meanings.en: I stop, he/she/you (formal) stop (present subjunctive of parar / pararse)
meanings.note: First- or third-person singular present subjunctive of 'parar' (and pronominal 'pararse a + infinitive', meaning 'to pause/take the time to do something', as in 'que yo me pare aquí a contarte'). Also serves as the formal 'usted' imperative ('¡Pare!').

examples.text: Lo que pasa que una persona que yo me pare aquí a contarte, no hay.
examples.trans: The thing is that there isn't anyone special enough for me to stop here and tell you about.

examples.text: Dile al director que no pare el rodaje hasta que terminemos esta secuencia.
examples.trans: Tell the director not to stop the shoot until we finish this sequence.

meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg parezco.

examples.text: Este rincón parece un jardín secreto.
examples.trans: This corner looks like a secret garden.

examples.text: La idea nos pareció excelente.
examples.trans: The idea seemed excellent to us.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la pared, las paredes.

examples.text: La pared está aquí.
examples.trans: The wall is here.

examples.text: Vemos las paredes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the walls from the door.

meanings.note: Always feminine even when referring to two people.

examples.text: La pareja está aquí.
examples.trans: The couple is here.

examples.text: Vemos las parejas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the couples from the door.

meanings.note: Used both for blinking one's eyes and for a blinking indicator light.

examples.text: La luz roja del teléfono parpadea sin parar.
examples.trans: The red light on the telephone keeps blinking.

examples.text: Parpadeé dos veces al salir al sol de la mañana.
examples.trans: I blinked twice when stepping out into the morning sun.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la mejor parte.

examples.text: La parte está aquí.
examples.trans: The part is here.

examples.text: Vemos las partes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the parts from the door.

meanings.en: match, game (in sports); friendly match ('partido amistoso')
meanings.note: Masculine noun. In 'Paquita Salas', Pedrín uses 'jugar un partido amistoso' ('to play a friendly match') as a gentle, humorous metaphor for a casual romantic encounter without formal commitment.

meanings.en: political party; good catch ('buen partido'); advantage ('sacar partido')
meanings.note: Also denotes a political organization ('partido político'), an eligible partner ('un buen partido'), or benefit/advantage in the idiom 'sacar partido de algo' ('to make the most of something').

examples.text: Yo estoy dispuesto a jugar un partido amistoso
examples.trans: I am willing to play a friendly match

examples.text: Sacaron mucho partido de aquella aparición sorpresa en televisión.
examples.trans: They got a lot of mileage out of that surprise television appearance.

meanings.note: Masculine plural of 'partido'. In 'Paquita Salas', 'partidos amistosos' ('friendly matches') refers figuratively to friendly, no-strings-attached romantic moments later in life.

examples.text: todavía hay... partidos amistosos.
examples.trans: there are still... friendly matches.

examples.text: Los domingos por la tarde siempre escuchábamos los partidos de fútbol por la radio.
examples.trans: On Sunday afternoons we always used to listen to the soccer matches on the radio.

partir.gloss: to split; to cut; to divide; to depart

meanings.en: to split; to cut; to divide; to depart
meanings.note: Partir por la mitad is the everyday Spanish phrase for tearing, cutting, or splitting something cleanly in half.

examples.text: Alguien partió la tarjeta de la receta por la mitad.
examples.trans: Someone tore the recipe card in half.

examples.text: Rocío partió el bizcocho caliente en ocho trozos iguales.
examples.trans: Rocío cut the warm sponge cake into eight equal slices.

meanings.note: Printed music sheets for piano or voice.

examples.text: La partitura está aquí.
examples.trans: The sheet music is here.

examples.text: Vemos las partituras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sheet music from the door.

pasado.gloss: last; past (la semana pasada = last week)

meanings.en: last; past (la semana pasada = last week)
meanings.note: Agrees with its noun.

examples.text: Es una pieza pasada.
examples.trans: It is a last piece.

examples.text: Bombilla nueva la semana pasada, jabón limpio y mucha agua caliente.
examples.trans: New bulb last week, clean soap, and plenty of hot water.

meanings.note: Plural pasadores; small metal pivot pin inside a hinge or piano action.

examples.text: El pasador de latón sujeta la pieza de madera.
examples.trans: The brass pin holds the wooden part in place.

examples.text: Empuja el pasador fino con la punta de las pinzas.
examples.trans: Push the thin pin in with the tip of the tweezers.

meanings.en: happening, going on, occurring; passing, spending time (gerund of pasar)
meanings.note: Gerund (present participle) of 'pasar'. Used with 'estar' in progressive constructions to describe current events ('lo que está pasando' = 'what is happening / going on') or enjoying oneself ('pasándolo bien').

examples.text: Maquillar un poquito lo que está pasando, ¿no?
examples.trans: Sugarcoat what's going on a little bit, right?

examples.text: ¿Me puedes explicar qué está pasando exactamente en esta agencia?
examples.trans: Can you explain to me what exactly is going on in this agency?

related.gloss: to happen; to pass; to spend time

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Estuvo en Pasapalabra treinta veces.
examples.trans: She was on Pasapalabra thirty times.

examples.text: Vemos Pasapalabra por la tarde.
examples.trans: We watch Pasapalabra in the evening.

pasar.gloss: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen

meanings.en: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen
meanings.note: ¿Qué pasa? = What's wrong?; No pasa nada = No problem.

examples.text: ¡Pase, por favor, y siéntese!
examples.trans: Come in, please, and have a seat!

examples.text: Pasa la farmacia verde a la derecha.
examples.trans: Pass the green pharmacy on your right.

meanings.en: you stopped by, dropped in, passed (second-person singular imperfect subjunctive of pasar / pasarse)
meanings.note: Second-person singular ('tú') imperfect subjunctive ('-se' form, interchangeable with 'pasaras') of 'pasar' / 'pasarse'. In Peninsular Spanish, 'pasarse (por un lugar)' means 'to drop by / swing by', and the imperfect subjunctive is triggered after a conditional verb like 'Te diría que te pasases' ('I would tell you to drop by').

examples.text: Te diría que te pasases, pero reunión...
examples.trans: I'd tell you to stop by, but I have a meeting...

examples.text: Me encantaría que te pasases mañana por la oficina para leer el guion.
examples.trans: I would love for you to stop by the office tomorrow to read the script.

meanings.note: A short journey on foot, or a wide tree-lined street.

examples.text: Dieron un paseo largo por la tarde.
examples.trans: They took a long walk in the afternoon.

examples.text: Es un paseo muy bonito.
examples.trans: It is a very beautiful walk.

meanings.note: Masculine plural of 'paseo'. Almost always paired with the verb 'dar' in the idiom 'dar un paseo' / 'dar paseos' ('to go for a walk / take strolls').

examples.text: pasábamos las horas en el campo dando paseos con las ovejas.
examples.trans: we used to spend hours in the countryside taking walks with the sheep.

examples.text: Por las tardes nos gusta dar largos paseos por las calles de Madrid.
examples.trans: In the evenings we like to take long walks through the streets of Madrid.

related.gloss: to stroll, walk, take for a walk

meanings.note: The corridor inside a house, hotel or train.

examples.text: El baño está al final del pasillo.
examples.trans: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.

examples.text: No corras por el pasillo.
examples.trans: Don't run in the corridor.

examples.text: # Pasión, tesón, que andando
examples.trans: # Passion, tenacity, because walking

examples.text: Yo Pasión
examples.trans: I Pasión

meanings.note: Oír pasos = to hear footsteps.

examples.text: El paso está aquí.
examples.trans: The footstep is here.

examples.text: Vemos los pasos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the footsteps from the door.

meanings.note: Built from pastel ('pastry/cake') + -ería; refers both to the pastry shop/kitchen and the craft of pastry baking.

examples.text: Toda la pastelería huele a mantequilla, limón y almendra tostada.
examples.trans: The whole bakehouse smells of butter, lemon, and toasted almond.

examples.text: Compramos dulces recién hechos en la pastelería de nuestra calle.
examples.trans: We bought freshly baked pastries at the pastry shop on our street.

examples.text: Suena a pastillas para dormir.
examples.trans: It sounds like sleeping pills.

examples.text: Tomo una pastilla con agua.
examples.trans: I take a pill with water.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (feminine 'pastora', plural 'pastores'). Also used in 'perro pastor' ('sheepdog / herding dog', such as 'pastor alemán' = 'German shepherd').
Also denotes a Protestant minister or spiritual shepherd.

examples.text: Él es Pedrín, el pastor. Y, bueno, cuando era niña,
examples.trans: He is Pedrín, the shepherd. And, well, when I was a little girl,

examples.text: El pastor llevaba a todo el rebaño por los caminos del monte.
examples.trans: The shepherd led the whole flock along the mountain paths.

pasábamos.gloss: we used to spend / we were passing

meanings.en: we used to spend (time), we would spend; we were passing
meanings.note: First-person plural ('nosotros') imperfect indicative of 'pasar'. Used to describe habitual or ongoing actions in the past ('pasábamos las horas' = 'we used to spend hours'). Note the mandatory written accent on the antepenultimate syllable ('-sá-').

examples.text: pasábamos las horas en el campo dando paseos con las ovejas.
examples.trans: we used to spend hours in the countryside taking walks with the sheep.

examples.text: De jóvenes pasábamos todos los veranos en el pueblo de mis abuelos.
examples.trans: When we were young we used to spend every summer in my grandparents' village.

related.gloss: to spend (time); to pass; to happen

pata.gloss: leg (of furniture or an animal); paw

meanings.en: leg (of furniture or an animal); paw
meanings.note: Used for animal legs/paws and the legs of tables, chairs, and beds; human legs are las piernas.

examples.text: Levanta la mesa despacio para que no raspen las patas.
examples.trans: Lift the table slowly so the legs do not scrape.

examples.text: Mateo niveló las cuatro patas de la silla de madera.
examples.trans: Mateo levelled all four legs of the wooden chair.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.text: El patio está aquí.
examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: Cultural and architectural heritage.

examples.text: El patrimonio es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The heritage is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el patrimonio.
examples.trans: We talk about the heritage.

paz.gloss: peace (hacer las paces = to make peace)

meanings.en: peace (hacer las paces = to make peace)
meanings.note: Plural las paces.

examples.text: La paz es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The peace is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la paz.
examples.trans: We talk about the peace.

examples.text: Fernando Canelón es representante de los artistas más importantes de este país.
examples.trans: Fernando Canelón is the agent for the most important artists in this country.

examples.text: Yo país
examples.trans: I país

meanings.note: Kitchen or polishing cloth.

examples.text: El paño está aquí.
examples.trans: The cloth is here.

examples.text: Vemos los paños desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cloths from the door.

examples.text: Ahí estaré yo para recoger los pedacitos.
examples.trans: I'll be right there to pick up the little pieces.

examples.text: Hablamos de pedacito en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about little pieces at the office.

meanings.note: Plural los pedales.

examples.text: El pedal derecho del piano mantiene vivo el acorde.
examples.trans: The right piano pedal sustains the chord.

examples.text: Los dos pedales de latón brillan bajo la lámpara.
examples.trans: Both brass pedals gleam beneath the lamp.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: pido, pidió).

examples.text: Pido un café con leche, por favor.
examples.trans: I will order a coffee with milk, please.

examples.text: El cartero me pidió una firma.
examples.trans: The postman asked me for a signature.

meanings.en: Pedrín (masculine given name, affectionate diminutive of Pedro)
meanings.note: Traditional Peninsular Spanish diminutive of 'Pedro' formed with the affectionate suffix '-ín'. In 'Paquita Salas', Pedrín is the kind-hearted village shepherd from Paquita's hometown in La Rioja.

examples.text: Él es Pedrín, el pastor. Y, bueno, cuando era niña,
examples.trans: He is Pedrín, the shepherd. And, well, when I was a little girl,

examples.text: Un padre... Ay, Pedrín.
examples.trans: Like a father... Oh, Pedrín.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from pegar.

examples.text: Es una pieza pegada.
examples.trans: It is a taped piece.

examples.text: Hay una cerradura diminuta en el cierre delantero, y miren pegada debajo: ¡una vieja llave de latón!
examples.trans: There is a tiny keyhole on the front latch, and look taped underneath: an old brass key!

meanings.note: From pegar ('to stick'); used for wet paint, syrup, or humid heat.

examples.text: No toques el marco aún: el barniz sigue pegajoso.
examples.trans: Do not touch the frame yet: the varnish is still tacky.

examples.text: Lávate las manos si te quedan pegajosas de limón.
examples.trans: Wash your hands if they feel sticky with lemon.

pekín.gloss: Beijing, Peking (capital of China; song title)

meanings.en: Beijing, Peking (capital city of China; indie-pop song title in 'Paquita Salas')
meanings.note: Standard Spanish name for Beijing, the capital of China (also spelled 'Pequín'). In 'Paquita Salas', it appears as the title of the wistful indie-pop song 'Pekín' by the Madrid band El Buen Hijo.

examples.text: En los subtítulos aparece la indicación musical: ("Pekín", de El buen hijo).
examples.trans: In the subtitles the musical cue appears: ("Pekín", by El Buen Hijo).

examples.text: (Suena "Pekín", de El buen hijo) mientras pasean por el campo.
examples.trans: ("Pekín", by El Buen Hijo plays) while they walk through the countryside.

meanings.note: Pelearse por algo = to squabble over something.

examples.text: De niños se peleaban por las esquinas.
examples.trans: As children they squabbled over the corner pieces.

examples.text: Nunca peleamos por cosas pequeñas.
examples.trans: We never fight over small things.

examples.text: Tienes que ver una peliculita suya.
examples.trans: You have to watch a film or two of hers.

examples.text: Ponemos una peliculita esta noche.
examples.trans: Let's put on a movie tonight.

examples.text: Mi madre le cortaba el pelo.
examples.trans: My mother used to cut her hair.

examples.text: Tiene el pelo largo.
examples.trans: She has long hair.

examples.text: Qué gusto quitarme la peluca.
examples.trans: What a relief to take off the wig.

examples.text: Yo peluca
examples.trans: I peluca

examples.text: Rodé una película en China.
examples.trans: I shot a film in China.

examples.text: Es una película muy bonita.
examples.trans: It's a very lovely film.

pelín.gloss: tiny bit (un pelín = a touch / a hair)

meanings.en: tiny bit (un pelín = a touch / a hair)
meanings.note: Very natural Peninsular Spanish expression: un pelín alto / bajo / salado.

examples.text: La sopa está riquísima, solo un pelín espesa.
examples.trans: The soup is delicious, just a touch thick.

examples.text: Sube el cuadro un pelín del lado de la ventana.
examples.trans: Raise the picture a hair on the window side.

meanings.en: sorrow, grief, heartache; pity, shame ('¡qué pena!')
meanings.note: Feminine noun immortalized in the opening lyric of the 'Paquita Salas' theme song ('Paquita tiene una pena'). Very common in idioms like 'dar pena' ('to make someone feel sad or sorry') and '¡Qué pena!' ('What a shame! / What a pity!').

meanings.en: trouble, effort ('valer/merecer la pena'); penalty, punishment
meanings.note: Used in 'merecer la pena' or 'valer la pena' ('to be worth the trouble / worthwhile'), as well as in legal contexts for a sentence or penalty.

examples.text: # Paquita tiene una pena, Paquita quiere más.
examples.trans: # Paquita has a sorrow, Paquita wants more.

examples.text: Me da mucha pena que ya no nos veamos tanto como antes.
examples.trans: It makes me really sad that we don't see each other as much as before.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from pensar.

examples.text: Es una pieza pensada.
examples.trans: It is a thought-out piece.

examples.text: Bien pensado, Clara. Javier lee normas municipales de edificios cada semana.
examples.trans: Smart thinking, Clara. Javier reads city building rules every single week.

meanings.note: Gerund (present participle) of the stem-changing verb 'pensar'. Takes the preposition 'en' when meaning 'thinking about someone or something' ('pensando en ti').

examples.text: pero es que lo he estado pensando...
examples.trans: but the thing is I have been thinking about it...

examples.text: Llevo toda la semana pensando en cómo organizar la fiesta del estreno.
examples.trans: I've spent the whole week thinking about how to organize the premiere party.

pensar.gloss: to think; to plan to (pensar + infinitive)

meanings.en: to think; to plan to (pensar + infinitive)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: pienso).

examples.text: Pienso abrir la cafetería a las ocho.
examples.trans: I plan to open the cafe at eight.

examples.text: ¿Qué piensas de esta pintura azul?
examples.trans: What do you think of this blue paint?

meanings.note: Irregular comparative of malo; plural peores.

examples.text: Es una pieza peor.
examples.trans: It is a worse piece.

examples.text: Peor que una tubería... al mediodía llegó una carta certificada del dueño del edificio.
examples.trans: Worse than a pipe... a registered letter came from the building owner at noon.

meanings.note: Traditional Spanish masculine nickname for José; in Paquita Salas, Pepe is Paquita's ex-husband and former business partner who leaves PS Management.

examples.text: Oye, a ver si ves a mi Pepe, que lo vas a dar mucha alegría.
examples.trans: Hey, see if you can drop in on my Pepe, you'll make him really happy.

examples.text: Hombre, Pepe, ¡cuánto tiempo sin verte por la oficina!
examples.trans: Well, Pepe, how long has it been since we saw you around the office!

meanings.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective 'pequeño'.
Used as a feminine noun ('la pequeña') to refer to a young girl or affectionately to a younger woman.

examples.text: pero una cosa pequeña.
examples.trans: just a small thing.

examples.text: Esta sala de ensayo se nos queda un poco pequeña para toda la compañía.
examples.trans: This rehearsal room is getting a bit small for the whole company.

meanings.note: Hermano pequeño = younger brother; de pequeño = as a child.

examples.text: Es una pieza pequeña.
examples.trans: It is a small piece.

examples.text: Hay una pequeña tarjeta de cartón atada al asa.
examples.trans: There is a small cardboard card tied to the handle.

perder.gloss: to lose; to leak (perder agua); to miss (a train)

meanings.en: to lose; to leak (perder agua); to miss (a train)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: pierde).

examples.text: Date prisa o perdemos el tren.
examples.trans: Hurry up or we will miss the train.

examples.text: La tubería vieja perdía unas gotas.
examples.trans: The old pipe was leaking a few drops.

meanings.note: Objetos perdidos = lost property.

examples.text: Es una pieza perdida.
examples.trans: It is a lost piece.

examples.text: Clara, llama enseguida a objetos perdidos de la estación.
examples.trans: Clara, call the station lost-and-found office right away.

meanings.note: Perdona (tú) and perdone (usted) mean 'excuse me' when getting someone's attention.

examples.text: Perdona, ¿sabes a qué hora sale el autobús?
examples.trans: Excuse me, do you know what time the bus leaves?

examples.text: Perdone la molestia, señor.
examples.trans: Pardon the interruption, sir.

meanings.note: Everyday polite apology or attention-getter.

examples.text: Perdón por llegar cinco minutos tarde.
examples.trans: Sorry for arriving five minutes late.

examples.text: ¿Perdón? ¿Puede repetir el número?
examples.trans: Pardon? Could you repeat the number?

meanings.en: forgive me, excuse me, pardon me
meanings.note: Second-person singular (tú) affirmative imperative of 'perdonar' with the enclitic object pronoun 'me'. Used both for genuine apologies and as a polite discourse marker before excusing oneself.

examples.text: Perdóname, Paquita, que me voy a tumbar un momento.
examples.trans: Excuse me, Paquita, I'm going to lie down for a moment.

examples.text: Perdóname, es que vengo de hacer un casting lejos.
examples.trans: Forgive me, I've just come from doing a casting far away.

meanings.note: One of the most widely used fresh green herbs in Spanish home cooking.

examples.text: Cortamos unas hojas de perejil fresco de la maceta del patio.
examples.trans: We snipped a few leaves of fresh parsley from the courtyard pot.

examples.text: Un poco de perejil picado da mucho color y aroma a la sopa.
examples.trans: A little chopped parsley gives great colour and aroma to the soup.

meanings.note: Used alone as 'Perfect!'.

examples.text: Es una pieza perfecta.
examples.trans: It is a perfect piece.

examples.text: La clienta de la habitación cuatro se queda toda la semana. ¡Todo debe estar perfecto!
examples.trans: The guest in room four is staying all week. Everything must be perfect!

meanings.note: Papel de periódico is 'newspaper / newsprint' used for wrapping fragile wares.

examples.text: Leo el periódico de la mañana con una taza de café.
examples.trans: I read the morning newspaper with a cup of coffee.

examples.text: Envolvemos las tazas nuevas en papel de periódico.
examples.trans: We wrap the new cups in newspaper.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza permanente.
examples.trans: It is a permanent piece.

examples.text: con tinta permanente
examples.trans: in permanent ink

meanings.note: Con permiso is said politely when stepping past someone or entering.

examples.text: El permiso es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The permission is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el permiso.
examples.trans: We talk about the permission.

permitir.gloss: to allow; to let (¡Permítame! = Allow me!)

meanings.en: to allow; to let (¡Permítame! = Allow me!)
meanings.note: Regular -ir verb.

examples.text: ¿Me permite mirar este mapa?
examples.trans: Will you allow me to look at this map?

examples.text: Esta ventana permite ventilar toda la sala.
examples.trans: This window lets the whole room air out.

meanings.note: Core contrast conjunction.

examples.text: Hace frío fuera, pero dentro se está bien.
examples.trans: It is cold outside, yet inside it is cosy.

examples.text: Es pequeño, pero tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: It is small, but it has lots of light.

examples.text: Me encantan los perritos calientes.
examples.trans: I love hot dogs.

examples.text: Tiene un perrito muy simpático.
examples.trans: She has a very friendly little dog.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('el perro'); used generically for any dog or specifically for a male dog.

examples.text: -"Hola, Rex". (FINA) Mira qué cara tiene el perro.
examples.trans: -"Hello, Rex." (FINA) Look at the face on that dog.

examples.text: Sacaron al perro a pasear por el parque del Retiro antes del rodaje.
examples.trans: They took the dog for a walk through Retiro Park before the shoot.

meanings.note: Window blind or rolling metal shopfront shutter.

examples.text: La persiana está aquí.
examples.trans: The roller shutter is here.

examples.text: Vemos las persianas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the roller shutters from the door.

meanings.note: Always feminine (una persona amable) regardless of who it refers to.

examples.text: La persona está aquí.
examples.trans: The person is here.

examples.text: Vemos las personas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the persons from the door.

examples.text: No conozco todavía el personaje.
examples.trans: I don't know the character yet.

examples.text: Es el personaje principal.
examples.trans: She is the main character.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la personalidad'). In 'tener personalidad', it praises an actor or artist for having distinctive charisma and presence.
Often used in the plural ('personalidades') to refer to prominent figures in entertainment, culture, or politics.

examples.text: Nos gusta la gente con personalidad, y para eso, Europa.
examples.trans: We like people with personality, and for that, Europe.

examples.text: Buscamos a una actriz con mucha personalidad que destaque en el casting.
examples.trans: We are looking for an actress with a lot of personality who stands out in the audition.

meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg pertenezco.

examples.text: Esta maleta pertenece a la vecina.
examples.trans: This suitcase belongs to the neighbour.

examples.text: Esos libros pertenecen a la biblioteca.
examples.trans: Those books belong to the library.

meanings.note: Describes a heavy suitcase, wrench, or coat.

examples.text: Es una pieza pesada.
examples.trans: It is a heavy piece.

examples.text: Cerrada y vaciada. Pásame la llave inglesa pesada de tu izquierda.
examples.trans: Off and drained. Pass me the heavy wrench on your left.

pesar.gloss: to weigh (pesar mucho = to be very heavy)

meanings.en: to weigh (pesar mucho = to be very heavy)
meanings.note: Spanish says pesa mucho ('it weighs a lot') for 'it is heavy'.

examples.text: Esta caja de madera pesa bastante.
examples.trans: This wooden box is fairly heavy.

examples.text: El paquete pequeño apenas pesaba nada.
examples.trans: The small parcel weighed almost nothing.

meanings.note: Used for physical weight or pressure on a key or step.

examples.text: La mesa de roble aguanta mucho peso sin moverse.
examples.trans: The oak table holds plenty of weight without budging.

examples.text: Reparte bien el peso de las cajas al bajarlas.
examples.trans: Balance the weight of the boxes well when carrying them down.

meanings.note: Tocar el piano = to play the piano.

examples.text: Por las tardes alguien toca una melodía suave en el viejo piano del salón.
examples.trans: In the afternoons someone plays a gentle melody on the old parlor piano.

examples.text: Hace veinticinco años daba clases de piano muy cerca de esta calle.
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago I gave piano lessons very close to this street.

meanings.note: Colloquial feminine noun (masculine 'pibe'); originally a Rioplatense/Italian borrowing, it is widely used in Madrid urban and youth slang ('mi piba' = my girlfriend).

examples.text: Muchas gracias, pero es que he quedado con mi piba.
examples.trans: Thank you very much, but the thing is I'm meeting up with my girlfriend.

examples.text: Esa piba tiene muchísimo talento para la comedia.
examples.trans: That girl has a ton of talent for comedy.

meanings.note: Metal lever handle on a door.

examples.text: El picaporte está aquí.
examples.trans: The door handle is here.

examples.text: Vemos los picaportes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the door handles from the door.

picar.gloss: to chop; to mince; to itch

meanings.en: to chop; to mince; to itch
meanings.note: Spelling changes c -> qu before -e (piqué); means both 'to chop finely' and 'to itch'.

examples.text: Javier pica perejil fresco y zanahoria sobre la tabla.
examples.trans: Javier chops fresh parsley and carrot on the board.

examples.text: Con el polvo de lijar madera me pica la nariz.
examples.trans: Sanding dust makes my nose itch.

meanings.en: beak, bill; mouth, lips (colloquial); peck on the lips
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('el pico'). Colloquially refers to a person's mouth or lips (e.g., 'cerrar el pico' = to shut one's mouth, or puckering the lips).

meanings.en: peak, summit; a bit over (in 'y pico')
meanings.note: Used in numerical expressions like 'treinta y pico' ('thirty-something' / 'thirty and change').

examples.text: Niña, el pico. Es Lidia San José, la niña de "¡Ala... Dina!".
examples.trans: Girl, watch your mouth. That's Lidia San José, the girl from "¡Ala... Dina!".

examples.text: Niña, el pico, de verdad, eh. ¡Es que no me sale!
examples.trans: Girl, the lip movement, seriously. I just can't get it right!

related.gloss: to bite, to sting, to snack
little beak, quick peck on the lips

meanings.note: Estar de pie means 'to stand / be standing'; ir a pie means 'to walk'.

examples.text: Después de seis horas de pie agradezco una silla.
examples.trans: After six hours on my feet I welcome a chair.

examples.text: Descansa los pies sobre este taburete bajo de madera.
examples.trans: Rest your feet on this low wooden stool.

meanings.note: De piedra = made of stone.

examples.text: La piedra está aquí.
examples.trans: The stone is here.

examples.text: Vemos las piedras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stones from the door.

meanings.note: Plural of the feminine noun 'piedra'. Featured in the expressive idiom 'si las piedras hablaran' ('if these stones/walls could talk').

examples.text: Ay, si las piedras de la plaza hablaran...
examples.trans: Oh, if the stones of the square could speak...

examples.text: El camino hacia la ermita del pueblo está lleno de piedras.
examples.trans: The path to the village chapel is full of stones.

meanings.note: Plural las pieles; covers fruit peel (la piel del limón), human skin, and leather.

examples.text: La piel amarilla de este limón huele de maravilla.
examples.trans: The yellow peel of this lemon smells wonderful.

examples.text: Mateo guarda sus herramientas en una bolsa de piel.
examples.trans: Mateo keeps his tools in a leather bag.

meanings.note: Second-person singular (tú) affirmative imperative or third-person singular present indicative of the stem-changing verb 'pensar' (e > ie).

examples.text: Pues piensa... que siempre que lo estés viendo, yo estoy ahí detrás de todo.
examples.trans: Well think... that whenever you are watching it, I am right there behind everything.

examples.text: Ella siempre piensa en el bienestar de sus actrices antes que en el suyo.
examples.trans: She always thinks about the well-being of her actresses before her own.

examples.text: Venga, poneos las pilas. Ahora vengo. A currar, ¿eh?
examples.trans: Come on, get moving. I'll be right back. Get to work, okay?

examples.text: Hablamos de pila en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about batteries (ponerse las pilas = get moving) at the office.

examples.text: A ti ya te pillaré, Canelón. Vámonos.
examples.trans: I'll catch up with you later, Canelón. Let's go.

examples.text: Yo pillar
examples.trans: I pillar

meanings.en: they caught (red-handed), they busted; they got/grabbed
meanings.note: Third-person plural preterite indicative of 'pillar'. Very common in Peninsular Spanish for being caught doing something secret ('nos pillaron').

examples.text: Y, nada, nos pillaron.
examples.trans: And, well, they caught us.

examples.text: Se colaron en la fiesta de los Goya, pero los de seguridad los pillaron enseguida.
examples.trans: They snuck into the Goya Awards party, but security caught them right away.

related.gloss: to catch, to grab, to get (infinitive)

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('el pimiento'). Roasted red peppers ('pimientos riojanos' or 'del piquillo') are a celebrated agricultural specialty of La Rioja, including Paquita's hometown of Navarrete.

examples.text: En Navarrete hay mucha alcachofa, mucho pimiento, hay melocotón...
examples.trans: In Navarrete there are lots of artichokes, lots of peppers, there are peaches...

examples.text: Mi madre me ha mandado dos botes de pimientos asados del pueblo.
examples.trans: My mother sent me two jars of roasted peppers from the village.

meanings.note: Rueda pinchada = flat tyre.

examples.text: Es una pieza pinchada.
examples.trans: It is a punctured piece.

examples.text: La furgoneta del reparto tiene una rueda pinchada. ¡Mirad la nevera!
examples.trans: The delivery van has a flat tyre. Look in the fridge!

meanings.note: Formed from pinchar ('to prick') + -azo; means a sudden jab of pain, a needle prick, or a flat tyre.

examples.text: Sentí un pequeño pinchazo en el tobillo al bajar la escalera.
examples.trans: I felt a small twinge in my ankle coming down the stairs.

examples.text: Hoy camino sin ningún pinchazo después de descansar dos días.
examples.trans: Today I am walking without a single twinge after resting two days.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from pintar.

examples.text: Es una pieza pintada.
examples.trans: It is a painted piece.

examples.text: Solo una llave dorada pintada encima de la puerta. Enséñale esta válvula al dependiente.
examples.trans: Only a painted golden key above the door. Show the clerk this valve.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: En primavera pintamos la puerta azul.
examples.trans: In spring we paint the blue door.

examples.text: El abuelo pintó una llave dorada.
examples.trans: Grandfather painted a golden key.

meanings.note: Pintura fresca = wet paint.

examples.text: La pintura es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The paint is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la pintura.
examples.trans: We talk about the paint.

meanings.note: Usually plural (unas pinzas) when referring to precision tweezers.

examples.text: Necesito unas pinzas finas para sujetar el pasador.
examples.trans: I need thin tweezers to hold the pin.

examples.text: Guarda las pinzas pequeñas en el bolsillo del maletín.
examples.trans: Keep the small tweezers in the toolkit pocket.

pisar.gloss: to step on; to tread on

meanings.en: to step on; to tread on
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: No pises el papel marrón junto a las contraventanas.
examples.trans: Do not step on the brown paper next to the shutters.

examples.text: Cuidado al pisar las baldosas húmedas de la entrada.
examples.trans: Be careful stepping on the damp entrance tiles.

meanings.note: In Spain, un piso primarily means an apartment.

examples.text: El piso está aquí.
examples.trans: The flat / apartment is here.

examples.text: Vemos los pisos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the flat / apartments from the door.

meanings.note: In a mystery or treasure hunt, una pista is a clue; also means a dance floor (pista de baile) or sports court (pista de tenis).

examples.text: Lee la pista de la postal una vez más, Clara.
examples.trans: Read the clue on the postcard one more time, Clara.

examples.text: Seguimos las cuatro pistas por la calle de los Tilos.
examples.trans: We followed all four clues along Calle de los Tilos.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la pistola'). Often used hyperbolically in expressions of pressure or coercion such as 'con una pistola en la sien' ('with a gun to one's head').

examples.text: ¿Eh? Con una pistola en la sien.
examples.trans: Huh? With a gun to my head.

examples.text: En el thriller policiaco su personaje tenía que llevar una pistola de fogueo.
examples.trans: In the police thriller her character had to carry a prop gun with blanks.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Es Piti al teléfono.
examples.trans: It's Piti on the phone.

examples.text: Dile a Piti que me invite.
examples.trans: Tell Piti to invite me.

meanings.note: Used in cafés and inns for daily menus and task lists.

examples.text: Clara apuntó las tres tareas en la pizarra.
examples.trans: Clara wrote the three tasks on the board.

examples.text: Colgamos una pizarra pequeña junto a la puerta del café.
examples.trans: We hung a small menu board beside the café door.

meanings.note: Una pizca de sal is the standard cooking measure for a tiny pinch.

examples.text: Añade una pizca de sal fina a la masa dulce.
examples.trans: Add a pinch of fine salt to the sweet pastry.

examples.text: Probamos una pizca de crema con una cuchara limpia.
examples.trans: We taste a tiny dab of cream with a clean spoon.

examples.text: Aquí tiene su pizza dos mitades, alitas y panes de ajo con queso.
examples.trans: Here is your half-and-half pizza, wings, and cheesy garlic bread.

examples.text: ¿Para qué quieres que lo coja? Estoy tumbada con tres pizzas y dos botellas de vino.
examples.trans: Why do you want me to pick up? I'm lying here with three pizzas and two bottles of wine.

meanings.note: Metal nameplate on a door or chest.

examples.text: La placa está aquí.
examples.trans: The plate is here.

examples.text: Vemos las placas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the plates from the door.

meanings.note: Diminutive of la plaza.

examples.text: La placita está aquí.
examples.trans: The little square is here.

examples.text: Vemos las placitas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the little squares from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los planes.

examples.text: Nuestro plan para hoy es arreglar la fuente del patio antes del almuerzo.
examples.trans: Our plan for today is to fix the courtyard fountain before lunch.

examples.text: Si llueve esta tarde, cambiaremos de plan y tomaremos chocolate en el salón.
examples.trans: If it rains this afternoon, we will change plans and have hot chocolate in the parlor.

examples.text: Venga, Belinda, cariño. Llevas aquí tres horas y tenemos mucha plancha.
examples.trans: Come on, Belinda, darling. You've been here three hours and we have a lot of work waiting.

examples.text: Hablamos de plancha en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about pending work (tener plancha) at the office.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; participle planchado/a means 'ironed / pressed' (manteles bien planchados).

examples.text: Clara planchó los cuatro manteles blancos antes de poner las mesas.
examples.trans: Clara ironed the four white tablecloths before setting the tables.

examples.text: Las cortinas limpias y recién planchadas dejan pasar toda la luz.
examples.trans: The clean, freshly ironed curtains let all the light through.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Planeamos una cena tranquila mañana.
examples.trans: We are planning a quiet dinner tomorrow.

examples.text: ¿Planeaste tú esta sorpresa?
examples.trans: Did you plan this surprise?

meanings.note: Architectural drawing or city street map.

examples.text: El plano está aquí.
examples.trans: The blueprint is here.

examples.text: Vemos los planos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the blueprints from the door.

meanings.note: Planta baja = ground floor; primera planta = first floor; also a green plant.

examples.text: La planta está aquí.
examples.trans: The floor / storey is here.

examples.text: Vemos las plantas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the floor / storeys from the door.

meanings.note: Quedarse plantado = stand frozen/stranded.

examples.text: Es una pieza plantada.
examples.trans: It is a planted piece.

examples.text: ¿Has plantado tú mismo esas hierbas, Mateo?
examples.trans: Did you plant those herbs yourself, Mateo?

meanings.note: Participle of plastificar ('to laminate'); una carta plastificada wipes clean easily in cafés.

examples.text: Las cartas plastificadas del café no se manchan con el té.
examples.trans: The laminated café menus do not get stained by tea.

examples.text: Lleva su carné de la biblioteca en una funda plastificada.
examples.trans: He carries his library card in a laminated sleeve.

meanings.note: Describes silver metal.

examples.text: Es una pieza plateada.
examples.trans: It is a silver piece.

examples.text: ¡Qué alivio! Aquí tiene su llave plateada, Javier.
examples.trans: What a relief! Here is your silver key, Javier.

meanings.note: Refers to dinner plates, teacup saucers, and cooked courses.

examples.text: Coloca cada taza blanca sobre su plato limpio.
examples.trans: Set each white cup on its clean saucer.

examples.text: La sopa caliente es el mejor plato para la lluvia.
examples.trans: Hot soup is the best dish for rainy weather.

meanings.note: Diminutive la placita names a cosy neighbourhood square.

examples.text: La plaza está aquí.
examples.trans: The square is here.

examples.text: Vemos las plazas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the squares from the door.

meanings.note: Silla plegable = folding chair.

examples.text: Es una pieza plegable.
examples.trans: It is a folding piece.

examples.text: sillas plegables
examples.trans: folding chairs

meanings.note: Stem changes e -> ie in stressed present forms (pliego, pliegas, pliega, pliegan); g -> gu before -e (plegué).

examples.text: Plegamos las sillas de madera después del concierto.
examples.trans: We fold up the wooden chairs after the concert.

examples.text: Esta mesa pequeña se pliega en dos segundos.
examples.trans: This small table folds up in two seconds.

pleno.gloss: full; bright (a plena luz del sol)

meanings.en: full; bright (a plena luz del sol)
meanings.note: A plena luz del sol = in broad daylight.

examples.text: Es una pieza plena.
examples.trans: It is a full piece.

examples.text: ¿Puedo mirar otra vez la etiqueta de cartón aquí a plena luz del sol?
examples.trans: May I look at the cardboard tag again here in bright sunlight?

meanings.note: Related to plegar ('to fold'); denotes the physical fold line in paper, letters, or fabric.

examples.text: Abra el papel antiguo con cuidado por el pliegue.
examples.trans: Unfold the old paper carefully along the crease.

examples.text: La carta tenía dos pliegues marcados en el centro.
examples.trans: The letter had two sharp creases in the middle.

meanings.note: In Spanish LGBTQ+ and colloquial usage, 'tener pluma' or 'subirse de pluma' refers to noticeably campy or effeminate mannerisms.
Literal sense of the feminine noun 'la pluma'.

examples.text: pero se les sube de pluma, no... Sí.
examples.trans: but they get a bit too campy, right... Yes.

examples.text: Que se les sube mucho de pluma, dicen.
examples.trans: They say their campiness really comes out.

related.gloss: feather duster (in 'ver el plumero' = see someone's true colors)

meanings.note: Before a noun (el pobre caballero), expresses sympathy.

examples.text: Es una pieza pobre.
examples.trans: It is a poor piece.

examples.text: Entonces dime por qué el pobre caballero del mostrador parece a punto de llorar.
examples.trans: Then tell me why the poor gentleman behind the front desk looks ready to cry.

meanings.en: the poor, poor people; poor, broke, unfortunate
meanings.note: Plural of 'pobre'. Used as a substantive plural noun ('los pobres') to mean 'poor people' (often jokingly when a friend becomes famous or wealthy) and as an adjective meaning 'unfortunate' (before the noun) or 'broke' (after the noun).

examples.text: ¿Ya no quieres nada con los pobres?
examples.trans: You do not want anything to do with the poor anymore?

examples.text: ¡Pobres chavales, llevan cuatro horas esperando para entrar al casting!
examples.trans: Poor kids, they've been waiting four hours to get into the audition!

meanings.note: Un poco de mantequilla = a little butter.

examples.text: ¿Quiere un poco de miel en el té?
examples.trans: Would you like a little honey in your tea?

examples.text: Quedan pocos minutos para el mediodía.
examples.trans: Few minutes remain until noon.

podemos.gloss: we can, we are able to

meanings.en: we can, we are able to, may we
meanings.note: First-person plural (nosotros/nosotras) present indicative of the modal verb 'poder'. Frequently used in questions ('¿podemos...?') to make requests or try to calm a situation.

examples.text: Paquita, ¿podemos quitar esta puta frase que no me sale?
examples.trans: Paquita, can we cut this fucking line that I just can't get right?

examples.text: Mariona, ¿nos podemos tranquilizar un momento, por favor?
examples.trans: Mariona, can we calm down for a moment, please?

related.gloss: to be able to, can (infinitive); power

poder.gloss: can; to be able to; may

meanings.en: can; to be able to; may
meanings.note: Irregular: puedo, pude, podría.

examples.text: ¿Puedo ver la etiqueta otra vez?
examples.trans: May I look at the tag again?

examples.text: Hoy podemos desayunar en el patio.
examples.trans: Today we can have breakfast in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Common-gender noun ('el/la policía') when referring to an individual officer (or, in the Spanish title of 'Inspector Rex', a police dog).
Always feminine singular ('la policía') when referring collectively to the police force as an institution.

examples.text: de "Rex, un policía diferente", se pone...
examples.trans: of "Rex, a different kind of police officer", she gets...

examples.text: Le dieron el papel de inspector de policía en una serie de Antena 3.
examples.trans: They gave him the role of police inspector in an Antena 3 series.

meanings.note: Quitar el polvo = to dust.

examples.text: El polvo es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The dust is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el polvo.
examples.trans: We talk about the dust.

meanings.en: I would put/place, he/she/you would put
meanings.note: First- or third-person singular conditional indicative of the irregular verb 'poner' (stem 'pondr-'). Commonly used to offer polite suggestions.

examples.text: pondría un fondo blanco ahí. Tengo esta pared libre.
examples.trans: I would put a white backdrop there. I have this wall free.

examples.text: Yo no pondría esa foto en el videobook porque tiene mala luz.
examples.trans: I wouldn't put that photo in the showreel because the lighting is bad.

meanings.en: we put, we place, we write down/include
meanings.note: First-person plural (nosotros/nosotras) present indicative of 'poner'. In Paquita Salas, 'le ponemos que...' refers to padding an actress's CV with extra credits.

examples.text: Digo, pues le ponemos que ha hecho un capitulito,
examples.trans: I say, well let's put down for her that she did a little episode,

examples.text: Si nos ponemos de acuerdo con el representante, firmamos el contrato hoy mismo.
examples.trans: If we reach an agreement with the agent, we'll sign the contract today.

poner.gloss: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)

meanings.en: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)
meanings.note: Irregular: pongo, pon, puse, puesto; ponerse nervioso = get nervous.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas limpias en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two clean cups on the table.

examples.text: Pon la maleta junto al mostrador.
examples.trans: Set the suitcase beside the counter.

meanings.note: First- or third-person singular present subjunctive (or usted imperative) of the irregular verb 'poner' (stem 'pong-'). In Peninsular Spanish, 'poner un café/una caña' is the standard idiom for serving or pouring a drink.

examples.text: Oye, he hecho café. ¿Quieres que te ponga uno?
examples.trans: Hey, I made coffee. Do you want me to pour you one?

examples.text: Dile al camarero que nos ponga unos torreznos para picar.
examples.trans: Tell the waiter to bring us some fried pork belly strips to snack on.

ponme.gloss: put on for me, pour me

meanings.en: put on for me, play for me; pour/serve me
meanings.note: Irregular second-person singular (tú) affirmative imperative 'pon' (from 'poner') with the enclitic indirect object pronoun 'me'. Used both for playing media ('ponme otro capítulo') and ordering food or drinks in Spain ('ponme una caña').

examples.text: Ponme otro capítulo.
examples.trans: Put another episode on for me.

examples.text: Eh... ¡Ponme otro capítulo!
examples.trans: Hey... Put another episode on for me!

related.gloss: to put, to turn on, to serve (infinitive)

examples.text: No puedo. No, no. Ponte así.
examples.trans: I cannot. No, no. Get like this.

examples.text: Yo Ponte
examples.trans: I Ponte

meanings.en: a little bit, a tad, slightly (in 'un poquillo')
meanings.note: Colloquial diminutive of 'poco' formed with the suffix '-illo'. Very common in conversational Peninsular Spanish ('un poquillo') to soften or downplay a statement.

examples.text: La chica se agobió un poquillo y yo me la traje aquí de fugitiva.
examples.trans: The girl got a little bit overwhelmed and I brought her here as a runaway.

examples.text: Estoy un poquillo nerviosa por la prueba de vestuario de mañana.
examples.trans: I'm a little bit nervous about tomorrow's costume fitting.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Used both for fine teacups and classic white ceramic electrical fuses.

examples.text: Mi abuela tenía una tetera blanca de porcelana.
examples.trans: My grandmother had a white porcelain teapot.

examples.text: Mateo cambió el fusible viejo de porcelana.
examples.trans: Mateo replaced the old porcelain fuse.

meanings.note: One word without accent (distinct from ¿por qué? = why?).

examples.text: Abro la ventana porque hace calor.
examples.trans: I open the window because it is warm.

examples.text: Sonríe porque huele a canela.
examples.trans: She smiles because it smells of cinnamon.

examples.text: Dejamos el vestido al portero.
examples.trans: We'll leave the dress with the doorman.

examples.text: El portero abre la puerta.
examples.trans: The doorman opens the door.

examples.text: Natalie Portman es un ejemplo perfecto.
examples.trans: Natalie Portman is a perfect example.

examples.text: Yo Portman
examples.trans: I Portman

meanings.note: Augmentative of puerta; drops the written accent in plural portones.

examples.text: Colgamos el cartel de madera junto al portón principal.
examples.trans: We hung the wooden sign beside the main front gate.

examples.text: El portón de la calle se cierra a las diez.
examples.trans: The street gate closes at ten o'clock.

meanings.note: Charming small inn with rooms around a courtyard.

examples.text: La posada está aquí.
examples.trans: The inn is here.

examples.text: Vemos las posadas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the inns from the door.

examples.text: Porque esto no habría sido posible sin ti. ¡Gracias, Paquita!
examples.trans: Because this wouldn't have been possible without you. Thank you, Paquita!

examples.text: Hablamos de posible en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about possible at the office.
