examples.text: Hablamos de segurísimo en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about completely sure at the office.

meanings.note: Las seis = six o'clock.

examples.text: Me despierto a las seis y media.
examples.trans: I wake up at six thirty.

examples.text: Tengo seis limones en la cesta.
examples.trans: I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Postage stamp or official ink stamp.

examples.text: El sello está aquí.
examples.trans: The stamp is here.

examples.text: Vemos los sellos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stamps from the door.

meanings.note: Fin de semana = weekend; la semana que viene = next week.

examples.text: La semana está aquí.
examples.trans: The week is here.

examples.text: Vemos las semanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the weeks from the door.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Esta noche tiene la Seminci.
examples.trans: Tonight she has Seminci.

examples.text: Vamos al estreno de la Seminci.
examples.trans: We're going to the Seminci premiere.

meanings.note: En palabras sencillas = in plain words.

examples.text: Es una pieza sencilla.
examples.trans: It is a simple piece.

examples.text: ¡En palabras sencillas, por favor! ¿Qué dice la cláusula catorce?
examples.trans: In plain words, please! What does Clause fourteen say?

meanings.note: False friend: means 'sensible', whereas 'sensitive' is sensible!

examples.text: Es una pieza sensata.
examples.trans: It is a sensible piece.

examples.text: sensato
examples.trans: sensible

meanings.note: False friend: means sensitive or emotional, not sensible/practical.

examples.text: Me he puesto sensible.
examples.trans: I got emotional.

examples.text: Es una persona muy sensible.
examples.trans: She's a very sensitive person.

meanings.note: Estar sentado = to be sitting.

examples.text: Es una pieza sentada.
examples.trans: It is a seated piece.

examples.text: Esperen: ¿quién está sentado a diez metros en nuestro patio ahora mismo?
examples.trans: Wait—who is sitting ten metres away in our courtyard right now?

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: me siento, ¡siéntese!).

examples.text: Siéntese junto a la ventana, por favor.
examples.trans: Sit down by the window, please.

examples.text: Nos sentamos bajo el limonero.
examples.trans: We sit down under the lemon tree.

meanings.note: Plural sentimentales.

examples.text: Ese reloj de bolsillo tiene un enorme valor sentimental para toda la familia.
examples.trans: That pocket watch has tremendous sentimental value for the whole family.

examples.text: Había que enderezar el alambre igualmente; nada sentimental, solo buen mantenimiento.
examples.trans: The wire needed straightening anyway—nothing sentimental, just good maintenance.

sentir.gloss: to feel; to be sorry (lo siento)

meanings.en: to feel; to be sorry (lo siento)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie in present, e -> i in preterite 3rd: sintió).

examples.text: Lo siento mucho por la espera.
examples.trans: I am very sorry about the wait.

examples.text: Aquí cada huésped se siente en casa.
examples.trans: Here every guest feels at home.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.

examples.text: Esa maleta azul es mía.
examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

examples.text: Trabaja en una serie nueva.
examples.trans: She's working on a new series.

examples.text: Veo muchas series españolas.
examples.trans: I watch lots of Spanish series.

meanings.note: Masculine singular adjective serio; exceedingly common in the adverbial phrase "en serio" to express disbelief, ask for confirmation, or emphasize sincerity.
Describes a person or organization that is responsible and trustworthy, or a grave situation.

examples.text: ¿En serio te vas? Te lo hace ella, lo hará perfecto.
examples.trans: Are you seriously leaving? She'll do it for you, she'll do it perfectly.

examples.text: ¿En serio? Se va a poner muy contenta. Hasta luego.
examples.trans: Really? She's going to be so happy. See you later.

meanings.note: Atención y servicio = guest service.

examples.text: El servicio está aquí.
examples.trans: The service is here.

examples.text: Vemos los servicios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the services from the door.

meanings.note: Cloth or paper table napkin.

examples.text: La servilleta está aquí.
examples.trans: The napkin is here.

examples.text: Vemos las servilletas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the napkins from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: sirvo, sirve, sirvió).

examples.text: Servimos desayuno caliente de ocho a diez.
examples.trans: We serve hot breakfast from eight to ten.

examples.text: La encargada sirvió tres tazas de té de menta.
examples.trans: La encargada served three cups of mint tea.

examples.text: Nosotros buscamos a la actriz tres sesenta.
examples.trans: We are looking for the three-sixty actress.

examples.text: Yo sesenta
examples.trans: I sesenta

examples.text: Carmen Sevilla.
examples.trans: Carmen Sevilla.

examples.text: Yo Sevilla
examples.trans: I Sevilla

meanings.note: Hacer señas = to wave / motion to someone.

examples.text: La seña está aquí.
examples.trans: The wave is here.

examples.text: Vemos las señas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the waves from the door.

señalar.gloss: to point; to point at / out

meanings.en: to point; to point at / out
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Señala en el mapa dónde estamos.
examples.trans: Point on the map to where we are.

examples.text: Señaló con el lápiz la segunda hoja.
examples.trans: He pointed at the second sheet with his pencil.

meanings.note: Takes el when talking about someone (el señor Martín), no article when addressing directly (¡Buenos días, señor!).

examples.text: El señor está aquí.
examples.trans: The sir is here.

examples.text: Vemos los señores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sirs from the door.

meanings.note: Polite form of address: señora Carmen.

examples.text: La señora está aquí.
examples.trans: The madam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las señoras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the madams from the door.

meanings.note: Unaccented conjunction, distinct from accented sí ('yes').

examples.text: Avísame si necesitas otra manta.
examples.trans: Let me know if you need another blanket.

examples.text: Mira si queda leche en la nevera.
examples.trans: Check whether any milk is left in the fridge.

meanings.note: Invariable past participle of the verb ser, used with forms of the auxiliary verb haber to form all compound perfect tenses.

examples.text: Él siempre ha sido muy de no parar quieto.
examples.trans: He has always been the type who never sits still.

examples.text: Porque esto no habría sido posible sin ti. ¡Gracias, Paquita!
examples.trans: Because this wouldn't have been possible without you. Thank you, Paquita!

siempre.gloss: always (siempre que = whenever / as long as)

meanings.en: always (siempre que = whenever / as long as)
meanings.note: Opposite of nunca.

examples.text: El patio siempre está tranquilo.
examples.trans: The courtyard is always quiet.

examples.text: Ven siempre que quieras tomar café.
examples.trans: Come whenever you want to have coffee.

meanings.note: Feminine anatomical noun (la sien, plural las sienes). Frequently appears in figurative hyperbole such as "con una pistola en la sien" ("under extreme duress / with a gun to one's head").

examples.text: ¿Eh? Con una pistola en la sien.
examples.trans: Huh? With a gun to my temple.

examples.text: Me laten las sienes después de toda la mañana haciendo llamadas.
examples.trans: My temples are throbbing after spending all morning making calls.

siento.gloss: I feel, I regret; (lo siento) I'm sorry

meanings.en: (lo siento) I'm sorry, excuse me, I regret it
meanings.note: First-person singular present indicative of sentir (e > ie stem change). With the neuter object pronoun "lo", "lo siento" is the standard everyday expression of apology or sympathy.

meanings.en: I feel; (me siento) I feel / I sit down
meanings.note: Also serves as the first-person singular present indicative of sentirse ("to feel") and sentarse ("to sit down").

examples.text: Lo siento. ¿Tú quién eres?
examples.trans: I'm sorry. Who are you?

examples.text: Hola, lo siento. Oye, chicas, tenemos una urgencia.
examples.trans: Hi, I'm sorry. Listen, girls, we have an emergency.

meanings.note: Las siete y cuarto = seven fifteen.

examples.text: La habitación siete mira al patio.
examples.trans: Room seven overlooks the courtyard.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las siete y media.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at seven thirty.

meanings.note: ¿Qué significa eso? = What does that mean?

examples.text: ¿Qué significa esta palabra antigua?
examples.trans: What does this old word mean?

examples.text: Dos toques significan que llaman arriba.
examples.trans: Two rings mean someone is calling upstairs.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine: la siguiente postal, el día siguiente.

examples.text: Bajamos en la siguiente parada.
examples.trans: We get off at the next stop.

examples.text: Al día siguiente, todo está tranquilo.
examples.trans: The following day, everything is calm.

meanings.note: En silencio = quietly.

examples.text: El silencio es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The silence is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el silencio.
examples.trans: We talk about the silence.

meanings.note: Regular four-form adjective from silencio ('silence').

examples.text: El patio interior es muy silencioso por la noche.
examples.trans: The inner courtyard is very quiet at night.

examples.text: Buscamos un rincón silencioso para leer y tomar té.
examples.trans: We look for a quiet corner to read and drink tea.

meanings.note: Wooden or folding chair.

examples.text: La silla está aquí.
examples.trans: The chair is here.

examples.text: Vemos las sillas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the chairs from the door.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Ahora está con Silvia.
examples.trans: He's with Silvia now.

examples.text: Silvia hace judo.
examples.trans: Silvia does judo.

meanings.note: Formed from simple + -mente.

examples.text: Simplemente quería darte las gracias.
examples.trans: I simply wanted to thank you.

examples.text: Ponlo simplemente encima de la mesa.
examples.trans: Just set it on top of the table.

meanings.note: Plural form of the adjective simple, which is invariable for gender. Placed after the noun ("cosas simples"), it means straightforward or modest; placed before the noun, it means "mere".

examples.text: En un evento de un champú... Cosas así, cosas simples.
examples.trans: At a shampoo event... Things like that, simple things.

examples.text: A veces las ideas más simples son las que mejor funcionan.
examples.trans: Sometimes the simplest ideas are the ones that work best.

meanings.note: Followed by bare nouns (sin azúcar, sin sal) or infinitives (sin abrir = unopened).

examples.text: Tomo el té sin azúcar, gracias.
examples.trans: I take my tea without sugar, thank you.

examples.text: Salió de casa sin abrigo.
examples.trans: He left home without a coat.

meanings.note: Formed from sincera + -mente.

examples.text: Sinceramente, el bizcocho está delicioso.
examples.trans: Honestly, the sponge cake is delicious.

examples.text: Te lo digo muy sinceramente.
examples.trans: I mean it very sincerely.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number.

examples.text: Es una pieza sincera.
examples.trans: It is a honest piece.

examples.text: Señor, antes de subir, le debo una disculpa sincera.
examples.trans: Sir, before going upstairs, I owe you an honest apology.

meanings.note: Used in negative or conditional contexts.

examples.text: No cayó ni siquiera una gota.
examples.trans: Not even a single drop fell.

examples.text: Descansa cinco minutos siquiera.
examples.trans: Rest even just five minutes.

meanings.note: Feminine diminutive of sirena ("mermaid") formed with the suffix -ita. Capitalized as "la Sirenita", it refers to the classic fairy-tale and animated character.

examples.text: —Yo soy la Sirenita. —Pero ¿qué vas a ser la Sirenita? Anda...
examples.trans: —I am the Little Mermaid. —What do you mean you're going to be the Little Mermaid? Come on...

examples.text: Las niñas del taller querían vestirse de sirenitas para la función.
examples.trans: The girls in the workshop wanted to dress up as little mermaids for the show.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ending in -a (el sistema), belonging to the group of Greek-derived nouns in -ma (like el problema, el tema, el guion/drama) that take masculine articles and adjectives.

examples.text: Nos gusta mucho el sistema europeo.
examples.trans: We really like the European system.

examples.text: Se ha caído el sistema informático y no podemos mandar los correos.
examples.trans: The computer system has crashed and we can't send the emails.

meanings.note: Everyday Peninsula favourite for 'place' or 'seat'.

examples.text: El sitio está aquí.
examples.trans: The place is here.

examples.text: Vemos los sitios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the place from the door.

meanings.note: Informal second-person singular (tú) affirmative imperative of the reflexive verb sentarse (sienta + enclitic pronoun te). Carries a written accent on the first syllable because it is stressed on the third-to-last syllable (esdrújula).

examples.text: Cuando digas "acción", Magüi. Siéntate.
examples.trans: Whenever you say "action", Magüi. Sit down.

examples.text: Bueno, ven. Ven, siéntate y cuéntame.
examples.trans: Well, come here. Come, sit down and tell me.

sobrar.gloss: to be left over; to have to spare

meanings.en: to be left over; to have to spare
meanings.note: Often used in 3rd person (sobra tiempo, sobran monedas).

examples.text: Pagamos las tazas y todavía sobran cinco euros.
examples.trans: We paid for the cups and there are still five euros left over.

examples.text: ¿Sobra un poco de leche caliente en la jarra?
examples.trans: Is there a little warm milk left in the jug?

sobre.gloss: on; upon; about; out of (nueve sobre diez)

meanings.en: on; upon; about; out of (nueve sobre diez)
meanings.note: Sobre todo = above all / mostly; also a homograph noun el sobre ('envelope').

examples.text: Deja la llave sobre el mostrador.
examples.trans: Leave the key on the counter.

examples.text: Sacó nueve sobre diez en la prueba.
examples.trans: She scored nine out of ten on the test.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb; sobrevivir a algo = survive something.

examples.text: Este olivo sobrevivió a muchas heladas.
examples.trans: This olive tree survived many frosts.

examples.text: Mis tazas favoritas sobrevivieron al viaje.
examples.trans: My favourite cups survived the trip.

meanings.note: Feminine socia; business partner in a firm or club member.

examples.text: Mi socio se encarga de la oficina hasta el sábado.
examples.trans: My partner is looking after the office until Saturday.

examples.text: Los dos socios abrieron el estudio hace cinco años.
examples.trans: The two partners opened the studio five years ago.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Hola, Sofi, ¿qué tal?
examples.trans: Hello, Sofi, how are things?

examples.text: Sofi recibe a los invitados.
examples.trans: Sofi welcomes the guests.

meanings.note: Hace sol = it is sunny.

examples.text: El sol es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The sun is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el sol.
examples.trans: We talk about the sun.

examples.text: Solamente necesita querer. Y querer es poder, eso está claro, Paquita.
examples.trans: You only need to want it. And where there's a will there's a way, that's clear, Paquita.

examples.text: Hablamos de solamente en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about only, solely at the office.

meanings.note: Una ventana soleada = a sunny window.

examples.text: Es una pieza soleada.
examples.trans: It is a sunny piece.

examples.text: La vieja buhardilla soleada... ¡seguidme, rápido!
examples.trans: The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

soler.gloss: to usually do; to tend to (soler + infinitive)

meanings.en: to usually do; to tend to (soler + infinitive)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: suelo, suele, suelen) used in present/imperfect + infinitive.

examples.text: Suelo tomar café a las ocho.
examples.trans: I usually have coffee at eight.

examples.text: Estos muros suelen guardar el fresco.
examples.trans: These walls usually keep the air cool.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.text: Solo necesito cinco minutos más.
examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.

examples.text: Queda una sola habitación libre.
examples.trans: Only a single room remains vacant.

examples.text: Un chupito para soltarte.
examples.trans: A shot to loosen you up.

examples.text: Suelta la maleta aquí.
examples.trans: Set the suitcase down here.

examples.text: Magüi está solucionándolo.
examples.trans: Magüi is sorting it out.

examples.text: Solucionamos el problema hoy.
examples.trans: We'll sort out the problem today.

meanings.note: A la sombra means 'in the shade'.

examples.text: Nos sentamos a la sombra fresca del limonero.
examples.trans: We sit in the cool shade of the lemon tree.

examples.text: La lámpara dibuja una sombra suave en la pared.
examples.trans: The lamp casts a soft shadow on the wall.

meanings.note: Built from sombra ('shade'), because a brimmed hat casts shade over the face; quitarse el sombrero = to take off one's hat.

examples.text: Un señor mayor con sombrero gris se paró a escuchar en la acera.
examples.trans: An older gentleman in a grey hat stopped to listen on the pavement.

examples.text: Se quitó el sombrero con respeto al entrar en la sala.
examples.trans: He took off his hat respectfully as he stepped into the room.

meanings.note: Third-person plural (ellos/ellas/ustedes) present indicative of ser. Used to express identity, inherent traits, origin, time, or cost.
As a masculine noun (el son), denotes a pleasant musical sound or traditional Cuban music genre, and appears in idioms like "sin ton ni son" ("without rhyme or reason").

examples.text: Cuidado con las medias, que son caras.
examples.trans: Careful with the stockings, they are expensive.

examples.text: Bueno, es que no sabes cómo son.
examples.trans: Well, the thing is you do not know how they are.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: suena).

examples.text: El despertador suena a las seis y media.
examples.trans: The alarm clock rings at six thirty.

examples.text: El piano sonaba cálido bajo la lluvia.
examples.trans: The piano sounded warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Proper female given name (derived from Sophia). In Paquita Salas, mentioned during a children's drama workshop when a student insists on playing "Sonia".

examples.text: ¿Eh? —Yo soy Sonia. —Pero ¿qué vas a ser Sonia?
examples.trans: Huh? —I am Sonia. —What do you mean you're going to be Sonia?

examples.text: Sonia nos ha confirmado que vendrá al estreno de la obra.
examples.trans: Sonia has confirmed to us that she will come to the premiere of the play.

meanings.note: El sonido de la lluvia = the sound of the rain.

examples.text: El sonido está aquí.
examples.trans: The sound is here.

examples.text: Vemos los sonidos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sounds from the door.

meanings.note: Conjugates like reír (sonrío, sonrió); imperative plural: ¡sonreíd!.

examples.text: La panadera siempre sonríe al abrir el horno.
examples.trans: The baker always smiles when opening the oven.

examples.text: Al probar el bizcocho, sonrió enseguida.
examples.trans: Upon tasting the cake, he smiled right away.

meanings.note: Derived from sonreír ('to smile'); invariable for masculine and feminine (un vecino sonriente, una vecina sonriente).

examples.text: En el dibujo aparecen dos vecinos sonrientes con platos de bizcocho.
examples.trans: In the drawing appear two smiling neighbours with plates of cake.

examples.text: Clara recibió a los huéspedes con cara sonriente.
examples.trans: Clara welcomed the guests with a smiling face.

examples.text: Esta sonrisa no es de felicidad.
examples.trans: This smile is not one of happiness.

examples.text: Tiene una sonrisa preciosa.
examples.trans: She has a lovely smile.

meanings.note: Hecho una sopa = soaked through.

examples.text: La sopa está aquí.
examples.trans: The soup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las sopas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the soups from the door.

meanings.note: Beber un sorbo = drink a sip.

examples.text: El sorbo está aquí.
examples.trans: The sip is here.

examples.text: Vemos los sorbos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sips from the door.

examples.text: A mí me ha sorprendido mucho.
examples.trans: It really surprised me.

examples.text: Siempre nos sorprende su talento.
examples.trans: Her talent always surprises us.

examples.text: ¡La tenemos! La voy a llamar y darle la sorpresa.
examples.trans: We've got her! I'm going to call her and give her the surprise.

examples.text: Yo sorpresa
examples.trans: I sorpresa

meanings.note: Mi cafetería soñada = my dream cafe.

examples.text: Es una pieza soñada.
examples.trans: It is a dream piece.

examples.text: soñada
examples.trans: dream (dreamed-of)

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: sueño).

examples.text: Anoche soñé con un viaje en tren.
examples.trans: Last night I dreamed about a train journey.

examples.text: Siempre sueña con tener su propia cafetería.
examples.trans: She always dreams of having her own cafe.

examples.text: Mira en la carpeta de spam.
examples.trans: Look in the spam folder.

examples.text: El correo entró en el spam.
examples.trans: The email went into spam.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave, señora.
examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza suave.
examples.trans: It is a soft piece.

examples.text: Y mire: esta chaqueta de lana suave está limpia y nueva. Pruébela.
examples.trans: And look: this soft wool cardigan is clean and unworn. Try it on.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells z -> c: suavicé.

examples.text: La miel suaviza el té caliente.
examples.trans: Honey mellows hot tea.

examples.text: Las cortinas gruesas suavizan el eco.
examples.trans: Heavy curtains soften the echo.

meanings.note: Third-person singular present indicative of subir. In the colloquial Peninsular expression "subirse de pluma", describes someone becoming noticeably more camp or flamboyant.

meanings.en: go up!, come up!, get in!
meanings.note: Informal second-person singular (tú) affirmative imperative of subir.

examples.text: Pero se les sube de pluma, ¿no?... Sí.
examples.trans: But they get a bit too camp, right?... Yes.

examples.text: Sube al despacho, que tenemos que firmar el contrato.
examples.trans: Come up to the office, we have to sign the contract.

related.gloss: to go up, to rise, to upload

subir.gloss: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs

meanings.en: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs
meanings.note: Works both intransitively and transitively.

examples.text: Subo las toallas limpias a la primera planta.
examples.trans: I carry the clean towels up to the first floor.

examples.text: Subieron despacio la escalera de madera.
examples.trans: They climbed the wooden stairs slowly.

meanings.note: Las tablas del suelo = the floorboards.

examples.text: El suelo está aquí.
examples.trans: The floor is here.

examples.text: Vemos los suelos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the floors from the door.

examples.text: El enchufe está un poco suelto.
examples.trans: The socket is a bit loose.

examples.text: Lleva una camisa suelta.
examples.trans: She's wearing a loose shirt.

examples.text: (Suena "Pekín", de El buen hijo)
examples.trans: Music playing.

examples.text: Yo Suena
examples.trans: I Suena

meanings.note: Pura suerte = sheer luck.

examples.text: La suerte es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The luck is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la suerte.
examples.trans: We talk about the luck.

meanings.note: El mejor sueño = the best sleep.

examples.text: El sueño es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The sleep is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el sueño.
examples.trans: We talk about the sleep.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb.

examples.text: El dueño sufre por cada pequeño detalle.
examples.trans: El dueño frets over every small detail.

examples.text: El tejado no sufrió daños con la tormenta.
examples.trans: The roof suffered no damage in the storm.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Sujeta bien la linterna, por favor.
examples.trans: Hold the flashlight steady, please.

examples.text: Sujetó la nota con un clip metálico.
examples.trans: She clipped the note with a metal paperclip.

meanings.note: Irregular adjectival participle of sujetar.

examples.text: Es una pieza sujeta.
examples.trans: It is a fastened piece.

examples.text: Espere un momento, señor: ¿ha leído la página dos sujeta debajo?
examples.trans: Wait a moment, sir—did you read page two clipped underneath?

examples.text: Pues he montado una banda. ¡Estoy supercontenta!
examples.trans: Well, I've put together a band. I'm super happy!

examples.text: Hablamos de supercontento en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about super happy at the office.

meanings.en: knew, were to know (I / he / she / it / usted)
meanings.note: First- and third-person singular imperfect subjunctive (-ra form) of saber, built on the irregular stem sup-. Famously featured in the show's opening theme song ("¡Ay, si Paquita supiera!").

examples.text: ¡Ay, si Paquita supiera!
examples.trans: Oh, if Paquita knew!

examples.text: Ojalá supiera quién ha filtrado la noticia a la prensa.
examples.trans: I wish I knew who leaked the news to the press.

meanings.en: you knew, you were to know
meanings.note: Second-person singular (tú) imperfect subjunctive (-ra form) of saber. Very common in the emphatic conversational construction "si supieras..." ("if you only knew...").

examples.text: Es que, de verdad, si supieras la cara que se les quedó.
examples.trans: It is just that, really, if you knew the look on their faces.

examples.text: ¡Si supieras lo que me ha costado conseguirte esta entrevista!
examples.trans: If you only knew what it took for me to get you this interview!

meanings.note: ¡Por supuesto! is a warm, emphatic 'Of course!'.

examples.text: Es una pieza supuesta.
examples.trans: It is a supposed piece.

examples.text: ¡Por supuesto! Cada viernes, cuando fallaba una nota al piano, fruncía el ceño mirando la pared.
examples.trans: Of course! Every Friday when he missed a piano note, he frowned at the wall.

meanings.note: Al sur = to the south.

examples.text: El sur es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The south is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el sur.
examples.trans: We talk about the south.

examples.text: (SUSPIRA)
examples.trans: (SIGHS)

examples.text: Yo SUSPIRA
examples.trans: I SUSPIRA

meanings.note: ¡Qué susto! = What a fright!

examples.text: El susto está aquí.
examples.trans: The fright is here.

examples.text: Vemos los sustos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the frights from the door.

meanings.note: Onomatopoeic regular -ar verb whose repeated s and r sounds echo a soft whisper.

examples.text: ¡Susurrad los dos, que los huéspedes todavía duermen!
examples.trans: Whisper, both of you—the guests are still sleeping!

examples.text: Carmen le susurró un secreto al oído a Rocío.
examples.trans: Carmen whispered a secret in Rocío's ear.

meanings.en: of hers, of his, of yours, of theirs; hers, his, yours, theirs
meanings.note: Feminine singular stressed (postnominal) possessive determiner and pronoun corresponding to unstressed su. Follows the noun in phrases like "una amiga suya" ("a friend of hers/his").

forms.title: Stressed Possessive Forms (3rd Person / usted / ustedes)

examples.text: Pues Paca es muy amiga suya. Sí, somos muy amigas.
examples.trans: Well, Paca is a very good friend of hers. Yes, we are very good friends.

examples.text: La idea de cambiar el final del capítulo fue totalmente suya.
examples.trans: The idea of changing the ending of the episode was entirely hers.

meanings.note: Forms: suyo, suya, suyos, suyas.

examples.text: El patio es todo suyo.
examples.trans: The courtyard is all yours.

examples.text: Tranquila, no es culpa suya.
examples.trans: Do not worry, it is not your fault.

meanings.note: El sábado means 'on Saturday'; los sábados means 'on Saturdays'.

examples.text: Los sábados vamos temprano al mercado de la plaza.
examples.trans: On Saturdays we go early to the market in the square.

examples.text: Este sábado abrimos las ventanas de la galería.
examples.trans: This Saturday we open the sunroom windows.

meanings.note: Sábanas limpias = clean sheets.

examples.text: La sábana está aquí.
examples.trans: The bedsheet is here.

examples.text: Vemos las sábanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bedsheets from the door.

sácalo.gloss: take it out!, bring it out!

meanings.en: take it out!, bring it out!, let it out!
meanings.note: Informal second-person singular (tú) affirmative imperative of sacar (saca) combined with the enclitic masculine/neuter direct object pronoun lo. Takes a written accent to maintain stress on the initial syllable.

examples.text: Pues si tienes algo, sácalo. Qué alegría.
examples.trans: Well, if you have something, bring it out. What a joy.

examples.text: Ese talento que llevas dentro, sácalo en el escenario.
examples.trans: That talent you carry inside, bring it out on stage.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.text: Sí, la habitación está lista.
examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.

examples.text: ¡Claro que sí, pase usted!
examples.trans: Of course, come right in!

meanings.note: Brick basement beneath a building.

examples.text: El sótano está aquí.
examples.trans: The cellar is here.

examples.text: Vemos los sótanos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cellars from the door.

meanings.note: Thin interior brick wall (from Arabic tašbīk).

examples.text: El tabique está aquí.
examples.trans: The partition wall is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tabiques desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the partition walls from the door.

meanings.note: Tablas de madera = wooden planks.

examples.text: La tabla está aquí.
examples.trans: The plank is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tablas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the planks from the door.

meanings.note: Wooden wall board with hooks for room keys.

examples.text: El tablero está aquí.
examples.trans: The board is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tableros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the boards from the door.

meanings.note: Electronic tablet or chocolate bar.

examples.text: La tableta está aquí.
examples.trans: The tablet is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tabletas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tablets from the door.

meanings.note: Backless wooden stool used in kitchens, workshops, or cafés.

examples.text: Acerca ese taburete alto junto a la encimera, por favor.
examples.trans: Bring that tall stool over by the counter, please.

examples.text: Guardamos dos taburetes de madera debajo de la barra.
examples.trans: We keep two wooden stools underneath the counter.

tal.gloss: such (¿qué tal? = how is / how are?)

meanings.en: such (¿qué tal? = how is / how are?)
meanings.note: ¿Qué tal todo? is everyday Spanish for 'How is everything?'.

examples.text: ¡Hola! ¿Qué tal el viaje?
examples.trans: Hello! How was the trip?

examples.text: ¿Qué tal se ve la mesa aquí?
examples.trans: How does the table look here?

examples.text: Es una actriz con mucho talento.
examples.trans: She's an actress with a lot of talent.

examples.text: Buscamos nuevos talentos.
examples.trans: We look for new talent.

meanings.note: Usar la talla... = to wear size... (for clothes).

examples.text: La talla está aquí.
examples.trans: The clothing size is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tallas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the clothing sizes from the door.

meanings.note: Madera tallada = carved wood.

examples.text: Es una pieza tallada.
examples.trans: It is a carved piece.

examples.text: Abre el papel blanco... ¡no! ¡La locomotora de madera tallada del abuelo!
examples.trans: Open the white paper... no! Grandfather's carved wooden locomotive!

meanings.note: Plural los talleres.

examples.text: El taller está aquí.
examples.trans: The workshop is here.

examples.text: Vemos los talleres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the workshops from the door.

meanings.note: Masculine compound noun formed by joining taller ("workshop") and teatro ("theater"), used colloquially as a shorthand for "taller de teatro".

examples.text: Estoy dando un taller-teatro para niños.
examples.trans: I am giving a theater workshop for children.

examples.text: En el taller-teatro del barrio aprendimos a improvisar sin guion.
examples.trans: At the neighborhood theater workshop we learned to improvise without a script.

meanings.note: Drops the written accent in the plural: los talones.

examples.text: Pon una almohada blanda debajo del talón derecho.
examples.trans: Put a soft pillow underneath your right heel.

examples.text: Estos zapatos nuevos no me rozan nada los talones.
examples.trans: These new shoes do not rub my heels at all.

meanings.note: Positive counterpart of tampoco.

examples.text: Yo también quiero un trozo de bizcocho.
examples.trans: I want a piece of sponge cake too.

examples.text: También tenemos té de menta.
examples.trans: We also have mint tea.

meanings.note: Negative counterpart of también.

examples.text: Tampoco hay espejo en la pared.
examples.trans: There is no mirror on the wall either.

examples.text: —No tengo prisa. —Yo tampoco.
examples.trans: 'I am in no rush.' 'Me neither.'

meanings.note: Shortened form of tanto used before adjectives and adverbs (¡qué mañana tan luminosa!).

examples.text: ¡Qué patio tan tranquilo!
examples.trans: What a peaceful courtyard!

examples.text: ¿Por qué sale el agua tan fría?
examples.trans: Why is the water running so cold?

meanings.note: After a verb, invariable tanto means 'so much' (¿por qué mira tanto?).

examples.text: ¿Cómo recuerdas eso después de tantos años?
examples.trans: How do you remember that after so many years?

examples.text: Gracias por tener tanta paciencia.
examples.trans: Thank you for having so much patience.

meanings.note: The lid of a box, pot or piano; in a Spanish bar also a small plate of food.

examples.text: ¿Dónde está la tapa de la olla?
examples.trans: Where is the lid of the pot?

examples.text: Pedimos una tapa de tortilla.
examples.trans: We order a small plate of tortilla.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Rocío tararea una canción alegre mientras amasa el pan.
examples.trans: Rocio hums a cheerful song while kneading the bread.

examples.text: Carmen tarareó la primera línea del vals antiguo.
examples.trans: Carmen hummed the opening line of the old waltz.

meanings.note: Tardar diez minutos en llegar = take ten minutes to get there.

examples.text: Tardo cinco minutos en llegar al puente.
examples.trans: It takes me five minutes to reach the bridge.

examples.text: El agua caliente no tardó nada en subir.
examples.trans: The hot water took no time at all to reach upstairs.

meanings.note: Por la tarde = in the afternoon; ¡Buenas tardes! = Good afternoon!; llegar tarde = arrive late.

examples.text: ¡Buenas tardes! ¿Tienen una habitación libre?
examples.trans: Good afternoon! Do you have a room free?

examples.text: Perdón por llegar un poco tarde.
examples.trans: Sorry for arriving a little late.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a planned task or household job.

examples.text: Tachamos cada tarea cumplida en la pizarra.
examples.trans: We cross off each completed task on the board.

examples.text: Solo nos quedan dos tareas fáciles para esta tarde.
examples.trans: We only have two easy tasks left for this afternoon.

meanings.note: Pagar con tarjeta = pay by card.

examples.text: La tarjeta está aquí.
examples.trans: The card is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tarjetas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cards from the door.

meanings.note: Everyday word in Spain for a jam or honey jar.

examples.text: Guardamos la mermelada casera en tarros de cristal.
examples.trans: We keep the homemade jam in glass jars.

examples.text: Abre el tarro grande de miel con cuidado.
examples.trans: Open the big jar of honey carefully.

meanings.note: Usual word in Spain for a sweet tart or birthday cake.

examples.text: Hay tarta de chocolate para el postre.
examples.trans: There is chocolate cake for dessert.

examples.text: Mi abuela hace una tarta de manzana riquísima.
examples.trans: My grandmother makes a delicious apple tart.

meanings.note: Plural los taxis.

examples.text: El taxi está aquí.
examples.trans: The taxi is here.

examples.text: Vemos los taxis desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the taxis from the door.

meanings.note: Una taza de té = a cup of tea.

examples.text: La taza está aquí.
examples.trans: The cup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tazas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cups from the door.

meanings.note: Object/reflexive pronoun corresponding to tú.

examples.text: Te guardo un rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I am saving a cinnamon roll for you.

examples.text: ¿Cómo te llamas?
examples.trans: What is your name?

examples.text: Ella hace mucho teatro.
examples.trans: She does a lot of theatre.

examples.text: Los teatros abren a las ocho.
examples.trans: Theatres open at eight.

meanings.note: Indoor ceiling (distinct from outdoor tiled tejado).

examples.text: El techo está aquí.
examples.trans: The ceiling is here.

examples.text: Vemos los techos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ceilings from the door.

meanings.note: A door key is la llave; a piano key is la tecla.

examples.text: Esta tecla del ordenador no funciona.
examples.trans: This computer key doesn't work.

examples.text: El piano tiene teclas blancas y negras.
examples.trans: The piano has white and black keys.

examples.text: No entiendo bien la tecnología.
examples.trans: I don't understand technology very well.

examples.text: Las nuevas tecnologías cambian todo.
examples.trans: New technologies change everything.

meanings.note: Sloping exterior roof covered in tiles.

examples.text: El tejado está aquí.
examples.trans: The tiled roof is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tejados desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tiled roofs from the door.

meanings.note: Material for clothes, curtains or old cable covers.

examples.text: Esta camisa es de una tela muy suave.
examples.trans: This shirt is made of a very soft fabric.

examples.text: Compro tela para las cortinas.
examples.trans: I'm buying fabric for the curtains.

examples.text: En PS hemos hecho tele, cine y, sobre todo, teatro.
examples.trans: At PS we've done telly, film, and above all, theatre.

examples.text: Yo tele
examples.trans: I tele

examples.text: Es una crítica para televisión.
examples.trans: It is a critique for television.

examples.text: Trabaja mucho en televisión.
examples.trans: She works a lot in television.

meanings.note: Por teléfono = by phone / on the phone.

examples.text: El teléfono está aquí.
examples.trans: The telephone is here.

examples.text: Vemos los teléfonos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the telephones from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: tiemblo, tiemblan).

examples.text: Con el frío me tiemblan las manos.
examples.trans: In the cold my hands shake.

examples.text: Su voz tembló un poco de emoción.
examples.trans: His voice trembled slightly with emotion.

temer.gloss: to fear; to be afraid that

meanings.en: to fear; to be afraid that
meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Temo que hoy va a llover toda la tarde.
examples.trans: I fear it is going to rain all afternoon today.

examples.text: Temía despertar a los vecinos de abajo.
examples.trans: He was afraid of waking the downstairs neighbours.

meanings.note: Pleasantly warm (not scalding hot).

examples.text: Es una pieza templada.
examples.trans: It is a warm piece.

examples.text: Toque el radiador: abajo está templado, pero arriba se está enfriando.
examples.trans: Feel the radiator—the bottom is warm, while the top is turning cool.

examples.text: Tiene un gran tempo para la comedia.
examples.trans: She has great timing for comedy.

examples.text: Cuida mucho el tempo de la escena.
examples.trans: Pay close attention to the pace of the scene.

meanings.note: Opposite of tarde.

examples.text: Nos levantamos temprano cada día.
examples.trans: We get up early every day.

examples.text: Hoy llegaste muy temprano.
examples.trans: Today you arrived very early.

meanings.note: Owner of a small neighbourhood shop (tienda).

examples.text: El tendero está aquí.
examples.trans: The shopkeeper is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tenderos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shopkeepers from the door.

examples.text: Tendría que ser una cosa... muy concreta, muy autoral.
examples.trans: It would have to be something... very specific, very auteur.

examples.text: Yo Tendría
examples.trans: I Tendría

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.text: Tenemos ocho habitaciones tranquilas.
examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Plural tensiones.

examples.text: La tensión es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The tension is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la tensión.
examples.trans: We talk about the tension.

examples.text: Estás un poco tensa, ¿eh?
examples.trans: You're a bit tense, aren't you?

examples.text: Fue un momento tenso.
examples.trans: It was a tense moment.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: no lo tiente).

examples.text: El olor a canela tienta a cualquiera.
examples.trans: The smell of cinnamon tempts anyone.

examples.text: Mejor no tentemos a la suerte.
examples.trans: Better not tempt luck.

teníamos.gloss: we had, we used to have

meanings.en: we had, we used to have, we were having
meanings.note: First-person plural (nosotros) imperfect indicative of tener. Used to describe ongoing past possession, background situations, or previously scheduled commitments ("teníamos reunión").

examples.text: Y nosotros teníamos un chiquito que estaba en "Los Borgia".
examples.trans: And we had a young guy who was in "The Borgias".

examples.text: Que teníamos reunión. Llego 20 minutos antes.
examples.trans: We had a meeting. I arrive 20 minutes early.

meanings.note: Shortens to tercer before masculine singular nouns (el tercer escalón).

examples.text: Es una pieza tercera.
examples.trans: It is a third piece.

examples.text: ¡Vamos, carrera hasta la tercera planta!
examples.trans: Come on, race you to the third floor!

meanings.note: Used with de to describe plush velvet pouches, curtains, or upholstery: una bolsa de terciopelo ('a velvet pouch').

examples.text: La brújula estaba guardada dentro de una bolsa de terciopelo.
examples.trans: The compass was kept inside a velvet pouch.

examples.text: Las cortinas rojas del teatro son de terciopelo grueso.
examples.trans: The red theatre curtains are made of heavy velvet.

meanings.note: Gerund (present participle) of the regular -ar verb 'terminar'. Frequently used in progressive constructions with 'estar' or verbs of state like 'quedarse' ('quedarse terminando algo').

examples.text: Tú te quedas terminando la prueba, ¿vale?
examples.trans: You stay here finishing the audition test, okay?

examples.text: Estoy terminando de leer el guion del capítulo.
examples.trans: I am finishing reading the episode script.

terminar.gloss: to finish (terminar de + inf = finish doing)

meanings.en: to finish (terminar de + inf = finish doing)
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Termino mi turno a las tres.
examples.trans: I finish my shift at three.

examples.text: Terminamos de pintar antes de comer.
examples.trans: We finished painting before lunch.

examples.text: En su cara se ve terror.
examples.trans: On her face you can see terror.

examples.text: No me gustan las películas de terror.
examples.trans: I don't like horror films.

examples.text: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old".
examples.trans: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old".

examples.text: Yo Terés
examples.trans: I Terés

meanings.note: Appears in un mapa del tesoro ('a treasure map') and buscadores de tesoros ('treasure hunters').

examples.text: Ernesto dijo que habéis sacado un tesoro bajo las piedras.
examples.trans: Ernesto said that you dug up a treasure under the stones.

examples.text: La receta partida parece un auténtico mapa del tesoro.
examples.trans: The split recipe looks like a real treasure map.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (almost always used in the singular) referring to firm, unwavering perseverance in pursuing a goal. Featured in the lyrics of the show's opening theme song.

examples.text: Pasión, tesón, que andando se hace el camino.
examples.trans: Passion, tenacity, for the path is made by walking.

examples.text: Con mucho tesón logró conseguir su primer papel en el teatro.
examples.trans: With great tenacity she managed to land her first role in the theater.

meanings.note: Built from té (tea).

examples.text: La tetera está aquí.
examples.trans: The teapot is here.

examples.text: Vemos las teteras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teapots from the door.

meanings.en: the (English definite article in quoted dialogue)
meanings.note: Unadapted English definite article appearing in Paquita Salas when actress Lidia San José struggles through an English-language callback audition line ('It is very important to give this envelope to the emperor'). Often pronounced [de] or [te] by Spanish speakers with limited English phonology.

examples.text: "It is very important to give this envelope to the emperor."
examples.trans: "It is very important to give this envelope to the emperor." (Audition line in English)

examples.text: Lidia se bloqueó justo al decir "'give' this envelope to the..." en el casting.
examples.trans: Lidia froze right as she said "'give' this envelope to the..." at the audition.

meanings.en: this (English demonstrative determiner/pronoun in quoted dialogue)
meanings.note: Quoted English word from the comedic English-language audition scene in Paquita Salas ('give this envelope to the emperor'), where Spanish actors attempt to perform in English without really speaking the language.

examples.text: En la prueba de inglés, Lidia repetía nerviosa: "But it's very important 'give' this".
examples.trans: In the English audition, Lidia nervously repeated: "But it's very important 'give' this."

examples.text: Tenía que decir "'give' this envelope to the emperor", pero se inventó la mitad de la frase.
examples.trans: She had to say "'give' this envelope to the emperor," but she made up half the sentence.

meanings.note: Unadapted English loanword widely used in Peninsular Spanish film and television industry jargon. Typically pronounced [ˈtɾileɾ] or [ˈθɾileɾ] in Spain. The RAE recommends 'película de suspense' as a native alternative, though 'thriller' is standard in casting.

examples.text: Es un thriller policiaco con mucho suspense.
examples.trans: It is a crime thriller with a lot of suspense.

examples.text: Le han ofrecido el papel protagonista en un thriller español.
examples.trans: They have offered her the lead role in a Spanish thriller.

meanings.note: Used after prepositions (para ti, a ti, por ti); combines with con as contigo; never carries a written accent.

examples.text: He guardado una taza de té caliente para ti.
examples.trans: I saved a cup of hot tea for you.

examples.text: Ahora te toca elegir la mesa a ti.
examples.trans: Now it is your turn to choose the table.

meanings.note: Describes a gentle, pleasant warmth (pan tibio, agua tibia), similar to templado.

examples.text: El pan recién salido del horno todavía está tibio y tierno.
examples.trans: The bread fresh from the oven is still warm and soft.

examples.text: Disuelve la levadura en medio vaso de agua tibia.
examples.trans: Dissolve the yeast in half a glass of lukewarm water.

meanings.note: ¿Qué tiempo hace? asks about the weather; a tiempo = on time.

examples.text: El tiempo está aquí.
examples.trans: The time is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tiempos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the times from the door.

meanings.note: Masculine plural of 'tiempo'. Often used in the plural to refer to historical periods, social eras, or changing circumstances, as in the idiom 'los tiempos cambian' ('times change').

examples.text: Bueno, los tiempos cambian. Bien.
examples.trans: Well, times change. Good.

examples.text: En otros tiempos, nuestra agencia representaba a las mayores estrellas del país.
examples.trans: In other times, our agency represented the biggest stars in the country.

meanings.note: Small local shop.

examples.text: La tienda está aquí.
examples.trans: The shop is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tiendas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shops from the door.

meanings.note: In Spain, pan tierno is freshly baked bread with a soft crumb.

examples.text: Las hogazas salen tiernas por dentro y muy crujientes.
examples.trans: The loaves come out soft inside and very crusty.

examples.text: Las zanahorias tiernas dan un dulzor suave al caldo.
examples.trans: Tender young carrots give a gentle sweetness to the broth.

examples.text: Está mejor. Le he escondido los Tigretones.
examples.trans: She's better. I've hidden the Tigretones cakes from her.

examples.text: Yo tigretón
examples.trans: I tigretón

meanings.note: Shade tree with heart-shaped green leaves; its blossom makes tila tea.

examples.text: Las hojas de tilo tienen un tono verde precioso.
examples.trans: Linden leaves have a gorgeous shade of green.

examples.text: En la plaza vieja dan sombra cuatro tilos altos.
examples.trans: Four tall linden trees shade the old square.

meanings.note: Tocar el timbre = ring the bell.

examples.text: El timbre está aquí.
examples.trans: The bell is here.

examples.text: Vemos los timbres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bells from the door.

meanings.note: Con tinta permanente = in permanent ink.

examples.text: La tinta es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The ink is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la tinta.
examples.trans: We talk about the ink.

meanings.note: Used informally to refer to an unspecified man ('un tipo por ahí'). Can have a slightly detached or suspicious nuance depending on tone.
Standard noun used in 'tipo de + noun' ('kind/sort of').

examples.text: ¿Vamos a otro lado? Porque hay un tipo por ahí mirándonos raro.
examples.trans: Shall we go somewhere else? Because there is a guy over there looking at us weirdly.

examples.text: ¿Qué tipo de papeles estás buscando ahora mismo?
examples.trans: What kind of roles are you looking for right now?

meanings.note: Related to tirar ('to pull'); denotes a narrow strip of cloth, paper, tape, or lemon peel.

examples.text: Fijaos en la tira de tela blanca pegada alrededor de la tapa.
examples.trans: Look at the strip of white cloth stuck around the lid.

examples.text: Cortó la masa en tiras largas y finas.
examples.trans: She cut the dough into long, thin strips.

meanings.note: Tirar a la basura = throw in the bin.

examples.text: Tira el sobre viejo al contenedor azul.
examples.trans: Throw the old envelope into the blue recycling bin.

examples.text: Tiró suavemente del cordón de la campana.
examples.trans: She pulled the bell cord gently.

meanings.note: From tirar ('to pull'); un tirón en el tobillo means 'a strain / pull in the ankle'.

examples.text: Noté un pequeño tirón al bajar del último escalón.
examples.trans: I felt a slight pull stepping off the bottom stair.

examples.text: Abre el cajón despacio y sin dar tirones bruscos.
examples.trans: Open the drawer slowly without giving sharp tugs.

examples.text: Tengo un libro que se titula La magia que hay en ti.
examples.trans: I have a book titled The Magic Within You.

examples.text: Hablamos de titular en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about is titled at the office.

meanings.note: Escribir con tiza / a tiza means 'to write in chalk'.

examples.text: El menú del día está escrito con tiza blanca.
examples.trans: Today's menu is written in white chalk.

examples.text: Necesito un trozo de tiza para la pizarra de la entrada.
examples.trans: I need a piece of chalk for the entrance board.

meanings.en: to (English infinitive marker and preposition in quoted dialogue)
meanings.note: Quoted English preposition and infinitive particle from the English callback audition scene in Paquita Salas ('to give this envelope to the emperor'), highlighting the characters' comedic struggle with English scripts.

examples.text: En el guion ponía claramente: "It is very important to give this envelope to the emperor".
examples.trans: In the script it clearly read: "It is very important to give this envelope to the emperor."

examples.text: Se quedó en blanco después de decir "'give' this envelope to the...".
examples.trans: She went blank after saying "'give' this envelope to the...".

meanings.note: Clean bath or hand towel.

examples.text: La toalla está aquí.
examples.trans: The towel is here.

examples.text: Vemos las toallas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the towels from the door.

meanings.note: Everyday anatomical noun.

examples.text: Envuelve el tobillo con un paño frío diez minutos.
examples.trans: Wrap your ankle with a cold cloth for ten minutes.

examples.text: Con buen calzado caminas seguro sin torcerte los tobillos.
examples.trans: With sturdy shoes you walk safely without twisting your ankles.

tocar.gloss: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)

meanings.en: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)
meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells c -> qu: toqué.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de tocar el timbre.
examples.trans: Someone just rang the bell.

examples.text: De niño tocaba el piano los viernes.
examples.trans: As a boy he played the piano on Fridays.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'still' or 'not yet'.

examples.text: El café todavía está caliente.
examples.trans: The coffee is still hot.

examples.text: Todavía no son las doce.
examples.trans: It is not twelve o'clock yet.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

examples.text: Toma, te he traído un té.
examples.trans: Here, I have brought you a tea.

examples.text: Yo Toma
examples.trans: I Toma

meanings.note: ¡Toma! = Here you go!; tomar un café = have a coffee.

examples.text: ¿Qué quiere tomar para desayunar?
examples.trans: What would you like to have for breakfast?

examples.text: Toma, aquí tienes la linterna.
examples.trans: Here you go, here is the flashlight.

meanings.note: Staple ingredient of Mediterranean soups, salads, and toast.

examples.text: Compramos tomates maduros en el puesto de la esquina.
examples.trans: We bought ripe tomatoes at the corner stall.

examples.text: Asamos los tomates con ajo y ramas de tomillo.
examples.trans: We roast the tomatoes with garlic and thyme sprigs.

meanings.note: Classic Mediterranean herb that grows wild on sunny hillsides and in courtyard pots.

examples.text: El tomillo fresco da un aroma de campo maravilloso a las lentejas.
examples.trans: Fresh thyme gives a wonderful country aroma to the lentils.

examples.text: Plantamos tomillo, romero y menta junto al muro del jardín.
examples.trans: We planted thyme, rosemary, and mint beside the garden wall.

meanings.note: Musical key or pitch, voice tone, or shade of colour.

examples.text: Carmen escribió el final en el mismo tono mayor.
examples.trans: Carmen wrote the ending in the same major key.

examples.text: Este tono de verde combina con el limonero.
examples.trans: This shade of green matches the lemon tree.

meanings.en: nonsense, foolishness, silly remarks or actions
meanings.note: Feminine plural of 'tontería' (derived from 'tonto', silly/foolish). Extremely common in Peninsular colloquial expressions such as 'decir tonterías' (to talk nonsense), 'hacer tonterías' (to fool around), and 'dejarse de tonterías' (to cut the nonsense).

examples.text: Anda, qué tonterías. —Yo soy gay.
examples.trans: Come on, what nonsense. —I'm gay.

examples.text: Anda, no digas tonterías, ¿eh?
examples.trans: Come on, don't talk nonsense, huh?

meanings.note: Dos toques cortos = two short rings.

examples.text: El toque está aquí.
examples.trans: The ring is here.

examples.text: Vemos los toques desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rings from the door.

torcer.gloss: to twist; to lean; to bend (torcerse = go crooked)

meanings.en: to twist; to lean; to bend (torcerse = go crooked)
meanings.note: Stem-changing o -> ue (tuerzo, tuerce) and c -> z before o/a.

examples.text: Si el pasador está flojo, la pieza se tuerce.
examples.trans: If the pin is loose, the part leans sideways.

examples.text: No tuerzas la llave antigua dentro de la cerradura.
examples.trans: Do not twist the old key inside the lock.

meanings.note: Heavy rainstorm with wind, thunder, and lightning.

examples.text: Guardamos los cojines antes de que empiece la tormenta.
examples.trans: We put the cushions away before the storm starts.

examples.text: Después de la tormenta el patio huele a tierra mojada.
examples.trans: After the storm the courtyard smells of wet earth.

meanings.note: Apretar un tornillo = tighten a screw.

examples.text: El tornillo está aquí.
examples.trans: The screw is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tornillos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the screws from the door.

examples.text: A ver, Paquita, las cartas. Fíjate, la carta de la torre.
examples.trans: Let me see the cards, Paquita. Look, the Tower card.

examples.text: Se viene todo abajo. La torre no miente, mi vida. Sí que se te va.
examples.trans: Everything comes crashing down. The Tower doesn't lie, darling. She really is leaving you.

torreznos.gloss: crispy fried pork belly strips, pork rinds

meanings.en: thick strips of marinated pork belly fried until crispy; Spanish bacon rinds
meanings.note: Masculine plural of 'torrezno' (especially famous in Soria and Castile). In Paquita Salas, 'unos torreznos' with a gin-tonic is Paquita's iconic comfort food and signature bar order throughout the series.

examples.text: Pues ponme un gin-tonic y unos torreznos.
examples.trans: Well, get me a gin and tonic and some crispy fried pork belly strips.

examples.text: Hola, buenas, ¿qué tal? Mira, me pones unos torreznos y una ginebra.
examples.trans: Hello there, how are you? Look, could you get me some crispy pork belly and a gin?

meanings.en: coughs (third-person singular present indicative of toser)
meanings.note: Inflected form of the regular -er verb 'toser' ('to cough'). Frequently appears in script stage directions and closed captions, such as '(FINA TOSE)'. Also the informal singular imperative ('¡tose!').

examples.text: ¿A que sí, Fina? (Fina tose).
examples.trans: Isn't that right, Fina? (Fina coughs.)

examples.text: Siempre tose un poco antes de hablar cuando se pone nerviosa.
examples.trans: She always coughs a little before speaking when she gets nervous.

meanings.note: A classic Spanish breakfast is una tostada con tomate.

examples.text: Para desayunar quiero una tostada con tomate.
examples.trans: For breakfast I want toast with tomato.

examples.text: Las tostadas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The toast is on the table.

examples.text: La carpeta está llena totalmente.
examples.trans: The folder is completely full.

examples.text: Estoy totalmente de acuerdo.
examples.trans: I completely agree.

meanings.en: works (third-person singular present indicative of trabajar)
meanings.note: Inflected form of the regular -ar verb 'trabajar' ('to work'). Also serves as the second-person singular affirmative imperative ('tú trabaja').

examples.text: —Luisito, ¿sabes que Paca trabaja en la tele?
examples.trans: —Luisito, do you know that Paca works in TV?

examples.text: Ahora trabaja como representante de actores en Madrid.
examples.trans: Now she works as a talent agent in Madrid.

examples.text: Es muy trabajadora, con muchas ganas de hacer cosas.
examples.trans: She's very hard-working, and really eager to do things.

examples.text: Yo trabajador
examples.trans: I trabajador

meanings.note: Used for people working (machines use funcionar).

examples.text: Trabajo en recepción de lunes a viernes.
examples.trans: I work at the front desk Monday through Friday.

examples.text: Hoy trabajamos todos en equipo.
examples.trans: Today we all worked as a team.

trabajazo.gloss: fantastic job; great piece of work

meanings.en: fantastic job; great piece of work

examples.text: Me ha encantado, un trabajazo.
examples.trans: I loved it, a fantastic piece of work.

examples.text: Habéis hecho un trabajazo hoy.
examples.trans: You've done a tremendous job today.

meanings.note: Ir al trabajo = go to work.

examples.text: El trabajo está aquí.
examples.trans: The work is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trabajos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the works from the door.

meanings.note: Irregular: traigo, traje; future traeré.

examples.text: Ahora mismo le traigo una cuchara.
examples.trans: I will bring you a spoon right now.

examples.text: Ayer trajo flores del mercado.
examples.trans: Yesterday she brought flowers from the market.

meanings.en: I bring, I am bringing, I have with me
meanings.note: First-person singular present indicative of the irregular verb 'traer' ('to bring'). It exhibits the irregular velar/palatal stem extension '-ig-' ('traigo'), which also forms the basis for the entire present subjunctive ('traiga, traigas...').

examples.text: Que traigo un paquete para Belinda Washington.
examples.trans: I'm bringing a package for Belinda Washington.

examples.text: Por eso traigo un regalo, una sorpresa para vosotros.
examples.trans: That's why I've brought a gift, a surprise for you all.

examples.text: Conoces este traje de memoria.
examples.trans: You know this suit by heart.

examples.text: Lleva un traje azul marino.
examples.trans: She's wearing a navy-blue suit.

examples.text: El personaje tenía una trama increíble.
examples.trans: The character had an incredible storyline.

examples.text: La trama de la película engancha.
examples.trans: The plot of the film is gripping.

meanings.note: Tiene trampa = there is a trick/catch to it.

examples.text: La trampa está aquí.
examples.trans: The trick is here.

examples.text: Vemos las trampas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tricks from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective 'tranquilo'. In conversational Peninsular Spanish, '¡Tranquila!' or 'Tú tranquila' is constantly used as a reassuring interjection meaning 'Don't worry!', 'Take it easy!', or 'Relax!' when addressing a woman.

examples.text: No te preocupes. Quédate ahí tranquila.
examples.trans: Don't worry. Just stay there calmly.

examples.text: Tú tranquila, tómate el café, que te tengo que contar algo.
examples.trans: You just relax, drink your coffee, because I have to tell you something.

examples.text: Tranquilízate, todo tiene solución.
examples.trans: Calm down, everything can be sorted.

examples.text: Su voz me tranquiliza.
examples.trans: Her voice calms me down.

meanings.note: Said alone to reassure someone ('Easy, don't worry!').

examples.text: Es una pieza tranquila.
examples.trans: It is a quiet piece.

examples.text: Seca, calentita y tranquila. Ahora decidme qué falta.
examples.trans: Dry, warm, and quiet. Now tell me what is missing.

meanings.note: Transmisión de propiedad = property transfer.

examples.text: La transmisión está aquí.
examples.trans: The transfer is here.

examples.text: Vemos las transmisiones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the transfers from the door.

meanings.note: Concise preposition meaning 'behind' or 'after'.

examples.text: La calle tras la reja está vacía.
examples.trans: The street behind the gate is empty.

examples.text: Día tras día cuidamos el jardín.
examples.trans: Day after day we tend the garden.

meanings.note: Opposite of delantero ('front'); la puerta trasera is 'the back door'.

examples.text: Entramos con las cajas por la puerta trasera.
examples.trans: We came in with the boxes through the back door.

examples.text: Las ventanas traseras dan a una calle muy tranquila.
examples.trans: The back windows look onto a very quiet street.

tratar.gloss: to treat; to deal with; to try (tratar de)

meanings.en: to treat; to deal with; to try (tratar de)
meanings.note: Tratar bien a alguien = treat someone kindly; tratar de + infinitive = try to.

examples.text: En esta posada tratamos a todos con cariño.
examples.trans: At this inn we treat everyone warmly.

examples.text: Trata de descansar un rato antes de cenar.
examples.trans: Try to rest a while before dinner.

meanings.note: ¡Trato hecho! = It's a deal!

examples.text: ¿Me ayudas hoy y yo te ayudo mañana? ¡Trato hecho!
examples.trans: You help me today and I help you tomorrow? Deal!

examples.text: En este hotel el trato es muy amable.
examples.trans: In this hotel the service is very friendly.

examples.text: Hoy terminan su trayectoria aquí en la escuela Primera Fila.
examples.trans: Today they finish their journey here at the Primera Fila school.

examples.text: Yo trayectoria
examples.trans: I trayectoria

examples.text: Mi destino está claramente trazado.
examples.trans: My destiny is clearly mapped out.

examples.text: Yo trazado
examples.trans: I trazado

meanings.note: Past participle of 'traer' ('to bring'). Takes a written acute accent on the 'í' ('traído') to mark the hiatus between the strong vowel 'a' and the stressed weak vowel 'i'. Primarily used with 'haber' to form compound tenses like the Peninsular present perfect ('he traído').

examples.text: Toma, te he traído un té.
examples.trans: Here, I have brought you a tea.

examples.text: ¿Has traído los currículums de las actrices nuevas?
examples.trans: Have you brought the résumés of the new actresses?

meanings.note: Treinta y cinco = thirty-five.

examples.text: Nos dan treinta días de plazo.
examples.trans: They give us thirty days' notice.

examples.text: Son las nueve y treinta y cinco.
examples.trans: It is nine thirty-five.

meanings.note: Plural los trenes.

examples.text: El tren está aquí.
examples.trans: The train is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trenes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the trains from the door.

meanings.note: Diminutive of el tren.

examples.text: El trenecito está aquí.
examples.trans: The little train is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trenecitos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the little trains from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ponemos tres mesas bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We set three tables under the tree.

examples.text: Empieza con tres frases cortas.
examples.trans: Start with three short sentences.

meanings.note: Estar triste = to feel sad.

examples.text: Es una pieza triste.
examples.trans: It is a sad piece.

examples.text: ¡Una viajera no puede estar triste su primera tarde en Valencia!
examples.trans: A traveller cannot sit sad on her first evening in Valencia!

examples.text: Cariño, claro que vas a triunfar.
examples.trans: Darling, of course you're going to triumph.

examples.text: Yo triunfar
examples.trans: I triunfar

examples.text: Mira, la carta de la estrella, la carta de la fama y del triunfo.
examples.trans: Look, the Star card, the card of fame and triumph.

examples.text: Hablamos de triunfo en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about triumph at the office.

meanings.en: mate, dude, girl, friend (colloquial Peninsular slang addressing a woman)
meanings.note: Feminine counterpart of colloquial 'tronco' (literally 'tree trunk'). Used in informal Peninsular Spanish—especially Madrid youth and casual speech—as an affectionate or emphatic vocative among female friends ('¡Joder, tronca!').

examples.text: ¡Joder, tronca!
examples.trans: Damn it, girl! / Dude!

examples.text: Oye, tronca, no te ralles por lo del casting, que lo hiciste genial.
examples.trans: Hey, girl, don't stress out over the audition, you did great.

meanings.note: Stem-changing e → ie verb (tropiezo, tropiece) with z → c before -e; takes con before the obstacle (tropezar con una piedra).

examples.text: Volveré a colocar la piedra plana para que nadie tropiece.
examples.trans: I will put the flat stone back in place so nobody trips.

examples.text: Casi tropiezo con el escalón de la entrada.
examples.trans: I almost tripped over the front step.

meanings.note: Un trozo de bizcocho = a piece of cake.

examples.text: El trozo está aquí.
examples.trans: The piece is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trozos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pieces from the door.

meanings.note: El tráfico del centro = city-centre traffic.

examples.text: El tráfico es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The traffic is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el tráfico.
examples.trans: We talk about the traffic.

meanings.note: Unaccented possessive (tu llave / tus llaves), distinct from accented pronoun tú.

examples.text: ¿Dónde está tu caja de herramientas?
examples.trans: Where is your toolbox?

examples.text: Reconocí tu letra enseguida.
examples.trans: I recognized your handwriting right away.

meanings.note: Water or heating pipe.

examples.text: La tubería está aquí.
examples.trans: The pipe is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tuberías desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pipes from the door.

meanings.note: Tubo de cobre = copper pipe.

examples.text: El tubo está aquí.
examples.trans: The pipe is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tubos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pipes from the door.

examples.text: ¿Para qué quieres que lo coja? Estoy tumbada con tres pizzas y dos botellas de vino.
examples.trans: Why do you want me to pick up? I'm lying here with three pizzas and two bottles of wine.

examples.text: Hablamos de tumbado en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about lying down at the office.

tumbar.gloss: to lie down; to knock down

meanings.en: to lie down, to stretch out (especially reflexive: tumbarse)
meanings.note: In Peninsular Spanish, 'tumbarse' (or 'irse a tumbar' with clitic climbing: 'me voy a tumbar') is the standard everyday verb for lying down on a bed, sofa, or the beach.

meanings.en: to knock down, to fell, to reject/fail (a project or exam)
meanings.note: Used transitively ('tumbar algo/a alguien') to mean knocking someone down or rejecting a proposal/failing a candidate.

examples.text: Perdóname, Paquita, que me voy a tumbar un momento.
examples.trans: Excuse me, Paquita, I am going to lie down for a moment.

examples.text: Después de comer siempre le gusta tumbarse un rato en el sofá.
examples.trans: After lunch she always likes to lie down for a while on the sofa.

related.gloss: to go to bed, to lie down

tuppers.gloss: Tupperware containers, food containers (with home-cooked meals)

meanings.en: plastic food containers; portions of home-cooked food packed in containers
meanings.note: Plural of 'tupper' (from the trademark Tupperware), pronounced [ˈtapeɾs] in Spain and Hispanicized by the RAE as 'táper' (plural 'táperes'). Culturally in Spain, 'hacer unos tuppers' refers not just to the plastic boxes, but to the affectionate practice of mothers or grandmothers sending homemade meals home with family or friends.

examples.text: —Toma, te he hecho unos "tuppers".
examples.trans: —Here, I have made you some Tupperware containers of food.

examples.text: Mi madre siempre me llena la maleta de "tuppers" con croquetas y lentejas.
examples.trans: My mother always fills my suitcase with Tupperware containers of croquettes and lentils.

meanings.note: Nos tuteamos = let's use informal 'tú' with each other.

examples.text: Aquí nos tuteamos desde el primer día.
examples.trans: Here we use informal 'you' from day one.

examples.text: ¿Podemos tutearnos mientras tomamos café?
examples.trans: May we use first-name terms over coffee?

tuviéramos.gloss: we had, we might have (imperfect subjunctive)

meanings.en: we had, we were to have, we might have (first-person plural imperfect subjunctive of tener)
meanings.note: Inflected form of the irregular verb 'tener' ('to have'), built on the preterite stem 'tuv-'. Used in subordinate clauses after past-tense main verbs or counterfactual 'si' clauses ('si tuviéramos...'). Equivalent to 'tuviésemos'.

examples.text: Qué raro que no nos avisaran de que tuviéramos reunión. Ya verás.
examples.trans: How strange that they didn't let us know we had a meeting. You'll see.

examples.text: Si tuviéramos más presupuesto, contrataríamos a una estrella internacional.
examples.trans: If we had a bigger budget, we would hire an international star.

meanings.en: yours, of yours (feminine singular stressed possessive pronoun or determiner)
meanings.note: Feminine singular form of the stressed (postnominal/predicative) second-person singular informal possessive 'tuyo'. Used after the verb 'ser' ('es tuya' = 'it is yours') or after a noun ('una idea tuya' = 'an idea of yours'), contrasting with the unstressed prenominal determiner 'tu' ('tu casa').

examples.text: ¿Esta casa de quién es? Esta casa es tuya, mamá.
examples.trans: Whose house is this? This house is yours, Mom.

examples.text: Una amiga tuya ha llamado a la oficina preguntando por ti.
examples.trans: A friend of yours called the office asking for you.

meanings.note: Standard written abbreviation for 'televisión'. In script subtitles and closed captions (as in Paquita Salas), '(TV)' marks dialogue coming from a television screen in the scene. In everyday Peninsular speech, people usually say 'la tele' or 'la televisión' rather than spelling out the letters.

examples.text: (TV) "¿Vamos a otro lado? —¿Porque hay un tipo por ahí?". —(FINA) Mira.
examples.trans: (TV) "Shall we go somewhere else? —Because there's a guy over there?" —(FINA) Look.

examples.text: Lleva más de veinte años trabajando en series de TV y teatro.
examples.trans: She has spent more than twenty years working in TV series and theater.

meanings.note: Accented té ('tea') distinguishes the noun from pronoun te ('you').

examples.text: El té está aquí.
examples.trans: The tea is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tés desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teas from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine counterpart of el tío ('uncle').

examples.text: La tía de Ernesto tocaba el piano todos los viernes.
examples.trans: Ernesto's aunt played the piano every Friday.

examples.text: Mi tía prepara el mejor bizcocho de limón del barrio.
examples.trans: My aunt bakes the best lemon sponge cake in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Feminine tía = aunt; in casual Spain Spanish tío also means 'mate'.

examples.text: Mi tío vive en Alicante.
examples.trans: My uncle lives in Alicante.

examples.text: Mis tíos vienen a comer el domingo.
examples.trans: My aunt and uncle are coming for lunch on Sunday.

meanings.note: Title of a song, book, or official certificate.

examples.text: El título de la canción está escrito con tinta negra.
examples.trans: The title of the song is written in black ink.

examples.text: No recuerdo el título exacto de esa novela.
examples.trans: I do not remember the exact title of that novel.

meanings.en: drink, have (food/drink); take (time/calmly) — informal singular imperative of tomarse
meanings.note: Second-person singular ('tú') affirmative imperative of 'tomar' combined with the enclitic reflexive/aspectual pronoun 'te' ('toma' + 'te' -> 'tómate', gaining a written accent to preserve stress on the first syllable). With food and beverages ('tómate el café'), 'te' is an aspectual dative of consumption meaning 'drink/eat up'.

examples.text: Tú tranquila, tómate el café, que te tengo que contar algo.
examples.trans: You just relax, drink up your coffee, because I have to tell you something.

examples.text: Tómate unos días de descanso antes de empezar el rodaje.
examples.trans: Take a few days off to rest before filming starts.

meanings.note: Accented subject pronoun (tú mismo = you yourself).

examples.text: Tú conoces muy bien el barrio.
examples.trans: You know the neighbourhood very well.

examples.text: Pruébalo tú mismo.
examples.trans: Try it yourself.

meanings.note: Natural exclamation of effort, relief, or sudden heat/rain.

examples.text: ¡Uf, cuánto pesa esta contraventana de madera maciza!
examples.trans: Whew, how heavy this solid wood shutter is!

examples.text: ¡Uf, entramos en el pasillo justo antes del chaparrón!
examples.trans: Phew, we got into the hallway right before the downpour!

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.en: some, a few (feminine plural indefinite article or pronoun)
meanings.note: Feminine plural of 'una'. Used before feminine plural nouns ('unas fotos', 'unas pilas') to express an indefinite small quantity ('some, a few').
When placed before a cardinal number modifying a feminine noun ('unas veinte actrices'), it means 'approximately' or 'around'.

examples.text: Cogimos y pusimos su cara en unas fotos de otra actriz.
examples.trans: We went ahead and put her face onto some photos of another actress.

examples.text: Unas pilas, no. Vas equivocada.
examples.trans: Some batteries, no. You're mistaken.

examples.text: Tengo este traje de uniforme.
examples.trans: I wear this suit like a uniform.

examples.text: Los niños llevan uniforme.
examples.trans: The children wear a uniform.

unir.gloss: to unite; to join; to bring together

meanings.en: to unite; to join; to bring together
