meanings.note: Regular -ir verb: unir a los vecinos = bring neighbours together.

examples.text: El puente une los dos barrios.
examples.trans: The bridge joins the two neighbourhoods.

examples.text: La música une a la gente.
examples.trans: Music brings people together.

meanings.note: Feminine noun in -dad; en la universidad means 'at university / in college'.

examples.text: Javier conoció a su profesor de mapas en la universidad.
examples.trans: Javier met his map professor at university.

examples.text: La biblioteca antigua de la universidad está en el centro.
examples.trans: The old university library is in the city centre.

meanings.note: Shortens to un before masculine singular nouns.

examples.text: Toma uno recién salido del horno.
examples.trans: Take one fresh out of the oven.

examples.text: Contamos del uno al ocho.
examples.trans: We count from one to eight.

meanings.en: some, a few, a pair of (masculine plural indefinite article or pronoun)
meanings.note: Masculine plural of 'un' / 'uno'. Very common in Spanish when ordering food or drinks ('unos torreznos', 'unos vinos') or introducing an unspecified small group ('unos niños').
Used before numbers ('unos diez minutos') to indicate an approximate amount ('around ten minutes').

examples.text: Pues ponme un gin-tonic y unos torreznos.
examples.trans: Well, get me a gin and tonic and some crispy pork belly strips.

examples.text: Y hay unos niños esperando en la puerta del teatro.
examples.trans: And there are some children waiting at the door of the theater.

meanings.note: Una urgencia = an emergency.

examples.text: La urgencia está aquí.
examples.trans: The emergency is here.

examples.text: Vemos las urgencias desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the emergencies from the door.

examples.text: Llámame cuando puedas, urgente.
examples.trans: Call me when you can, urgent.

examples.text: Tengo dos mensajes urgentes.
examples.trans: I have two urgent messages.

meanings.note: Invariable masculine singular form when used with auxiliary 'haber' to form compound tenses ('la he usado poco' = 'I have used it little').
When functioning as an adjective, it inflects for gender and number ('usado, usada, usados, usadas').

examples.text: La he usado poco, la verdad.
examples.trans: I have used it very little, honestly.

examples.text: Vendió su coche usado para poder pagar el alquiler del piso.
examples.trans: He sold his used car so he could pay the rent on the apartment.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Uso gafas solo para leer letra pequeña.
examples.trans: I wear glasses only for reading fine print.

examples.text: Usamos limones frescos del patio.
examples.trans: We use fresh lemons from the courtyard.

meanings.note: Takes 3rd-person singular verbs (¿quiere usted...?).

examples.text: ¿Cómo se llama usted?
examples.trans: What is your name?

examples.text: Pase usted por aquí, por favor.
examples.trans: Come this way, please.

meanings.note: Takes 3rd-person plural verbs (pasen ustedes).

examples.text: ¿Tienen ustedes una reserva?
examples.trans: Do you all have a reservation?

examples.text: El patio es para todos ustedes.
examples.trans: The courtyard is for all of you.

meanings.note: Light exclamation for a small slip or surprise.

examples.text: ¡Uy, casi se me cae la taza!
examples.trans: Oops, I nearly dropped the cup!

examples.text: ¡Uy, qué tarde es ya!
examples.trans: Oh my, how late it is already!

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from vaciar.

examples.text: Es una pieza vaciada.
examples.trans: It is a drained piece.

examples.text: Cerrada y vaciada. Pásame la llave inglesa pesada de tu izquierda.
examples.trans: Off and drained. Pass me the heavy wrench on your left.

vaciar.gloss: to empty; to drain; to clear out

meanings.en: to empty; to drain; to clear out
meanings.note: Present boot forms take í: vacía.

examples.text: Vacío la cafetera antes de lavarla.
examples.trans: I empty the coffee pot before washing it.

examples.text: Vaciaron la tubería para cambiar la pieza.
examples.trans: They drained the pipe to replace the part.

meanings.note: Opposite of lleno (full).

examples.text: Es una pieza vacía.
examples.trans: It is an empty piece.

examples.text: Aunque la cuatro está vacía, el cable viejo suena dos veces.
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire rings twice.

meanings.note: Spain's ubiquitous single-word confirmation (from valer).

examples.text: —Nos vemos a las doce. —¡Vale!
examples.trans: 'See you at twelve.' 'Okay!'

examples.text: Vale, yo llevo las tazas al patio.
examples.trans: Alright, I will carry the cups to the courtyard.

valer.gloss: to be worth; to cost; to work / count

meanings.en: to be worth; to cost; to work / count
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg valgo.

examples.text: Cada minuto de calma vale oro.
examples.trans: Every minute of peace is worth its weight in gold.

examples.text: ¿Vale este billete para el tren regional?
examples.trans: Is this ticket valid for the regional train?

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Vamos en coche a Valladolid.
examples.trans: We're going by car to Valladolid.

examples.text: La Seminci se celebra en Valladolid.
examples.trans: Seminci is held in Valladolid.

meanings.note: Plural los valses.

examples.text: El piano suena precioso con este vals antiguo.
examples.trans: The piano sounds lovely with this old waltz.

examples.text: Un vals tiene siempre tres tiempos por compás.
examples.trans: A waltz always has three beats per bar.

meanings.note: Al vapor means 'steamed' in cooking (verduras al vapor).

examples.text: Un vapor aromático de limón subía desde el cazo caliente.
examples.trans: A fragrant lemon steam rose from the hot saucepan.

examples.text: El vapor de la tetera empañó el cristal de la ventana.
examples.trans: The steam from the teapot fogged up the windowpane.

meanings.note: Un vaso de agua = a glass of water.

examples.text: El vaso está aquí.
examples.trans: The drinking glass is here.

examples.text: Vemos los vasos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the drinking glasss from the door.

meanings.note: First- and third-person singular present subjunctive of the irregular verb 'ir' (to go), often used in 'irle bien/mal a alguien' (for things to go well/badly for someone).
Used colloquially as an exclamative determiner before a noun ('¡vaya leche!') or standalone interjection to express surprise, admiration, or annoyance.

examples.text: "-¡Esto! -Joder, vaya leche".
examples.trans: "-This! -Fuck, what a slap".

examples.text: No aguantas que a tus amigos les vaya bien. ¿Me has entendido?
examples.trans: You can't stand your friends doing well. Did you understand me?

meanings.note: From vecino ('neighbour'); same singular form for m/f, plural vecinales.

examples.text: Montamos una pequeña biblioteca vecinal junto al jardín.
examples.trans: We set up a small community book corner by the garden.

examples.text: El centro vecinal organiza conciertos los viernes por la tarde.
examples.trans: The neighbourhood centre holds concerts on Friday afternoons.

meanings.note: Feminine: la vecina.

examples.text: El vecino está aquí.
examples.trans: The neighbour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los vecinos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the neighbours from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Mide exactamente veinte milímetros.
examples.trans: It measures exactly twenty millimetres.

examples.text: Son las once y veinte.
examples.trans: It is eleven twenty.

meanings.note: Numbers 21–29 are written as one word in Spanish.

examples.text: Eso pasó hace veinticinco años.
examples.trans: That happened twenty-five years ago.

examples.text: Hay veinticinco sillas en total.
examples.trans: There are twenty-five chairs in total.

meanings.note: Written as a single word in Spanish (21–29 combine into one word).

examples.text: Dos docenas de sillas son veinticuatro sillas.
examples.trans: Two dozen chairs is twenty-four chairs.

examples.text: La recepción está tranquila las veinticuatro horas.
examples.trans: The front desk is peaceful twenty-four hours a day.

meanings.note: Single fused word for veinte + y + nueve.

examples.text: Febrero tiene veintinueve días ese año.
examples.trans: February has twenty-nine days that year.

examples.text: Conté veintinueve monedas de cambio.
examples.trans: I counted twenty-nine coins in change.

meanings.note: Written as a single word (veinte + y + ocho -> veintiocho).

examples.text: La melodía cambia suavemente en el compás veintiocho.
examples.trans: The melody shifts gently in bar twenty-eight.

examples.text: Este mes de febrero tiene exactamente veintiocho días.
examples.trans: This month of February has exactly twenty-eight days.

examples.text: Tengo veintiséis años.
examples.trans: I am twenty-six years old.

examples.text: Hay veintiséis sillas en la sala.
examples.trans: There are twenty-six chairs in the room.

meanings.note: A la misma velocidad = 'at the same speed / rate'; a toda velocidad = 'at top speed'.

examples.text: Los dados iguales de zanahoria se cocinan a la misma velocidad.
examples.trans: Equal-sized carrot cubes cook at the exact same speed.

examples.text: El tren regional cruzó el valle a buena velocidad.
examples.trans: The regional train crossed the valley at a good speed.

examples.text: Lo que yo iba a hacer es Velvet.
examples.trans: What I was meant to do is Velvet.

examples.text: Yo Velvet
examples.trans: I Velvet

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: En ese puesto venden flores frescas.
examples.trans: At that stall they sell fresh flowers.

examples.text: Vendieron la casa familiar hace tres años.
examples.trans: They sold the family house three years ago.

examples.text: Venga, vamos al coche.
examples.trans: Come on, let's go to the car.

examples.text: Venga, sonreíd.
examples.trans: Come on, smile.

venir.gloss: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)

meanings.en: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)
meanings.note: Irregular: vengo, vienes, viene, vine.

examples.text: Gracias por venir esta mañana.
examples.trans: Thank you for coming this morning.

examples.text: Nos vemos la semana que viene.
examples.trans: See you next week.

meanings.note: En venta = for sale.

examples.text: La venta es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The sale is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la venta.
examples.trans: We talk about the sale.

meanings.note: Una ventana soleada = a sunny window.

examples.text: La ventana está aquí.
examples.trans: The window is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ventanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the windows from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los ventiladores.

examples.text: Pon el ventilador a velocidad suave en el pasillo.
examples.trans: Set the fan to low speed in the hallway.

examples.text: Dos ventiladores mueven el aire seco hacia las ventanas.
examples.trans: Two fans move dry air toward the windows.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos luego en el patio!
examples.trans: See you later in the courtyard!

meanings.note: El verano que viene = next summer.

examples.text: El verano está aquí.
examples.trans: The summer is here.

examples.text: Vemos los veranos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the summers from the door.

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.text: La verdad está aquí.
examples.trans: The truth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verdades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the truths from the door.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza verde.
examples.trans: It is a green piece.

examples.text: Mateo, ¿me oyes? ¡Acabo de pasar la farmacia verde!
examples.trans: Mateo, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

meanings.note: Sopa de verduras = vegetable soup.

examples.text: La verdura está aquí.
examples.trans: The vegetable is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verduras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the vegetables from the door.

meanings.note: A painful feeling of humiliation or distress.

examples.text: Sintió mucha vergüenza al equivocarse.
examples.trans: She felt a lot of embarrassment upon making a mistake.

examples.text: Qué vergüenza verte así.
examples.trans: What a shame to see you like this.

meanings.note: Iron courtyard gate opening onto the street.

examples.text: La verja está aquí.
examples.trans: The wrought-iron gate is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verjas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the wrought-iron gates from the door.

examples.text: ¿Sabes recitar un verso?
examples.trans: Do you know how to recite verse?

examples.text: Lee el primer verso despacio.
examples.trans: Read the first line of verse slowly.

meanings.note: Compound form of the infinitive 'ver' (to see) and the enclitic second-person singular pronoun 'te'. Very common in greetings such as 'me alegro de verte' (glad to see you).

examples.text: Venga, vale. Me alegro de verte.
examples.trans: Alright, okay. Nice seeing you.

examples.text: Tenía muchas ganas de verte por la oficina para hablar del papel.
examples.trans: I was really looking forward to seeing you around the office to talk about the role.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine; un piano vertical = an upright piano.

examples.text: Escribe la palabra en una línea vertical.
examples.trans: Write the word in a vertical line.

examples.text: Tenemos un piano vertical en casa.
examples.trans: We have an upright piano at home.

meanings.note: Quoted English adverb used in *Paquita Salas* during broken-English ("spanglish") casting sessions to parody Spanish industry professionals and actors struggling with basic English lines.

examples.text: En el casting en inglés repetía: «But it's very important 'give' this».
examples.trans: In the English audition he kept repeating: "But it's very important 'give' this."

examples.text: Intentaba sonar internacional diciendo: «It's easy, but it's very important».
examples.trans: She tried to sound international by saying: "It's easy, but it's very important."

meanings.note: Second-person singular ('tú') future indicative of 'ver'. Especially frequent in the conversational reassurance or warning 'ya verás' (you'll see / just wait and see).

examples.text: Te voy a enseñar el videobook de la prima de Álex, ya verás cómo te gusta.
examples.trans: I'm going to show you the showreel of Álex's cousin—you'll see how much you like it.

examples.text: Le pedí que tuviéramos reunión hoy mismo. Ya verás qué bien sale todo.
examples.trans: I asked for us to have a meeting right today. You'll see how well everything turns out.

meanings.note: Second-person singular ('tú') present indicative of 'ver'. Frequently used as an interrogative discourse marker ('¿ves?' / '¿lo ves?') to draw attention or say 'see, I told you so'.

examples.text: Mira, mira, ¿ves aquí?
examples.trans: Look, look, do you see here?

examples.text: ¿Ves? ¡Es que yo no sé hacer "zoom"! ¡Uy! Se me ha puesto negra y todo.
examples.trans: See? I just do not know how to zoom! Oops! It has gone completely black.

meanings.note: Plural los vestidos.

examples.text: El vestido está aquí.
examples.trans: The dress is here.

examples.text: Vemos los vestidos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the dresss from the door.

examples.text: ¿Qué hago aquí vestida así?
examples.trans: What am I doing here dressed like this?

examples.text: Ella siempre viste muy bien.
examples.trans: She always dresses very well.

meanings.note: Hotel entrance hall.

examples.text: El vestíbulo está aquí.
examples.trans: The lobby is here.

examples.text: Vemos los vestíbulos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lobbys from the door.

meanings.note: Natural grain lines in timber or stone (seguir la veta).

examples.text: Lija siempre la tabla siguiendo la veta natural.
examples.trans: Always sand the board following the natural wood grain.

examples.text: El aceite limpio resalta las vetas oscuras del nogal.
examples.trans: Clean oil brings out the dark grain of the walnut.

vez.gloss: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)

meanings.en: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)
meanings.note: Plural las veces; a veces = sometimes; otra vez = again.

examples.text: La vez está aquí.
examples.trans: The time / occasion is here.

examples.text: Vemos las veces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the time / occasions from the door.

meanings.en: (I/he/she/it) was seeing, was watching, used to watch
meanings.note: First- and third-person singular imperfect indicative of 'ver' (to see/watch). Also used idiomatically in 'verlo venir' (to see it coming).

examples.text: Que si "House of Cards"... No sabía que eso lo veía nadie aquí.
examples.trans: Going on about "House of Cards"... I didn't know anyone here watched that.

examples.text: Yo llevaba unos días que lo veía venir, ¿sabes? No me lo creo.
examples.trans: For a few days now I could feel it coming, you know? I can't believe it.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Siempre viajo en tren junto a la ventana.
examples.trans: I always travel by train next to the window.

examples.text: Viajamos a Valencia el lunes por la mañana.
examples.trans: We travelled to Valencia on Monday morning.

meanings.note: Guía de viajes = travel guide.

examples.text: El viaje está aquí.
examples.trans: The trip is here.

examples.text: Vemos los viajes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the trips from the door.

meanings.note: Masculine: el viajero.

examples.text: La viajera está aquí.
examples.trans: The traveller is here.

examples.text: Vemos las viajeras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the travellers from the door.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Vicenta es una película preciosa.
examples.trans: Vicenta is a lovely film.

examples.text: Macarena protagoniza Vicenta.
examples.trans: Macarena stars in Vicenta.

meanings.note: Cantar victoria means 'to declare victory / celebrate prematurely'.

examples.text: Terminar antes del miércoles ya es una gran victoria.
examples.trans: Finishing before Wednesday is already a big victory.

examples.text: Celebramos nuestras pequeñas victorias con té y tarta.
examples.trans: We celebrate our small victories with tea and tart.

meanings.note: Toda la vida = one's whole life.

examples.text: La vida está aquí.
examples.trans: The life is here.

examples.text: Vemos las vidas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lifes from the door.

examples.text: ¿Te puedo mandar su videobook?
examples.trans: Can I send you her showreel?

examples.text: Grabamos un videobook nuevo.
examples.trans: We recorded a new showreel.

meanings.note: Before a noun (un viejo amigo), means 'long-standing / dear old'.

examples.text: Es una pieza vieja.
examples.trans: It is an old piece.

examples.text: La vieja buhardilla soleada... ¡seguidme, rápido!
examples.trans: The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: Gerund (present participle) of the verb 'ver', commonly combined with 'estar', 'seguir', or 'llevar' to form progressive aspect constructions.

examples.text: Pues piensa... que siempre que lo estés viendo, yo estoy ahí detrás de todo.
examples.trans: Well think... that whenever you are watching it, I am right there behind everything.

examples.text: Estábamos viendo la gala de premios en la tele del salón.
examples.trans: We were watching the awards ceremony on the living room TV.

meanings.note: Second-person singular ('tú') present indicative of the stem-changing irregular verb 'venir' (e -> ie). With reflexive 'te vienes', it means 'you come along / move here'.

examples.text: No, de visita. Pero si tú nunca vienes de visita.
examples.trans: No, just visiting. But you never come just to visit.

examples.text: Te vienes a Madrid, y yo te represento, ¿vale?
examples.trans: You come to Madrid, and I represent you, okay?

meanings.note: hace viento = it is windy.

examples.text: Hoy hace mucho viento.
examples.trans: It's very windy today.

examples.text: El viento cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: The wind shuts the window.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el viernes ('on Friday'), los viernes ('on Fridays').

examples.text: El viernes está aquí.
examples.trans: The Friday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los viernes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Fridays from the door.

meanings.note: Vigas de madera = wooden roof beams.

examples.text: La viga está aquí.
examples.trans: The ceiling beam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las vigas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ceiling beams from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: El vecino vigila que la caldera funcione bien.
examples.trans: El vecino watches to make sure the boiler runs properly.

examples.text: Vigilamos la maleta hasta el mediodía.
examples.trans: We guarded the suitcase until noon.

meanings.note: Used in dressings and diluted in warm water to clean glass streak-free.

examples.text: Unas gotas de vinagre dejan los cristales brillantes.
examples.trans: A few drops of vinegar leave the windowpanes sparkling.

examples.text: Guarda la botella de vinagre blanco en el armario.
examples.trans: Keep the bottle of white vinegar in the cupboard.

examples.text: Macarena vino a verme porque tú te estás quedando antigua.
examples.trans: Macarena came to see me because you're getting outdated.

examples.text: Yo vino
examples.trans: I vino

meanings.note: Drops the written accent mark in the plural because -es makes it naturally stressed on -li-: los violines.

examples.text: Nuestro vecino toca el violín desde que tenía ocho años.
examples.trans: Our neighbour has played the violin since he was eight years old.

examples.text: El violín y el piano sonaron juntos bajo el limonero.
examples.trans: The violin and the piano sounded together under the lemon tree.

examples.text: Tú harás Velvet, Vis a vis y El secreto de Puente Viejo.
examples.trans: You'll do Velvet, Vis a vis, and El secreto de Puente Viejo.

examples.text: Yo Vis
examples.trans: I Vis

meanings.note: Light window curtain letting daylight in while screening the view.

examples.text: El visillo está aquí.
examples.trans: The sheer curtain is here.

examples.text: Vemos los visillos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sheer curtains from the door.

meanings.note: Tener visita means 'to have company / visitors'.

examples.text: Preparamos la sala para la visita del miércoles.
examples.trans: We prepare the room for Wednesday's visit.

examples.text: Gracias por su amable visita a nuestra posada.
examples.trans: Thank you for your kind visit to our inn.

vista.gloss: view; sight; eyesight (a la vista = in sight)

meanings.en: view; sight; eyesight (a la vista = in sight)
meanings.note: Buena vista = sharp eyes / a lovely view.

examples.text: La vista está aquí.
examples.trans: The view is here.

examples.text: Vemos las vistas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the views from the door.

meanings.note: Echar un vistazo = to take a quick look.

examples.text: El vistazo está aquí.
examples.trans: The quick look is here.

examples.text: Vemos los vistazos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the quick looks from the door.

examples.text: (CLARA VITOREA)
examples.trans: (CLARA CHEERS)

examples.text: Yo VITOREA
examples.trans: I VITOREA

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb.

examples.text: Vivo a dos calles de la plaza.
examples.trans: I live two streets from the square.

examples.text: Mis primos vivieron aquí muchos años.
examples.trans: My cousins lived here for many years.

meanings.note: Applied to colours (verde vivo = bright green) as well as living things.

examples.text: Al secarse queda un tono verde vivo y luminoso.
examples.trans: Once dry it leaves a bright, luminous shade of green.

examples.text: Los colores vivos alegran la entrada en días grises.
examples.trans: Vivid colours brighten the entrance on grey days.

volar.gloss: to fly; to sell out / disappear fast

meanings.en: to fly; to sell out / disappear fast
meanings.note: Stem changes o -> ue in stressed present forms (vuelo, vuelas, vuela, vuelan; subjunctive vuele, vuelen).

examples.text: El pan recién hecho vuela cada sábado por la mañana.
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread disappears fast every Saturday morning.

examples.text: Los pájaros vuelan sobre el limonero del patio.
examples.trans: Birds fly above the courtyard lemon tree.

meanings.en: we return, we come back, we get back together
meanings.note: First-person plural ('nosotros/nosotras') present indicative of 'volver' (to return / to do again with 'volver a + infinitive').

examples.text: Y..., pues, Clara, que volvemos.
examples.trans: And... well, Clara, we're coming back.

examples.text: Volvemos a abrir la agencia después del verano con nuevos talentos.
examples.trans: We are reopening the agency after the summer with new talent.

volver.gloss: to return; to come back; to do again (volver a + inf)

meanings.en: to return; to come back; to do again (volver a + inf)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: vuelvo), past participle vuelto; volverse + adj = become.

examples.text: Vuelvo en cinco minutos.
examples.trans: I will be back in five minutes.

examples.text: Volvió a sonreír enseguida.
examples.trans: He smiled again right away.

meanings.note: Standard everyday plural of tú in Peninsula Spanish; feminine plural is vosotras.

examples.text: ¿Vosotros también queréis té con limón?
examples.trans: Do you all want tea with lemon too?

examples.text: Guardamos esta mesa tranquila para vosotros.
examples.trans: We saved this quiet table for you all.

meanings.note: Plural las voces; en voz baja = in a low voice.

examples.text: La voz está aquí.
examples.trans: The voice is here.

examples.text: Vemos las voces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the voices from the door.

vuelta.gloss: turn; return (de vuelta = back; media vuelta = turn around)

meanings.en: turn; return (de vuelta = back; media vuelta = turn around)
meanings.note: Dar una vuelta = take a stroll / make one turn.

examples.text: La vuelta está aquí.
examples.trans: The turn is here.

examples.text: Vemos las vueltas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the turns from the door.

examples.text: Chicos, valéis mucho. De verdad, luchad por vuestros sueños.
examples.trans: Guys, you're worth so much. Truly, fight for your dreams.

examples.text: Yo vuestro
examples.trans: I vuestro

meanings.note: Válvula de latón = brass valve.

examples.text: La válvula está aquí.
examples.trans: The valve is here.

examples.text: Vemos las válvulas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the valves from the door.

meanings.note: Second-person singular ('tú') affirmative imperative of 'vender' (vende) combined with the enclitic direct object pronoun 'lo' (it/him), requiring a written accent to preserve stress on the antepenultimate syllable.

forms.title: Affirmative Imperative of vender with Clitic Pronouns

examples.text: Véndelo como si fuera el proyecto más importante de la temporada.
examples.trans: Sell it as if it were the most important project of the season.

examples.text: Si ya no usas ese despacho, véndelo y quítate de gastos.
examples.trans: If you don't use that office anymore, sell it and cut your expenses.

examples.text: Paquita, ahora todo va vía link.
examples.trans: Paquita, everything goes by link nowadays.

examples.text: Yo vía
examples.trans: I vía

meanings.en: Washington (surname of actress and presenter Belinda Washington)
meanings.note: Refers in *Paquita Salas* to British-born Spanish actress, singer, and television presenter Belinda Washington, who plays a fictionalized version of herself represented by Paquita.

examples.text: Que traigo un paquete para Belinda Washington.
examples.trans: I'm bringing a package for Belinda Washington.

examples.text: Belinda Washington lleva muchos años trabajando en televisión y teatro en España.
examples.trans: Belinda Washington has spent many years working in television and theater in Spain.

examples.text: A ver si la quitas de la web.
examples.trans: See if you can take her off the website.

examples.text: Yo web
examples.trans: I web

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: ¿Me mandas un WhatsApp luego?
examples.trans: Will you send me a WhatsApp later?

examples.text: Te escribo por WhatsApp.
examples.trans: I'll message you on WhatsApp.

meanings.note: Proper name from the episode.

examples.text: Míralo en Wikipedia.
examples.trans: Look it up on Wikipedia.

examples.text: Busca en Wikipedia si existe.
examples.trans: Check on Wikipedia whether it exists.

examples.text: Bonita, muy XVIII. De época.
examples.trans: Pretty, very eighteenth century. Period appropriate.

examples.text: Yo XVIII
examples.trans: I XVIII

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: ¡Ya está! = All done!; ya no = no longer.

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is already ready.

examples.text: ¡Ya voy con las llaves!
examples.trans: Coming right now with the keys!

meanings.en: years (quoted English noun in 'X years old')
meanings.note: Quoted English plural noun used in *Paquita Salas* when actresses record self-tapes in heavily accented English ('I am 25 years old'). In Spanish, age is expressed with 'tener X años'.

examples.text: En su vídeo de casting dijo: «Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old».
examples.trans: In her audition video she said: "Hello, my name is Mariona Terés, and I am 25 years old."

examples.text: Se aprendió de memoria la frase con «years old» para la prueba en inglés.
examples.trans: She memorized the phrase with "years old" for the English screen test.

meanings.note: Means 'egg yolk' (yema de huevo, opposite of la clara), 'fingertip' (la yema del dedo), or a plant 'bud'.

examples.text: Para la crema de limón batimos cuatro yemas de huevo con azúcar.
examples.trans: For the lemon curd we whisk four egg yolks with sugar.

examples.text: Las yemas dan un color amarillo dorado precioso a los pasteles.
examples.trans: The yolks give a lovely golden-yellow colour to pastries.

meanings.note: Often omitted in Spanish unless adding contrast or emphasis.

examples.text: Yo abro la puerta y tú llevas la linterna.
examples.trans: I will open the door and you carry the flashlight.

examples.text: Soy yo, abre por favor.
examples.trans: It is me, please open up.

examples.text: Silvia es yudoca.
examples.trans: Silvia does judo.

examples.text: Los dos hermanos son yudocas.
examples.trans: Both siblings do judo.

meanings.note: Silent medial -h-; pronounced [θanaˈoɾja] in Peninsular Spanish.

examples.text: Pela seis zanahorias frescas para la sopa de lentejas.
examples.trans: Peel six fresh carrots for the lentil soup.

examples.text: Cortamos la zanahoria en dados iguales sobre la tabla.
examples.trans: We dice the carrot into even cubes on the board.

meanings.note: Plural los zapatos.

examples.text: El zapato está aquí.
examples.trans: The shoe is here.

examples.text: Vemos los zapatos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shoes from the door.

meanings.note: Masculine English loanword adapted into Spanish (sometimes spelled 'zum'). Typically used in the phrase 'hacer zoom' (to zoom in/out with a camera or phone screen).

examples.text: ¿Ves? ¡Es que yo no sé hacer "zoom"! ¡Uy! Se me ha puesto negra y todo.
examples.trans: See? I just do not know how to zoom! Oops! It has gone completely black.

examples.text: No tiene muy buena luz, y yo no sé hacer "zoom" con esto.
examples.trans: It does not have very good light, and I do not know how to zoom with this.

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for fruit juice (zumo de naranja).

examples.text: El zumo está aquí.
examples.trans: The juice is here.

examples.text: Vemos los zumos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the juices from the door.

examples.text: Mira el de Miguel Ángel Muñoz.
examples.trans: Look at Miguel Ángel Muñoz's one.

examples.text: Yo Ángel
examples.trans: I Ángel

meanings.en: Los Angeles (in 'Los Ángeles', California); angels (plural of 'ángel')
meanings.note: Capitalized in 'Los Ángeles' to refer to the entertainment capital in California where Spanish actors aspire to audition; as a common masculine plural noun ('los ángeles', IPA /ˈaŋxeles/), it means 'angels'.

examples.text: Pues, mira, acabo de llegar de Los Ángeles, de hacer unas pruebas.
examples.trans: Well, look, I just got back from Los Angeles, after doing some screen tests.

examples.text: Muchos actores españoles sueñan con mudarse a Los Ángeles para triunfar en el cine.
examples.trans: Many Spanish actors dream of moving to Los Angeles to make it big in film.

meanings.note: Plural los árboles.

examples.text: El árbol está aquí.
examples.trans: The tree is here.

examples.text: Vemos los árboles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the trees from the door.

meanings.note: Top floor under the roof; carries a written accent on á.

examples.text: Javier duerme en la habitación tranquila del ático.
examples.trans: Javier sleeps in the quiet attic room.

examples.text: Subimos al ático para buscar el libro verde.
examples.trans: We go up to the attic to look for the green book.

meanings.note: Accented él ('he/him') is distinct from unaccented article el ('the').

examples.text: Él trabaja en el ayuntamiento.
examples.trans: He works at City Hall.

examples.text: Sube a hablar con él un minuto.
examples.trans: Go upstairs and talk to him for a minute.

meanings.note: Feminine noun denoting a historical period or personal stage of life ('en aquella época').
In film, television, and theater jargon, 'una serie/película de época' or 'vestuario de época' refers to a period drama or period costume set in a past century (like *Puente Viejo*).

examples.text: Me han hablado de una cosita de época que se va a hacer a nivel europeo.
examples.trans: They told me about a little period piece that is going to be done at a European level.

examples.text: Bonita, muy XVIII. De época.
examples.trans: Pretty, very eighteenth century. Period appropriate.

meanings.note: False friend: means 'success', whereas 'exit' is la salida!

examples.text: El éxito está aquí.
examples.trans: The success is here.

examples.text: Vemos los éxitos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the successs from the door.

examples.text: Somos íntimas amigas desde hace años.
examples.trans: We have been close friends for years.

examples.text: Fue una cena muy íntima.
examples.trans: It was a very intimate dinner.

examples.text: Hay que abrir un poco la óptica.
examples.trans: We need to broaden our perspective a little.

examples.text: Yo óptica
examples.trans: I óptica

meanings.note: Used in the plural with the definite article ('los Óscar', invariable in standard Spanish) to refer to the Hollywood Academy Awards, the ultimate symbol of international acting prestige.

examples.text: Se veía ya en una gala de los Óscar, que si en un rodaje en Estados Unidos...
examples.trans: She could already picture herself at an Oscars gala, or on a film shoot in the United States...

examples.text: Para Paquita, que una actriz suya gane un Goya es como ganar un Óscar.
examples.trans: For Paquita, having one of her actresses win a Goya is like winning an Oscar.

meanings.note: Carries a written accent on ú.

examples.text: Es una pieza última.
examples.trans: It is a last piece.

examples.text: Diez, once, doce. Exacto hasta la última moneda. ¡Gracias!
examples.trans: Ten, eleven, twelve. Exact to the last coin. Thank you!

examples.text: Lo único que quiero es descansar.
examples.trans: The only thing I want is to rest.

examples.text: Es una oportunidad única.
examples.trans: It is a unique opportunity.
